speaker: Warsh
text: Thank you for the opportunity to speak today about financial intermediation and developments in the capital markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: New financial instruments and changing models of financial intermediation are having a profound impact on global financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: London, home to one of the worldâs fastest growing and much admired financial centers, represents a most appropriate venue to discuss these changes.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: During the past few decades--particularly the last few years--we have witnessed an escalating supply of new financial instruments scarcely able to match surging demand.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Through the technique of unbundling risks--dividing them by category and tranche--financial instruments proliferated to enable risks to be borne by those most willing to accept them.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: And with the benefit of ample liquidity, which I described in previous remarks as broadly equal to confidence, financial products quickly found deep markets, ensuring robust trading.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, liquidity-fueled innovation has made markets substantially more âcompleteâ--that is, more risks are more readily priced and traded without significant diminution in value than in prior periods.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: 3 The concept of âcomplete marketsâ is, in my view, a useful, aspirational, and theoretical construct, even though perfectly complete markets, in which every agent is able to costlessly trade claims on every state of the world, represents an unachievable goal.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: After all, the fundamental departures from the complete markets paradigm--transactions costs and asymmetric information--will never vanish.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Nevertheless, in these heady times, one wonders whether some market participants may treat recent developments as a testament to an all-but-assured path to complete markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In my remarks today, I will discuss how liquidity and financial innovation are making markets more complete--or more precisely, less incomplete--than in earlier periods.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: 4 I will also describe how the acceleration toward complete markets conflated the roles among financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Finally, I will consider the possible consequences should this trend toward complete markets be slowed or upended by some form of negative liquidity shock.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial Intermediation:  Remembering the âGood Old Daysâ Broadly speaking, intermediaries facilitate the transfer of capital and risk between borrowers and savers.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The case for financial intermediation rests on two premises: (1) borrowers hold superior information about their own financial condition and prospects than prospective providers of capital; (2) the search and screening costs to match creditors and debtors without the services of trusted third parties are prohibitive.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The history of financial intermediation, thus, is the story of individual types of institutions--FDIC-insured commercial banks, SEC-registered broker dealers, Federal Reserve-supervised holding companies, just to name a few--adapting their products and practices to meet customer demands.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Traditionally, commercial banks played critical roles as principals in the financial intermediation process.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Community banks today--to a somewhat greater degree than their larger money-center brethren--most clearly retain the traditional commercial banking approach to financial intermediation.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Community banks finance relatively opaque entities, such as private companies and households.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: They raise funds primarily by issuing demand deposits.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: They deploy capital by underwriting loans, monitoring borrowers, and retaining some loans in portfolio as long-term investments.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Of course, when banks originate and hold loans, they internalize the costs of their own underwriting standards, and so have strong incentives to screen borrowers and enforce contractual covenants, as appropriate.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Investment banks also served important roles in financial intermediation.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Somewhat unlike commercial banks, investment banks traditionally acted more as agents, distributing, rather than holding, most of their resulting exposures.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: They focused predominantly on the business of underwriting; that is, helping firms gain access to the public securities markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In this role, investment banks added value to the intermediation process, in part, by de facto certification of a companyâs operations, practices, and prospects.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As repeat players in the underwriting business, investment banks sought to maintain prudent underwriting standards to bolster their reputations as effective screeners of companies.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In so doing, they built significant value in their distribution networks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial intermediation has also long been provided by less-regulated institutions.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: For decades, relatively high net worth, sophisticated investors formed private pools of capital to invest their funds.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: To allow flexibility in their investments, these pooled investment vehicles were structured to be exempt from regulation as investment companies.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Reflecting the nature of the investor base, these informal pools often sought to gain exposure to asset classes to diversify their portfolios.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: These traditional roles of financial intermediaries seem, somehow, oddly quaint in 2007.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As I will next describe, financial intermediaries have been transformed by their own actionsââtheir massive investments in human and technological capital to develop new financial productsââand by the worldwide rise in liquidity that has added depth and resiliency to the markets for these new products.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The Brave New World:  Massive Financial Innovation and Ample Liquidity No single statistic can put the recent surge of financial product and market innovation into perspective.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: I will, however, cite a few illustrative indicators.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The value added by the U.S. financial sector gives a rough sense of the effect these innovations have had on the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In 1960, financial services accounted for about 3-1/2 percent of U.S. gross domestic product.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: By 2006, that percentage had more than doubled.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Securitized products are one important area of product and market innovation.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Of the $3.6 trillion in net borrowing in U.S. credit markets in 2006, $820 billion, or nearly one-fourth, was securitized.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As of year-end 2006, roughly 30 percent of the outstanding balances of corporate bonds and household credit resided in asset-backed securities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In addition, use of derivative products has soared; the notional amount of interest rate swaps and options has tripled in the past four years to nearly $300 trillion.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The notional amount of credit default swaps has almost quintupled in only two years, from $6.4 trillion outstanding in 2004 to $29 trillion in 2006.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Product and market innovations, such as these, have contributed to the high degree of liquidity found today in global financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As I have discussed in prior remarks, âliquidityâ in the sense of âtrading liquidityâ reflects the ability to transact quickly without exerting a material effect on prices.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Underlying this concept is the fact that although the many buyers and sellers have different views on the most likely outcomes, the distributions of possible outcomes for which they demand risk-based compensation can be quantified.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Liquidity exists when investors are confident and willing to take risks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Liquidity, then, can be viewed as confidence on the part of buyers and sellers of securities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: By disaggregating a security into its constituent risk components, financial innovation can unlock this liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Strong global economic performance provides another important support for the high liquidity and levels of confidence in todayâs capital markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Many economies have achieved a marked reduction in the volatility of real output and core inflation in the past twenty years or so.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Liquidity can flourish if investors interpret strong performance to mean that future economic outcomes will be benign and that âtailâ realizations are either highly improbable or, at the very least, quantifiable and, hence, can be traded upon.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: There is little doubt, then, that liquidity in most financial markets is high today and that investors seem willing to take risks, even at todayâs market-prevailing prices.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In the United States, term premiums on long-term Treasury yields are very low, corporate bonds appear to be nearly âpriced for perfection,â and stock prices are setting new records.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Credit markets are highly accommodative for issuers, and the volume of loans to finance highly leveraged transactions is escalating rapidly.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: These prices, terms and credit conditions may reflect solid economic fundamentals--low output and inflation uncertainty, healthy corporate balance sheets, and corporate profits that exceed market expectations--and if so, they may help to ease the effects of fluctuations in liquidity should they occur.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The prices and conditions may also reflect increased appetite for risk; or, far less auspiciously, they may be indicative of investor overconfidence.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The Brave New World: More Complete Markets and Conflating Roles The powerful combination of liquidity and financial innovation has made markets seemingly more complete--that is, more risks are priced and traded without undue penalty owing to their unique nature or shallowness of the relevant financial market.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial innovation, by definition, makes markets more complete by expanding the set of available types of securities and reducing transaction costs.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: And liquidity provides some degree of assurance that funds will readily flow into new structures and new securities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The benefits of more complete markets are three-fold.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: First, they allow firms and households to hedge a variety of risks, a considerable benefit when volatility is costly.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Second, they make it more feasible for investors to fine tune the risk-return profiles of their portfolios.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The concomitant reduction in risk premiums required by investors should reduce capital costs for all economic agents.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Third, risks once held within the four walls of financial institutions are converted into tradable securities and distributed and dispersed to a broader base of institutions and interests.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Liquidity and financial innovation have also led to a conflation of the roles played by financial intermediaries, themselves.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Intermediation has moved increasingly to financial markets and away from regulated bank institutions.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The core functions of financial institutionsââcreating, distributing, and owning riskââhave remained the same, but the type of firm performing the various functions appears to have changed dramatically.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: This conflation of roles has the potential to alter some incentives in the credit extension process.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: And these roles may well change with further product and market developments, and, not least of all, due to a potential ebbing of liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: First, consider the changing role of commercial banks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In the syndicated loan market, lead banks have increasingly distributed large shares of syndicated loans to other banks and institutional lenders, many in the form of collateralized loan obligations (CLOs).
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In addition, commercial banks in some cases now sell entire loans rather than retain them on their books.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, they now securitize a variety of credit exposures, such as credit cards and mortgages, and sell them to structured entities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: While banks still maintain large loan exposures, including most recently those for âequity bridges,â the increased trend to distribute rather than hold some residual risks is unmistakable.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Second, consider the critical role played by investors purportedly with high tolerance for risk.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: A CLO structure does not in and of itself convert a pool of low-rated securities into tranches of high-rated securities through some form of alchemy.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Rather, a class of investors must be willing to hold the most concentrated risks as residual claimants.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Today, that role appears to be tailor-made for hedge funds, and sometimes the trading desks at leading investment banks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: By serving as willing counterparties in a variety of contracts, these institutions, in my view, are serving as a critical linchpin in the development of more complete markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Third, consider the evolving role of investment banks, no longer just originating and distributing primary securities, but increasingly owning assets in portfolio.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The more traditional agent role surely provided an enviable advantage in gauging investor appetite for new securities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Similarly, their expertise in pricing public securities may have served them well in developing new financial products--so well in fact that they are increasingly creating and underwriting new securitized and risk-management products.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As part of their modern-day underwriting role, investment banks sometimes hold (at least for a time) the residual or other tranches, of these new products.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Even more recently, many one-time broker-dealers have increased their principal investing by serving as general partners of private equity funds.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Changes in intermediation roles certainly raise potential challenges, though they may be alleviated somewhat by reputation and other market-based factors.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The increased specialization of some commercial banks as originators and distributors--and less as long-term owners--of some loans may have lessened their incentives to screen borrowers, and to write and monitor loan covenants.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Notably, this incentive problem may be more pronounced when they sell an entire loan, as in mortgage securitization programs, and less so when the bank retains some portion of the loan, as with syndicated loans.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, in the subprime mortgage market, for example, some believe that investment banks that pool and structure loans might have insufficient incentives in some cases to effectively screen.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: After all, critics assert, a borrower walks into a commercial bank for a loan, not into the investment bank that packages and distributes the loan through a structured vehicle.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Greater liquidity or confidence does little to mitigate these problems; indeed, it could exacerbate them if confidence begets complacency.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: For instance, if in liquid times, investors in structured products become complacent, they may not fully evaluate or accurately model the nature of the underlying assets in structured entities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Complacent investors also may be willing to buy new debt offerings that are light on traditional covenants if they come to believe that outcomes are assuredly benign.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, without strong covenants on existing debt, firms can raise additional funds without triggering defaults, which may decrease defaults in the short run, but perhaps increase them in the long run.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In these cases, this âglossâ of confidence could cause a misallocation of resources, if companies or consumers without compelling prospects for full repayment nonetheless readily obtain credit.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: We, as policymakers, should be careful, and indeed humble, in making definitive judgments in this fast-changing area.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Investment banks and commercial banks with enduring reputations--and growing private pools seeking permanent capital--are wont to protect their credibility and financial strength, even in liquid market conditions.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: To the extent that investment banks hold portions of the equity or lower-rated tranches of the securitized pools, they have strong incentives to screen effectively.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, evidence from secondary markets that suggests that investors differentiate securitized pools according to the identity of the originating banks, and not just by credit ratings, provides some comfort that traditional certification functions are at work.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: What Happens When Liquidity Falters?
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Of course, we as policymakers should be careful not to suffer from a failure of imagination in considering the causes and consequences of an unexpected negative shock to liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: (Surely, financial innovators have not suffered from a lack of imagination.)
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, we must ask ourselves what may happen when liquidity falters.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Well, consider the consequence if stock prices sold off globally, implied volatility jumped, and record trading volumes overwhelmed the trading capacity on the stock exchanges.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Consider a spike in a measure of implied U.S. equity-market volatility so large that it would be in the top 1/2 of one percent of one-day changes in nearly a generation.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Then, reflect on the likely divergence of opinions on the possible causes of such a rapid change in sentimentââperhaps it was a freefall in stock prices in a growing emerging-market economy, or escalating concerns about lending standards in some markets, or rapidly changing animal spirits eroding investor confidence.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Well, it does not take a long memory to recall that this scenario played out for a few days in late February, a bit more than three months ago.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As you all know, share prices quickly recovered, and implied volatility reverted to near-record low levels.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: What lessons can be drawn from such an episode?
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Perhaps because of more complete markets, shocks to liquidity are less likely to become self-fulfilling and less likely to impose more lasting damage.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: That hypothesis seems particularly credible when the shock is based neither on rapidly changing economic fundamentals nor a genuine breakdown in market infrastructure.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In the recent episode, opportunistic capital apparently viewed large movements in asset prices as trading opportunities.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Or, perhaps, striking as it was, we have not yet witnessed a scenario that subjects the latest product innovations and behavior of market participants to a sufficiently stringent stress test.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Some highly-leveraged private pools of capital may be unable to ride out bouts of very high turbulence if they are compelled to sell assets to meet margin calls or withdrawals, and by so doing, amplify the initial shocks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The losses would be sharper and correlations would be higher for assets in which markets quickly become shallow.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In theory, to the extent that more complete markets yield deeper, more robust asset markets and better-diversified positions, the dynamics of the disturbance should be more manageable.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: But, the question of actual experience versus theory remains.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Of course, a reduction in liquidity rooted in economic fundamentals would likely be more protracted and beget far more serious consequences.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In a period of sustained and diminished liquidity, it is indeed plausible that financial intermediaries could revert to their traditional roles, thereby likely worsening the efficiency and completeness of markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In such a case, those who pine for the good old days and purported good old roles of commercial and investment banks might not enjoy the economic environment that accompanies their return.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Even so, over the long-term, I remain a watchful optimist:  Reductions in liquidity are unlikely to turn back the clock on financial innovation.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The knowledge of how to bundle, distribute, and price risk cannot be erased from our collective memories.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Nor can this knowledge be walled off from the rest of the world by one country or financial center.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The culture of capitalism remains on the march.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: First-mover advantages are growing, even while the half-life of financial innovation is shrinking.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The growth of competing financial centers around the globe is testament to the enduring power of financial innovation and the dynamism of financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In my judgment, while the completeness of markets will remain an elusive goal, and the depth and breadth of financial markets will invariably be tested in ways that punish the ill-advised and unprepared, the secular trend toward more complete markets is unlikely to abate.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Cyclical variances, however, are far more difficult to predict with precision.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Perhaps, then, we should consider the growth in financial innovation as being analogous to Mooreâs Law, which has for more than a generation accurately predicted the growth in computing power of a transistor at constant cost.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: 7 Neither Mooreâs Law nor the development of new financial products is a mathematical or physical certainty based on some geometric extrapolation or law of the universe.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Rather, it is an ex post description of that which already transpired, an occurrence caused by a healthy mix of investment in human and technological capital, a culture of capitalism, and sound regulatory and legal policies.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As a result, meaningful erosion of any these core elements could impair the future evolution of financial products and jeopardize the continued development of markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Conclusion Innovations in financial products and practices, combined with strong liquidity, have accelerated the trend toward more complete markets.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: These changes have altered the roles of traditional financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In so doing, the products and practices of financial intermediation have, in my view, forever changed.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As for the financial intermediaries themselves, they will continue to evolve with changing economic and financial risks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed perhaps some may retreat to the practices of an earlier era if liquidity falters.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In this case, markets may, for a time, become less complete.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: However, I believe that the advances of intellectual capital and the culture of capitalism will likely continue to increase the ability of markets to transfer risk even as liquidity fluctuates.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: As policymakers, we should continually review the changing financial landscape.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: 8 Our regulatory and supervisory responses should be as dynamic as the financial intermediaries and the products they proffer, while adhering to our long-standing objectives to promote financial stability, investor protection, and market integrity.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: In general, our regulatory frameworks should not be based on a product or class of institutions.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Rather, we should strive to develop common, principles-based, risk-focused approaches that can adapt as intermediaries makes choices about whether to be originators, distributors or owners of risk (or all of the above).
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Among the key elements of such approaches are an emphasis on robust stress testing, enhanced counterparty risk management, and safe and efficient market infrastructures.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The opinions I will be expressing are my own and do not necessarily correspond with those of my colleagues in the Federal Reserve System.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Nellie Liang and Daniel M. Covitz , of the Federal Reserve Boardâs staff, provided valuable contributions to these remarks.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Kevin Warsh (2007), â Market Liquidity: Definitions and Implications ,â speech delivered at the Institute of International Bankers Annual Washington Conference, Washington, March 5, www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/warsh20070305a.htm.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: The notion of complete markets in an idealized economy was first formalized in Kenneth J. Arrow and Gerard Debreu (1954), âExistence of Equilibrium for a Competitive Economy,â Econometrica, vol.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: While some of the data I cite are U.S.-based, the trends of financial innovation and strong liquidity are also apparent in many other advanced economies.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Warsh
text: Insurance of commercial bank deposits has the potential to mitigate these incentives to screen and monitor borrowers.
speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

text: Other sources of liquidity include increased international capital flows as a result of excess savings in some emerging-market and oil-exporting countries, which have flowed to U.S. and other financial markets with sound legal and regulatory structures.

speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speech_title: Financial Intermediation and Complete Markets
speech_venue: At the European Economics and Financial Centre, London, England

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am pleased to be here today to chair the Federal Reserve Board's public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA).
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The hearing will focus specifically on how the Board might use its rulemaking authority under HOEPA to address concerns about abusive mortgage lending practices.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the course of this hearing, we will hear from key players in the home mortgage market:  lenders, brokers, secondary market participants, consumer advocacy and community development organizations, academics and researchers, and state regulators.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Although they play different roles, all share a common goal:  encouraging responsible mortgage lending for the benefit of individual consumers and the American economy as a whole.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Congress enacted HOEPA in 1994 in response to concerns about abusive lending in the home equity market, and the Federal Reserve Board was given broad authority to implement its provisions and to adopt regulations that the Board finds to be necessary and proper to effectuate its purposes.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, the Board has the responsibility to prohibit acts or practices it finds unfair or deceptive, or otherwise designed to evade HOEPA.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Board understands its rulemaking responsibility under HOEPA but is not alone in facing the important task of preventing unfair and deceptive practices.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Other regulators share in our responsibility to ensure responsible mortgage lending through enforcement powers.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The states have extensive regulatory authority--and responsibility--under their own anti-predatory lending statutes, various other relevant legal authorities, and especially their mortgage industry licensing acts--which give them considerable control over the activities of mortgage brokers and lenders.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Many of the states, including notably those that are represented on this afternoon's panel, have been very active in reining in bad actors in their mortgage markets.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The FTC also shares in our enforcement responsibilities under HOEPA and other federal laws.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Finally, the other federal financial regulatory agencies each have a duty to enforce federal consumer protection laws, including HOEPA, with respect to the depository institutions under their respective supervisory ambits.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In light of the sheer magnitude of the task, we are very pleased that these regulators all contribute to the goal of ensuring a healthy, competitive, and responsible mortgage market.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We are committed to working closely with other federal and state regulators to ensure that the laws that protect consumers are enforced.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: HOEPA also directs the Board to hold hearings such as the one we hold today, to assess the effectiveness of regulations and laws in protecting consumers.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Hearings provide us with valuable information.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In our most recent prior hearings , held last summer in four cities around the country, our goals included assessing the effectiveness of our 2001 amendments to the HOEPA rules in curbing abusive lending practices while preserving access to credit.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We also wanted to gather information on the effectiveness of the mortgage disclosures required by our Regulation Z, pursuant to the Truth in Lending Act, to inform our review of those disclosures, which is underway now.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Rising foreclosures in the subprime market over the past year have led the Board to consider whether and how it should use its rulemaking authority to address these concerns.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In doing so, however, we must walk a fine line.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We must determine how we can help to weed out abuses while also preserving incentives for responsible lenders.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A robust and responsible subprime mortgage market benefits consumers by allowing borrowers with blemished or limited credit histories to become homeowners, access the equity in their homes, or have the flexibility to refinance their loans as needed.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this task we have several tools at our disposal.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These include required disclosures by lenders, rules to prohibit abusive practices, principles-based guidance with supervisory oversight, less formal efforts to work with industry participants to promote best practices, and consumer education materials.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve currently is conducting a thorough review of its policies with respect to each of these tools.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Last year, together with other federal banking regulators, we issued guidance concerning so-called nontraditional mortgages.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have also issued proposed supervisory guidance concerning underwriting standards and disclosures for subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The agencies are finishing their review of the comments received and expect to issue the final version soon.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: And the Federal Reserve produces a range of consumer education materials, including information to help potential borrowers understand adjustable-rate and other alternative mortgages, and we actively promote financial education by partnering with outside organizations.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The two tools that we will focus on today, however, are lender disclosures to consumers and rules that prohibit or restrict lending practices.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Disclosures provide information that is critical to the effective functioning of markets.
speech_title: Encouraging Responsible Mortgage Lending: Prospective Rulemaking Initiatives
speech_venue: At the public hearing under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA), Federal Reserve Board, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A core principle of economics is that markets are more competitive, and therefore more efficient, when accurate information is available to all participants.

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke

text: The External Finance Premium and the Financial Accelerator Both real and monetary shocks produced the Great Depression, and in my 1983 paper I argued that banking and financial markets propagated both types of impulses, without distinguishing sharply between the two.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the nonmonetary side, Mark Gertler and I showed how, in principle, the effects of a real shock (such as a shock to productivity) on financial conditions could lead to persistent fluctuations in the economy, even if the initiating shock had little or no intrinsic persistence (Bernanke and Gertler, 1989).

speaker: Bernanke
text: A key concept in our analysis was the external finance premium, defined as the difference between the cost to a borrower of raising funds externally and the opportunity cost of internal funds.

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, the theory predicts that the external finance premium that a borrower must pay should depend inversely on the strength of the borrower's financial position, measured in terms of factors such as net worth, liquidity, and current and future expected cash flows.

speech_venue: At the The Credit Channel of Monetary Policy in the Twenty-first Century Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, Atlanta, Georgia

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke
text: The inverse relationship of the external finance premium and the financial condition of borrowers creates a channel through which otherwise short-lived economic shocks may have long-lasting effects.

speaker: Bernanke

text: Monetary Policy and the Credit Channel The ideas I have been discussing today have also been useful in understanding the nature of the monetary policy transmission process.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some evidence suggests that the influence of monetary policy on real variables is greater than can be explained by the traditional "cost-of-capital" channel, which holds that monetary policy affects borrowing, investment, and spending decisions solely through its effect on the level of market interest rates.

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke
text: One such supplementary channel, the so-called credit channel, holds that monetary policy has additional effects because interest-rate decisions affect the cost and availability of credit by more than would be implied by the associated movement in risk-free interest rates, such as Treasury rates.

speech_venue: At the The Credit Channel of Monetary Policy in the Twenty-first Century Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, Atlanta, Georgia

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke
text: The balance-sheet channel of monetary policy is closely related to the idea of the financial accelerator that I have already discussed.

speaker: Bernanke
text: That theory builds from the premise that changes in interest rates engineered by the central bank affect the values of the assets and the cash flows of potential borrowers and thus their creditworthiness, which in turn affects the external finance premium that borrowers face.
