speaker: Mishkin
text: Governor Mishkin presented identical remarks at the New Perspectives on Financial Globalization Conference, International Monetary Fund, Washington, D.C., on April 26, 2007
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the United States and many other countries, students learn that the key to success is hard work.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Yet when we look at many developing countries, we see people who work extremely hard for long hours.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Their wages are low, and so they remain poor.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: And as a whole, their countries remain poor.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If hard work does not make a country rich, what does?
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The right institutions are essential.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nobel laureate Douglass North defines institutions as the "rules of the game in a society, or, more formally, humanly devised constraints that shape human intervention."
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Among the institutions that are most crucial to economic growth are those that enable a country to allocate capital to its most productive uses.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such institutions establish and maintain strong property rights, an effective legal system, and a sound and efficient financial system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In recent years, the field of economic development has come to the conclusion that "institutions rule" and are critical to economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 1 An extensive literature focuses on financial development as a significant force driving economic development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, developing good institutions that foster financial development is not easy:  It takes time for institutions to evolve and adapt to local circumstances.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, vested interests in poor countries often oppose the necessary reforms because they believe that such reforms will weaken their power or allow other people to cut into their profits.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: How can poorer countries overcome these obstacles?
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: How can they change the distribution of power to forge the political will to promote institutional reform?
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: I should note that the opinions I will express today are my own and not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Elements of Institutional Reform Before examining the role of globalization in promoting financial development, letâs first look briefly at what steps must be taken to build an institutional infrastructure that will ensure a well-functioning financial system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Strong property rights are needed to encourage productive investment because it will not be undertaken if the returns on investment are likely to be taken away by the government or others.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Hernando de Soto, in his important book The Mystery of Capital , argues that the inability of the poor in developing countries to acquire property rights is a central reason that they are unable to gain access to capital and so remain mired in poverty.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the use of collateral is a crucial tool that helps the financial system make loans because it reduces losses when loans go sour.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: A person who would pledge land or capital for a loan must, however, legally own the collateral.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Unfortunately, as de Soto has documented, legalizing the ownership of capital is extremely expensive and time consuming for the poor in developing countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In one of his many astonishing examples, obtaining legal title to a dwelling on urban land in the Philippines required taking 168 bureaucratic steps through 53 public and private agencies over a period of 13 to 25 years.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: A legal system that enforces contracts quickly and fairly is an essential step in supporting strong property rights and financial development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, lenders write restrictive covenants into loan contracts to prevent borrowers from taking on too much risk, but such covenants have value only if they can be legally enforced.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: An inefficient legal system in which loan contracts cannot be enforced will prevent productive lending from taking place.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If setting up legitimate businesses or obtaining legal title to property is too expensive, the poor will never have access to the legal system and will be cut off from lending that could help them start small businesses and escape poverty.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 3 Setting up a simple business in the United States generally requires only filling out a form and paying a nominal licensing fee.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In contrast, de Soto's researchers found that legally registering a small garment workshop in Peru required 289 days; at 6 hours per day, the cost was about $1,200, which was approximately thirty times the monthly minimum wage.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The lack of property rights for all but the very rich, as documented by de Soto, is a serious impediment to financial development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Government is often the primary source of financial repression in developing countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Rapacious governments whose rulers treat their countries as personal fiefdoms are not uncommon:  We have seen these governments in Saddam Hussein's Iraq, Robert Mugabe's Zimbabwe, and Ferdinand Marcos's Philippines.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even officials in less tyrannical governments have been known to use the power of the state to get rich.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Not surprisingly, then, many governments pay lip service to property rights but do not encourage a rule of law to protect them.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Eliminating corruption is essential to strengthening property rights and the legal system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: When corrupt officials demand bribes, they reduce the incentives for entrepreneurs to make investments.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The ability to buy off judges weakens the enforcement of legal contracts that enable the economic and financial system to function smoothly.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Improve the quality of financial information.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: High-quality financial information is essential to well-functioning financial markets.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If lenders cannot figure out what is going on in a firm, they will be unable to screen out good from bad credit risks or to monitor the firm to ensure that it does not take on too much risk at the lenderâs expense.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: To make reliable and accurate information more accessible, accounting standards must be high enough so that prospective lenders can make sense of what is in a businessâs books.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Rules that require businesses to disclose information must be enforced to enable prospective investors to make sensible decisions about whether the business deserves to get their hard-earned money.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: For people to be willing to buy stocks, another way to channel funds to business, rules must be established to ensure that the managers of corporations act in the stockholdersâ interest.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If managers find it easy to steal from the corporation, or to use funds for their own personal use rather than for the benefit of the company, no one will want to invest in the company.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finding the right balance of control between management and stockholders is a challenge with which even we in the United States continue to struggle.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Develop sound, prudential regulation and supervision of the banking system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Banks are the main institutions that allocate credit in developing countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The skills necessary for bank officers to assess risks and make good lending decisions are critically important and often scarce.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Poor lending policies may cause too much capital to be channeled toward low-return projects and insufficient capital to be directed toward the high-return projects needed to propel income and growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, deterioration in banks' balance sheets caused by insider lending or excessive risk-taking that leads to a proliferation of bad loans can cause banks to cut back sharply on lending, with negative effects on the economy.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If the deterioration in banksâ balance sheets is severe enough, it can result in banking and currency crises that substantially disrupt the economy, phenomena that unfortunately have been all too common in developing countries over the past several decades.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 5 Preventing banking crises must start with prudential regulation , in which rules set by the government ensure that banks have sufficient capital and manage risks well.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: To guarantee that these regulations are enforced, the government must also engage in prudential supervision , in which it monitors banks by examining them on a regular basis to ensure that they are complying with government regulations.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The role of microfinance in developing countries is receiving much attention these days.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Microfinance is a positive development; it has clearly helped substantial numbers of poor people escape poverty, and the Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Muhammad Yunus for his pioneering efforts in this area was certainly well deserved.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 6 However, microfinance is not a substitute for the institution building I am talking about here.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalizing to Advance Institutional Reform Now that we understand what kinds of institutions are needed to promote financial development and economic growth, letâs turn to the question of how developing countries can improve the likelihood that these institutions are developed.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: One of the most powerful weapons for stimulating institutional development is globalization.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Wealth is not something that can be attained by remaining closed off to the rest of the world.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Poorer countries would do better by embracing globalization--that is, opening their financial markets and their markets for goods and services to other nations so that funds, goods, and, often, the ideas that accompany them can flow in.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such inflows can help them achieve reforms that build productivity and wealth that will benefit all their citizens.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, countries need to take care that the foundations of the fundamental institutions discussed above are in place, and they must monitor the pace of reform.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Opening financial markets Now letâs look at how opening financial markets to foreigners promotes financial development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalizing the domestic financial system by opening financial markets to foreigners encourages financial development and growth in wealth in two ways.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, opening financial markets to foreign capital directly increases access to capital and lowers its cost for those with productive investments to make.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 7 We know that labor is cheap in poor countries, and so we might think that capital would be especially productive there.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Just think of how hugely profitable a factory might be in a country where wages are one-tenth of those in the United States.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although some of that differential would likely reflect the higher productivity of American workers, capital should, nevertheless, have extremely high returns in such countries, and, in principle, we should expect substantial flows of capital from rich countries (where the returns on capital should be relatively low) to poor countries (where they should be far higher).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such capital flows could lead to substantial benefits for poor countries in the form of larger capital stocks, higher productivity, and more rapidly growing incomes.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In fact, as we well know, at present capital flows are moving, on net, from poor countries to rich ones, that is, in a direction opposite to the one we would expect.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Many reasons have been proposed for this apparent paradox, but one of them certainly is the weakness of financial systems in poor countries, as described earlier.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: This point leads us to a second benefit of financial globalization:  Opening markets to foreign financial institutions promotes reforms to the financial system that improve its functioning.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Allowing foreign financial institutions to operate in an emerging-market country brings in expertise and best practices, such as those designed to screen good from bad credit risks and to monitor borrower activities to reduce the amount of risk they take.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 8 Because of their familiarity with more-advanced financial systems, foreign financial firms also are likely to increase the pressure on the domestic government to institute reforms that will make the financial system work more effectively.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: As domestic financial institutions start to lose business to better-run and more trustworthy foreign institutions, they will realize the need for a better legal and accounting infrastructure that will make it easier for them to make loans to new customers.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Domestic financial institutions will then be far more likely to advocate for and support the reforms that achieve this result.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, this is not to say that in a genuinely corrupt and anticompetitive environment financial globalization, by itself, can still engender an efficient, dynamic, and modern financial system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Recent research has shown that when some countries opened up to international capital markets too soon in the absence of some basic supporting conditions, vulnerabilities to sudden stops of capital flows increased.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, some preconditions must exist with respect to a minimum level of institutional quality, financial market development, and macroeconomic stability before financial globalization can further improve financial market and institutional development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 9 That said, given these preconditions and some constituency for progress and reform, financial globalization can be a powerful force in support of such efforts.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Opening trade in goods Next, letâs consider how opening domestic markets to foreign goods can promote the development of better institutions.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although not immediately obvious, opening domestic markets to foreign goods, known as "trade liberalization," can be a key driver of financial development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: It can weaken the political power of entrenched business interests that might otherwise block institutional reforms, a point that is emphatically made by Rajan and Zingales (2004) in their book Saving Capitalism from the Capitalists .
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Trade liberalization, which promotes a more competitive environment, will lower the revenue of entrenched firms so that they will need greater access to external sources of capital.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, they will be more likely to support reforms that promote a deeper and more efficient financial system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In fact, research indicates that a deeper financial sector is positively associated with greater trade openness (Rajan and Zingales, 2003; Svaleryd and Vlachos, 2002).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Free trade also promotes financial deepening by reducing corruption.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: High tariffs breed corruption because importers have incentives to pay customs officials to look the other way when the importers avoid tariffs by smuggling in goods.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Not surprisingly, countries that restrict international trade are found to be more corrupt (Ades and Di Tella, 1994).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even when developing countries are unwilling to tear down all barriers to imports of foreign goods, they can still generate incentives for institutional reform by removing obstacles that prevent domestic producers from engaging in international trade.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Facilitating production for overseas markets creates a greater need for a well-functioning financial system because, to compete effectively in the international arena, firms need better access to capital.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If they canât get capital, they wonât be able to make the investments they need to increase productivity and price their goods competitively.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Accordingly, international trade creates a demand for reforms that will make the financial system more efficient.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: We are seeing how the globalization of trade is driving financial reform in China.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: As Chinese enterprises increasingly enter international markets, they need a better financial system that can ensure that the allocation of their high domestic savings is done efficiently and is responsive to market developments.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although it has taken time, globalization is helping to generate the demand for an improved financial system, which is driving the reform process.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Communist leadership recognizes that the old development model must change.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The government has announced that state-owned banks are being put on the path to be privatized and has allowed foreign investment in Chinaâs banking system ($20 billion in 2005).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 10 The government is also engaged in legal reform to make contracts more enforceable.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In August 2006, the National Peopleâs Congress enacted a new bankruptcy law that gives creditors greater protection if a firm goes bankrupt, and last month it approved a law that gives individuals more legal protection for their property.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: China, of course, is an example of a country that has actively encouraged exports as a means of propelling its economic growth and development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: To some extent, China may have gone too far in its use of policy to promote export growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Increased reliance on market-determined prices will help ensure that the allocation of resources into the export sector does not exceed their efficient use.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The goal should be to raise productivity toward world-class standards in all sectors of the economy.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Recently Chinaâs authorities have agreed that some rebalancing of the sources of growth away from exports and toward domestic demand is in order.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Among Chinaâs East Asian neighbors, the importance of developing industries to meet demand for domestic uses also is receiving increasing attention.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The problem of export restrictions
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nevertheless, developing production for exports may still be useful for those countries at the lowest rungs of the developmental ladder, and it is surprising that many of the worldâs poorest developing countries still not only do not encourage an export orientation but in fact maintain a regime of taxes, restrictions, and other policies that effectively discourage it.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: This problem remains especially serious in some African economies and may help explain why their growth performance has been so disappointing.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The primary way that governments discourage exports is by imposing large taxes on them.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because high export taxes are one method of obtaining revenue, governments may be attracted to them to solve their budget problems.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: They may also use these taxes to punish their political opponents, who are often involved in a particular export industry.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The government can then distribute the resulting revenue to their supporters.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The most pernicious forms of export taxes are those that are hidden through the governmentâs setting a fixed official exchange rate that artificially keeps the domestic currency at a value well above what it would be worth in terms of foreign currency (say, U.S. dollars) in a free market.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The government then makes it illegal to sell dollars for the larger amount of domestic currency that could be obtained in the black market.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The difference between the official exchange rate and the free, black-market rate (often called the "black-market premium") imposes a tax on exporters because they are forced to sell the dollars they earn to the government or to the central bank at the official rate, and thus they receive a much lower price for their goods in terms of the domestic currency.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although in recent decades a great many countries have abandoned currency controls and dismantled their black markets, such controls still exist in some of the poorest economies, especially in Africa.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In some countries, the tax from the black-market premium is confiscatory.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: An example from history illustrates this point.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In 1982 Ghana had a black-market premium of more than 1,000 percent, and so exporters of cocoa (primarily from a tribe different from that of the ruling government party) were getting only 6 percent of the world price.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Given such a high tax rate, it came as no surprise that cocoa exports, which had accounted for 19 percent of Ghanaâs gross domestic product in the 1950s, accounted for only 3 percent by 1982 (Easterly, 2001, p. 222).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: During the twenty years when the black-market premium was so high, the average income of Ghanaians fell 30 percent.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Like many such unwarranted controls on economic life, high black-market premiums also breed corruption, with all its negative effects, because they create strong incentives to bribe officials or to smuggle goods to avoid paying the black-market-premium tax.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: (Indeed, one of the reasons that governments in poorer countries often use this method of taxation rather than an explicit tax is that it allows government officials to get rich from the bribes they receive.)
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Other Gains from Trade Liberalization Although we have been focusing on how globalization promotes financial development, we shouldnât forget that trade globalization, which involves both trade liberalization and an export orientation, is a key driver of economic growth for reasons additional to those already mentioned.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The first economics course that college students encounter always teaches the concept of comparative advantage:  By trading with another country, you can focus your production on what you are really good at so that your productivity will be high.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: This higher productivity then leads to higher economic welfare.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Trade liberalization, more importantly, promotes competition in domestic markets, which in turn forces domestic firms to increase productivity and make better products, both of which drive economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: If a foreigner produces a better product that can be imported, domestic firms must make a better product at a lower price to keep selling their product at home.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: One graphic example of how trade promotes competition occurred in India, which up until 1991 had protected its tool industry with a 100 percent tariff (tax on imports).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: After the Indian government cut the tariff sharply, Taiwanese firms initially grabbed one-third of the Indian market.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the next decade, however, Indian firms boosted their productivity almost to the levels of Taiwanese firms, thereby winning back the domestic market.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Eventually Indian tool firms became so efficient that they were able to start selling their goods abroad and became substantial exporters.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Decreasing barriers to imports also helps promote exports.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Increased competition from imports lowers the profits firms can earn by focusing solely on the domestic market, and so they naturally concentrate more of their energy on exporting.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, trade liberalization helps developing countries gain access to foreign markets in advanced countries, as illustrated by the fact that the United States, through free-trade agreements, has been more willing to lower tariffs for countries such as Mexico and Chile if they do the same for the United States.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Empirical evidence indicates that trade liberalization has positive effects on productivity and economic growth for both importing and exporting countries:  It has even been found to be associated with more-rapid increases in life expectancy and a reduction in infant mortality.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 14 Yet, as is often the case in economics, empirical evidence is never completely clear cut:  Some economists question whether the evidence strongly supports a positive link between trade liberalization and growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 15 Nonetheless, the logic of the benefits of trade liberalization and the preponderance of the evidence supporting its positive effects lead most members of the economics profession, including me, to the following conclusion:  Trade liberalization is highly beneficial not only for the overall economy but also for its constituent sectors.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The resulting economic growth is a rising tide that raises all boats and is an important tool for poverty alleviation.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: But even if trade liberalization is not adopted, giving domestic producers the opportunity to sell goods to rich countriesâ markets can be an important engine for growth in the worldâs poorest countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: One crucial way that governments in developing countries can encourage exports is by providing the transportation infrastructure--ports, roads, and airports--that make it easier for businesses to send their goods abroad.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because foreigners donât have a natural predilection to buy your goods, you have to be supercompetitive--your goods have to be better and cheaper than the goods made in foreign countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Domestic firms have to focus even more on being highly productive, and boosting productivity will lead to rapid economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Japanâs experience shows what focusing on exporting can accomplish.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the immediate aftermath of World War II, Japan was a poor country.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Its economic infrastructure had been destroyed by the war.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: To convince Americans and others to buy Japanese products, Japanese firms had to produce goods that were cheaper and better than their American-made counterparts.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result, the export industries in Japan became enormously productive and supercompetitive.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Productivity grew, and three decades after World War II, Japan became one of the richest countries in the world.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: South Korea, one of the great Asian success stories even with its crisis in the late 1990s, had very high barriers to trade until the 1990s, and its early development strategy did not include opening its domestic market to foreign goods.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, through its export sector, South Korea has participated fully in global markets, and this participation has been a key to its success.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: South Koreaâs development strategy focused on promoting its export sector, and it is the export sector that led to high productivity and economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, all examples of successful growth stories in developing economies (China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Taiwan, Chile) have involved export sectors that met the test of international competition, and some of these economies have also pursued trade liberalization.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: In almost all the industrializing East Asian economies, future growth will likely have to follow a more balanced path that relies less on exports and more on production for the domestic market.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such adjustments are needed not only to secure such economiesâ further development but also to alleviate the pattern of external imbalances around the global economy.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: It is in the worldâs poorest countries--especially in Africa and Latin America--that additional participation in global markets has the highest priority.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Only by embracing global markets can developing countries raise living standards.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: 16 Trade liberalization has a critical role to play in economic growth by directly stimulating domestic firms to become more productive.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: And along with financial globalization, it can also encourage emerging-market economies to develop the institutions that foster financial development.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization should be one of the highest priorities for developing countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Role of Advanced Countries Can we in the advanced countries help?
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Yes, we can do so by supporting the opening of our markets to goods and services from emerging-market countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: By encouraging these countries to increase their participation in global markets, we create exactly the right incentives for them to implement the hard measures that will enable them to grow rich.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: As we have seen, exporters have strong incentives to be productive so that they can take advantage of access to our markets, and thus they will make the investments needed for growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: They also will push for the institutional reforms to make financial markets more efficient and promote financial deepening.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: By getting financial markets to work well, exporters will have access to the capital they need to increase their business.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Opening our markets to emerging-market countries is an important way that those in advanced countries can help emerging-market economies become successful.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: While providing aid to poor countries can, in the right circumstances, help eradicate poverty, it often will not work because it usually does not create the right incentives to promote economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: A handout is almost never as effective as a hand up.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some are concerned about the consequences for us if we in the United States allow free competition in our markets for goods and services from countries where wages are low.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Keeping many countries poor and their workers unproductive may seem to be to our benefit.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: But as shown in the examples of post-World War II recovery in Europe and Japan, and in the rapid growth in the 1970s and 1980s in the newly industrialized economies of Asia, higher standards of living throughout the global economy actually work to our benefit.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Prosperity in our trading partners creates growing markets for U.S. exports of high-value goods.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: And over time, as workersâ productivity abroad rises, so will their wages and incomes.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: It is true that the changes brought about in our economy by globalization impose significant costs on some domestic workers.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: We need to develop policies to help those workers without undermining the global trading system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The costs to us of damaging that system would far outweigh the benefits that some might gain from protectionist measures.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin

text: Studies focusing more specifically on the necessary preconditions for, and the appropriate sequencing of, financial reforms, macroeconomic policies, and institutional development, on the one hand, and capital account liberalization, on the other, include Eichengreen (2001), Alfaro and others (2004), and Klein (2005).

text: The four largest state-owned banks, with 70 percent of Chinaâs bank deposits, are scheduled to be privatized in the following order:  the Construction Bank, the Bank of China, the Industrial and Commercial Bank, and the Agricultural Bank.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, almost all economists think that trade liberalization, a key element of globalization, is a good thing.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, in Kearl and others (1979), 97 percent of economists agreed (generally or with some provisions) with the statement that "tariffs and import quotas reduce general economic welfare."
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: A typical view advocating trade liberalization is expressed by Jagdish Bhagwati, one of the most prominent trade theorists in the world, in Bhagwati (2004).

speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The literature on the effects of trade liberalization on growth and poverty is immense.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: See the surveys in Temple (1999); Bourguignon and others (2002); Winters, McCulloch, and McKay (2004); and Wolf (2004).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Earlier studies found that trade openness was associated with higher growth rates (Dollar, 1992; Sachs and Warner, 1995; and Edwards, 1998).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, because the direction of causation from this evidence is difficult to establish, other researchers have used instrumental variable procedures to establish causality from trade liberalization to growth (for example, Frankel and Romer, 1999).

speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Using a different approach to identify the direction of causation, Lee, Ricci, and Rigobon (2004) also find that trade openness has a positive effect on growth.

speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, Harrison (1996) and especially Rodriguez and Rodrik (2000).
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The finding in Jones and Olken (2005) that growth take-offs are primarily associated with large and steady expansions in international trade provides further support for this view.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Can we in the advanced countries help?
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Yes, we can do so by supporting the opening of our markets to goods and services from emerging-market countries.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: By encouraging these countries to increase their participation in global markets, we create exactly the right incentives for them to implement the hard measures that will enable them to grow rich.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: As we have seen, exporters have strong incentives to be productive so that they can take advantage of access to our markets, and thus they will make the investments needed for growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: They also will push for the institutional reforms to make financial markets more efficient and promote financial deepening.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: By getting financial markets to work well, exporters will have access to the capital they need to increase their business.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Opening our markets to emerging-market countries is an important way that those in advanced countries can help emerging-market economies become successful.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: While providing aid to poor countries can, in the right circumstances, help eradicate poverty, it often will not work because it usually does not create the right incentives to promote economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: A handout is almost never as effective as a hand up.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some are concerned about the consequences for us if we in the United States allow free competition in our markets for goods and services from countries where wages are low.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Keeping many countries poor and their workers unproductive may seem to be to our benefit.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: But as shown in the examples of post-World War II recovery in Europe and Japan, and in the rapid growth in the 1970s and 1980s in the newly industrialized economies of Asia, higher standards of living throughout the global economy actually work to our benefit.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Prosperity in our trading partners creates growing markets for U.S. exports of high-value goods.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: And over time, as workersâ productivity abroad rises, so will their wages and incomes.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: It is true that the changes brought about in our economy by globalization impose significant costs on some domestic workers.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: We need to develop policies to help those workers without undermining the global trading system.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: The costs to us of damaging that system would far outweigh the benefits that some might gain from protectionist measures.
speech_title: Globalization and Financial Development
speech_venue: At the Econometric Society at Duke University Lecture, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Mishkin
text: Promoting trade liberalization helps us not only do good but also do well.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I would like to thank Christina Romer and David Romer for giving me the chance to address participants in the Summer Institute, sponsored by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER).
