text: Fortunately, this recent period of turbulence in financial markets has occurred at a time when U.S. commercial banks are strongly capitalized, reflecting years of robust profits.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: As the nation's central bank, the Federal Reserve seeks to promote general financial stability and to help to ensure that financial markets operate in an orderly manner.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accordingly, the Federal Reserve has taken some steps in recent weeks to provide liquidity and to promote the orderly functioning of markets.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: We continue to follow these developments in financial markets closely, particularly those that may have a broad impact on real economic activity.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Today I plan to offer some thoughts about ways to analyze and assess the impact of banking crises on real economic activity.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Others at this conference will be addressing some of the specifics of the Asian financial crisis in 1997-98 and the status of economies and financial systems of Asian countries today, so I believe I can best contribute by setting up a conceptual and empirical framework that can be applied to various types of financial crises, including Asia in 1997-98.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Much of what I plan to discuss is based on a paper I published earlier this year with colleagues at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, Luc Laeven and Daniela Klingbiel, titled "Banking Crises, Financial Dependence, and Growth".
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 In particular, this research focuses on a key question for policy, namely, through what channels can financial turmoil have an impact on real economic activity?
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: We study the effect of different types of crises on the performance of various sectors and firms in economies with differing levels of development of their banking and financial systems.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Surprisingly, little systematic empirical work had been done detailing the mechanisms by which financial crises can generate problems in the real economy.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 3 I will provide a brief overview of these results and then draw some lessons that policymakers might keep in mind when considering ways to help prevent and mitigate future crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a final introductory thought, I want to note that my remarks today on banking crises relate to research conducted on a range of countries, many of them emerging-market countries, and are not a commentary on current financial conditions or on the health of the U.S. banking system, which, as I noted above, is quite good.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Framework for Assessing and Analyzing Banking Crises Financial crises can assume various forms.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am going to focus primarily on financial crises involving the banking sector and do so for several reasons.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, banks play a prominent role in the credit intermediation process in most countries, providing funding to firms beyond the cash flow provided by their normal operations.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Banks also typically serve as custodian of a significant portion of household saving.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In many Asian countries, for example, banks play a key role in channeling credit to firms--particularly those firms not able to acquire funding from capital markets or other sources--and also hold substantial consumer deposits.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, much of the literature on financial crises indicates that crises involving the banking sector can lead to disruptions in the real economy.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: The definition of banking crisis I will use today, consistent with the definition in our recent paper, is an episode during which the capital of the banking sector has been depleted due to loan losses, resulting in a negative net worth of the banking sector.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 4 Therefore, the use of the term "banking crisis" in our research refers to major disruptions in a country's banking system, not just minor downturns or disturbances.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: By focusing on banking crises in our research paper, we were able to isolate the impact of banks on the provision of credit and liquidity to firms during times of distress.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe that combining this type of empirical research on banking crises with practical experience from bank supervisors and market participants, such as those attending this conference, helps us all to understand and address the problems associated with banking crises--and perhaps even to help to prevent them.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Much work has been done on how financial intermediaries and financial markets facilitate investment by firms and, hence, promote economic growth.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 5 Financial intermediaries and financial markets are generally thought to reduce information asymmetry problems that can make raising external funds difficult and expensive for firms.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Well-functioning and well-developed financial intermediaries and markets thus should particularly benefit firms that rely most heavily on external funding to finance their growth.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 6 Conversely--and this is the novel aspect of our research--crises in the financial sector thus should have a disproportionately negative impact on firms that rely heavily on external sources of finance.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In particular, we investigate whether the impact of a banking crisis on sectors dependent on external sources of financing varies with the level of development of the financial system.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: If the banking system is the key element allowing firms that depend heavily upon external funding sources to finance their growth, then an impairment of these intermediaries--in a system where such intermediaries are important--should have a disproportionate contractionary impact on precisely those sectors that flourished in "normal" times, due to their reliance on banks.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, an important element of our analysis is the level of development of a country's financial system, that is, whether it is "deep" (more developed) or "shallow" (less developed).
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: To address these issues, we gathered data from thirty-eight developed and developing countries that have experienced a banking crisis during the last quarter century.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 8 We documented clear linkages between the state of the banking system and the performance of the real economy.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: More specifically, we find that in well-developed and deep financial systems, sectors highly dependent on external sources of funding tend to experience a greater contraction during a banking crisis than do externally dependent sectors in countries with shallower financial systems.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, sectors of the real economy that rely heavily on external finance (that is, do not fund capital expenditures through cash flow) tend to experience a substantially slower growth of value added during a banking crisis than those sectors that do not rely so heavily on external funding.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: This effect is more pronounced in countries with more developed financial systems.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our results hold for a wide group of countries and over a long time span, but as I note below, have particular relevance to emerging market countries.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: While these results are consistent with a so-called credit channel impact of banking crises on real economic activity, there are further implications of the "credit channel" view that we explore in more detail.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Among firms that depend heavily on outside financing, young firms with short histories and firms with a large fraction of hard-to-measure intangible assets, for example, may have particular difficulties raising funds from the market due to information problems.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Instead, such firms would tend to depend heavily on banks and other intermediaries for funding.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consistent with this, we find a greater negative impact of banking crises on growth for industries dominated by young firms that are highly dependent on external finance and for industries with high levels of intangible assets.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: While all of these results are consistent with a "credit channel" view of the impact of banking crises on real economic activity, we certainly need to explore some alternative explanations before drawing final conclusions.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In particular, many factors may be correlated with the level of financial development of a country, so we want to make sure that the level of financial development is not simply standing in for something else.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: The differences in financial development, for example, can arise from historical, political, cultural, and legal reasons.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: There is a well-developed literature emphasizing, for instance, that the nature of a country's legal system and the manner in which laws are enforced can have an effect on the development of its financial system.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 9 Similarly, other country-specific factors also might have an influence on how financial institutions and markets behave.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: If one of these factors, rather than financial development, is driving the results, we might have to interpret those results differently.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a way to try to address such questions of interpretation, we controlled for the quality of the political and legal institutions in the countries included in our data analysis.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: We found that our results still hold, namely that a banking crisis has a more pronounced effect on a country's economy when its financial system is more developed and when its firms rely more on external finance, even after taking into account a variety of proxies for the differences in the quality of institutions and legal structures across countries.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Furthermore, we explored differences in the effect of banking crises on countries based on their overall levels of development.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, we wanted to assess separately the impact of banking crises in less-developed countries versus more-developed countries since, of course, overall economic development and financial sector development tend to be correlated.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Interestingly, when we remove Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries from our sample, the effects of banking crises were more pronounced, indicating that banking crises in emerging market countries likely do more harm to the overall economy than in developed countries.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Interestingly, our research also provides evidence that crises affecting the banking sector can have a more serious impact on the real economy than alternative economic disruptions such as economic contractions or shocks such as currency crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 10 That is, banking crises have represented a unique shock to a country's financial system.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: These results suggest that the "credit channel" effects on real economic activity we document are operating through the banking system.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In short, the results highlight that a healthy banking system generally contributes to strong economic growth, and banking crises can present a substantial drag on the real economy.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: This underscores why we consider it important to analyze the economic impact of financial crises involving the banking sector, and to mitigate potential drivers of such crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, in the case of Asia a decade ago, the trouble experienced by the region's banks, given their dominant role in Asian financial systems, created disruptions that spread across Asia.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Problems in the real economies of Asian countries would likely not have been so great had the banking systems been stronger.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: So far I have been discussing results that focus on the real growth impact on sectors or industries.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: We were able to obtain data on the impact on individual firms but for a smaller sample than for the sectors or industries.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: We use a variety of measures for individual firm performance, such as real growth in sales, real growth in earnings before interest and taxes, and real stock market returns.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: The results are the same as in the sectoral level data I described above:  The performance of firms heavily dependent upon external sources of funding is disproportionately negatively affected in deep financial systems during periods of banking crisis.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition to providing microeconomic support for the credit channel view, individual firm data also allow us to examine important hypotheses about the impact that transparency and public disclosure by individual firms can have to mitigate the effects of banking crises on those firms.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: One author, using data from the Asian crisis, has investigated the relationship between stock market performance and quality of public disclosure.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: 11 Our recent paper also delved into this issue by using certain proxies for individual firm disclosure practices, such as having a listing in the United States (hence disclosing by U.S. standards) or by being audited by one of the major international accounting firms.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our results suggested that greater public disclosure had a favorable impact on stock market performance, both during the crisis period as well as afterward.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, there is a large literature supporting the idea that a country can benefit by promoting transparency and disclosure.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: But I know that there is still ongoing debate about the effects of globalization on financial markets and economies and I believe that further research and discussion about the benefits of openness and transparency are worthwhile.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Perhaps a discussion on this topic will ensue at this conference over the next two days.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: I will pose one final topic before moving on to some policy suggestions.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe it is important to try to understand the long-term impact of a crisis on the financial system and the real economy.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In particular, it is useful to examine whether a particularly deep crisis or a recent one may have effects on participants in that country during the next crisis.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Interestingly, our recent work provided some evidence that past crises do not necessarily create a stoppage of bank credit to firms once "normal" times returned, but when the next crisis occurred, its impact on growth was usually deeper in magnitude.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thoughts on Preventing and Managing Banking Crises Having raised some issues for consideration about banking crises--and having tried to provide some answers, where possible--I would now like to offer some thoughts that policymakers may consider as they try to prevent and manage banking crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: I note that market participants should also consider these ideas, since it is not just policymakers who can learn lessons from past crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, one of the major lessons to be learned from past banking crises is the importance of a healthy banking system.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Maintaining a safe and sound banking system, given the key role that banks play in most financial systems, contributes to the health of a country's overall economy.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Most countries do this by some form of banking supervision, generally accepting that the added protection to the banking system in the form of supervision is worth the costs of the regulatory burden.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Effective banking supervision has helped foster a banking system in the United States that today is safe, sound, and well-capitalized.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: One of the ways that bank supervisors can help promote a healthy banking system is to focus banks on the development of improved risk-management techniques.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, identifying, assessing, and promoting sound risk-management practices have become central elements of good supervisory practice.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Bankers should ensure that their risk-management practices include a focus on less likely outcomes, not just the most common ones, and that the bank is being adequately compensated for the risk it is bearing.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: The use of exercises such as stress tests and scenario analyses can help bankers identify certain points of vulnerability that may arise during potential downturns.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In some countries, bank supervisors have an explicit responsibility to ensure that banks adhere to existing laws and maintain and implement appropriate consumer protection policies.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, in the United States the federal banking agencies play an important role in fostering not just a safe and sound banking system, but also one that is diverse and fair in meeting the needs of consumers.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Good banking supervision is vital to the health of banks, particularly when the banking system has some type of government support--for example, either explicit or implicit deposit insurance.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: But ensuring a safe and sound banking system that is also competitive and profitable has its challenges.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Clearly, banking supervision on its own can create some distortions or burden, so it is also very important to let market forces work as much as possible, with reliance on market participants--in their role as depositors, counterparties, creditors, and shareholders--to exercise discipline on banks.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Policymakers have to find the right balance between the more visible hand of government supervision and the invisible hand of market forces.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, pursuing sound macroeconomic policies is another way for policymakers to help prevent banking and financial crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: For instance, it is beneficial to have sound and sustainable monetary and fiscal policy to provide a stable operating environment for entrepreneurs and financial institutions and markets.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Many past crises were precipitated either by an external shock affecting an already vulnerable financial system or by market participants targeting vulnerabilities in certain markets or in certain institutions or governments.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: History has taught us that if a condition or policy looks unsustainable, it most likely is and market forces will eventually bring it to an end.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: To paraphrase Herb Stein, if a policy cannot go on forever, it won't!
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, I referred earlier to research on the benefits of disclosure and transparency.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our analysis contributes to the evidence that having an open and transparent financial system and economy, accompanied by reliable and accurate accounting standards, generally benefits a country and its market participants.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: A core principle of economics is that markets are more competitive, and therefore more efficient, when accurate information is available to both consumers and suppliers.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Information is thus critical to the effective functioning of financial markets:  timely and accurate financial information about markets, market participants, and governments is important for all actors to be able to make informed decisions.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: This is of course true during normal times, but perhaps more so during a crisis when market participants and governments are sometimes trying to determine where problems lie and how severe they might be.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Lack of information can present additional problems during a crisis, and incorrect or incomplete information provided by firms, governments, and other institutions can severely undermine their credibility, worsening the problem.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusion These conferences on the Asian crisis serve as excellent forums to analyze the events of ten years ago and share views on ways to prevent and mitigate future crises.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: They also allow market participants to offer feedback on past policy steps, including which past policies helped and which ones hindered.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Policymakers and market participants must remember that preventing and mitigating financial crises requires a blend of sharp analysis, keen judgment, practical experience, and rigorous understanding of how markets work--in both normal times and times of stress.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: I have tried to provide a framework for analyzing the impact of banking crises on real economic activity, described some results analyzing crises from around the world during the last quarter century, and offered three policy lessons:  the importance of a healthy banking system, of sound macroeconomic policy, and of high levels of transparency and disclosure.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: This is by no means an exhaustive list but I hope it can provide a useful starting point for the discussions that will take place during the rest of the day.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a final thought, I counsel policymakers and market participants alike to remember that no two crises are the same.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recall that the Asian crisis of 1997-98 actually manifested itself differently across Asian countries, with each country having its own set of problems and needing to find its own solutions.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, there is never a single remedy to each crisis and each brings its own surprises and risks.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: Clearly, we can all learn a lot from past crises--which is the value in holding conferences like this one.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: But we should not assume that past remedies will fully solve the next set of problems or address all future risks.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Kroszner
text: The key is to take lessons from the past and tailor them appropriately to future situations of potential distress.
speech_title: Analyzing and Assessing Banking Crises
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Conference on the Asian Financial Crisis Revisited, San Francisco, California(via videoconference)

speaker: Mishkin

speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In light of these events, we will need to make the best possible real-time judgments about the extent to which the recent developments in financial markets are likely to affect economic activity in the period ahead.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That said, the economy ended the second quarter on a positive note.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Commerce Departmentâs Bureau of Economic Analysis recently reported that the economy expanded at an annual rate of 4 percent in the second quarter, about 1/2 percentage point higher than the first estimate.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, the jump in growth followed a sluggish first-quarter gain:  That choppiness in growth reflected large swings in several factors that are often volatile, including inventory investment, federal defense outlays, and net exports.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Smoothing through this volatility, the underlying pattern of activity in the first half of the year essentially represented a continuation of the moderate growth that had prevailed since the spring of last year when growth in real gross domestic product stepped down from an above-trend pace.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Many of the spending indicators for the current quarter have remained consistent with that earlier trend.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, for the most part, these data cover a period that predates the recent onset of financial turbulence.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The step-down in the growth of real output that began in mid-2006 and proceeded through the middle of this year primarily reflected weakness in the housing market.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Declines in real residential investment subtracted nearly 1-1/4 percentage points from the growth of real GDP in the second half of last year and about 3/4 percentage point in the first half of this year.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, the demand for housing appears to be weakening further amid credit conditions for home mortgage lending that are generally tighter, but especially so in the subprime segment.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Sales of existing single-family homes in July were more than 20 percent below their peak in mid-2005, while sales of new homes in July were more than 37 percent below their peak.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although housing starts have also moved down over the past year, the decline thus far has lagged the downturn in sales, and the backlog of unsold new homes has climbed to a very high level relative to sales.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Given this sizable backlog and the likelihood that sales will remain weak or weaken further in coming months, cutbacks in housing construction are likely to continue to be a drag on economic activity in future quarters.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Turning to consumer spending, real outlays decelerated considerably in the second quarter.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To some extent, a moderation from the very rapid pace of growth around the turn of the year probably was to be expected.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the second quarter, in particular, a jump in energy prices eroded the purchasing power of gains in household income, placing downward pressure on the growth of real spending at that point.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even so, early indications are that household spending is holding up reasonably well thus far in the current quarter:  Real outlays for goods excluding motor vehicles posted a solid increase in July, and sales of light motor vehicles--which had slumped in June and July--rebounded last month.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Having said that, several factors suggest that consumer spending will be subdued in the period ahead.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: This summerâs retrenchment in equity markets and the sharp deceleration in house prices have damped gains in household wealth this year and are likely to restrain consumer outlays.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, at least some households are likely to find it more difficult or expensive to borrow, and consumer sentiment--which turned down in August--could soften further if households become more anxious about recent financial market developments.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Business investment in equipment and software weakened toward the end of last year and remained sluggish in the first quarter.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In part, the slowing reflected a downturn in outlays for capital goods that are used heavily by the motor vehicle and construction industries, two sectors in which activity had softened considerably.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: But spending on other types of equipment also was soft in the first quarter.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the second quarter, however, demand for these other types of equipment bounced back strongly, and the gains were extended in July--as reported in the most recent data on orders and shipments of capital goods.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: We have no direct readings on capital spending in August, but the limited indicators currently in hand--such as the Institute for Supply Managementâs survey of purchasing managers--have held up reasonably well and remain at levels consistent with modest growth in manufacturing production and business investment.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, all this could change noticeably if many firms were to face significantly tighter credit conditions or if business sentiment were to soften appreciably.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Regarding international developments, the recent deterioration in financial market conditions has had effects around the world, but the economies of our major trading partners appear set to continue their expansion.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That growth should continue to stimulate demand for U.S. exports of goods and services.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Turning to the labor market, payroll employment has weakened.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As reported on Friday, nonfarm payrolls fell 4,000 last month, and private payrolls rose only 24,000.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Smoothing through the recent monthly numbers, private payrolls increased an average of about 70,000 per month over the past three months; this is down from gains near 120,000 per month in the first five months of the year and about 165,000 per month in the second half of 2006.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As for the economyâs longer-run growth rate, a key determinant is the trend in labor productivity.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As you know, from 1995 to 2000, productivity in the nonfarm business sector increased at an average annual rate of 2-1/2 percent, well above the lackluster pace of the preceding twenty-five years.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Then, remarkably, productivity accelerated further, rising at an average of about 3-1/2 percent per year for the first three years of this decade, despite the challenges of a recession, the fall of the dot-com market, a broad stock market correction, and the terrorist attacks.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Since the middle of 2004, however, the growth of labor productivity has slowed, registering an average annual rate of about 1-1/4 percent.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Previously, that figure had looked higher, but this summerâs annual revision of the national income and product accounts marked down productivity growth over the 2004 to 2006 period by an average of 0.3 percentage point per year.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Part of the recent deceleration in productivity almost surely reflects a typical cyclical response to a slowing economy.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The difficult questions, of course, are whether some of the recent slowing also reflects a downshift in the underlying trend, and, if so, to what extent?
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The latest evidence suggests that structural productivity might be increasing somewhat more slowly than it did during the second half of the 1990s, but the confidence band around any such estimate of trend productivity growth surely is very wide.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 2 These issues remain an area of active debate, the outcome of which will be essential for gauging the economyâs potential rate of growth going forward.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Let me turn now to inflation and inflation dynamics.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the past year, the price index for total personal consumption expenditures (PCE) rose 2.1 percent, down from nearly 3-1/2 percent during the comparable period twelve months earlier.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Recently, topline inflation has been boosted by sizable increases in food prices; energy-price increases slowed considerably over the past twelve months after sizable advances in earlier years.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Excluding food and energy, core PCE prices decelerated over the past year; the July reading on the twelve-month change stood at 1.9 percent, almost 1/2 percentage point less than it was a year earlier.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In my view, inflation expectations have been a key element in the recent performance of core inflation.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: By a range of measures, inflation expectations appear to have remained contained even as headline inflation moved temporarily higher.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: According to the Reuters/University of Michigan Survey of Consumers, the median expectation of inflation five to ten years ahead has been essentially flat since the beginning of last year.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, measures of long-run inflation compensation derived from spreads between yields on nominal and inflation-indexed Treasury securities have not pushed above the range that has prevailed in the past couple of years.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I discussed in a speech earlier this year, I read the evidence as suggesting that householdsâ long-run inflation expectations are consistent with PCE price inflation in the neighborhood of 2 percent.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 3 To be sure, this figure is sensitive to the assumptions used to tease such estimates from the available data, so I do not want to overstate its precision.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Still, the professional forecasters surveyed by the Philadelphia Fed also project PCE inflation to be close to 2 percent over the next five to ten years.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I look at the incoming inflation data, I would judge them to be consistent with expectations in this range; moreover, I believe that having expectations reasonably well anchored in this range has been a helpful influence on the path of actual inflation.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, let me be clear: I do not subscribe to a deus ex machina view of the inflation process, in which inflation is driven solely by inflation expectations and is little influenced by the balance of aggregate demand and aggregate supply.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, I take the view that expectations of future resource utilization are also an important factor affecting inflation outcomes.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: If households and businesses believe that the Federal Reserve will set monetary policy in a way that keeps aggregate demand in reasonable alignment with aggregate supply over time, then expectations of future resource utilization will be stable, and current resource utilization will provide less information about future inflation movements.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In that situation, which I believe describes the current environment, inflation expectations will be a key driver of inflation dynamics.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The stable inflation expectations we have seen lately derive from confidence that monetary policy will keep inflation under control.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: If monetary policy allowed aggregate demand to get out of sync with supply and if the Fed was not expected to bring demand back into balance with supply, then inflation expectations would be much less likely to remain stable.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: This is why I believe that the Federal Reserve must remain vigilant on inflation but give appropriate attention to keeping demand from falling below supply as well.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: What does this all mean for the inflation outlook?
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: At present, labor and product markets appear to be in reasonable balance.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: And I would expect the pressures on inflation that we have experienced from food and energy prices to abate.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Accordingly, with inflation expectations remaining stable around their current level, I see inflation as remaining in alignment with long-run expectations at around a 2 percent pace for the PCE deflator.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, I believe that the risks to the inflation outlook have become more balanced, given the greater downside risks to real growth.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Let me shift gears and discuss developments in financial markets.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As you know, the recent turmoil had its beginnings in the subprime mortgage market.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 4 The development of the subprime market in the 1990s was an important financial innovation that enabled borrowers with higher credit risk to obtain mortgages that previously were unavailable to them.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: This expansion appears likely to have been a significant factor in raising the rate of homeownership from 64 percent, the level in 1994, to about 68 percent currently.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, subprime and other nonprime lending played an important role in the high volume of home sales in the mid-2000s.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, data collected under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act indicate that about 25 percent of the loans used to purchase single-family, owner-occupied homes in 2005 were high-priced loans, including primarily subprime and some near-prime mortgages.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, as has been the case in previous instances of rapid financial innovations, adequate mechanisms to control excessive risk-taking may not have been in place during the subprime marketâs greatest growth.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: One innovation, further development of securitized products, gave mortgage lenders greater access to the capital markets and spread risks more broadly.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, securitization also widened the separation of the originators from the ultimate holders of the loans--that is, those who bought securities backed by loans.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In this setup, a classic principal-agent problem can arise if originators (the agents) do not have a sufficient incentive to shield the owners of the securities (the principals) from suffering higher-than-expected losses.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Against a backdrop of continued strong investor demand for high-yielding securities, some lenders began loosening underwriting standards for subprime mortgages in late 2005.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Loans to subprime borrowers were approved with high loan-to-value ratios and incomplete income documentation.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Had house prices kept appreciating, loan-to-value ratios would have fallen and some borrowers would have been able to refinance, perhaps into a prime loan with a lower interest rate.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: But, instead, as the housing market softened and interest rates rose, delinquencies in the adjustable-rate subprime market began to soar and reached nearly 15 percent in July.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 6 Among other types of nonprime mortgages, delinquencies on fixed-rate subprime mortgages have been fairly steady at less than 6 percent; rates on mortgages in alt-A pools have increased to nearly 3 percent, up notably from the 1 percent rate of only a year ago.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The rise in delinquencies in the subprime market has led to the collapse of some large subprime lenders and inflicted substantial losses on holders of subprime residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS) and of some collateralized debt obligations (CDOs).
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result, underwriting standards have been tightened, and fewer households are qualifying for subprime loans.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, some borrowers apart from the subprime segment are reportedly finding it more difficult to qualify for loans or are having to pay more for them.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: These developments have contributed materially to the drop in demand for housing this year.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Without a doubt, they also have caused significant hardship for many individuals and families.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Recently, we have watched the deterioration in financial conditions extend beyond the subprime market.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Investors appear to have reassessed their outlook and their tolerance for risk, especially for structured financial products and for securities of highly leveraged firms.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Bond spreads--especially those for speculative-grade debt--widened substantially in June and July, and the volatility of equity prices increased as well.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In mid-August, following several events that led investors to believe that credit risks might be larger and more pervasive than previously thought, the functioning of financial markets, including short-term and interbank funding markets, became increasingly impaired.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Notably, many asset-backed commercial paper programs found rolling over their paper increasingly difficult.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To help restore orderly conditions, the Federal Reserve in recent weeks has increased the provision of reserves, cut the discount rate, and changed its usual discount-window lending practices in order to facilitate term borrowing, together with other measures.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Stepping back from the rush of unfolding events, we are seeing a pattern that occurs from time to time.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Financial markets and institutions perform the essential function of channeling funds to those individuals or firms having the most productive investment opportunities.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, an increase in uncertainty and concerns about the quality of information can lead investors to pull back from financial markets and restrict productive lending--with potentially adverse implications for real activity.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That is essentially the story I laid out in a paper delivered at the Kansas City Fedâs Jackson Hole conference about ten years ago.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In my view, such an increase in uncertainty is an important part of what we have observed recently and stems from heightened concerns about the value of financial securities related to certain types of loans, about who is holding these securities, and about how a revaluation of these securities might affect the balance sheets of various financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Consequently, investors have become less willing to put funds into various financial markets, particularly into the more opaque segments of those markets.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As best we can tell thus far, the imprint of these developments on economic activity appears likely to be most pronounced in the housing sector.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, economic activity could be affected more severely in other sectors should heightened uncertainty lead to a broader pullback in household and business spending.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That scenario cannot, in my view, be ruled out, and I believe it poses an important downside risk to economic activity.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: I also believe that the process of adjustment that is under way in financial markets--of investors reassessing the outlook for risk and their tolerance for that risk--will ultimately create a more solid financial footing for the real economy.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: But in the meantime, the FOMC is monitoring the situation and is prepared to act as needed to mitigate the adverse effects on the economy arising from the disruptions in financial markets.
speech_title: Outlook and Risks for the U.S. Economy
speech_venue: To the Money Marketeers of New York University, New York, New York

text: Thank you for your interest and attention.
