speaker: Kohn
text: I appreciate this opportunity to speak on the occasion of the Deutsche Bundesbank's fiftieth anniversary by participating on this panel on "Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s."
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: I was reassured in my acceptance of Axel's invitation by David Laidler's survey paper, which found more successes than not over the past two decades.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: A concise summary of this success is evident in the performance of consumer price inflation in the advanced economies.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Median inflation in that group (as defined by the International Monetary Fund) has held near 2 percent for this decade.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, in the IMF's latest World Economic Outlook , four out of five countries in this group are expected to post inflation rates between 1 percent and 3 percent this year.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: That good performance has helped to anchor inflation expectations, which, in turn, generates many benefits.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Anchored inflation expectations damp the pass-through of supply-related price shocks.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: They also permit central banks to respond more forcefully to output fluctuations.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Most significantly, the improved inflation performance has come with, not at the expense of, output stability.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Although a consensus has not formed on how much of the "Great Moderation" in the growth of real output can be attributed to monetary policy, everyone agrees that at least a portion of it can.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: David views these macroeconomic outcomes as a triumph of monetarism, but not because the formulaic policy prescription associated with that doctrine succeeded (or, for that matter, was even tried on a sustained basis).
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Rather, the underlying tenets of monetarism ultimately seeped into the collective central banking unconscious and fostered better decisionmaking.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The beliefs that David identifies are threefold:  That market economies are inherently self-righting, that open economies perform best under flexible exchange rates, and that central bankers should focus on price stability as their long-run objective.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: David suggests that monetarism failed when its proponents got too prescriptive by advocating rigid rules for money growth.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Among the lessons he takes from the failed monetarist experiment are that central banking is an applied science and that our imperfect understanding of how economies and markets function implies that a good dose of humility is required--and I agree.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: As evidence of that humility on my part, let me also agree with David that two important questions about the conduct of monetary policy have not yet been resolved.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: This is unfortunate because these two questions are both longstanding sources of debate and central to current policy concerns.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: First, what is the best way to pursue price stability, and, second, how should asset prices be taken into account in steering policy?
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In many countries, though not my own, the answer to the first question has been that price stability should be pursued through the formal apparatus of an inflation target, which typically includes establishing an inflation goal by the government, setting metrics to evaluate central bank performance, and periodically communicating progress to the public.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Although correlation does not convey causation, the spread of such regimes has coincided with sustained low global inflation.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, no adopter of an inflation target has subsequently abandoned it.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Before anyone jumps to the conclusion that Frankfurt is a stop on my road to Damascus, let this Saul state that for me the case remains open.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Inflation has come down worldwide, in countries without, as well as with, inflation targets.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, I share David's puzzlement about why an explicit inflation goal should make a substantial difference in performance given the paucity of evidence showing that choosing a target directly affects the level of the public's inflation expectations.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, I am relatively more persuaded that inflation targeting helps reduce the variance of inflation expectations.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Evidence has accumulated to suggest that stock prices, interest rates, and measures of inflation expectations seem to vary less in economies in which the central bank has an explicit long-run goal for inflation.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: I suspect that this better anchoring of expectations and the success of inflation targeting in many countries is attributable in part to aspects of the political economy that David identified.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: A formal inflation target represents a national embrace of a goal, in which elected authorities recognize the primacy of price stability and publicly support--indeed, even require--the central bank's pursuit of that goal.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: To the extent that elected authorities channel the desires of the electorate, a central bank directed to adopt an inflation target is being given a strong signal as to the goal's importance to the public at large.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: This affirmation has often been reinforced by the granting of operational independence to the central bank to achieve that goal most effectively.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: An important effect of such public acceptance of price stability is that it erodes the standing of those who would direct central bank action toward other ends.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In such an environment, workers, businesspeople, and investors can make plans with the expectation that nominal magnitudes will be predictable and so devote their attention to more productive matters.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: For the European Central Bank, this framework was established by treaty.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In most other instances, the adoption of an inflation target involved laws and mutual understandings, not constitutional changes.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The early adopters of inflation targets were parliamentary democracies, which is not too surprising given that in such a system a single branch of government can enact laws and put them into effect.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: With regard to an inflation goal, the parliament can erect the formal apparatus and the finance minister can serve as the government's point of contact with the central bank.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The system in the United States is different in that two independent branches of government are responsible for economic policy making, making agreement on a single goal problematic.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, those two branches have already spoken as to the appropriate aim of the nation's central bank:  The Congress, in a law the President signed, has given the Federal Reserve a dual mandate that directs us to foster maximum employment and stable prices over time.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: This instruction is not an accident of history, in that, in the past, the Congress has shown no appetite to amend its legislation.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Nor is this instruction unreasonable, in that the dual mandate has come to be interpreted as assigning us the responsibility for attaining price stability in the long run, which will bring with it maximum employment, and of being mindful of resource utilization in the succession of short runs that make up the long run.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The dual mandate seems proper and fitting, given that economic costs are incurred both by having inflation stray from its long-run goal and by having output deviate from the economy's potential to produce; and it seems to produce results not too different in practice from those associated with central banks that are flexible inflation targeters.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: As I said earlier, anchoring expectations has value, in that it makes planning easier, reduces resources spent on predicting and protecting against unexpected variations in nominal magnitudes, and grants a central bank greater scope to lean against fluctuations in output while keeping inflation contained.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The latter is particularly attractive given our dual mandate, in that better-anchored inflation expectations could produce the win-win outcome of improving the attainment of both goals.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: For that reason, in its consideration of its communications strategies, the Federal Open Market Committee has been discussing whether mechanisms could be put in place that could better anchor inflation expectations in a manner consistent with the institutional framework of our dual mandate.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The second of David's open issues--whether central banks should lean against possible asset price bubbles--was the key topic in my discussion here eighteen months ago, at Otmar's festschrift.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: My answer then is my answer now.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: A central bank should focus on the outlook for the macroeconomy and generally relegate asset prices to the subordinate role of inputs to the forecast process.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: I view this as the simple application of humility that David and I find so admirable.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Although economic theory provides no settled answers to any topic, its predictions are especially imprecise with regard to asset pricing, which has two implications for central bankers.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: First, little confidence can be attached to the determination that an asset bubble exists except in the most extreme of circumstances.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, even less confidence can be attached to predictions of the effects of policy on asset prices, and in particular on any speculative element in those prices.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, monetary policy actions addressed at a perceived bubble in one sector may have undesirable effects on other asset prices and the economy more generally.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, my preferred policy framework remains three pronged:  First, assign the single instrument of monetary policy to its macroeconomic objective; second, rely on regulation to erect a resilient financial structure; and, third, in the event that market judgments prove to be wrong and financial prices adjust sharply, apply the tool of monetary policy to the macroeconomic task at hand.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: That task is not always easily captured by simple statistical regularities.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Relationships between financial markets and economic results are complex and nonlinear, especially when markets are not behaving normally.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: When investors are ebullient, their expectations of outsized capital gains can feed on themselves and back on the economy.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: On the way down, investors' loss of confidence, a reduction in credit availability, and a tightening of terms and conditions for credit have the potential to have pronounced effects on activity and inflation.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The world is, no doubt, different than when we gathered here eighteen months ago.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: However, it is far too soon to pass judgment on what went wrong in the U.S. housing market and why.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: I suspect that, when studies are done with cooler reflection, the causes of the swing in house prices will be seen as less a consequence of monetary policy and more a result of the emotions of excessive optimism followed by fear experienced every so often in the marketplace through the ages.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: To some extent, too, the amplitude of the housing cycle was heightened by the newness of the subprime market, the fragmentation of regulatory oversight responsibility for that market, and the complexity and opacity of the newer instruments for transforming and distributing risk.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Low policy interest rates early in this decade helped feed the initial rise in house prices.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the worst excesses in the market probably occurred when short-term rates were already well on their way to more normal levels, but longer-term rates were held down by a variety of forces.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: And similar, sometimes even sharper, trajectories of house prices have been witnessed in some economies in which the central banks said they were paying more attention to asset prices.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The action the Federal Open Market Committee took this Tuesday can be interpreted as the application of the third leg of my preferred policy triad, in that it was taken "to forestall some of the adverse effects on the broader economy that might otherwise arise from the disruptions in financial markets and promote moderate growth over time."
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In the past, such efforts to cushion the restraint induced by declines in asset prices have fueled the assertion that Federal Reserve policy is asymmetrical in its response to booms and busts in asset prices.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Such an asymmetry is said to have the potential to feed "moral hazard" in that investors would spend less effort evaluating underlying values as they were lulled by the protection they expected to be provided by monetary policy action.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In point of fact, Federal Reserve policy makers have not been asymmetrical in intent or in actions, in that we have always focused sharply on the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Asset prices have mattered in the determination of policy because they have mattered for our outlook.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: I am confident that the federal funds rate would not have been as high in 2000 if it had not been for the level of equity prices that year, nor would the federal funds rate have been as elevated in 2006 in the absence of the tight credit spreads, low term premiums, and the impetus from housing wealth.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: And I doubt policy would have been eased this week if housing prices had continued their upward march.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In each instance, however, policy was motivated not by the desire to achieve any particular level of asset prices, but rather by the Federal Reserve's assessment of how changes in asset prices were affecting the forecast of growth and inflation.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: I would also caution that a symmetrical response to the macroeconomic outlook will need to reflect the inherent asymmetries in business cycles.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In the typical boom-bust cycle, asset prices tend to rise relatively gradually over a protracted period but fall sharply in a shorter stretch of time, which financial economists refer to as "rising by the escalator and falling by the elevator."
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Perhaps because those asset prices are important to spending, key macroeconomic indicators, such as the unemployment rate, exhibit a similar pattern.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: It is not surprising then that a macro-focused monetary policy will leave an asymmetric footprint in the data.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In the end, my humble advice is to evaluate policymakers relative to the tasks the law has given them.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: In my judgment, the record over the past twenty-five years of steady growth with two mild recessions and gradually declining inflation to a reasonably low level does not betray an asymmetry in our policy responses in the metric that counts--macroeconomic performance.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: Vincent Reinhart, of the Board's staff, contributed to the preparation of these remarks.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Kohn
text: The views expressed are my own and not necessarily shared by my colleagues on the Board or the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Success and Failure of Monetary Policy since the 1950s
speech_venue: At Monetary Policy over Fifty Years, a conference to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Deutsche Bundesbank, Frankfurt, Germany

speaker: Warsh
text: It is good to be back in upstate New York.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Thank you to the School of Business of the University of Albany for inviting me.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I am particularly heartened to see old friends, new students, and prominent business leaders in attendance.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I played in the New York State Public High School Tennis Championships on the other side of this campus, so this is certainly familiar terrain.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: However, I hope to perform better in my remarks today than I did with my racquet twenty years ago.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I have been honored to serve in Washington, D.C. for the past 5-1/2 years.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: My knowledge of the economy has deepened by working with my colleagues to put fiscal and monetary policy into practice.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Nonetheless, with each passing day, it is more obvious that I learned much of what I need to know about the real economy in my first eighteen years here in upstate New York.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The current period of heightened financial market volatility has drawn more attention than usual to the policy actions of the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Returning home at this time serves as a useful reminder that the decisions we make in Washington matter on the front lines of the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Our monetary tools, for example, affect the ability of aspiring homeowners to take out a first mortgage.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: They also matter to retirees on fixed budgets, who are vulnerable to escalating prices, and to graduates of this and other universities looking for jobs.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Our supervision and regulatory policies, to cite another example, matter to businesses, large and small, looking to borrow from banks to expand their operations.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: On the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), my colleagues and I seek to deploy our monetary policy tools to help keep the U.S. economy on an even keel.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 1 We try to provide the right mix of policy prescriptions, patience, and perspective to counter possible adverse developments.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In evaluating the state of the U.S. economy, its prospects, and the current stance of policy, we typically turn to such arcana from the economics textbooks as the term structure of interest rates, the shape of the Phillips curve, trends on the natural rate of unemployment, changing risk premiums, the exchange value of the dollar, and marginal propensities to consume as asset values change, to name just a few.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: While these indicators and relationships are important, many of the enduring teachings needed to evaluate the financial markets and U.S. economy (particularly in times of financial tumult) are well known without the technical jargon all across the country:  Trees don't grow to the sky.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: There is no free lunch.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: You shouldn't put all your eggs in one basket.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: There is no substitute for doing your own homework.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And my favorite, that which can't go on forever usually doesn't.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: My intent today is not to suggest that the Federal Reserve is somehow omniscient regarding the path of the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Nor is it my intent to suggest that the Federal Reserve's knowledge and tools are sufficiently surgical to steer the U.S. economy completely unscathed through the choppy waters of financial market turbulence.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And of course, I do not literally mean to suggest that common aphorisms provide an infallible compass to guide the economy past shocks of one sort or another.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Instead, my goal is to describe the Federal Reserve's monetary responsibilities, highlight the critical role of liquidity in financial markets, and discuss the recent financial market turmoil.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: While the subprime-mortgage markets showed some of the earliest and most pronounced indications of weakness, I believe that problems afflicting the subprime-mortgage markets served more as the trigger than the fundamental cause of recent market turmoil and economic uncertainty.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Monetary Responsibilities and Financial Markets By way of background, allow me to highlight the Federal Reserve's dual mandate for monetary policy, as embodied in the Federal Reserve Act.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve's statutory objectives are to institute policies that foster maximum employment and price stability.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To ensure that these objectives are consistent with each other and with strong, enduring economic performance over time, my colleagues, past and present, interpret "maximum employment" to mean maximum sustainable employment.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In pursuing this objective, the Federal Reserve is trying to foster an environment in which those who are looking for work can reasonably find it.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Similarly, we generally interpret our congressional mandate to ensure "price stability" to mean that inflation (the rate of price change for a broad range of products and services) is at sufficiently low and predictable levels so that it is not a factor in the economic planning of households and businesses.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The principal instruments of monetary policy conducted by the Federal Reserve--open market operations, the discount rate, and reserve requirements--do not operate in a vacuum.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 3 Rather, they operate dynamically in association with ever-changing financial market conditions to produce effects on the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, well-functioning financial markets are a precondition for a sustainable, prosperous economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial markets facilitate the flow of capital from individuals and institutions that have savings to individuals and institutions with investment opportunities that are deemed worthwhile.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: When functioning properly, financial markets may also lower financing costs by allocating risks to suppliers of capital most willing and able to bear them.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investments that build human and physical capital, in turn, generate economic growth and ultimately raise living standards.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In addition, financial markets should serve as a shock absorber of sorts for both individuals and businesses.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The capital cushions of financial intermediaries, for example, should help mitigate the impact of financial shocks on the overall economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Conversely, when financial markets function poorly, the capital allocation process I just described is impaired, and worthwhile investment projects may go unfunded.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In the extreme, savers refuse to part with their funds for capital investments at virtually any price.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Instead, they retreat to the shore for safety, waiting for calmer seas and cooler heads to prevail.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As I have noted previously, "While policymakers and market participants know with certainty that these episodes will occur, [we] must be humble in [our] ability to predict the timing, scope, and duration of these periods of financial distress."
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To avoid these outcomes altogether, some believe that the Federal Reserve should treat financial stability itself as a goal.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Often that is seen to imply a preference by policymakers for the perpetuation of existing financial institutions and products.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: That is not a view I share.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The level of economic activity would invariably be lower if financial stability alone were our guiding light; protecting incumbents at the expense of innovators would prove detrimental to the long-term vibrancy of the economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We should be extremely wary of protecting financial institutions and their various stakeholders from incurring losses.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Such actions distort asset prices and critically impair the efficiency of capital allocation.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The desire for well-functioning markets does not require us to insulate asset prices or individual financial institutions from the buffeting of the marketplace.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Liquidity and Well-Functioning Financial Markets Now, let me briefly highlight a key attribute of well-functioning financial markets:  they function best when they attract sufficient liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In previous remarks, I advanced the notion that liquidity can be thought of as roughly comparable to investor confidence.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 5 Liquidity exists when investors are confident and willing to assume risks.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And liquidity persists when risks are quantifiable and investors are creditworthy.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To trace the origins of recent financial markets turmoil, let's recall a time when the environment was more benign and financial markets were flush with liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: This does not require a long memory, as it aptly characterized our capital markets just four months ago.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In early June, I remarked that:
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These financial market conditions were, in part, I argued, the consequence of a long period of remarkably supportive macroeconomic conditions, the acceleration in financial innovation, particularly the growth of structured finance products, and the continued export of the culture of capitalism to emerging-market countries.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Taken together, confidence fostered the continued propagation of new securities, new products, and new markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Not surprisingly, liquidity was ample.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Did Success Sow the Seeds of Distress?
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: So, what could go wrong?
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In times of abundant liquidity, investors that were no longer comfortable with their financial positions could readily sell their holdings.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Similarly, financial institutions could distribute the securities they originated with few constraints.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Like others who had grown increasingly watchful about the ebullience in the financial markets, I wondered whether the risks were being given their due:
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: If, in liquid times, investors in structured products become complacent, they may not understand fully the value of the underlying assets.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: High levels of confidence, perhaps even complacency, were also observable in the behavior of many financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Many hedge funds, growing in size and scope, invested in less-liquid assets in search of higher expected returns.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Many commercial banks increased sponsorship of structured investment vehicles to invest in long-term securities, often financing them off-balance-sheet with short-term commercial paper.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Those financial intermediaries that recognized the risks of extrapolating high levels of liquidity indefinitely were threatened with eroding market share and less-impressive profit profiles.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: They may have hoped that robust trading markets would allow them to exit positions ahead of a crowded trade.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: But, to paraphrase an old Wall Street saw, they don't ring a bell when the markets are at the top or at the bottom.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As you know, liquidity conditions started to deteriorate by mid-July.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Subprime-mortgage markets suffered significantly from a rapid withdrawal of liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: They were a particularly tempting target:  Many subprime mortgage products were newer, performance histories were shorter, prices were rising faster, securitization structures were more complex, disclosure was more opaque, and credit standards were weaker than most other asset classes.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: But, were subprime credit problems the source of contagion causing broader reductions in liquidity and market functioning, as has become a common refrain?
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Or did reductions in liquidity--and concomitant changes in investor sentiment--simply manifest themselves first in the subprime-mortgage markets?
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: If the latter is the case, then the true causes of recent financial tumult may well have preceded the turmoil in the subprime-mortgage markets altogether.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And policy prescriptions should be judged accordingly.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Subprime Lending:  The Spark, Not the Cause Throughout the summer, delinquency rates for subprime adjustable-rate mortgages jumped as house prices decelerated and effective interest rates rose.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The rate of serious delinquencies for subprime mortgages with adjustable interest rates reached close to 15 percent in July.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investors incurred large losses from forced sales of securities backed by subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Credit-rating agencies downgraded numerous securities backed by subprime and alt-A mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The resulting investor skepticism about the accuracy of ratings, combined with mounting losses at mortgage lenders, caused investors to pull back from a broad range of structured products, even though unrelated to mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Financing for leveraged buyouts halted; demand for securities backed by syndicated loans evaporated.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investors began to shun non-mortgage related asset-backed commercial paper.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These subsequent financial problems may not be a reflection of subprime contagion after all.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Instead, it may be that investors fundamentally lost confidence in their ability to value a broad range of assets, particularly those that rely on robust securitization and secondary markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, uncertainty about the ability of large financial institutions to fund their commitments eroded confidence in counterparties more generally.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Risk premiums and term premiums rose rapidly, and investors sought refuge.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The principles, products, and practices that served so many so well for so long seemed somehow ill-suited to the evolving financial architecture.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Markets that rely less on securitizations, and are more transparent, have fared better in recent days and weeks.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The stock market, while quite volatile, is about unchanged from mid-June levels.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In the corporate bond market, spreads have widened somewhat, but current levels are close to historic averages, and issuance of investment-grade bonds has been quite sizable.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Issuance of speculative-grade bonds has been sharply reduced, but aside from difficulties of LBO-related deals, this may reflect issuers' willingness to await improved conditions.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Not unlike prior episodes, it seems increasingly apparent that many investors and financial intermediaries became so content with the benign economic conditions and robust financial markets that they tended to act with confidence greater than warranted by the fundamentals.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, some may have overly relied on credit ratings as sole gatekeepers for evaluating risks.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: So perhaps, in some sense, markets can become too liquid.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In this case, markets may appear to function smoothly, but the risk-based pricing that lies at the heart of how financial markets efficiently allocate capital is impaired.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The gloss of confidence may cause a misallocation of resources, and investors and financial intermediaries can be sidelined for a time, undermining the normal functioning of market operations.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Conclusion Some months ago, I asked, "What happens when liquidity falters?"
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 8 Highlighting the risks of a liquidity shock at some indeterminate point in the future is easier than ascertaining the consequences with precision.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Reduced liquidity conditions in markets today stem from a pullback in investors' willingness to take risks, which may have been triggered, but I argue not caused, by losses in subprime-mortgage markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Thus, a broader reassessment of risk positions appears at work, especially for products that are opaque or complex.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investors who had relied on credit ratings alone are now confronted with having to perform their own credit and market valuations.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Some may now find they are not well-equipped to make these evaluations.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: How quickly markets normalize may depend on the speed with which investors and counterparties gain comfort in their abilities to value assets.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The adjustment process by private investors has increased the risk that banks may increasingly be called upon as backup providers of funding.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve responded to these developments by providing reserves to the banking system; it announced a cut in the discount rate of 50 basis points and adjustments to the Reserve Banks' usual discount window practices to facilitate the provision of term financing.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In addition, earlier this week, the FOMC lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The action was intended to help forestall some of the adverse effects on the broader economy that might arise from the disruptions in financial markets and to promote moderate growth over time.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Recent developments in financial markets, including impaired price discovery, have increased the uncertainty surrounding the economic outlook.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: What originated as a liquidity shock could potentially give rise to increases in credit risk.
speech_title: Financial Market Developments
speech_venue: To the State University of New York at Albanyâs School of Business, Albany, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Committee will continue to assess the effects of these and other developments on economic prospects and will act as needed to meet our dual mandate, fostering price stability and economic growth.
