speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the shorter run, we at the Federal Reserve aim to achieve our dual mandate of not only stabilizing prices but also reducing the volatility of output and employment around their maximum sustainable levels.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization affects the ability of monetary policy makers to stabilize prices and output in two ways: (1) through its effects on the behavior of inflation and output and (2) through its effects on the ways in which monetary policy influences inflation and output--that is, on the monetary transmission mechanism.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I will look at each in turn and will then use the analysis to address another important issue for monetary policy makers:  Has globalization been a key driver of improvements in inflation performance and the decline in inflation that we have been seeing throughout the world?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: (Please note that my comments here reflect my own views and not necessarily those of others on the Board of Governors or the Federal Open Market Committee.)
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization and Inflation We should never forget Milton Friedman's adage that "inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon."
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the long run, as long as a central bank has an independent monetary policyââthat is, it is not locked into a fixed-exchange-rate regime in which its hands are tiedââthe rate of inflation is determined by monetary policy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization, however, can have an effect on the incentives for central banks to control inflation and, more directly, on inflation developments in the short and medium runs.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Kenneth Rogoff (2003) argues that globalization has led to greater price flexibility, which has reduced the ability of central banks to use inflation surprises to boost output.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In other words, the Phillips curve will steepen, making more stark the short-run tradeoff between unemployment and inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result, central banks will be less tempted to try to exploit the short-run tradeoff between inflation and unemployment, as in the Barro-Gordon (1983) model, and so will be less likely to pursue overly expansionary monetary policy that leads to higher inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: A major problem with Rogoff's argument is that instead of steepening with the growth of globalization in recent years, the Phillips curve has become flatter, not only in the United States but also in many other countries throughout the world (Borio and Filardo, 2007; International Monetary Fund, 2006; Ihrig and others, 2007; Pain, Koske, and Sollie, 2006).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, even though Rogoff's argument is reasonable from a theoretical viewpoint, it is hard to make the case that it is important in the current economic environment.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization, because it makes markets more competitive, also has the potential to spur productivity growth.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Higher productivity growth can lead to a reduction in inflation because it directly lowers prices if monetary policy does not become more expansionary.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, such growth makes it easier for the monetary authorities to allow inflation to fall because output growth will continue to be rapid when inflation is declining.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This may have been the situation in the United States in the late 1990s, when productivity growth surged and inflation declined.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The rise in productivity growth during this period in the United States, however, did not seem to spill over to other industrial countries, a result that cast doubt on whether globalization has indeed accelerated the transmission of productivity growth across national borders.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because globalization increases competition, it can also reduce markups (price over costs), and this reduction may lead to lower relative prices, as is argued by Chen, Imbs, and Scott (2007).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, lower markups and price levels should have only transitory effects on inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, the prediction of lower markups from globalization seems to conflict with the high corporate profit rates that we are currently observing around the world.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: These effects from the greater price flexibility and increased competition in domestic markets that have arisen from globalization, while theoretically plausible, are often at variance with salient features of the world economy, and so they do not explain why inflation has declined in recent years.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, another very dramatic feature of globalization is that it has brought more than a billion new workers into the global economic system from China and India.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some observers claim that through its sales of low-cost goods, developing Asiaââand especially Chinaââhas been "exporting deflation" and will continue to do so until wages in these countries rise.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although this effect, too, is plausible, research suggests that its importance should not be exaggerated.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: If China were truly exporting deflation, the effect should be evident primarily in the behavior of import prices.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research at the Federal Reserve Board by Kamin, Marazzi, and Schindler (2006) estimates that purchases of manufactures from China have lowered U.S. import price inflation roughly 1 percentage point annually over the past decade, a decline that has led to a short-run lowering of consumer price inflation of about one-tenth of 1 percentage point and a somewhat larger effect over the longer term.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research at the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) by Pain, Koske, and Sollie (2006) arrives at a similar estimate of the effect of trade in manufactures with developing countries on U.S. inflation:  negative 0.2 to negative 0.3 percentage point.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: At the same time, the additional demand for primary commodities by developing Asia, especially China and India, is putting upward pressure on global prices of these goods.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: During 2004-06, the region accounted for about 40 percent of the global growth in demand for oil and more than 70 percent of the growth in demand for copper and zinc.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The global commodities boom, which has been stimulated by the emergence of the Chinese and Indian economies on the international scene, has been an important offset to the deflationary effects from their low-priced goods and services.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Analysis by the Board's staff, which weights the negative effect on U.S. inflation from cheaper manufactures against the positive effect from higher commodity prices, finds that the net effect in recent years could go either way but in any case is probably quite small.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Looking back before the recent boom in commodities prices, the staff's best estimate is that China's and India's entrance on the global trading scene has had a small negative effect on inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research at the OECD (Pain, Koske, and Sollie, 2006) reaches similar conclusions, finding a net effect of 0 to negative 1/4 percentage point for the United States, the euro area, and the OECD economies in aggregate.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Laurence Ball (2006) makes an important point that cheaper imports from places like China lower relative prices for imported goods but ultimately do not affect inflation, which is the change in overall prices.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Following the argument made by Milton Friedman (Friedman, 1974), Ball points out that for every decline in the relative price of one good or service in a price index like the consumer price index (CPI), there is by definition a rise in the relative price of some other good or service.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Any pattern of relative-price changes is compatible with a particular level of the inflation rate.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: What determines the overall inflation rate is not relative prices for one category of goods and services but rather the balance between overall demand and supply in the economy, which ultimately is influenced by monetary policy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Ball therefore takes the view that cheap imports from China and other low-wage economies should not affect inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I would not go as far as Ball does for the reason that changes in relative prices in an important category of goods and services could affect inflation for a considerable period of time.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nevertheless, his argument, as well as the research cited earlier, indicates that many of the exaggerated claims that globalization has been an important factor in lowering inflation in recent years just do not hold up.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization and Output The increasing integration of the global economy can have several effects on output.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: It is thus of concern to monetary policy makers because it can affect both output volatility and our forecasts of the economy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization may stabilize output by enabling producers to service a diversified global market rather than just the domestic market.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research at the Federal Reserve Board (Ihrig and others, 2007) documents that net exports tend to be negatively correlated with domestic demand and thus stabilize output; other research (Guerrieri, Gust, and López-Salido, 2007) finds that shocks to domestic demand move output less in more open economies.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the opposite direction, greater trade integrationââincluding greater trade in services (Markusen, 2007)ââcould raise output volatility as countries become more vulnerable to foreign shocks.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: There is indeed some evidence that this situation has occurred in Mexico (Bergin, Feenstra, and Hanson, 2007).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As with the effects of greater trade integration on the volatility of output, the effects of financial globalization can go both ways.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Increasing global diversification lowers the likelihood that financial shocks will be concentrated in individual economies and thus lead to economic downturns.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, as I have emphasized in my writings (Mishkin, 2006a), financial globalization can help promote institutional reforms that can make the financial system more stable, thereby contributing to more output stability.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, as I have also emphasized in my work (Mishkin, 2006a, chap.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 4), financial globalization makes it easier for capital inflows to fuel excessive risk-taking on the part of financial institutions and allows financial shocks to be transmitted more readily across borders.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: On balance, my sense is that economic globalization has the potential to be stabilizing for individual economies as both real and financial shocks are spread more evenly across larger numbers of economic agents.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: One might even speculate that globalization has contributed to the so-called Great Moderation, the decline in output variability in countries like the United States over the past twenty years, and this hypothesis should be a topic for future research.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The bottom line, however, is that it is not at all clear whether globalization increases or reduces output volatility.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: That said, as I have emphasized in my speeches and writings (Mishkin, 2006a, b; Mishkin, 2007b), I strongly believe that globalization is and has been a key factor in promoting economic growth.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization not only promotes a more competitive economic environment--which forces business to innovate--but it also creates strong incentives for institutional reform to make markets work better.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization in recent years has not only enabled hundreds of millions of  people in countries like China and India to escape abject poverty (income of less than $1 per day) but has also helped economies like ours in the United States to be highly dynamic, which is essential to our future economic well-being.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization and the Monetary Transmission Mechanism Four questions naturally arise when we consider whether globalization has changed the monetary transmission mechanism, that is, how monetary policy influences inflation and output:  (1) Has globalization led to a decline in the sensitivity of inflation to domestic output gaps (the difference between actual and potential output) and thus to domestic monetary policy?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In other words, has globalization made the Phillips curve flatter?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: (2) Are foreign output gaps playing a more prominent role in the domestic inflation process, so that domestic monetary policy has more difficulty stabilizing inflation?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: (3) Can domestic monetary policy still control domestic interest rates and so stabilize both inflation and output?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: (4) Are there other ways, besides possible influences on inflation and interest rates, in which globalization may have affected the transmission mechanism of monetary policy?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Has globalization led to a decline in the sensitivity of inflation to domestic output gaps (the difference between actual and potential output) and thus to domestic monetary policy?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In recent years, we have clearly witnessed a decline in the sensitivity of inflation to the domestic output gap (a flattening of the Phillips curve) in the United States and other advanced countries (Borio and Filardo, 2007; International Monetary Fund, 2006; Ihrig and others, 2007; Pain, Koske, and Sollie, 2006).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization might make inflation less responsive to rising domestic resource utilization because households and businesses can go outside the country to buy goods and services, so there will be less pressure for domestic prices to rise.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Another way of thinking about this point is to recognize that globalization might reduce the likelihood of having supply bottlenecks as domestic resource utilization rises.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although this story is a plausible one, research at the Federal Reserve Board and elsewhere finds no evidence that the flattening of the Phillips curve reflects the process of increasing trade integration (Ihrig  and others, 2007; Ball, 2006; Wynne and Kersting, 2007).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Rather than globalization being an important factor leading to flatter Phillips curves, I would argue (as in Mishkin, 2007a) that flatter Phillips curves are the direct result of better monetary policy that has anchored inflation expectations.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because monetary authorities are focusing more on establishing a stronger nominal anchor, a rise in resource utilization will not lead to a rise in expected inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Instead, households and businesses will expect monetary authorities to take the necessary steps to ensure that the economy will not overheat, and, as a result, they will not push for higher prices and wages.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Not only is this explanation for decreased sensitivity of inflation to output gaps more consistent with empirical evidence (see Mishkin, 2007a; Roberts, 2006), but it is more consistent with the timing of when Phillips curves became flatter.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the United States, Phillips curves started to flatten in the 1980s, well before the recent surge of globalization but just after inflation expectations started to become anchored.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Are foreign output gaps playing a more prominent role in the domestic inflation process, so that domestic monetary policy has more difficulty stabilizing inflation?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As economies have become more open, foreign factors may have become more important in the determination of domestic inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research at the Bank for International Settlements (Borio and Filardo, 2007) seems to provide evidence that foreign resource slack has superseded domestic slack as a key determinant of domestic inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, research at the Federal Reserve Board (Ihrig and others, 2007) and at the OECD (Pain, Koske, and Sollie, 2006) point out that the specification of the Phillips curve in Borio and Filardo (2007) is problematic.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Their key findings are not robust to alternative specifications.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, their specification leads to econometric difficulties because it causes serial correlation of the residuals that is not corrected for.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Using more-conventional specifications of Phillips curves, the research at the Federal Reserve Board (Ihrig and others, 2007) and the OECD (Pain, Koske, and Sollie, 2006), as well as Ball (2006), finds that foreign output gaps are not important determinants of domestic inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, foreign factors could more plausibly play a role in the inflation process through import prices.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As economies become more open and imports play a bigger role in the economy, consumer prices may become more sensitive to import prices.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, CPI inflation does appear to have become more sensitive to import prices over time, both in the United States and in other OECD countries (Pain, Koske, and Sollie, 2006).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Can domestic monetary policy still control domestic interest rates and so stabilize both inflation and output?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In principle, the increasing global integration of financial markets, by reducing the scope for individual central banks to control domestic interest rates, could hamper the ability of monetary policy to stabilize prices and economic activity.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, some evidence appears to suggest that foreign factors influence interest rates; for example, the global saving glut does seem to have led to somewhat lower long-term interest rates by reducing term premiums (Warnock and Warnock, 2006).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: More generally, research points to important linkages between U.S. and foreign interest rates and other asset prices (Ehrmann, Fratzscher and Rigobon, 2005; Faust and others, 2007).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, central banks still retain the ability to control short-term interest rates, which affect the domestic cost of credit and long-term interest rates, and so can continue to do their job of stabilizing inflation and output.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Are there other ways, besides possible influences on inflation and interest rates, in which globalization may have affected the transmission mechanism of monetary policy?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The preceding discussion might lead to the conclusion that globalization has not had important effects, either on the behavior of inflation or the ability of monetary policy to affect the economy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, globalization might have an effect on the process of monetary transmission that does not operate through Phillips-curve-type mechanisms.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: One of the key transmission channels of monetary policy is the exchange rate.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: A tightening of monetary policy, for example, raises U.S. interest rates relative to those abroad, thereby inducing upward pressure on the foreign exchange value of the dollar.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: An appreciation of the dollar, in turn, restrains exports (because the price of U.S. goods rises when measured in foreign currencies) and stimulates imports (because imports become cheaper in dollar terms).
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The resulting decrease in net exports implies a reduction in aggregate demand.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, an appreciation of the dollar that leads to a decline in import prices also helps restrain overall U.S. inflation.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: By expanding the share of tradable goods and services in the economy, globalization might increase the role of the exchange rate as a transmission channel of monetary policy and could reduce the role of the interest rate channel.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The larger the share of imports and exports in the economy, the greater the change in net exportsââand, hence, in the contribution of net exports to gross domestic product (GDP) growthââfor a given change in the exchange rate.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, the larger the share of imports in the economy, the larger should be the effect on overall CPI inflation of a given change in import prices when the exchange rate changes.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 4 (This effect is explicitly incorporated in Federal Reserve staff models of U.S. inflation, which weight import prices by the share of imports in the consumption basket.)
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: By the same token, the effect of the interest rate channel on overall economic activity may be diminished by greater trade integration as changes in domestic demand are offset by induced changes in imports.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Guerrieri, Gust, and López-Salido (2007), for example, find that shocks to domestic demand move output less in more-open economies because they lead to larger offsetting movements in the trade balance.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Supporting this result, Ihrig and others (2007) conclude that correlations between real GDP growth and real domestic demand growth have declined in recent decades in the United States and several other industrial economies.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition to increasing the sensitivity of the economy to changes in exchange rates, globalization may have increased the sensitivity of exchange rates to monetary policy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the past few decades, as capital controls have been eliminated in most major economies and the levels of home bias in portfolio investment have declined, financial markets around the world have become more tightly integrated.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: An implication of this financial globalization is that demand for domestic and foreign assets is likely to have become more sensitive to international differences in perceived rates of return.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Accordingly, monetary policy actions may now exert more influence on exchange rates than was the case when markets were less tightly integrated and assets of different countries were perceived to be less substitutable for each other.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This linkage between globalization and the effect of monetary policy on exchange rates is somewhat speculative but represents a worthwhile avenue for further research.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Why Has Inflation Declined in Recent Years?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: What does all the preceding analysis tell us about why we have had better inflation performance in recent years?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I don't know of anyone who would have predicted twenty years ago that inflation would be so low and stable in so many countries.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Has globalization been an important part of the story of inflation's remarkable decline in recent years?
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In terms of direct effects, the discussion here provides a clear-cut answer:  No.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Inflation has come down in the old-fashioned way.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Tighter monetary policy and a commitment to price stability by central banks throughout the world have led to lower inflation and an anchoring of inflation expectations.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: These policies have had huge benefitsâânot only the achievement of low and stable inflation but also an improvement in the overall performance of the economy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Globalization, however, may have helped reduce inflation in more-subtle ways.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: By fostering increased interactions among central banks, academics, and the public in many different countries, globalization has helped spread a common culture that stresses the benefits of achieving price stability.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The resulting increased focus on price stability has been a key reason for the reduction of inflation worldwide.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conclusion The increasing integration of global product, labor, and financial markets has the potential to significantly alter the behavior of the economy, a development that could complicate the task of monetary policy.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In practice, however, the behavior of the U.S. and global economies does not appear to have radically changed in recent years.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve and other central banks retain the ability to stabilize prices and output.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nonetheless, central bankers must continue to monitor the evolution of the economy and the changes that may result from the ongoing globalization process.
speech_title: Globalization, Macroeconomic Performance, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Domestic Prices in an Integrated World Economy Conference, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.
