speaker: Kohn
text: The economic picture has evolved rapidly over the past few months, and on September 18, the Federal Reserve eased monetary policy, cutting its target for the federal funds rate 1/2 percentage point.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: I thought it might be useful this morning to give you my take on why this action was necessary and my sense of what might lie ahead for the economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: I need to emphasize that these are my views and are not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: A brief recap of where the economy has been will be helpful in understanding where we are now and where we might be headed.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The economy has been growing at about a 2 percent pace since the middle of 2006 despite being held back by a weakening housing market.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Job gains have averaged about 125,000 per month over the past year or so, and the unemployment rate has hovered around 4-1/2 percent, a fairly low rate historically for the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: When the members of the Federal Reserve Board and the presidents of Federal Reserve Banks made their semi-annual economic projections this past July, most of us saw growth strengthening a little next year as the drag from the housing adjustment abated, with the unemployment rate perhaps drifting up just a little.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Inflation had been buffeted by large swings in food and energy prices, but underlying inflation rates had edged down since the summer of 2006; on balance, we expected relatively low inflation ahead, although we were concerned that tight labor and product markets could lead to further price pressures.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: When the FOMC met in early August, this basic picture had not changed much.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The housing sector had continued to weaken; indeed, with subprime mortgage markets increasingly impaired and problems becoming evident in some other segments of mortgage markets, the contraction in residential construction seemed likely to be even deeper than we had previously anticipated.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: And increased resistance on the part of investors to some of the terms on the loans and bonds that were backing leveraged buyouts was a sign that a rethinking of risk exposures might be spreading beyond mortgage markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: But output overall still appeared to be expanding at a moderate pace; jobs and incomes, although rising less rapidly than before, were still advancing reasonably well, supporting sustained expansion in household spending; and businesses had successfully worked off the overhang of inventories that had emerged at the end of 2006.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, strong demand from abroad was providing considerable support to our exports.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The FOMC recognized that less accommodative conditions in some financial markets posed a threat to the strength of future economic growth.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, our primary concern remained the upside risks to inflation.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Shortly after the August FOMC meeting, however, financial market conditions deteriorated considerably further, following events that shook investor confidence, particularly in complex structured credit products.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The disruptions to nonprime mortgage markets became more severe and problems even extended to high-quality loans, as rates for prime jumbo mortgages jumped after the secondary markets for them shut down.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Importantly, the disruptions also spread beyond the mortgage markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Most notably, investors' concerns about exposures to subprime mortgage credit risk caused them to shun commercial paper that might be backed by such assets, in both Europe and the United States.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: This aversion, in turn, meant that commercial banks that had written backup liquidity lines for commercial paper programs or had other connections with these programs might have to make good on their actual or implied support by extending credit.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: With leveraged buyout credit and some mortgage originations also possibly staying on the balance sheet unexpectedly, the banks faced substantial, but uncertain, calls on their liquidity and capital.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: All this uncertainty led the banks and other short-term lenders to turn very cautious; interest rates on bank deposits and other sources of credit beyond just a few days rose steeply, funding in money markets became concentrated in the very short term, and concerned and uncertain lenders generally became much less willing to extend the credit needed for liquid and efficient financial markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Why the financial markets behaved as they have is a complex story that we will be sorting out for a while.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: For our purposes this morning, I will concentrate on the consequences for household and business borrowers and for the economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In particular, I expect that the financial market turmoil of the past few months will leave an imprint on the cost and availability of credit to many household and business borrowers.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The greatest effects have been on credit related to residential real estate; in addition to the problems with nonprime and jumbo first mortgages, second mortgages and home equity lines of credit that many households have been using to finance purchases of household durables and other consumer goods and services probably will become more expensive and less available as well.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Banks are likely to be especially cautious about making new loans and financing commitments while substantial uncertainty about the quality of loans and the extent of demands from previous commitments persists.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: So it would not be surprising to see less-generous credit for a wide variety of loans to business and households.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: And, the rates for some loans are tied directly to elevated libor or other rates in term funding markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: More generally, credit will probably not be as easily available and as inexpensive for many borrowers as it was a few months ago, even after market functioning improves.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In several segments of the financial markets, compensation for taking on risk had for some time seemed too low to be sustainable.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, more credit is likely to flow through banks, and leverage in the nonbank sectors of the financial markets will be lower.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The higher levels of capital relative to assets should form the basis for a more stable system, but the spread of lending rates over the cost of funds will need to rise so that capital can earn a competitive rate of return.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The deterioration in actual and expected financial market conditions between the August and September FOMC meetings changed our view of appropriate monetary policy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Whatever policy path previously seemed appropriate to support sustainable growth and price stability looked too high once credit conditions tightened substantially.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Our policy easing was aimed at helping to offset the effects of those tighter credit conditions and thereby to encourage moderate economic growth over time.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: It was not intended to, nor should it, short circuit a more realistic pricing of risk and the gains and losses that the repricing will entail for market participants.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Many people had expected the Federal Reserve to follow a gradual path of rate reductions in response to financial market developments--say, 25 basis points in September and another 25 basis points in October.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Such a path would be in keeping with how we have often approached our policy choices, as it has the advantage of allowing us to calibrate our policy as we see how the economic situation is evolving and responding to earlier policy moves.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: However, given the circumstances at the time of the September FOMC meeting, there were strong arguments in favor of the larger action of a 50 basis point decrease in the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: For one thing, it seemed that a decrease of that size could well be necessary to promote moderate growth.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: We had been holding the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 percent, well above the expected rate of inflation, in part to compensate for what had been very narrow yield spreads and readily available credit.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: We did not know how quickly markets would recover, the extent to which credit terms and standards would be tightened, or precisely how households and businesses would respond to recent or forthcoming financial developments.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: But, pending further evidence, a 50 basis point easing was not an unreasonable first approximation of what might be required to keep the economy on a sustainable growth path.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, I thought that economic performance would be better served by the Federal Reserve taking its chances on responding too much, or too rapidly, to the turmoil in financial markets rather than acting too little, or too slowly.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Sluggish or inadequate easing risked a weaker real economy that might cause lenders to pull back even more, leading to a deteriorating situation that could prove difficult to reverse.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: With the news on inflation relatively favorable of late and with inflation expectations seemingly well anchored, I believed that we would be able to offset the cut in the federal funds rate--if it turned out to be larger than needed--in time to preserve price stability.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Since the September FOMC meeting, we have seen some signs of improvement in some markets that were severely disrupted.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, investors appear to be differentiating more among risk characteristics of asset-backed commercial paper programs; term funding has become a little more readily available to banks and commercial paper issuers; and the run-off in commercial paper outstandings has slowed.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: But spreads in these markets are still quite high by historical standards and funding maturities are very short, leaving many markets vulnerable to unpleasant surprises.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In mortgage markets, spreads for rates on jumbo prime mortgage loans over those on conforming, agency eligible, loans have come down a bit, but are still elevated.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, it may be a while before market participants regain enough confidence to price and trade certain types of assets and more normal liquidity conditions are restored.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Our policy action will not be able to avert all of the weakness in the economy that may be in train for the next several months.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Monetary policy works with a lag, and the effects of our easing action will have their maximum effect only after several quarters.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In particular, housing markets are likely to remain depressed in coming months as housing demand is restrained by the difficulty in obtaining mortgages and perhaps also by spreading expectations on the part of buyers that house prices will fall, as they already have in a number of markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: And, although builders have reduced housing starts sharply, they have made very little progress in reducing the number of unsold new homes on the market.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, even absent a further deterioration in sales, residential construction would probably decline further in the months ahead, imparting a significant drag on overall growth in real gross domestic product.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Beyond housing, it is too early to tell what effect financial market turmoil is having on household and business spending, though very preliminary and partial information suggest that thus far the effects seem to be limited.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the available data indicate that the economy entered this period still expanding at a moderate pace.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, consumption held up well this summer supported by solid growth in real incomes.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: And, the recent data on orders and shipments of capital goods and on nonresidential construction indicated further growth in capital outlays in August.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, credit availability is likely to be tighter than before, consumer confidence is down, and businesses will probably be a little more cautious for a while, suggesting that these components of aggregate demand could become more subdued in coming months.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Over time, however, I anticipate that the economy will move back onto a moderate growth track.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The housing market should gradually recover as the cutback in production and lower prices help reduce the inventory overhang.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: And, as it does, the drag on growth from the declines in residential construction will abate, providing a boost to overall economic activity.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, households are likely to start to save more out of their current incomes as they come to realize that they cannot count on a rise in the value of their real estate to build their retirement nest eggs.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: However, households have been surprisingly resilient to recent economic shocks, and any rise in the saving rate probably would be gradual.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: More generally, consumer spending should continue to be supported by ongoing growth in employment and income.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In the business sector, balance sheets are in good shape, and most firms are not likely to face an appreciable tightening of credit availability.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, I anticipate that they will expand their investment spending to keep pace with rising household demands and with strength in export markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: In sum, once we get through the near-term weakness caused by the extra downleg from the housing contraction and any spillover from tighter credit conditions, I am looking for moderate growth with high levels of employment.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: But you should view these forecasts even more skeptically than usual.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The FOMC emphasized the considerable uncertainty in the outlook.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: As I noted earlier, we do not know how financial markets will evolve, and we do not know how households and businesses will respond to financial developments.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Naturally, these types of uncertainties are greatest when markets are behaving abnormally.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The recovery from the problems of the early 1990s was prolonged because banks had to rebuild capital; the rebound from the market crisis of 1998 was swifter, helped along by higher productivity growth and the rise in the stock market that accompanied the optimism about high-tech profits.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: We will need to be nimble in adjusting policy to promote growth and price stability.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Of course, we would not have eased policy if the outlook for inflation had not been favorable.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: The recent data on consumer price inflation have been encouraging.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Movements in energy prices have created volatility in overall inflation, but over the past twelve months both core and total prices for personal consumption expenditures rose 1.8 percent.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the near-term weakness in the economy should intensify competitive conditions in markets and reduce potential pressures on costs and prices.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: And, it will be critical for inflation expectations to remain well contained.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, I do not want to minimize the upside risks to inflation either.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Rates of resource utilization are still relatively high, and the slower rates of productivity growth over the past two years, coupled with a pickup in compensation growth, have led to a noticeable acceleration in unit labor costs.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the decline in the exchange value of the dollar has put upward pressure on prices of imported goods, which have both direct and indirect effects on overall consumer prices.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, and as the FOMC noted in our recent statement, we will need to monitor inflation developments carefully.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Allowing inflation to rise would not be in the public interest and would be contrary to our legislative mandate for stable prices and maximum employment.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Maintaining an environment of low and stable inflation facilitates planning, saving, and capital investment by households and businesses and thus is a prerequisite for allowing the economy to realize its potential.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: I assure you that we on the FOMC will continue to monitor economic developments closely and will act as necessary to promote both price stability and sustainable economic growth.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: Wendy Dunn and William Wascher , of the Boardâs staff, contributed to the preparation of these remarks.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce 207th Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Warsh
text: Thank you to the New York State Economics Association and our hosts here at Siena College for inviting me to participate in the conference.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: They say you can never go home again.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Well, I am testing that theory and am pleased to be back in upstate New York for the second time in as many weeks.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In my remarks at the School of Business at the University at Albany, I argued that the conditions causing the turmoil in the financial markets were long in the making and that these causes should not be conflated with the particular troubles in the mortgage markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I also posited that the financial market conditions may have proven to be overly ebullient, masking troubles that may have sown the seeds of financial distress.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 1 This evening, I will underscore the responsibility of the Federal Reserve during periods of financial market turmoil and offer some perspective on the current state of financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Gathering Storm Several months ago, many large, global commercial and investment banks appeared on pace to post another record year of corporate profits.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Underwriting and M&A activities were robust.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Sales and trading revenues were bolstered by the acceleration of financial innovation.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Principal investing appeared to be an increasingly accepted industry practice alongside traditional advisory business.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Private pools of capital were growing strikingly.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Public and private pension funds were reportedly increasing capital allocations to alternative investments.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And, thanks in part to accommodative credit markets, the golden age of private equity appeared upon us.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Finance companies and other nondepository financial institutions were increasingly able to thrive, proving to be formidable competitors for traditional banks and thrifts.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In sum, market functioning appeared robust, and risks underlying various assets were seemingly dispersed among a range of sovereignties, financial intermediaries, and investors.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: During this period of seemingly benign economic conditions, most market participants appeared more focused on the dynamics of the new financial architecture than on the policy judgments of central bankers.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Surely, market participants did not presume that the Federal Reserve was a mere spectator to market developments.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Nonetheless, discussions of the Fed and financial stability may have seemed somehow anachronistic with the new paradigm sweeping financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As you well know, by mid-August, volatility spiked in many markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Term premiums reappeared with force.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Signs of illiquidity were evident in a number of important markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And clarion calls for the Fed to bring stability to financial markets were loud.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Almost overnight, the role of the Federal Reserve and other central banks in fostering financial stability found its way to the front pages of major media.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: So, let me discuss the responsibilities of the Federal Reserve in promoting stable financial conditions.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Although our policy tools are powerful, and our judgments are informed, our pronouncements are not made in isolation.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The roles and responsibilities of other public agents, domestic and abroad, and private market participants are particularly critical during times of financial turmoil.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We are, after all, central bankers, not central planners.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Responsibilities of the Federal Reserve So what is the role of a central bank like the Federal Reserve in fostering financial stability?
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 2 Historically, episodes of financial instability and the sharp economic downturns that sometimes ensued were a driving force in the creation of the Federal Reserve itself.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: After earlier, sporadic, and ultimately less-than-successful attempts to create a central bank of the United States, the U.S. financial system found itself lacking an effective means to address the periodic financial crises that occurred in the second half of the nineteenth and in the early twentieth century.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 3 Against this backdrop, the Congress authored the Federal Reserve Act in 1913, creating the Federal Reserve System.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It is worth emphasizing that the Federal Reserve's concern with financial stability stems largely from the adverse implications of financial instability for overall economic performance.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 4 The Fed's interest in promoting financial stability is thus intimately connected with its macroeconomic objectives:  maximum sustainable employment and price stability.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: From the founding of the Federal Reserve to the present, a key question confronts policymakers and market participants alike:  What is financial stability?
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Perhaps it is better to address what it is not.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In my view, financial stability does not demand a state of lessened financial market movements, a state of muted volatility.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: More often than not, financial markets process new information efficiently:  If some unexpected news arrives, markets adjust, sometimes even sharply, and they should.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These types of movements are healthy, even necessary.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: They serve to quickly bring prices in line with underlying fundamentals.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And markets that move quickly and adroitly do not necessarily produce unstable financial conditions.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Nor should those who take up the cause of ensuring financial stability protect individual investors or financial institutions from substantial losses or insolvency.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To the contrary, a healthy and well-functioning financial system will tend to reward well-managed risk-taking and punish imprudence.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I am inclined to interpret the Federal Reserve's interest in promoting financial stability as a desire to foster conditions that favor sustainable growth and stable prices.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In this sense, financial stability concerns may rightly shape policymakers' views about the modal outlook for the economy as well as the risks surrounding this outlook.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial instability may thus be characterized as a situation in which the financial system becomes incapable of efficiently allocating resources at market-clearing prices across the economy.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 5 If financial markets become dysfunctional, financial intermediaries' flexibility may be impaired, and investors may become uncertain about their prospects.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And if this situation were to persist, overall macroeconomic performance could be threatened.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In an earlier period of financial turmoil, this phenomenon was termed "fear-induced disengagement."
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 6 Assessing Financial Stability The Federal Reserve is well positioned to monitor developments in financial markets and assess the quality of market functioning.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We have access to a wide range of financial and economic data and extensive contacts with market participants.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Particularly in times of financial distress, we must draw on a full range of market indicators.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We also glean important information by virtue of our responsibilities as a banking regulator and payment system operator.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And although such a dashboard of key information is exceedingly useful, it should not be confused with a crystal ball.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: For even if our understanding of the financial markets was somehow perfect, the transmission mechanism between financial markets and the real economy is only partially understood.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Like private market participants, the Federal Reserve is in the business of making policy judgments amid uncertainty and must assess the prospects for the real economy with considerable humility.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: What indicators might help us assess the economic and financial situation?
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We look to prices at which investors are willing to provide capital by reviewing risk premiums across a range of asset markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As an example, we monitor corporate credit spreads from bond, loan, and credit derivative markets, and we follow closely the evolution of pricing in mortgage markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We also look to the terms by which market participants are willing to lock up funds over various time horizons by reviewing term premiums embedded in financial market prices.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And we constantly revisit investors' willingness to conduct business with financial intermediaries to assess counterparty credit risk.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In this respect, market-based indicators are certainly informative, as are measures of current exposures of financial institutions obtained through the supervisory process.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: No central bank financial market dashboard is complete, however, if it does not give considerable weight to measures of price stability.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As a result, we constantly review inflation expectations, as measured by spot and forward TIPS spreads, surveys, commodity prices, and foreign exchange values.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Volume indicators are often particularly useful in assessing market functioning in times of market turmoil.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Volume indicators impart knowledge about the depth and extent of trading and the willingness of financial intermediaries to serve as market makers.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: By reviewing the sizes of issuance of various financial instruments as well as trade volumes in a number of markets, we try to assess the relative strength and resilience of markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And we try to assess the reliability of prices by reviewing information on bid-ask spreads and quote sizes where available.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Of course, these various price and volume indicators are not easy to disentangle, necessitating that our judgments on the state of market functioning customarily be provisional.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Throughout the turbulence of the past few months, we have followed a number of indicators that pointed to strains in several markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: For example, we saw spreads on subprime residential mortgage-backed securities soar and securitization volumes slow to a trickle as market participants became concerned about their ability to value those products amid mounting delinquency rates and defaults in the sector.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investors' lack of confidence in valuations was also apparent in other securitized products, as evidenced by higher spreads and lower issuance in markets for collateralized debt obligations and collateralized loan obligations.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The asset-backed and the lower-grade unsecured commercial paper markets also came under pressure; difficulties spread to other money markets, and term spreads in interbank funding markets climbed much above historical levels.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It is also true, however, that some financial indicators provided some reassurance during this period.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Important parts of the financial system continued to function well, especially in markets where less-complex financial products are traded and where investors are less reliant on the role of the rating agencies.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: For example, although equity markets were quite volatile at times, trading was generally not impaired, and investors were able to buy and sell stocks at market-prevailing prices, even at the times of greatest turbulence.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The markets for longer-term Treasury securities and investment-grade corporate bonds generally continued to function well, albeit at new market-clearing prices.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It is notable that the level of fails-to-deliver in Treasury trades did not spike amid the market turmoil despite very intense safe-haven demands for Treasury securities at times.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Of great importance, clearing and settlement systems proved to be extremely resilient throughout the episode, even if most post-trade infrastructure providers experienced record transaction volumes.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To be sure, mortgage lenders came under severe stress, and several large commercial and investment banks were subjected to strains brought about by higher contingent liabilities and various other commitments.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Still, at least by number, most financial institutions remained "open for business," willing to lend, albeit at tighter terms.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And although many hedge funds posted meaningful losses, on balance, they appear to have performed a useful function during this period of considerable tumult.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Although these positive signs are acknowledged, financial conditions were clearly stressed in recent months.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: When markets do not clear and some large financial institutions withdraw from risk-taking, it is prudent for a central bank to take account of the impaired nature of market functioning.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The specter of financial instability is heightened, and the prospect of harm to the overall economy is difficult to dismiss.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve responded to these developments by providing reserves to the banking system; it announced a cut in the discount rate of 50 basis points and adjustments to discount window practices to facilitate the provision of term funding.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In the current episode, the disruptions in the structured finance, mortgage, leveraged loan, commercial paper, and interbank term funding markets made credit considerably less available for many households and businesses and thus, ultimately, represented a risk to the performance of our macroeconomy.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As a result, the Federal Reserve took action to help forestall this risk, including the 50 basis points cut in the target federal funds rate on September 18.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Recent Financial Market Developments It is premature to judge the ultimate effects of our policy actions on financial conditions, let alone on macroeconomic performance.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Our dashboard of financial indicators, however, points to some encouraging signs, suggesting that financial conditions might be normalizing somewhat.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In particular, I am encouraged by the price differentiation in certain markets based upon company-specific and asset-specific assessments of fundamental value.

speaker: Warsh
text: Similarly, there are some signs of stabilization in the leveraged loan market.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Banks have been able to sell substantial parts of large deals to investors in recent weeks, and some collateralized loan obligations are coming to market.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Issuance of speculative-grade bonds resumed somewhat of late.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Still, the functioning of several markets continues to be strained, a condition which I would expect to continue for awhile.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Consequently, my colleagues and I on the FOMC will continue to assess the effects that these and other developments could have on the prospects for the economy.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We will rely not only upon economic modeling, but also real-time, forward-looking indicators to help inform our policy judgments.

text: The Federal Reserve is by no means the only institution in the United States that is concerned with the stability and functioning of the financial system.

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, the Federal Reserve works closely with a number of other U.S. government agencies on both a bilateral basis and jointly through the President's Working Group on Financial Markets to enhance the integrity, efficiency, orderliness, and competitiveness of financial markets and to maintain investor confidence.

speaker: Warsh

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, in today's tightly integrated international financial markets, fostering financial stability requires a global perspective.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: From the founding of the Federal Reserve to the present, a key question confronts policymakers and market participants alike:  What is financial stability?
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Perhaps it is better to address what it is not.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In my view, financial stability does not demand a state of lessened financial market movements, a state of muted volatility.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: More often than not, financial markets process new information efficiently:  If some unexpected news arrives, markets adjust, sometimes even sharply, and they should.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These types of movements are healthy, even necessary.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: They serve to quickly bring prices in line with underlying fundamentals.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And markets that move quickly and adroitly do not necessarily produce unstable financial conditions.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Nor should those who take up the cause of ensuring financial stability protect individual investors or financial institutions from substantial losses or insolvency.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To the contrary, a healthy and well-functioning financial system will tend to reward well-managed risk-taking and punish imprudence.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I am inclined to interpret the Federal Reserve's interest in promoting financial stability as a desire to foster conditions that favor sustainable growth and stable prices.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In this sense, financial stability concerns may rightly shape policymakers' views about the modal outlook for the economy as well as the risks surrounding this outlook.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial instability may thus be characterized as a situation in which the financial system becomes incapable of efficiently allocating resources at market-clearing prices across the economy.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 5 If financial markets become dysfunctional, financial intermediaries' flexibility may be impaired, and investors may become uncertain about their prospects.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And if this situation were to persist, overall macroeconomic performance could be threatened.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We have access to a wide range of financial and economic data and extensive contacts with market participants.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Particularly in times of financial distress, we must draw on a full range of market indicators.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We also glean important information by virtue of our responsibilities as a banking regulator and payment system operator.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And although such a dashboard of key information is exceedingly useful, it should not be confused with a crystal ball.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: For even if our understanding of the financial markets was somehow perfect, the transmission mechanism between financial markets and the real economy is only partially understood.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Like private market participants, the Federal Reserve is in the business of making policy judgments amid uncertainty and must assess the prospects for the real economy with considerable humility.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh

speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As an example, we monitor corporate credit spreads from bond, loan, and credit derivative markets, and we follow closely the evolution of pricing in mortgage markets.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We also look to the terms by which market participants are willing to lock up funds over various time horizons by reviewing term premiums embedded in financial market prices.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And we constantly revisit investors' willingness to conduct business with financial intermediaries to assess counterparty credit risk.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In this respect, market-based indicators are certainly informative, as are measures of current exposures of financial institutions obtained through the supervisory process.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: No central bank financial market dashboard is complete, however, if it does not give considerable weight to measures of price stability.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh

speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Volume indicators are often particularly useful in assessing market functioning in times of market turmoil.

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh

speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York
