speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: On the basis of our most recent data, it seems that the runoff in outstanding commercial paper may be slowing.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Similarly, there are some signs of stabilization in the leveraged loan market.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Banks have been able to sell substantial parts of large deals to investors in recent weeks, and some collateralized loan obligations are coming to market.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Issuance of speculative-grade bonds resumed somewhat of late.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Still, the functioning of several markets continues to be strained, a condition which I would expect to continue for awhile.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Consequently, my colleagues and I on the FOMC will continue to assess the effects that these and other developments could have on the prospects for the economy.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We will rely not only upon economic modeling, but also real-time, forward-looking indicators to help inform our policy judgments.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The views expressed herein are my own and do not necessarily reflect the views of other members of the Board of Governors or of the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I thank Board staff members James Clouse and Roberto Perli for their valuable contributions to these remarks.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Warsh, Kevin (2007), " Financial Market Developments ," speech delivered at the University at Albany, State University of New York, School of Business, Albany, NY, September 21, www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve is by no means the only institution in the United States that is concerned with the stability and functioning of the financial system.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, the Federal Reserve works closely with a number of other U.S. government agencies on both a bilateral basis and jointly through the President's Working Group on Financial Markets to enhance the integrity, efficiency, orderliness, and competitiveness of financial markets and to maintain investor confidence.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In addition, the Federal Reserve participates in a number of important international groups, such as the Financial Stability Forum, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the Committee on the Global Financial System, and the Committee on Payments and Settlement Systems, to name just a few.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Indeed, in today's tightly integrated international financial markets, fostering financial stability requires a global perspective.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The First Bank of the United States was created in 1791 and lasted until 1811.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Second Bank of the United States operated from 1816 to 1836.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Originally, the preamble to the Federal Reserve Act of 1913 stated that the Federal Reserve System was created "[T]o furnish an elastic currency, to afford means of rediscounting commercial paper, to establish a more effective supervision of banking in the United States, and for other purposes."
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Macroeconomic objectives were explicitly introduced later, with the 1977 amendment of the Federal Reserve Act, which stated, "The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Open Market Committee shall maintain long-run growth of the monetary and credit aggregates commensurate with the economy's long run potential to increase production, so as to promote effectively the goals of maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates."
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We should also recognize that financial instability is symmetric and could arise equally when credit flows too freely or at prices that are too low.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Those were the words used by then-Chairman Alan Greenspan in his comments on the 1998 financial crisis.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Alan Greenspan (2000), " Technology and Financial Services ," speech delivered before the Journal of Financial Services Research and the American Enterprise Institute Conference, in Honor of Anna Schwartz, Washington, DC, April 14, www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents.htm.
speech_title: Financial Stability and the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the New York State Economics Association 60th Annual Conference, Loudonville, New York

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is a pleasure to take part in this event.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I commend our hosts for bringing together such a broad range of participants and for developing an agenda that addresses issues of great significance to the banking community.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: My goal today is to offer a broad perspective of the Federal Reserve's various responsibilities and complementary roles.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The roles of the Federal Reserve may seem somewhat obscure and, to many, even disconnected.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would venture a guess that as bankers, you think first of examiners when you hear "Federal Reserve"--and perhaps do so with a groan.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: But as you know, bank supervision is only one of the Federal Reserve's functions.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In my remarks today, I will speak about some of the Federal Reserve's responsibilities and discuss how they relate to markets, financial institutions, and consumers.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Central Bank and Monetary Policy As the nation's central bank, the Federal Reserve has the unique power in the U.S. financial system to create money, giving it the ability to conduct monetary policy for the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: That power also enables the Federal Reserve to provide liquidity--a capability that is particularly important when the financial system is under stress.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, the Federal Reserve was established in 1913 as a means of addressing the periodic financial panics and accompanying economic downturns that had afflicted the nation at various times.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Congress has given the Federal Reserve specific objectives for the conduct of monetary policy--in particular, to conduct monetary policy in a way that promotes the long-run objectives of maximum sustainable employment and stable prices.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Monetary policy is implemented primarily through open market operations--that is, the purchase and sale of securities in the open market--which gives the Federal Reserve the ability to control short-term interest rates.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) oversees the conduct of open market operations and formulates monetary policy by setting an operating target for the federal funds rate that is judged to be consistent with fostering the Federal Reserve's long-run objectives.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As part and parcel of its pursuit of maximum sustainable employment and stable prices, the Federal Reserve has a broad responsibility to foster financial stability.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I should hasten to add that financial stability does not imply that asset prices will be stable at all times or that investors will be protected from significant losses.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Rather, financial stability is fundamentally about the efficient functioning of financial markets in channeling credit and financial resources to the most productive ends and allowing investors to effectively manage risks.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: During periods of financial distress, the Federal Reserve can promote financial stability by providing liquidity through both open market operations and the discount window.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: It can provide liquidity through open market operations by purchasing assets in the open market in exchange for newly created reserves.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: It can also address the liquidity needs of solvent but temporarily illiquid banks by lending to them through the discount window.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such lending can allow banks to meet payment obligations; to avoid "fire sales" of assets, which can disrupt financial markets; and to continue to lend to customers without tightening terms or credit standards, which can limit economic growth.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is important to note that the ability and willingness of the central bank to provide liquidity may be useful in reducing market uncertainty and bolstering investor confidence, even if the actual amount of liquidity provided turns out to be rather modest.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: For these reasons, the ability to provide liquidity is a critical tool of a central bank.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: This brief overview of the role of the Federal Reserve in fostering financial stability is instructive in considering the policy actions undertaken in response to recent disruptions and strains in financial markets.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve used a range of policy tools--including adjustments in short-term interest rates and the provision of liquidity--during this time of market unrest to counter the potential ill effects on the economy.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: On August 10, the Federal Reserve issued a statement announcing that it was providing liquidity to facilitate the orderly functioning of financial markets and would provide reserves as necessary to promote trading in the federal funds market at rates close to the target rate of 5-1/4 percent.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The announcement also noted that the discount window was available as a source of funding.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: On August 17, the FOMC issued a statement noting that financial market conditions had deteriorated and that tighter credit conditions and increased uncertainty had the potential to dampen economic growth.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The FOMC said that it judged the downside risks to growth to have increased appreciably and stated that it was prepared to act as needed to mitigate adverse effects on the economy arising from the disruptions in financial markets.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the same time, the Board of Governors announced that it had approved a 50 basis point reduction in the primary credit rate at the discount window, to 5-3/4 percent, to promote the restoration of orderly conditions in financial markets.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Given the turbulence in the short-term funding market, the Board also approved a change in the administration of the discount window that would allow the provision of term financing for as long as thirty days, renewable by the borrower.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: And on August 21, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York announced some temporary changes to the terms and conditions of the System Open Market Account securities lending program, including a reduction in the minimum fee, in an effort to facilitate lending of securities by the Fed to address heightened safe-haven demands for Treasury securities.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: These actions appeared helpful in mitigating some of the strains in financial markets, but financial market functioning had not returned to normal by the time of the September FOMC meeting.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: At that time, we judged that a 50 basis point lowering of the target federal funds rate was appropriate to offset the effects of tighter financial conditions on the economic outlook and reduce the risks that a further tightening in credit conditions could impact the housing market and lead to significant broader weakness in output and employment.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Bank Supervision While the Federal Reserve's role in conducting monetary policy and providing liquidity garners a great deal of media attention, its role in bank supervision and regulation is no less important.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve shares responsibility for regulating and supervising the safety and soundness of the U.S. banking system with a number of federal and state government agencies.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve supervises state-chartered banks that are members of the Federal Reserve System, the U.S. operations of foreign banks, and, in some cases, the foreign operations of U.S. banks.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, it is the umbrella supervisor of all bank holding companies and financial holding companies.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Although the banks and nonbank subsidiaries of these entities are often supervised by other agencies, the Federal Reserve coordinates with the primary supervisors in assessing the overall financial condition of the consolidated organization.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The scope of the Federal Reserve's supervisory activities includes regular examinations of depository institutions and inspections of holding companies to assess the safety and soundness of these entities and to ensure that they comply with relevant banking laws and regulations.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, the Federal Reserve contributes to the development of policies regarding banking supervision and regulation, collaborating with the other agencies to issue rules and guidance that help ensure that federally supervised banking entities are adhering to the high prudential standards that are essential to maintain a stable banking system.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve plays an instrumental role in developing policies that affect both domestic and international banking organizations.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: One visible example of such collaboration is the international effort known as Basel I and II that ultimately resulted in a framework that established minimum regulatory capital requirements, increased supervisory attention to banking institutions' capital adequacy and risk-management techniques, and enhanced public disclosure of banking organizations' risk exposures.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: These standards promote safety and soundness and reduce competitive inequi­ties among banking organizations operating within an increasingly global market.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The full range of its supervisory activities gives the Federal Reserve ongoing access to critical information about the banking system that is pertinent to our assessment of the state of the overall economy and has proved highly valuable during the most recent market stress.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: With data on financial institutions' managerial, operational, and risk-management systems, the Federal Reserve has information about the overall condition of the banking institutions it supervises as well as insight into developments in the broader financial markets.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such knowledge allows for a broad and deep understanding of developments in financial markets and financial institutions.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: These supervisory activities provide the Federal Reserve with access to real-time information that facilitates the formulation of policy responses during periods of financial stress.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, we are all well aware that the subprime mortgage market has presented supervisory concerns.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve has collaborated with various agencies to address these concerns, working to overcome challenges presented by the rapid pace of financial innovation and the complex regulatory scheme of the mortgage market.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The federal supervisory agencies first issued guidance on subprime lending in 1999 and expanded it in 2001 to emphasize that lending standards should include well-defined underwriting parameters, such as acceptable loan-to-value and debt-to-income ratios and minimum acceptable credit scores.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Further, it advises institutions actively involved in the securitization and sale of subprime loans to develop contingency plans that include alternate funding sources and measures for raising additional capital if necessary.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As the mortgage industry continued to expand its product offerings, the Federal Reserve and the other federal agencies observed in 2005 that lenders were increasingly offering nontraditional, or "exotic," mortgage loans, which defer the repayment of principal and, sometimes, interest.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of particular concern with these types of loans were the lack of principal amortization and the potential for negative amortization.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, the easing of underwriting standards and the marketing of these products to a wider spectrum of borrowers held the potential to create larger risks.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In 2006, the Federal Reserve and the other banking agencies issued guidance on nontraditional mortgage products to address these concerns.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: This guidance underscores the sound underwriting procedures, portfolio-risk management strategies, and consumer protection practices that institutions should follow to prudently originate and manage nontraditional mortgage loans.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: A major aspect of this guidance is the recommendation that a lender's analysis of repayment capacity include an evaluation of the borrower's ability to repay the debt by final maturity at the fully indexed rate, assuming a fully amortizing repayment schedule.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Continuing concerns about the subprime market led the federal regulators to issue further guidance this year regarding adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs).
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of particular concern were those ARM products that allow for low initial payments based on a fixed introductory rate that expires after a short period and then adjust to a variable rate, plus a margin, for the remaining term of the loan.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: These products may result in payment shock to some borrowers, heightening risks to both lenders and borrowers.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consumer Protection in Financial Services As you can see, the scrutiny of safety and soundness issues in the subprime mortgage market also raised concerns relating to consumer protection--another area of significant responsibility for the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Toward this end, the Federal Reserve has primary rule-writing authority for many consumer protection laws.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: It takes two fundamental approaches to consumer protection: one focuses on the provision of information, and the other involves the development and enforcement of rules against abusive and unfair practices.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I will speak first about the importance of providing consumers with pertinent and accurate information.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Clearly, information is critical to the effective functioning of markets.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: A core principle of economics is that markets are more competitive, and therefore more efficient, when accurate information is available to both consumers and suppliers.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: When information on alternatives is readily available, product offerings must meet customers' demands and offering prices must reflect those of market competitors.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: If consumers are well informed, they are in a better position to make decisions that are in their best interest.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Information helps and empowers individual consumers by improving their ability to compare products and choose those that will help them meet their personal goals, and this informed comparison shopping enhances competition.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result, a significant component of the rule-writing process involves crafting disclosure requirements that provide consumers with consistent and relevant information about the terms and fees of financial products.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve is keenly aware, however, that information alone may not always be sufficient to combat abusive practices--which brings me to the importance of rules and the enforcement of consumer protection measures.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, the consumer financial services laws implemented by the Federal Reserve contain a number of substantive protections, reflecting carefully considered legislative judgments that certain practices should be restricted or prohibited.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Enforcement of these rules is carried out through the Federal Reserve's supervisory oversight for compliance with consumer protection laws and regulations.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As consumer protection issues have emerged in relation to subprime mortgage lending, the Federal Reserve has sought to address concerns by using its various supervisory and rule-writing tools.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In doing so, it is extremely important to strike the right balance by seeking to protect consumers from abusive lending practices without restricting credit from responsible lenders to borrowers with shorter or lower-rated credit histories.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The guidance pieces on subprime and nontraditional mortgages that I mentioned earlier address many issues relating to consumer protection, in addition to safety and soundness.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: We are also undertaking other actions to address concerns related to the flow of information to consumers and enforcement of consumer protections.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: One concern is the need to improve the mortgage information that consumers receive.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As I mentioned earlier, effective disclosure empowers consumers and enhances competition.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: But to be effective, disclosures must give consumers information that they can readily understand at a time when the information is relevant.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I anticipate that to that end, the Federal Reserve will propose improvements to the rules governing the disclosure of mortgage loan terms and conditions and the timing of those disclosures.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: We will soon begin an extensive consumer testing process in order to ensure that the new draft disclosures we propose will be comprehensible and useful to borrowers.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: To further improve consumers' access to meaningful information, the Federal Reserve also plans to propose rule changes to address misleading practices in mortgage loan advertisements and solicitations.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition to providing consumers with better information, the Federal Reserve plans to exercise its rule-making authority under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA) to address unfair or deceptive mortgage lending practices.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: We plan to propose rules by the end of this year that would apply to subprime loans offered by all mortgage lenders.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The practices that may be addressed involve prepayment penalties, stated-income lending, failure to require escrows for taxes and insurance, and making loans without regard to the borrower's ability to repay.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the many Federal Reserve efforts to gather input from a variety of stakeholders, including a full-day hearing I chaired in June that yielded valuable insight from both the industry and consumer groups, these areas have been highlighted as practices for which there is a potential for abuse.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: With respect to supervision of consumer protection in subprime lending, I would like to highlight an important collaboration with other federal and state agencies to expand consumer compliance reviews to include selected non-depository mortgage lenders.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As I mentioned earlier, the regulatory scheme for the mortgage industry has become extremely complex as the breadth and depth of this market has grown over the past decade and the role of nonbank mortgage lenders, particularly in the subprime market, has increased.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: In fact, data collected under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act show that independent mortgage companies--those that are not depository institutions, subsidiaries of depository institutions, or holding company affiliates--made about 46 percent of higher-priced first-lien mortgages in 2006.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: 1 In addition, there has been an increased presence of mortgage brokers, often independent entities who take loan applications and shop them to depository institutions or other lenders.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The increased fragmentation of the mortgage process, from marketing of products to servicing of loans after origination, has created a number of challenges in monitoring practices of various nonbank market players.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: These market developments have resulted in the oversight of mortgage lending extending beyond the federal banking agencies, and this underscores the importance of collaborating with the state banking agencies and other organizations to address concerns in the subprime mortgage market.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Various outreach and research efforts have revealed the value of increasing the scrutiny of these lenders, to deepen our understanding of their policies and practices.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: To this end--and to take advantage of the dual-supervisory roles of federal and state agencies--we have launched a cooperative pilot project to conduct reviews of non-depository lenders with significant subprime mortgage operations.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The reviews will evaluate the companies' underwriting standards and senior-management oversight of risk-management strategies for ensuring compliance with consumer protection laws and regulations.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our partners in this initiative are the Office of Thrift Supervision, the Federal Trade Commission, and state agencies represented by the Conference of State Banking Supervisors (CSBS) and the American Association of Residential Mortgage Regulators.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: As part of this project, the Federal Reserve will review nonbank subsidiaries of bank holding companies for compliance with a number of regulations, including TILA, HOEPA, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act, and the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The other partners in the project will conduct similar reviews of non-depository subsidiaries of thrift holding companies, independent mortgage lending companies, and mortgage brokers doing business with these entities.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The partner agencies intend to share information about their findings with each other, review the lessons learned, and seek additional ways to cooperate to ensure effective and consistent supervision of these entities.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the conclusion of the reviews, the agencies will analyze the results and determine whether to continue the project and, if so, how to focus future reviews.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Finally, I would like to say a few words about what the Federal Reserve is doing to help borrowers who may be facing difficulty paying their mortgages.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Undoubtedly, foreclosures can have a devastating impact on borrowers, lenders, families, and communities.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: To the extent possible, efforts should be made to avoid foreclosure.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Toward that end, the Federal Reserve along with the other agencies have encouraged lenders and servicers to identify opportunities to work with borrowers confronting mortgage delinquency or foreclosure.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, lenders and servicers may be able to assist troubled borrowers by modifying the loan, deferring payments, extending the loan maturities, converting an adjustable-rate mortgage to a fixed-rate or fully-indexed loan, or capitalizing delinquent amounts.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The best outcome is a loss mitigation strategy that results in a mortgage obligation that the borrower can meet in a sustained manner.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: The use of these and other loss mitigation techniques is consistent with guidance that emphasizes the importance of prudent underwriting practices to help ensure that borrowers can meet the terms of their mortgage obligation and maintain homeownership.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusion In closing, I would like to reiterate that the Federal Reserve is committed to using its broad range of policy and supervisory tools to support efficient and fair markets.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I have touched on the ways the Federal Reserve has used some of its tools and described the various efforts we have under way.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve
speech_venue: At the National Bankers Association 80th Annual Convention, Durham, North Carolina

speaker: Kroszner
text: I assure you that the Federal Reserve will continue to use these tools, as well as to examine various other authorities, to respond in a deliberative and balanced manner that is in the interests of markets, financial institutions, and consumers.
speech_title: Markets, Financial Institutions, and Consumers: The Roles of the Federal Reserve

speaker: Bernanke
text: It is a privilege for me to open this conference dedicated to our colleague and friend, John Taylor.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: John's influence on monetary theory and policy has been profound indeed.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: That influence has been manifest in undergraduate lecture halls and graduate seminar rooms, in the best research journals, and in the highest ranks of government.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: His ability to crystallize important analytical insights and apply them to policy issues is unsurpassed.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, in a speech a few years ago, I noted three concepts named after John that are central to understanding our macroeconomic experience of the past three decades--the Taylor curve, the Taylor rule, and the Taylor principle (Bernanke, 2004).
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: I'd like to take a few minutes to review John's career and impressive body of work.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: After receiving his Ph.D. from Stanford nearly thirty-five years ago, John began his career as an assistant professor at Columbia University.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even in those early years, John revealed his interest in applying the analytical tools of economics to practical policy issues.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: He took a leave of absence from academia in 1976-77 to serve on the staff of the Council of Economic Advisers.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: I suspect that the circumstances of the mid-1970s intensified John's motivation to help improve economic performance through sound policymaking.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: During the late 1970s and early 1980s, John published a number of highly influential papers, including: "Conditions for Unique Solutions in Stochastic Macroeconomic Models with Rational Expectations," "Estimation and Control of a Macroeconomic Model with Rational Expectations," "Aggregate Dynamics and Staggered Contracts," and "Solution and Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Dynamic Nonlinear Rational Expectations Models."
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: (As you can tell, John has always had a penchant for catchy titles.)
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Beyond its important technical contributions, this work showed that the insights and methods of the rational expectations revolution could be applied to models with sticky wages and prices.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: That observation has proved enormously influential in subsequent policy research.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The rational expectations revolution helped to kill the idea of a long-run tradeoff between the levels of inflation and unemployment.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, John's analysis showed that, in the presence of aggregate supply shocks, attempts by monetary policymakers to reduce the volatility of inflation over time could be associated with higher volatility in unemployment, and vice versa.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: John's visual depiction of this policy tradeoff has come to be known as the Taylor curve.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Interestingly, John's work anticipated the possibility that improvements in the conduct of monetary policy or changes in the structure of the economy could result in a shift of the Taylor curve--that is, a change in the ability of policy to smooth both inflation and employment.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: And indeed, what economists have dubbed the Great Moderation--a simultaneous reduction in the volatility of inflation and the volatility of real economic activity--has occurred in the United States and in many other economies over the past quarter-century.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Over the course of the 1980s, John continued his work on rational expectations issues and monetary policy and macroeconomics more generally.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: He also began to broaden his focus to matters of international economics.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: He developed a multi-country rational expectations econometric model--a truly ambitious undertaking, especially in light of the limited computing capabilities of the era.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: By this point in his career, John had firmly established his reputation as a leader in the profession.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 1989, John became a member of the first President Bush's Council of Economic Advisers.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: During the next four years, he played a key role in shaping the Administration's positions on macroeconomic, fiscal, international finance, and trade issues.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The U.S. economy was entering a difficult period at that point.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Among other problems, significant pressures on bank balance sheets were beginning to emerge that would damp economic growth for the next several years.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: While dealing with the serious economic issues of the time, John and the other members of the Council simultaneously produced an impressive manifesto for policymaking.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: They developed a rules-based approach to the conduct of monetary and fiscal policy and published it in 1990 in the Economic Report of the President .
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: That essay laid the foundation for what is perhaps John's most well-known contribution to economics--the simple description of the determinants of monetary policy that eventually became known as the Taylor rule.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 John's analysis triggered an avalanche of studies examining the stabilization properties of Taylor rules in the context of macroeconomic models.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Other work investigated the ability of variants of the Taylor rule to describe empirically the actual course of monetary policy in the United States and in other economies.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Taylor rule also embeds a basic principle of sound monetary policy that has subsequently been referred to as the Taylor principle.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 According to this principle, when a shock causes a shift in the inflation rate, the central bank must adjust the nominal interest rate by more than one-for-one.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: This ensures that the real interest rate moves in the right direction to restore price stability.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Taylor principle provides essential guidance for central banks on how to anchor long-run inflation expectations and foster stable growth and low inflation.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Ever since its inception, John has emphasized that the Taylor rule should not be applied mechanistically.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The world is far too complicated for that.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: But he has argued that such rules can serve as useful benchmarks for the practical conduct of monetary policy.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In fact, policymakers at the Federal Reserve and many other central banks do routinely consult various policy rules as they make judgments on the appropriate stance of monetary policy.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: After a decade back at Stanford, John was called again to Washington by President Bush--this time the current President Bush.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: He served as Under Secretary for International Affairs at the U.S. Treasury from 2001 through 2005.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our economy faced severe challenges during that period--the terrorist attacks of September 11, a recession and the threat of deflation, corporate governance scandals, and economic issues posed by the conflicts in Afghanistan and Iraq.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Suffice it to say, John earned his stripes as the leader of the "Global Financial Warriors."
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As detailed in his book of the same title, John worked extensively on the financial reconstruction of Iraq and on the development of financial tools for fighting terrorism.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury Department recognized his efforts in 2004 with its Distinguished Service Award and in 2005 with the Alexander Hamilton Award for leadership in international finance.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: After his stint at Treasury, John returned once again to the less tumultuous life of a professor, ensconced in his offices at Stanford University and the Hoover Institution.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: I'm sure that, in between teaching and guiding the work of graduate students, he will continue to offer insightful commentary on monetary policy and other economic issues.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: And doubtless he will also continue to do pathbreaking research.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, with our appetites whetted by the Taylor rule, principle, and curve, we now look forward to the Taylor dictum, the Taylor hyperbola, and maybe even the Taylor conundrum.
speech_title: Opening remarks
speech_venue: To the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas(via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
