speaker: Kohn
text: The Role of Simple Rules in Monetary Policymaking It is a pleasure and an honor to speak at this conference honoring John Taylor and his contributions to monetary theory and policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: As you have already heard from Chairman Bernanke and the other speakers today, John has made a number of seminal contributions to the field of macroeconomics.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: What has distinguished John's work, in my view, is that he takes policymaking in the real world seriously.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Taking policymaking seriously involves understanding the constraints imposed on our decisions by partial information and incomplete knowledge of economic relationships.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: It also implies the use of empirically valid models that acknowledge the efforts of households and businesses to anticipate the future and maximize their welfare over time.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In the late 1980s and early 1990s, macroeconomics was focused mainly on real business cycles and endogenous growth theory.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: During this period, John was one of a very small number of academic economists who continued to pursue research aimed at informing the conduct of monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: John's Carnegie Rochester conference paper published in 1993 is an excellent example of this research.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Importantly, John's legacy to the Federal Reserve has not been confined to enhancing our understanding of monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, he has turned out legions of students who have followed in his footsteps in their interest in policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Many of them have spent time in the Federal Reserve, producing a rich array of contributions to policymaking and research.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: John and I have spent countless hours discussing how the Federal Reserve arrives at decisions about monetary policy and how it should arrive at decisions.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Those conversations began in earnest in the late 1980s, when John was on the Council of Economic Advisers, and they have continued to the present day.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: They have occurred not only in offices and classrooms in Washington and Stanford and at numerous conferences around the globe, but also around dinner tables in Washington and Palo Alto and on hiking trails from Vermont to Wyoming.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Those conversations made me a better policy adviser and then policymaker, and they have had the added and very special bonus of allowing Gail and me to count John and Allyn among our friends.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: I can't think of a better way to honor John's contributions than to continue that discussion around the dinner tables of Dallas by reflecting on the role of simple rules in informing policymaking.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Three Benefits of Simple Rules in Monetary Policymaking In his Carnegie Rochester conference paper, John considered a simple policy rule under which the nominal federal funds rate is adjusted in response to both the gap between real and trend gross domestic product (GDP) and the gap between the inflation rate and policymakers' target.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Based on data for the previous few years, John calibrated the long-run target for inflation and the two parameters that determine the responsiveness of the federal funds rate to the two gaps.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The equilibrium real interest rate was based on a longer history of actual real interest rates.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In the handout, Figure 1A depicts the actual nominal funds rate and the Taylor rule prescriptions between 1987 and 1992, as presented in John's paper.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Despite its simplicity, this policy rule fits the data remarkably well; it described a period of generally successful policymaking; and it adhered to the Taylor principle of adjusting the nominal rate more than one-for-one with changes in the inflation rate, so it provided a plausible template for future success.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: It is no wonder that John has been such a dedicated salesman and that his efforts have been so well received in academia and policy councils.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Following John's seminal contribution, many other economists have engaged in research on similar policy rules and, together with John, have identified several benefits of such rules in conducting monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: I will elaborate on three of them.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The first benefit of looking at a simple rule like John's is that it can provide a useful benchmark for policymakers.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: It relates policy setting systematically to the state of the economy in a way that, over time, will produce reasonably good outcomes on average.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Importantly, the emphasis is on levels and gaps, not growth rates, as inputs to the policy process.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: This emphasis can be a problem when a level, say of potential GDP, is in question, but in many respects it is also a virtue.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: For the United States, the two gaps relate directly to the legislative mandate of the Federal Reserve to achieve stable prices and maximum employment.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, those two gaps fit directly into most modern macroeconomic theories, which tell us something about their relationship and how that relationship can be affected by the type of shock hitting the economy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Model uncertainties make the simplicity of the rule particularly important for the policymaker because research suggests that the prescriptions from simple rules can be more robust than optimal-control policies.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Optimal-control policies can depend critically on the exact specification of the model, and clearly there is no consensus about which model best describes the U.S. economy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Federal Reserve policymakers are shown several versions of Taylor rules in the material we receive before each meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: I always look at those charts and tables and ask myself whether I am comfortable with any significant deviation of my policy prescription from those of the rules.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: A second benefit of simple rules is that they help financial market participants form a baseline for expectations regarding the future course of monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Even if the actual policy process is far more sophisticated than any simple rule could completely describe, the rule often provides a reasonably good approximation of what policymakers decide and a framework for thinking about policy actions.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, many financial market participants have used the Taylor rule to understand U.S. monetary policy over the past fifteen years.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Investors and other market participants are going to form expectations about policy and act on those expectations.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The more accurate and informed those expectations are, the more likely are their actions to reinforce the intended effects of policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: A third benefit is that simple rules can be helpful in the central bank's communication with the general public.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Such an understanding is important for the transmission mechanism of monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Giving the public some sense of how the central bank sees the output and inflation gaps and how they are expected to evolve will help it understand the central bank's objectives and how policymakers are likely to respond to surprises in incoming data.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Four Limitations of Simple Rules Simple rules have limitations, of course, as benchmarks for monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: To quote from John's Carnegie Rochester paper, "a policy rule can be implemented and operated more informally by policymakers who recognize the general instrument responses that underlie the policy rule, but who also recognize that operating the rule requires judgment and cannot be done by computer" (p. 198).
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In that context, four limitations of simple rules are important.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The first limitation is that the use of a Taylor rule requires that a single measure of inflation be used to obtain the rule prescriptions.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The price index used by John in the Carnegie Rochester paper was the GDP price deflator.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Other researchers have used the inflation measure based on the consumer price index (CPI).
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Over the past fifteen years, the Federal Reserve has emphasized the inflation rate as measured by changes in the price index for personal consumption expenditures (PCE).
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Many researchers have also explored the use of core price indexes, which exclude the volatile food and energy components, as better predictors of future inflation or as more robust indicators of the sticky prices that some theories say should be the targets of policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, over long periods, most of these measures behave very similarly.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: But policy is made in the here and now, and the various indexes can diverge significantly for long stretches, potentially providing different signals for the appropriate course of monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, the implementation of the Taylor rule and other related rules requires determining the level of the equilibrium real interest rate and the level of potential output; neither of them are observable variables, and both must be inferred from other information.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: John used   2 percent as a rough guess as to the real federal funds rate that would be consistent with the economy producing at its potential.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: But the equilibrium level of the real federal funds rate probably varies over time because it depends on factors such as the growth rate of potential output, fiscal policy, and the willingness of savers to supply credit to households and businesses.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Inaccurate estimates of this rate will mislead policymakers about the policy stance required to achieve full employment.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In a similar vein, real-time estimates of potential output can be derived in a number of ways and--as shown by Orphanides (2003) and others--they are subject to large and persistent errors.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: If policymakers inadvertently rely on flawed estimates, they will encounter persistent problems in achieving their inflation objective.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The third limitation of using simple rules for monetary policymaking stems from the fact that, by their nature, simple rules involve only a small number of variables.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the state of a complex economy like that of the United States cannot be fully captured by any small set of summary statistics.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, policy is best made looking forward, that is, on the basis of projections of how inflation and economic activity may evolve.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Lagged or current values of the small set of variables used in a given simple rule may not provide a sufficient guide to future economic developments, especially in periods of rapid or unusual change.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: For these reasons, central banks monitor a wide range of indicators in conducting monetary policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In his Carnegie Rochester paper, John mentioned the stock market crash of October 1987 as an example of how other variables can and should influence the course of monetary policy in some situations.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The final limitation I want to highlight is that simple policy rules may not capture risk-management considerations.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In some circumstances, the risks to the outlook or the perceived costs of missing an objective on a particular side may be sufficiently skewed that policymakers will choose to respond by adjusting policy in a way that would not be justified solely by the current state of the economy or the modal outlook for output and inflation gaps.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Policy Rules around 2003 Some of the ambiguities and potential pitfalls in the use of simple policy rules are highlighted by considering their prescriptions for a period earlier in this decade.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Turning to Figure 1B , the solid line indicates the actual federal funds rate between the first quarter of 1993 and the second quarter of 2007, and the dashed line shows the prescriptions of the Taylor rule using the same methodology that John used in his Jackson Hole remarks this year.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: 2 For the earlier part of the sample, the prescription from this simple rule tracks the actual funds rate relatively well.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: As John pointed out, a notable deviation happened beginning in 2002, and I would like to discuss that period to illustrate the limitations I noted earlier.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Inflation Measure The first limitation is related to the measure used for the inflation variable included in the rules.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The rule prescriptions depicted by the dashed line in Figure 1B are based on the headline CPI.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: But as you know, the FOMC often looks at core inflation, stripping out the effects of energy and food prices, as a better indicator of future price behavior.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The dotted line represents the rule prescriptions based on the chain-weighted core CPI, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics has produced since 2000.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Using this measure lowers the prescribed funds rate by about 2 percentage points during 2003, bringing the rule prescriptions much closer to the actual path of policy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The reason for the improvement is evident from Figure 2A , on the other side of the handout:  Even though the headline and core CPI measures were broadly similar in the mid- to late 1990s, these measures diverged substantially between 2003 and 2005.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Potential Output The second limitation relates to the challenge of judging the level of potential output in real time.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: To illustrate this point, Figure 2B plots three measures of the output gap.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: The solid line is the real-time estimate by the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) that was used in the Taylor rule prescriptions in Figure 1B, while the dashed line depicts the CBO's ex post estimate of the output gap as of the third quarter of 2007.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Back in 2003, the CBO estimated that output at that time was below potential by only 1 percent.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: With the benefit of four more years of data, the CBO currently estimates that the output gap for the first half of 2003 was considerably wider--about 3 percent.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the dotted line represents an alternative measure of resource utilization derived from the unemployment rate and an estimate of the natural rate of unemployment (NAIRU) taken from the Board staff's FRB/US model.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: In fact, the unemployment rate was rising through the middle of 2003, so the FOMC had every reason to believe that the output gap was widening at that time.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Using this unemployment-based measure rather than the real-time CBO measure would reduce the prescriptions of simple policy rules by roughly 1/2 percentage point in early 2003.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn
text: Other Variables The third limitation in my list was that the small set of economic measures included in simple rules may not fully reflect the state of the economy.
speech_title: John Taylor Rules
speech_venue: At the Conference on John Taylor's Contributions to Monetary Theory and Policy, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Dallas, Texas

speaker: Kohn

speech_title: John Taylor Rules

speaker: Bernanke
text: The past several months have been an eventful period for the U.S. economy.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In financial markets, sharpened concerns about credit quality induced a retrenchment by investors, leading in some cases to significant deterioration in market functioning.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: For some households and firms, credit became harder to obtain and, for those who could obtain it, more costly.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Tightening credit conditions in turn threatened to intensify the ongoing correction in the housing market and to restrain economic growth.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In response to these developments, the Federal Reserve has taken a number of measures to help ensure the normal functioning of financial markets and to promote sustainable economic growth and price stability.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In my remarks this evening I will review recent events, discuss the Federal Reserve's responses to those events, and conclude with some comments on the economic outlook in light of recent developments.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although financial markets around the world have come under pressure in the past few months, I will focus my comments primarily on the United States.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will also have little to say this evening about the serious implications of rising rates of mortgage delinquency and foreclosure for troubled borrowers and their communities or about the Federal Reserve's responses to these important problems; I have discussed these issues several times in the past and will return to them in the future.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Origins and Evolution of the Financial Turmoil Overall, U.S. economic performance so far this year has been reasonably good.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The rate of economic expansion slowed somewhat in late 2006 and early 2007, but growth in the second quarter was solid and some of that momentum appears to have carried over into the third quarter.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The pace of private-sector job creation has slowed this year, but the unemployment rate has moved up only a little from its recent lows.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: And, although energy prices have been volatile, indicators of the underlying inflation trend, such as core inflation, have moderated since the middle of last year.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moderate growth in overall economic activity has continued despite a notable contraction in the housing sector that began in the second half of 2005.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The housing correction has intensified this year as demand has declined further, inventories of unsold new homes have climbed relative to sales, and house prices have decelerated, with some areas of the country experiencing outright declines in home values.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In response to weak demand and bloated inventories, homebuilders have sharply curtailed new construction.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The decline in residential investment directly subtracted about 3/4 percentage point from the average pace of U.S. economic growth over the past year and a half.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In its regular reports to Congress, most recently in July, the Federal Reserve Board has highlighted as a downside risk the possibility that housing weakness might spill over to other parts of the economy--for example, by acting as a restraint on consumer spending.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus far, however, direct evidence of such spillovers onto the broader economy has been limited.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The housing correction has taken a more visible toll on the financial markets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, since early this year, investors have become increasingly concerned about the credit quality of mortgages, especially subprime mortgages.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The rate of serious delinquencies has risen notably for subprime mortgages with adjustable rates, reaching nearly 16 percent in August, roughly triple the recent low in mid-2005.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 Subprime mortgages originated in late 2005 and 2006 have performed especially poorly, in part because of a deterioration in underwriting standards.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, many recent-vintage subprime loans will experience their first interest-rate resets in coming quarters.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: With the softness in house prices likely to make refinancing more difficult, delinquencies on these mortgages are expected to rise further.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: At one time, most mortgages were originated by depository institutions and held on their balance sheets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Today, however, mortgages are often bundled together into mortgage-backed securities or structured credit products, rated by credit rating agencies, and then sold to investors.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As mortgage losses have mounted, investors have questioned the reliability of the credit ratings, especially those of structured products.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since many investors had not performed independent evaluations of these often-complex instruments, the loss of confidence in the credit ratings led to a sharp decline in the willingness of investors to purchase these products.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Liquidity dried up, prices fell, and spreads widened.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since July, few securities backed by subprime mortgages have been issued.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors' reluctance to buy has not been confined to securities related to subprime mortgages.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, the secondary market for private-label securities backed by prime jumbo mortgages has also contracted, and issuance of such securities has dwindled.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 Even though default rates on such mortgages have remained very low, the experience with subprime mortgages has evidently made investors more sensitive to the risks associated with other housing-related assets as well.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The problems in the mortgage-related sector reverberated throughout the financial system and particularly in the market for asset-backed commercial paper (ABCP).
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this market, various institutions have established special-purpose vehicles to issue commercial paper to help fund a variety of assets, including some private-label mortgage-backed securities, mortgages warehoused for securitization, and other long-maturity assets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors had typically viewed the commercial paper backed by these assets as quite safe and liquid, because of the quality of the collateral and because the paper is often supported by banks' commitments to provide lines of credit or to assume some credit risk.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the concerns about mortgage-backed securities and structured credit products (even those unrelated to mortgages) greatly reduced the willingness of investors to roll over ABCP, particularly at maturities of more than a few days.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The problems intensified in the second week of August after the announcement by a large overseas bank that it could not value the ABCP held by some of its money funds and was, as a result, suspending redemptions from those funds.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some commercial paper issuers invoked their right to extend the maturity of their paper, and a few issuers defaulted.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In response to the heightening of perceived risks, investors fled to the safety and liquidity of Treasury bills, sparking a plunge in bill rates and a sharp widening in spreads on ABCP.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The retreat by investors from structured investment products also affected business finance.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, issuance of collateralized loan obligations (CLOs) and collateralized debt obligations (CDOs), which in turn had been major buyers of leveraged syndicated loans, fell off significantly during the summer.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Demand for leveraged loans slowed sharply, reducing credit access for private equity firms and other borrowers seeking to finance leveraged buyouts (LBOs).
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Concerns about liquidity and credit risk surfaced even in markets in which securitization plays a much smaller role.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, spreads on lower-tier unsecured commercial paper jumped and issuance was limited to very short maturities.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In corporate bond markets, issuance of speculative-grade bonds dropped off sharply as risk spreads widened.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: And although equity prices have moved up on balance since late spring, swings in prices have been large; indeed, the expected stock-price volatilities implicit in options prices roughly doubled during the summer before falling back more recently.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the strains in financial markets intensified, many of the largest banks became concerned about the possibility that they might face large draws on their liquidity and difficult-to-forecast expansions of their balance sheets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: They recognized that they might have to provide backup funding to programs that were no longer able to issue ABCP.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, in the absence of an active syndication market for the leveraged loans they had committed to underwrite and without a well-functioning securitization market for the nonconforming mortgages they had issued, many large banks might be forced to hold those assets on their books rather than sell them to investors as planned.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In these circumstances of heightened volatility and diminished market functioning, banks also became more concerned about the possible risk exposures of their counterparties and other potential contingent liabilities.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These concerns prompted banks to become protective of their liquidity and balance sheet capacity and thus to become markedly less willing to provide funding to others, including other banks.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result, both overnight and term interbank funding markets came under considerable pressure.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Interbank lending rates rose notably, and the liquidity in these markets diminished.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: A number of the U.S. ABCP programs that had difficulty rolling over paper were sponsored by or had backup funding arrangements with European banks.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result, some of these banks faced potentially large needs for dollar funding, and their efforts to manage their liquidity likely contributed to the pressures in global money and foreign exchange swap markets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The U.S. subprime mortgage market is small relative to the enormous scale of global financial markets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: So why was the impact of subprime developments on the markets apparently so large?
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To some extent, the outsized effects of the subprime mortgage problems on financial markets may have reflected broader concerns that problems in the U.S. housing market might restrain overall economic growth.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the developments in subprime were perhaps more a trigger than a fundamental cause of the financial turmoil.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The episode led investors to become more uncertain about valuations of a range of complex or opaque structured credit products, not just those backed by subprime mortgages.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: They also reacted to market developments by increasing their assessment of the risks associated with a number of assets and, to some degree, by reducing their willingness to take on risk more generally.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be sure, these developments may well lead to a healthier financial system in the medium to long term:  Increased investor scrutiny of structured credit products is likely to lead to greater transparency in these products and more rigor in the credit-rating process.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: And greater caution on the part of investors seems appropriate given the very narrow spreads and the loosening in some underwriting standards seen before the recent episode began.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the shorter term, however, these developments do imply a greater measure of financial restraint on economic growth as credit becomes more expensive and difficult to obtain.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's Response to the Financial Turmoil Fortunately, the financial system entered the episode of the past few months with strong capital positions and a robust infrastructure.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The banking system is healthy.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Despite a few notable failures, hedge funds overall seem to have held up well, and their counterparties have not sustained material losses.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The clearing and settlement infrastructure generally worked well despite trading volumes that were extremely high in some cases.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nevertheless, the market strains were serious, as I have discussed, and they posed risks to the broader economy.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve accordingly took a number of steps to help markets return to more orderly functioning.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's initial action was to increase liquidity in short-term money markets through larger open market operations--the standard means by which it seeks to ensure that the federal funds rate stays at or near the target rate set by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: A number of other central banks took similar steps.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: One source of pressure in the overnight market was the demand for dollar funding by European banks to which I alluded earlier.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As Europe is in the latter part of its trading day when U.S. markets open, this extra demand for dollars at times led the federal funds rate to open well above the target.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The extra provision of liquidity by the Fed helped counter the resulting pressure on the funds rate early in the day; it also eased banks' concerns about the availability of funding and thus assisted the functioning of the interbank market.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be clear, an open market operation can provide market participants with increased liquidity; but the intervention does not directly increase participants' capital or allow them to shed risk.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In essence, these operations are short-term loans collateralized by government securities.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, whereas open market operations typically involve lending against government securities, loans through the discount window can be made against a much wider range of collateral, including mortgages and mortgage-backed securities.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nonetheless, the availability of the discount window is potentially significant for banks, as it gives them greater confidence that they can obtain additional liquidity as necessary.

text: The Federal Reserve also took some other steps in response to strains in financial markets, including reducing the fee that it charges for lending Treasury securities from its portfolio, thus helping to meet the heavy demands in the market for those securities.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Promoting financial stability and the orderly functioning of financial markets is a key function of central banks.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, a principal motivation for the founding of the Federal Reserve nearly a century ago was the expectation that it would reduce the incidence of financial crises by providing liquidity as needed.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In its supervisory role, the Federal Reserve--like other bank regulators--attempts to ensure that individual banks maintain adequate liquidity on hand and make provision to raise additional funds quickly when the need arises.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We must be wary of a subtle fallacy of composition, however.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even if each market participant holds a significant reserve of what--in normal times, at least--would be considered highly liquid assets, for the system as a whole the only truly liquid assets are cash and its equivalents.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The quantity of cash assets in the system at a point in time is, in turn, essentially fixed, being determined directly or indirectly by the central bank.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, whenever an investor sells less liquid assets to raise cash, the cash holdings of other market participants are reduced by an equal amount.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consequently, in highly stressed financial conditions, when the marketwide demand for liquidity rises sharply, one of two things must happen:  Either the central bank provides the liquidity demanded by lending against good collateral, or forced sales of illiquid assets will drive the prices of those assets well below their longer-term fundamental values, raising the risk of widespread insolvency and intensifying the crisis.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: In his classic 1873 treatise, Lombard Street , Walter Bagehot famously articulated the need for central banks to be prepared to lend freely against good collateral (what he called "good banking security") but at a penalty rate.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 A panic, said Bagehot, is a "species of neuralgia" and as such must not be starved (p. 25).

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: Of course, judgment is required to assess whether a particular set of market conditions is severe enough to warrant extraordinary injections of liquidity by the central bank; a too-aggressive intervention could unduly reduce the incentives of market participants to insure against more-normal liquidity risks.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the steps it took, the Federal Reserve strove to reach a middle ground, signaling its willingness and ability to provide liquidity to markets as needed without significantly distorting the incentives of individual banks and other market participants to manage their liquidity prudently.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's efforts to provide liquidity appear to have been helpful on the whole.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be sure, the volume of loans to banks made through the discount window, though it increased for a time, has been modest.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: However, collateral placed by banks at the discount window in anticipation of possible borrowing rose sharply during August and September, suggesting that some banks viewed the discount window as a potentially valuable option.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke

speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These underlying difficulties will be resolved only over time by financial markets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since mid-August the functioning of financial markets has improved to some degree, supported not only by liquidity provision but also by the monetary policy action taken in September, to which I will return in a moment.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, of course, the Federal Reserve can adjust the stance of monetary policy by changing its target for the federal funds rate.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The FOMC manages monetary policy to further its dual mandate to promote maximum sustainable employment and price stability.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: However, to allow time to gather and evaluate incoming information, possible policy action was deferred until the Committee's next regularly scheduled meeting on September 18.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: They agreed that significant spillovers to household and business spending were not yet evident.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: For example, auto sales had picked up in August from the low levels of earlier in the summer; and business investment did not appear to have been seriously affected by financial market developments, as highly rated firms continued to enjoy good access to credit.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Strong growth abroad was also viewed as supporting U.S. exports and domestic production.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: And as I have noted, the available evidence suggested that overall economic growth in the third quarter remained moderate.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, downside risks to both household and business spending had clearly increased over the period since the Committee's previous meeting.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, the weak housing market, somewhat downbeat consumer sentiment, and slower growth in private-sector employment increased the likelihood that consumption spending would slow in coming quarters.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Participants at the September meeting also reported somewhat greater caution in the outlooks of their business contacts.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Financial market conditions were expected to improve slowly at best; and even if conditions began to normalize, credit would likely remain noticeably tighter for many borrowers than had been the case during the summer.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Furthermore, any weakening in the economy could itself have a negative effect on still-fragile credit markets, possibly leading credit conditions to tighten further.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Regarding the other half of its mandate, to promote price stability, the Committee noted some improvement over the past year in measures of the trend component of inflation, such as core inflation.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But inflation risks remained, including still-high levels of resource utilization and elevated prices for oil and other commodities.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: The Committee agreed that continued close attention to inflation developments was warranted.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Overall, given the great difficulty of knowing how financial conditions would evolve or the extent of their effect on the economy, Committee members judged the level of uncertainty in the outlook to be unusually high.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, the Committee chose to cut its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points at the September meeting.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This action was intended to help offset the tightening of credit conditions resulting from the financial turmoil.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Risk-management considerations also played a role in the decision, given the possibility that the housing correction and tighter credit could presage a broader weakening in economic conditions that would be difficult to arrest.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: By doing more sooner, policy might be able to forestall some part of the potential adverse effects of the disruptions in financial markets.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As most of the meeting participants saw growth likely to run below trend for a while and with the incoming inflation data on the favorable side, the risks to inflation from this action seemed acceptable, especially as the Committee was prepared to reverse the policy easing if inflation pressures proved stronger than expected.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since the September meeting, the incoming data have borne out the Committee's expectations of further weakening in the housing market, as sales have fallen further and new residential construction has continued to decline rapidly.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The further contraction in housing is likely to be a significant drag on growth in the current quarter and through early next year.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, overall, the limited data that we have received since the September FOMC meeting are consistent with continued moderate increases in consumer prices.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the Committee noted in its post-meeting statement, we will continue to monitor inflation developments carefully.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: It does seem that, together with our earlier actions to enhance liquidity, the September policy action has served to reduce some of the pressure in financial markets, although considerable strains remain.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: From the perspective of the near-term economic outlook, the improved functioning of financial markets is a positive development in that it increases the likelihood of achieving moderate growth with price stability.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, in such situations, one must also take seriously the possibility that policy actions that have the effect of reducing stress in financial markets may also promote excessive risk-taking and thus increase the probability of future crises.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As I indicated in earlier remarks, it is not the responsibility of the Federal Reserve--nor would it be appropriate--to protect lenders and investors from the consequences of their financial decisions.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But developments in financial markets can have broad economic effects felt by many outside the markets, and the Federal Reserve must take those effects into account when determining policy.
speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, as I have emphasized, the Federal Reserve has a mandate from the Congress to promote maximum employment and stable prices, and its monetary policy actions will be chosen so as to best meet that mandate.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, although the Federal Reserve can seek to provide a more stable economic background that will benefit both investors and non-investors, the truth is that it can hardly insulate investors from risk, even if it wished to do so.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Developments over the past few months reinforce this point.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, market participants are learning and adjusting--for example, by insisting on better mortgage underwriting and by performing better due diligence on structured credit products.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Rather than becoming more crisis-prone, the financial system is likely to emerge from this episode healthier and more stable than before.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion I have sought this evening to put recent financial market developments in context and to explain the thinking behind the steps taken by the Federal Reserve.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This has been a challenging period.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

text: Conditions in financial markets have shown some improvement since the worst of the storm in mid-August, but a full recovery of market functioning is likely to take time, and we may well see some setbacks.

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York
