speech_title: The Recent Financial Turmoil and its Economic and Policy Consequences
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Bill Poole's career in the Federal Reserve System spans two decades separated by a quarter of a century.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: From 1964 to 1974 Bill was an economist on the staff of the Board's Division of Research and Statistics.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: He then left to join the economics faculty at Brown University, where he stayed for nearly twenty-five years.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Bill rejoined the Fed in 1998 as president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, so he is now approaching the completion of his second decade in the System.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As it happens, each of Bill's two decades in the System was a time of considerable research and analysis on the issue of how economic uncertainty affects the making of monetary policy, a topic on which Bill has written and spoken many times.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: I would like to compare the state of knowledge on this topic during Bill's first decade in the System with what we have learned during his most recent decade of service.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The exercise is interesting in its own right and has the added benefit of giving me the opportunity to highlight Bill's seminal contributions in this line of research.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Developments during the First Period: 1964-74 In 1964, when Bill began his first stint in the Federal Reserve System, policymakers and researchers were becoming increasingly confident in the ability of monetary and fiscal policy to smooth the business cycle.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: From the traditional Keynesian perspective, which was the dominant viewpoint of the time, monetary policy faced a long-term tradeoff between inflation and unemployment that it could exploit to keep unemployment low over an indefinitely long period at an acceptable cost in terms of inflation.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, improvements in econometric modeling and the importation of optimal-control methods from engineering were seen as having the potential to tame the business cycle.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Of course, the prevailing optimism had its dissenters, notably Milton Friedman.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Friedman believed that the inherent complexity of the economy, the long and variable lags with which monetary policy operates, and the political and bureaucratic influences on central bank decisionmaking precluded policy from fine tuning the level of economic activity.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Friedman advocated the use of simple prescriptions for monetary policy--such as the k percent money growth rule--which he felt would work reasonably well on average while avoiding the pitfalls of attempting to fine-tune the economy in the face of pervasive uncertainty (Friedman, 1968).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Other economists were more optimistic than Friedman about the potential benefits of activist policies.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nevertheless, they recognized that the fundamental economic uncertainties faced by policymakers are a first-order problem and that improving the conduct of policy would require facing that problem head on.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: During this decade, those researchers as well as sympathetic policymakers focused especially on three areas of economic uncertainty:  the current state of the economy, the structure of the economy (including the transmission mechanism of monetary policy), and the way in which private agents form expectations about future economic developments and policy actions.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Uncertainty about the current state of the economy is a chronic problem for policymakers.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: At best, official data represent incomplete snapshots of various aspects of the economy, and even then they may be released with a substantial lag and be revised later.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Apart from issues of measurement, policymakers face enormous challenges in determining the sources of variation in the data.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, a given change in output could be the result of a change in aggregate demand, in aggregate supply, or in some combination of the two.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As most of my listeners know, Bill Poole tackled these issues in a landmark 1970 paper, which examined how uncertainty about the state of the economy affects the choice of the operating instrument for monetary policy (Poole, 1970).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the simplest version of his model, Bill assumed that the central bank could choose to specify its monetary policy actions in terms of a particular level of a monetary aggregate or a particular value of a short-term nominal interest rate.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: If the central bank has only partial information about disturbances to money demand and to aggregate demand, Bill showed that the optimal choice of policy instrument depends on the relative variances of the two types of shocks.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, using the interest rate as the policy instrument is the better choice when aggregate demand is relatively stable but money demand is unstable, with money growth being the preferable policy instrument in the opposite case.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Bill was also a pioneer in formulating simple feedback rules that established a middle ground between the mechanical approach advocated by Friedman and the highly complex prescriptions of optimal-control methods.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, Bill wrote a Federal Reserve staff paper titled "Rules-of-Thumb for Guiding Monetary Policy" (Poole, 1971).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because his econometric analysis of the available data indicated that money demand was more stable than aggregate demand, Bill formulated a simple rule that adjusted the money growth rate in response to the observed unemployment rate.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Bill was also practical in noting the pitfalls of mechanical adherence to any particular policy rule; in this study, for example, he emphasized that the proposed rule was not intended "to be followed to the last decimal place or as one that is good for all time [but] .
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: as a guide--or as a benchmark--against which current policy may be judged" (p. 152).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Uncertainty about the structure of the economy also received attention during that decade.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, in his elegant 1967 paper, Bill Brainard showed that uncertainty about the effect of policy on the economy may imply that policy should respond more cautiously to shocks than would be the case if this uncertainty did not exist.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Brainard's analysis has often been cited as providing a theoretical basis for the gradual adjustment of policy rates of most central banks.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Alan Blinder has written that the Brainard result was "never far from my mind when I occupied the Vice Chairman's office at the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: a little stodginess at the central bank is entirely appropriate" (Blinder, 1998, p. 12).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: A key source of uncertainty became evident in the late 1960s and 1970s as a result of highly contentious debates about the formation of expectations by households and firms.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Friedman (1968) and Ned Phelps (1969) were the first to highlight the central importance of expectations formation, arguing that the private sector's expectations adjust in response to monetary policy and therefore preclude any long-run tradeoff between unemployment and inflation.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, Friedman and Phelps retained the view that monetary policy could exert substantial effects on the real economy over the short to medium run.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In contrast, Robert Lucas and others reached more dramatic conclusions, arguing that only unpredictable movements in monetary policy can affect the real economy and concluding that policy has no capacity to smooth the business cycle (Lucas, 1972; Sargent and Wallace, 1975).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although these studies highlighted the centrality of inflation expectations for the analysis of monetary policy, the profession did not succeed in reaching any consensus about how those expectations evolve, especially in an environment of ongoing structural change.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Developments during the Second Period:  1998-2007 Research during the past ten years has been very fruitful in expanding the profession's understanding of the implications of uncertainty for the design and conduct of monetary policy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the issue of uncertainty about the state of the economy, Bill's work continues to provide fundamental insights regarding the choice of policy instrument.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Money demand relationships were relatively stable through the 1950s and 1960s, but, in the wake of dramatic innovations in banking and financial markets, short-term money-demand relationships became less predictable, at least in the United States.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result, consistent with the policy implication of Bill's 1970 model, the Federal Reserve (like most other central banks) today uses the overnight interbank rate as the principal operating target of monetary policy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Bill's research also raised the possibility of specifying the operating target in other ways, for example, as an index of monetary or financial conditions; and it provided a framework for evaluating the usefulness of intermediate targets--such as core inflation or the growth of broad money--that are only indirectly controlled by policy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: More generally, the task of assessing the current state of the economy remains a formidable challenge.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, our appreciation of that challenge has been enhanced by recent research using real time data sets.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 For example, Athanasios Orphanides has shown that making such real-time assessments of the sustainable levels of economic activity and employment is considerably more difficult than estimating those levels retrospectively.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: His 2002 study of U.S. monetary policy in the 1970s shows how mismeasurement of the sustainable level of economic activity can lead to serious policy mistakes.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: On a more positive note, economists have made substantial progress over the past decade in developing new econometric methods for summarizing the information about the current state of the economy contained in a wide array of economic and financial market indicators (Svensson and Woodford, 2003).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Dynamic-factor models, for example, provide a systematic approach to extracting information from real-time data at very high frequencies.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: These approaches have the potential to usefully supplement more informal observation and human judgment (Stock and Watson, 2002; Bernanke and Boivin, 2003; and Giannone, Reichlin, and Small, 2005).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The past decade has also witnessed significant progress in analyzing the policy implications of uncertainty regarding the structure of the economy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: New work addresses not only uncertainty about the values of specific parameters in a given model of the economy but also uncertainty about which of several competing models provides the best description of reality.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some research has attacked those problems using Bayesian optimal-control methods (Brock, Durlauf, and West, 2003).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The approach requires the specification of an explicit objective function as well as of the investigator's prior probabilities over the set of plausible models and parameter values.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Bayesian approach provides a useful benchmark for policy in an environment of well-defined sources of uncertainty about the structure of the economy, and the resulting policy prescriptions give relatively greater weight to outcomes that have a higher probability of being realized.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In contrast, other researchers, such as Lars Hansen and Thomas Sargent, have developed robust-control methods--adapted from the engineering literature--that are aimed at minimizing the consequences of worst-case scenarios, including those with only a low probability of being realized (Hansen and Sargent, 2007).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: An important practical implication of all this recent literature is that Brainard's attenuation principle may not always hold.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, when the degree of structural inertia in the inflation process is uncertain, the optimal Bayesian policy tends to involve a more pronounced response to shocks than would be the case in the absence of uncertainty (Söderstrom, 2002).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The concern about worst-case scenarios emphasized by the robust-control approach may likewise lead to amplification rather than attenuation in the response of the optimal policy to shocks (Giannoni, 2002; Onatski and Stock, 2002; and Tetlow and von zur Muehlen, 2002).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, intuition suggests that stronger action by the central bank may be warranted to prevent particularly costly outcomes.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although Bayesian and robust-control methods provide insights into the nature of optimal policy, the corresponding policy recommendations can be complex and sensitive to the set of economic models being considered.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: A promising alternative approach--reminiscent of the work that Bill Poole did in the 1960s--focuses on simple policy rules, such as the one proposed by John Taylor, and compares the performance of alternative rules across a range of possible models and sets of parameter values (Levin, Wieland, and Williams, 1999 and 2003).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: That approach is motivated by the notion that the perfect should not be the enemy of the good; rather than trying to find policies that are optimal in the context of specific models, the central bank may be better served by adopting simple and predictable policies that produce reasonably good results in a variety of circumstances.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Given the centrality of inflation expectations for the design of monetary policy, a key development over the past decade has been the burgeoning literature on the formation of these expectations in the absence of full knowledge of the underlying structure of the economy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 For example, considerations of how the public learns about the economy and the objectives of the central bank can affect the form of the optimal monetary policy (Gaspar, Smets, and Vestin, 2006; Orphanides and Williams, 2007).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Furthermore, when the public is unsure about the central bank's objectives, even greater benefits may accompany achieving a stable inflation rate, as doing so may help anchor the public's inflation expectations.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: These studies also show why central bank communications is a key component of monetary policy; in a world of uncertainty, informing the public about the central bank's objectives, plans, and outlook can affect behavior and macroeconomic outcomes (Bernanke, 2004; and Orphanides and Williams, 2005).
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion Uncertainty--about the state of the economy, the economy's structure, and the inferences that the public will draw from policy actions or economic developments--is a pervasive feature of monetary policy making.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The contributions of Bill Poole have helped refine our understanding of how to conduct policy in an uncertain environment.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, we now appreciate that policy decisions under uncertainty must take into account a range of possible scenarios about the state or structure of the economy, and those policy decisions may look quite different from those that would be optimal under certainty.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, policy actions may be attenuated or augmented relative to the "no-uncertainty benchmark," depending on one's judgments about the possible outcomes and the costs associated with those outcomes.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The fact that the public is uncertain about and must learn about the economy and policy provides a reason for the central bank to strive for predictability and transparency, avoid overreacting to current economic information, and recognize the challenges of making real-time assessments of the sustainable level of real economic activity and employment.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Most fundamentally, our discussions of the pervasive uncertainty that we face as policymakers is a powerful reminder of the need for humility about our ability to forecast and manage the future course of the economy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy under Uncertainty
speech_venue: At the 32nd Annual Economic Policy Conference, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (via videoconference)

speaker: Mishkin
text: In discussing and thinking about the conduct of monetary policy, many central bankers focus on core inflationââthat is, a measure of inflation that excludes the rate of increase of prices for certain volatile components in price indexes.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: 1 The Federal Reserve, for example, pays particular attention to the rate of growth of the core personal consumption expenditure (PCE) deflator, which excludes food and energy prices.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, in the presentation of its twice yearly Monetary Policy Report to the Congress, the Federal Reserve Board reports the projections of Federal Open Market Committee participants regarding core PCE inflation, not headline inflation, the latter of which includes all items in the price index.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Here in Canada, unlike in the United States, the central bank maintains an explicit inflation target.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Bank of Canada states its target in terms of the headline consumer price index, and although this choice of inflation measure contrasts with the Federal Reserve's preferred index, the difference is not nearly as great as it appears on the surface.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: In fact, the Bank of Canada monitors a number of inflation measures and uses core inflation as an "operational guide" in coming to its monetary policy decisions and discussing these decisions with the public.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Does it make sense for a central bank to concentrate on core inflation?
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: After all, households almost daily pay for energy and food itemsââwhich are excluded from the most prominent measures of core inflationââwhen they fill up their cars at gas stations or visit a grocery store.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Households, particularly less-affluent households, spend a major portion of their budgets on food and energy.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: A focus on core inflation, which excludes these items, might be viewed as indicating that monetary policy makers are out of touch with what consumers really care about.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Wouldn't it be better for monetary policy authorities to focus on headline inflation so that they include food and energy in their monitoring of consumer price inflation?
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I will argue, this is not an either-or decision.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: It does indeed make sense for central banks to emphasize headline inflation when determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy over the medium run, but policymakers also are right to emphasize core inflation when deciding how to adjust policy from meeting to meeting.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because what central bankers are truly concerned withââboth for the purposes of internal deliberations and for communications with the publicââis the underlying rate of inflation going forward, and core inflation can be a useful proxy for that rate.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, focusing on core inflation can help prevent a central bank from responding too strongly to transitory movements in inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Why Monetary Policy Should Focus on Core Inflation Because households care about the prices of all the items they buy, it clearly does not make sense to pretend that people do not eat or drive.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, I have no qualm in stating that controlling headline inflation, not core inflation, isââalong with maintaining maximum sustainable employmentââthe ultimate aim of monetary policy.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nonetheless, I will argue that it is still useful for monetary policy makers to focus on core inflation when deciding how to respond to incoming economic news.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although monetary policy is capable of controlling overall inflation in the long run, it does not have the ability to control relative price movements such as those for food and energy.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: When a cold snap freezes the Florida orange crop or a tropical storm hits the gasoline refineries along the Gulf Coast, monetary policy cannot reverse the resulting spikes in prices for fresh orange juice or for gasoline at the pump.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Temporary supply shocks such as these raise the prices of food and energy relative to other prices and can have substantial effects on inflation in the short run.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: By including all itemsââincluding particularly volatile items like food and energyââheadline measures of inflation are inherently noisy and often do not reflect changes in the underlying rate of inflation, the rate at which headline inflation is likely to settle and that monetary policy can affect.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Measures of core inflation attempt to strip out or smooth volatile changes in particular prices to distinguish the inflation signal from the transitory noise.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, relative to changes in headline inflation measures, changes in core measures are much less likely to be reversed, provide a clearer picture of the underlying inflation pressures, and so serve as a better guide to where headline inflation itself is heading.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, if a particular shock to noncore prices is not temporary but, rather, turns out to be more persistent, then the higher costs are likely to put some upward pressure on core prices.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Central bankers must always be aware of this risk.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, research has shown that, over the past twenty-five years or more, headline inflation in the United States has tended to revert more strongly toward core inflation than core inflation has moved toward headline inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: 2 As that record suggests, core measures often are much better than headline indexes at providing a first approximation of the permanent changes to inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: When headline inflation has an important transitory component, a focus on core measures can help avoid monetary policy mistakes.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: If the monetary authorities react to headline inflation numbers, they run the risk of responding to merely temporary fluctuations in inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: We can think about this danger by considering a supply shock, that causes the relative price of energy to increase sharply, as in fact has happened over the past three years.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Let us suppose that we start out with both headline and core inflation at acceptably low levels.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, let's consider a supply shock that temporarily raises the price of energy by a large amount.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: In this case headline inflation will rise well above its underlying trend as the price of energy rises but will soon fall well below its underlying trend as the price of energy falls back to its initial level.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: On average, inflation will remain unchanged without any monetary policy action.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: But a tightening of monetary policy in reaction to the rise in headline inflation would lead to a decline in employment and inflation; and because of the long lags between monetary policy actions and changes in economic activity, that decline would occur some time down the road, when inflation would more likely be at or below its underlying trend.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The outcome of such a policy would be a more pronounced fall in inflation with a decline in employment.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such a policy would be bad indeed because it would increase volatility in inflation and employment, which is the opposite of what a central bank should be trying to achieve as it seeks to promote price stability and maximum sustainable employment.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: But what if a supply shock leads to a permanent shift in the relative price of energy?
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, almost all commentators characterize the current oil price shock that way, in part because they see the rise of new economic powers like China as adding to the demand for energy in the foreseeable future.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although in that case the rise in relative energy prices is not reversed, the rate of change in energy prices does not persist:  Headline inflation will rise with the increase in energy prices, but once energy prices reach their permanently high level, headline inflation will revert to its underlying trend rate.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, as long as the permanent change in relative energy prices does not lead to a change in the underlying trend rate of inflation ââa crucial assumptionââthen headline inflation will come back down again.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: This is what we seem to have seen recently in the United States.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: From a low near $30 per barrel in late 2003, the price of oil rose to $70 per barrel by the middle of 2006, and it has stayed high, with the current price more than $80.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: That move increased headline PCE inflation to the 4 percent level for a time, but it has since retreated to around 2 percent ( figure 1 ).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Monetary policy clearly can do little about the first-round effects of a permanent rise in energy prices, which include both its direct impact on the energy component of overall consumer prices and the pass-through of higher energy costs into prices of non-energy goods and services.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: But policy does have a critical role to play in determining the second-round effects associated with changes in the underlying trend rate of inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such second-round effects are likely to be quite limited as long as the rise in the relative price of energy does not lead to a rise in long-run inflation expectations, as has largely been the case in the recent period (figure 1).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, the stability of expectations rests on the central bank's strong long-term commitment to providing a nominal anchor, which, as I have argued elsewhere (Mishkin, 2007), describes the situation in the United States.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: With such a commitment firmly established, monetary policy then does not need to respond as much to the temporary rise in headline inflation to stabilize inflation over the longer run.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Under these circumstances, if monetary policy is tightened appreciably in the face of a surge in headline inflation, the policy would likely be excessively tight and lead to an unnecessary decline in employment.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because the point about headline inflation is so important, I would like to illustrate it further with simulations of FRB/US, the model of the U.S. economy created and maintained by the staff at the Federal Reserve Board.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: To keep the experiments as clean as possible, I assume that the economy begins at full employment and with both headline and core inflation at desired levels.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The economy is then assumed to experience a shock that raises the world price of oil about $30 per barrel over two years; the shock is assumed to slowly dissipate thereafter.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: In each of two scenarios, a Taylor rule is assumed to govern the response of the federal funds rate; the only difference between the two is that in one scenario the funds rate responds to core PCE inflation, while in the other it responds to headline PCE inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: 3 Figure 2 illustrates the results of these two scenarios.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The federal funds rate jumps higher and faster when the central bank responds to headline inflation rather than to core inflation, as would be expected (top-left panel).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Likewise, responding to headline inflation pushes the unemployment rate markedly higher than otherwise in the early going (top-right panel), and produces an inflation rate that is slightly lower than otherwise, whether measured by core or headline indexes (bottom panels).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: More important, even for a shock as persistent as this one, the policy response under headline inflation has to be unwound in the sense that the federal funds rate must drop substantially below baseline once the first-round effects of the shock drop out of the inflation data.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Responding to headline inflation is therefore inappropriate because it generates extensive variability in the unemployment rateââvariability that is much more subdued when policy responds to core inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, the pitfalls associated with reacting to realized headline inflation, as illustrated by this simulation, are well understood.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Accordingly, advocates of targeting headline inflation generally have in mind a strategy of responding to forecasts of headline inflationââforecasts that try to take account of inflation movements that are likely to be transitory.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: This is a further illustration of my basic point, namely, that it is important to distinguish between transitory and persistent inflation movements, and focusing on core inflation can help achieve that end.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The focus on core instead of headline inflationââand clear communication with the public about that focusââcan have another benefit:  It may help anchor inflation expectations when headline inflation increases temporarily but core inflation remains essentially unchanged.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: If the public understands that the central bank is using core inflation in formulating monetary policy and trusts that the central bank is right to do so, the public will realize that the central bank does not need to respond aggressively to a surge in headline inflation to keep inflation under control.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: And, with core inflation stable, the public will be less likely to think that the central bank has weakened its commitment to a strong nominal anchor when it does not tighten monetary policy to stabilize headline inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The result is that inflation expectations are likely to remain anchored, which may lead to better outcomes not only on inflation but on employment as well, because the central bank will not have had to tighten monetary policy as much in response to the energy price shock.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I noted earlier, figure 1 offers some support for this view:  It shows that the rise in headline inflation in the 2004-06 period, when core inflation remained quite stable, did not lead to an appreciable rise in long-run inflation expectations, even with a substantial decline in unemployment during this period.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Is Inflation Excluding Food and Energy the Best Measure of Underlying Inflation?
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The most popular core inflation measures used and published in the United States are quite straightforward:  They simply exclude changes in food and energy prices.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, such simple "exclusion" measures can likely be improved upon.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, many of the food categories excluded in the standard measure of core inflation, such as food away from home (restaurants), are not highly volatile and so likely should remain in an optimal core inflation measure.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: On the other hand, some items that are not excluded from the U.S. core measures, such as airline fares, tobacco, and apparel, are extremely volatile and thus are unlikely to be included in an optimal core inflation measure.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Bank of Canada, for example, uses a more targeted approach to its core inflation indicator, the CPIX.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of fifty-four consumer product categories, it excludes eight, which account for about 16 percent of the consumption basket (Macklem, 2001).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Most of the eight items are also excluded from the standard core measure in the United States.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, Canada's CPIX also excludes intercity transportation and tobacco, which are included in the U.S. core measures.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Another approach to estimating core inflation measures is statistical, in which certain prices are excluded at each point on the basis of statistical criteria.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Among these statistical measures are trimmed indexes, such as the trimmed mean and the weighted median consumer price indexes produced by the Cleveland Fed and the trimmed mean PCE price index produced by the Dallas Fed.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Each month, these measures throw out the components with the largest price changes, both positive and negative (though the Dallas measure is asymmetric).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Other approaches to estimating core inflation are theory-based measures employing common trends, unobserved components, or a particular model of the economy.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: 8 However, these theory-based approaches tend to be rather complex and require faith that the model they are based on is the right one.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Each of these measures of core inflation can be evaluated according to a variety of criteria, including the ability to forecast headline inflation over some period and the degree of correlation with alternative definitions of trend inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: According to some of these criteria, statistical and theory-based approaches are sometimes found to outperform simpler exclusion measures of core inflation, like the standard one excluding food and energy.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: As you can tell, this is an active area of research, but recent research done at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on U.S. data finds that no one particular core measure, including the standard one, dominates the others:  The relative performance of different core measures varies depending on the choice of the price index, the sample period, and the criteria for evaluating their performance (Rich and Steindel, 2007).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research on Canadian and U.K. data comes to similar conclusions (Hogan, Johnson, and Laflèche, 2001; Mankikar and Paisley, 2002).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Does the lack of empirical support for any one particular type of core measure suggest that our focus on the standard core measure should be abandoned?
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The simplicity and long history of the standard core measure that excludes food and energy gives it several major advantages.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Its simplicity makes it straightforward to explain and thus more understandable to the publicââassuming, of course, that we successfully communicate that we recognize the importance of food and energy items in people's consumption.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Its simplicity also makes its estimation very transparent.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: That transparency and the fact that it has been around a long timeââhence the characterization as "standard"ââboth prevent a central bank or a government authority from easily manipulating the measure to show good results.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: These features of the standard core measure therefore make it a credible device to keep inflation expectations anchored when supply shocks occur:  If the standard measure remains stable, then a surge in headline inflation is less likely to unhinge inflation expectations, which as we have seen can lead to both better inflation and better employment performance.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Why Central Banks Should also Focus on Headline Inflation Despite the advantages of core measures of inflation, their use in conducting monetary policy has been criticized.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: 9 Core measures of inflation attempt to remove the most volatile or transitory components of the inflation measure.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: But, because the nature of price shocks may change over time, items that have been highly volatile in the past may not be so in the future; hence, any core measure will itself likely be subject to transitory shocks.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Unfortunately, as noted above, empirical research suggests that no one measure of core inflation will work in all situations.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, central banks do not focus solely on core inflation; rather, they devote considerable resources to understanding inflation developments in an effort to distinguish signal from noise in the incoming data.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Another reason to keep watch over the broader inflation picture is that, if the rate of change in the price of an excluded item receives a permanent shock, then the headline inflation rate can deviate from the core measure for an extended period of time.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The longer this period of high headline inflation persists, the greater is the risk of second-round effects as the public begins to build this higher inflation into its expectations.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, from 1987 to 2002, energy price shocks appear to have been temporary in that energy prices were mean reverting; as a result, in this period, the average difference between core and headline PCE inflation was quite small.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Since 2002, however, the effect of energy price shocks have been more persistent, and headline inflation has averaged more than 1/2 percentage point above core inflation over this period.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the past year, energy prices have about leveled off on balance--or at least that was the case until a couple of weeks ago--and the rate of headline inflation for most of this year has come down close to that for core, one hopes alleviating the risk of second-round effects.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: But the increases in oil prices in recent days provide another reminder that shocks can persist longer than one might have at first expected.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: A prolonged divergence between core and headline measures of inflation could complicate central bank communications with the public because core inflation would require some adjustment before it would provide a clear gauge of underlying inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the weighted median CPI inflation rate, one popular measure of core inflation, has tended to be a biased measure of headline inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: The weighted median is exactly equal to owners' equivalent rent nearly half the time because that component has an extremely large share of the consumption basket and fairly low volatility (Bryan and Pike, 1991; Hogan and others, 2001; and Bryan and Meyer, 2007).
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, the productivity growth rate in residential construction is not terribly high, and so this sector is likely to have below-average productivity growth and above-average price increases.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, the weighted median CPI exceeded overall CPI inflation on average by 1/4 percentage point per year over the decade from 1992 to 2002, a period when changes in energy prices were transitory.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, to the extent that such a bias in a core inflation measure is stable or predictable, the central bank could easily take this into account in setting monetary policy.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: But even in that case, differences in average rates of inflation between the core measure and overall inflation could complicate communication with the public.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conclusion I have argued that a measure of core inflation that is easily understood and provides some greater signal about persistent movements in inflation than does headline inflation itself is extremely valuable for the conduct of monetary policy, and that is why the Federal Reserve pays so much attention to such measures.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, I have also argued that core measures have their limitations.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: A single core inflation measure cannot account for all types of shocks and can at times be misleading about what is happening to the underlying rate of overall inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: And if increases in headline inflation prove more persistent than initially expected, central bankers must be vigilant to ensure that they do not become embedded into expectations and thereby generate substantial second-round effects on inflation.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, because price stability ultimately involves control of overall, headline inflation, which after all is the inflation measure that households really care about, central bankers should and do pay attention to headline inflation as well as to core inflation measures.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada

speaker: Mishkin
text: A core inflation measure should not be seen as a substitute for thorough and careful analysis of the forces that are driving our economy and the inflation process.
speech_title: Headline versus Core Inflation in the Conduct of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Business Cycles, International Transmission and Macroeconomic Policies Conference, HEC Montreal, Montreal, Canada
