speaker: Kroszner
text: Price Discovery When markets are functioning properly, one of the key roles that they perform is what economists refer to as "price discovery."
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 Essentially, price discovery is the process by which buyers and sellersâ preferences, as well as any other available market information, results in the "discovery" of a price that will balance supply and demand and provide signals to market participants about how most efficiently to allocate resources..
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This market-determined price will, of course, be subject to change as new information becomes available, as preferences evolve, as expectations are revised, and as costs of production change.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In well-functioning markets, the price discovery process represents the efforts of market participants to use all available information to decide whether to buy or to sell or to abstain from buying and selling.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In efficient and competitive markets, participants will tend to undertake a certain amount of due diligence before making their decisions.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This means that prices do not just appear by themselves; a substantial amount of work is required by buyers and sellers for markets to produce prices that clear markets and provide useful signals to consumers and producers.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, this is one of the brilliant aspects of the market mechanism in that a number of participants, each pursuing their own interests and trying to maximize their own welfare and profits, determine a market-clearing price.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A core principle of economics is that markets are more competitive, and therefore more efficient, when accurate information is available to both buyers and sellers.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: But for markets to work best, market participants must utilize available information, including analysis of costs and benefits of obtaining such information.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the case of new and innovative products, there might be a particularly strong demand for information.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Then this information must be processed appropriately before decisions are made about whether to buy or sell.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In some instances, the price discovery process can break down and buyers and sellers are unable to discover any price at all--perhaps because of a lack of information or because of general uncertainty among market participants.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would suggest that this is fundamentally what has occurred in some financial markets over the past several months.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This has certainly not been the case in all markets.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, while equity markets in the United States have experienced greater price volatility in recent months, and credit spreads have widened in markets for highly-rated, traditional debt instruments, I believe this has been a function of reassessing risk rather than a broader failure of the price discovery process itself.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, investment-grade corporations faced little trouble in issuing traditional debt instruments during the market turbulence in August and did so in significant volumes.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In some financial markets, however, the price discovery process appears to have actually broken down.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In particular, I am referring to markets for structured credit products (for example, collateralized loan obligations and collateralized debt obligations) that are often complex and opaque, as well as instruments that are linked to these structured products, such as asset-backed commercial paper.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Why did the price discovery process fail in these markets but not in others?
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would suggest that there are two principal related causes.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, some investors may not have done sufficient due diligence with regard to complex structured products.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Prior to the recent market disruptions, many buyers and sellers of complex structured products appear not to have demanded sufficient information from sellers, and simply accepted investment-grade ratings of these securities as a substitute for their own risk analysis.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: When the problems in the subprime mortgage market began to emerge and delinquencies on subprime mortgages in pools backing these securities exceeded rating agency estimates, subsequently resulting in a number of downgrades, investors lost confidence in the quality of these ratings, and hence the quality of the information they had about these instruments, and pulled back from markets for structured products across the board.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A second, related factor contributing to the breakdown in price discovery is the recognition by investors of complexity and lack of transparency, both in the instruments themselves and in the markets more broadly.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The complex structures of the innovative instruments, and the lack of transparency with regard to the underlying assets backing these instruments, made them more difficult and costly to value than many investors originally thought.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the same time, many investors realized that it was difficult to identify where the risks were lodged.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This uncertainty, of course, is one of the trade-offs of a more market-intermediated finance system in which risks are more widely dispersed rather than concentrated in the banking system.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As problems in the subprime mortgage market became more apparent, investors became unwilling to purchase products that could have any exposure not only to subprime mortgages, but to housing-related assets and other structured products more generally.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Put simply, investors suddenly realized that they were much less informed than they originally thought.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In these circumstances, it is not necessarily surprising that investors pulled back from purchasing certain instruments at any price.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Prospects for Market Recovery In light of these factors, what is the prognosis for recovery in markets for complex structured credit instruments?
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would suggest that, while we have seen more normal price discovery activity slowly returning to some markets, the recovery may be a relatively gradual process, and these markets may not look the same when they re-emerge.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Both investors and sellers will need to take steps for the price discovery process to be re-established in these markets.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In observing the challenges to price discovery and the repricing of risk in many markets recently, I have been reminded of a Russian proverb that was made famous in the context of international relations but applies equally to investment decisions: "Trust, but verify."
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As I mentioned earlier, one of the reasons that the price discovery mechanism has broken down in some U.S. markets in recent months is that a number of investors failed to exercise due diligence and relied on rating agency assessments.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is, there was a lot of trust but not much verification.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would suggest that the value of independent due diligence on the part of investors is especially high for newer and more-complex products compared with more traditional, familiar, and less-complex products.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Reducing the chance of unanticipated losses may require significant effort on the part of investors looking to purchase complex structured products and the creators or sellers of those products.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: To be able to better understand the risk profile of such instruments, some market participants will have to invest in three ways to revive the price discovery mechanism.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, they will likely need to collect more detailed data.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In particular, investors will need to gather data more systematically to help them understand the nature and risks of the underlying assets and the structures of the instruments.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, investors will likely require enhanced systems to warehouse and model data related to these instruments to better understand their risk profile, especially under stress conditions.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, investors will likely need to ensure that they have the appropriate human capital expertise--that is, people--to interpret, understand, and act appropriately on the results of their modeling and analysis.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The investment in data, modeling, and assessment will take time so there may be an extended period before normal price discovery will return in markets for some existing products.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In turn, given the likely increase in the costs of producing and evaluating certain complex instruments, these actions and efforts may affect investorsâ risk-reward calculus by increasing required returns--or the "hurdle rates"--on these investments.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Creators and sellers may respond by reducing complexity, improving quality of underlying assets or increasing transparency and disclosure.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In light of recent events, market innovation may result in new instruments that satisfy the needs of both buyers and sellers--instruments that, of course, should not just be accepted on their face but should be subject to proper due diligence.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the end, investors will decide for themselves whether acquiring the data and expertise necessary to participate in certain markets is worth the cost.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result, it is likely that these markets and instruments will look different than they did prior to the recent market turmoil.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Let me close by highlighting the role of the Federal Reserve over the past several months as a backstop source of liquidity in interbank funding markets.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As price discovery broke down in a variety of markets, financial institutions, as intermediaries and liquidity providers themselves in the affected markets, became protective of their liquid reserves and balance sheet capacity.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result, overnight and term interbank funding markets have come under pressure.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve accordingly took a number of steps to try to alleviate these pressures.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Fedâs initial action in early August was to increase liquidity in short-term money markets through larger open-market operations--the standard means by which it seeks to ensure that the federal funds rate is maintained at or close to the target rate set by the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This extra provision of liquidity helped bring the funds rate down to its target early in the day; it also eased banksâ concerns about the availability of funding and thus assisted the functioning of the interbank market.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The vigorous provision of funds through open market operations succeeded in damping pressures in overnight funding markets.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Yet, markets for term interbank funding remained strained.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: On August 17, the Federal Reserve Board took further action by cutting the discount rate--the rate at which it lends directly to banks--by 50 basis points, or half a percentage point.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Fed also adjusted its usual practices to facilitate the provision of financing for as long as thirty days, renewable at the request of the borrower.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These actions also appear to have improved market functioning, though strains, particularly in term funding markets, persist even now.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, judging from forward curves in interbank and overnight indexed swaps markets, market participants expect pressures in term funding markets to persist for several quarters.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I should emphasize that the purpose of these actions was not to insulate financial institutions from the consequences of their business decisions, but rather to facilitate the orderly function of markets more broadly in the face of risks to the overall economy.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe that this provision of liquidity has contributed, at least in part, to the recent improvements we have seen in the functioning of financial markets.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Importantly, the Federal Open Market Committeeâs most recent action, the 50 basis point cut in the target federal funds rate in September, was an attempt to help offset the potential effects of financial market turmoil on real economic activity.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The breakdown in the price discovery process can, after all, have real economic consequences that the Federal Reserve should, in my opinion, consider when fulfilling its statutorily mandated goals of maximum employment and price stability.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusion In the months ahead, the Federal Reserve will continue to monitor developments in the financial markets and act as needed to support the effective functioning of these markets and to foster sustainable economic growth and price stability.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, we will be reviewing the events of the past several months to understand the likely causes and effects.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thank you very much, and I look forward to a lively dialogue following my esteemed colleaguesâ remarks.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These views are my own and do not necessarily reflect those of the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Reserve System as a whole.
speech_title: Recent Events in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speech_venue: At the Institute of International Bankers Annual Breakfast Dialogue, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In my remarks today I would like to address the issue of financial instability from two perspectives:  First, I will offer a conceptual framework that helps us understand why periods of financial instability arise, and second, I will describe how the Federal Reserve has used the provision of liquidity to reduce the damage to the economy during such periods of turmoil.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The interest of the Federal Reserve in financial stability does not arise out of a concern for the functioning of financial markets as such or out of a desire to aid distressed investors or institutions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Rather, the Federal Reserve vigorously promotes financial stability because of the intimate connection between a stable financial system and solid macroeconomic performance.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The financial system, comprising financial markets and institutions, channels funds to those individuals or firms that have productive investment opportunities.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The better the financial system performs this role, the more efficiently credit flows from lenders to borrowers and the more efficiently the economy operates.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: A period of financial instability arises when a shock to the financial system prevents it from channeling funds efficiently to productive uses; as I will describe, such a shock generally relates to problems in the flow of information.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Unless checked, such a seizing-up of the financial system can lead to a precipitous drop in lending and a steep decline in economic activity.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, a stable financial system is of vital importance for the Federal Reserve if it is to pursue its statutory goals of maximum sustainable employment and stable prices.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Asymmetric Information and Financial Instability We can better understand how financial instability can arise if we recognize the problem of asymmetric informationââwhen one party to a financial contract has much less information than the other party.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the borrower is usually much better informed than the lender concerning the potential risks and returns associated with the investment projects to be financed by a loan.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Asymmetric information leads to two basic problems: adverse selection and moral hazard.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Generally speaking, adverse selection arises when investments that are most likely to produce an adverse outcome are the most likely to be selected.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, investors who intend to take on large amounts of risk are the most likely to be willing to seek financing.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: When the problem of asymmetric information is particularly severe in the marketplace, lenders may decide to cut back on lending even though good credit risks exist.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 2 Clearly, minimizing adverse selection requires that lenders screen out bad credit risks.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moral hazard occurs when the lender is subjected to the hazard in which the borrower has an incentive to engage in activities that are undesirable from the lender's point of view, that is, activities that make it less likely that the loan will be repaid.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, a borrower may have an incentive to invest in high-risk projects in which the borrower does well if the project succeeds but the lender bears most of the loss if the project fails.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Again, if this conflict of interest between the borrower and lender becomes particularly pronounced in the marketplace, many lenders might decide that they would rather not make loans, which leads to suboptimal lending and investment.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To minimize moral hazard, lenders must impose restrictions (known as restrictive covenants) that penalize borrowers for engaging in certain activities; lenders must monitor those activities, and they must enforce the restrictions if the borrower violates them.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over time, the financial system has developed a variety of mechanisms to deal with informational asymmetries.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: These mechanisms include a strong network of financial intermediaries, sound and resilient financial markets, innovative financial products that spread risk to the investors most willing and able to bear it, and effective supervisory and regulatory frameworks.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, even the strongest financial system is not immune to shocks.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: When such shocks interfere materially with information flows, the problems of adverse selection and moral hazard can overwhelm the mechanisms intended to control them.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As lenders pull back and liquidity becomes scarce, a period of financial instability can ensue, carrying with it, as I mentioned at the outset, the threat of a serious decline in economic activity through a virtual cessation of lending.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Broadly speaking, at least four types of shocks can lead to financial instability.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The first type, and the one that has been the catalyst of many past crises, is a sharp increase in interest rates.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Higher interest rates increase the likelihood that borrowers will be poor credit risks because those taking on more risk are the most willing to pay the higher rates; not surprisingly, lenders have many times responded to sharp increases in interest rates by cutting back the supply of loans, which results in credit rationing.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The other types of shocks are a sudden increase in uncertainty, a deterioration of corporate and household balance sheets, and weakened financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some of these have clearly manifested themselves in the episode that has affected global financial markets in recent months.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In general, an increase in uncertainty makes it harder to obtain information about borrowers, thereby deterring lending, and may arise from the failure of a large financial institution, a market crash, a recession, or, as in the latest episode, an inability to value complex financial products.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Weak borrower balance sheets are also a deterrent to lending because they worsen credit risk and thus make the problems of adverse selection and moral hazard more prominent.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The harmful effects of balance sheet deterioration were evident in recent months, when concerns about borrower financial positions caused lenders to demand a substantial premium on loans and even to drastically cut the flow of credit.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, problems in the banking sector may also be a catalyst for financial instability because financial intermediaries that find themselves with weakened financial positions typically respond by cutting their lending.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: A central bank can respond to an episode of financial instability by temporarily providing the liquidity that financial intermediaries are unwilling or unable to supply.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Central banks typically inject liquidity into the system via the banking sector, but the intent is clearly to have the liquidity spread from there.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: From banks, liquidity typically finds its way to financial markets and to nonbank institutions that are unable to access securities markets.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, injections of liquidity have the potential to directly address the causes of financial instability and therefore to counteract the pernicious effects of financial instability on broad macroeconomic conditions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: With this understanding, we can now turn to some history.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Panic of 1907 and the Creation of the Federal Reserve During the National Banking Era, which began in 1865 and ended in 1914, when the Federal Reserve began operations, reserves were channeled to New York banks, which became providers of liquidity to the financial system through the New York Clearinghouse.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nevertheless, the banking system periodically suffered panics, as the demand for liquidity often exceeded what New York institutions could provide.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: These panics, in turn, caused large numbers of banks to fail or at least suspend the conversion of deposits into currency.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: During these episodes, interest rates tended to spike and equity markets to decline, often sharply.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Panic of 1907, the subject of this conference, was the last panic of the National Banking Era and one of the most severe.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: During the summer of 1907, U.S. financial institutions, especially those in New York, came under increasing pressure as interest rates crept up and U.S. gold reserves declined; those movements were due in part to increases in interest rates abroad as foreign central banks sought to maintain their gold reserves.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 4 The panic started in October with a run on the Knickerbocker Trust Company, one of the largest financial institutions at the time.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The stock market crashed, and the resulting surge in demand for liquid assets by banks that had New York correspondents, as well as by the general public, caused a sharp rise in interest rates, the failure of a number of financial institutions, and widespread suspensions of convertibility of deposits into currency.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The subsequent banking crisis arguably turned a mild recession into a sharp, though fairly short, contraction.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result of the 1907 crisis, the Congress set up the National Monetary Commission to consider whether the federal government should more actively manage the nation's money supply.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The committee's recommendations led to the creation of the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, an important impetus for the establishment of the U.S. central bank was the desire to prevent panics such as the one in 1907, whose detrimental effects on the rest of the economy were not lost on policymakers.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: At the time, the belief was widespread that the inelasticity of the currency contributed to the weakness of the financial system.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The supply of high-powered moneyââwhich included national bank notes, specie, U.S. notes, and silver certificatesââwas relatively fixed (inelastic) in the short run.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, even fairly moderate increases in demand for high-powered money led to higher interest rates.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, some of the increases in the demand for money were not random; they were associated with the crop cycle and were thus seasonal.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 6 Just as no existing mechanism or institution could quickly supply the liquidity needed to respond to a rise in the demand for money, none could supply it to resolve the ensuing crisis.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The establishment of the Federal Reserve provided the nation with an institution that was able to expand the money supply to virtually eliminate seasonal fluctuations in interest rates and thus mitigate the stress such fluctuations might put on the financial system.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The policymakers involved in establishing the Federal Reserve also believed that the institution would be able to meet the needs of the financial system at times when there was an unanticipated scramble for liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The founders tended to focus on the ability to rediscount commercial loans at the discount window, which was seen as a way of providing an elastic currency that would eliminate crises or at least mitigate them.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider In past research, I have examined the importance of liquidity provisions by central banks in overcoming the problem of asymmetric information, exacerbated by the increase in interest rates, and the uncertainty that generally accompany a financial crisis (Mishkin, 1997).
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Increased liquidity can help restrain rising interest rates and, amid an environment of heightened uncertainty, enable the institutions best able to make judgments about the creditworthiness of prospective borrowers to provide credit.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over time, the Federal Reserve has used various methods to provide liquidity to the financial system.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: At first, the ability to rediscount paper was seen as the main tool with which to provide liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: At other times, the Federal Reserve has changed interest rate ceilings or used open market operations.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Since 2003, the operation of the discount window has altered significantly.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The new facility allows banks in sound financial condition to borrow at will at a rate above the target federal funds rate.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The facility can be used to provide liquidity to financial institutions during a crisis in which financial markets become dysfunctional as well as during other periods of financial tightness that are not the result of a systemic event.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even with the Federal Reserve System in place, periods of financial stress have arisen since World War II.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: I will briefly review a few of the more recent ones and focus on the role of the Federal Reserve as a liquidity provider in mitigating them.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The first of these more recent episodes arose from the 1970 bankruptcy of the Penn Central Corporation, an important issuer of commercial paper.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Policymakers and market participants worried that the bankruptcy of such a major issuer would have a chilling effect on the commercial paper market, as uncertainties about the quality of other issuers would impede them from rolling over their commercial paper to obtain short-term financing.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 8 The Penn Central bankruptcy thus had the potential to send other companies into bankruptcy and possibly trigger a full-scale financial panic.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To forestall this possibility, the Federal Reserve provided liquidity to financial markets in two ways.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, the Federal Reserve Banks let the depositories in their respective Districts know that the discount window was available to enable them to make loans to customers who could not roll over their commercial paper.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, the Federal Reserve (along with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Federal Home Loan Bank Board) suspended the interest rate ceilings imposed by the Federal Reserve's Regulation Q on some large certificates of deposit, thus providing banks another means of financing increases in loans.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The second recent episode of financial instability was the stock market crash of 1987.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: A significant concern during this episode was the possibility of a breakdown in the clearing and settlement systems in the equity and futures markets.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To keep those markets functioning in an orderly fashion, brokerage firms needed to obtain massive amounts of credit from banks to meet margin calls from the clearing and settlement institutions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, although brokerages were clearly in need of additional funds to finance their activities, banks were understandably nervous about the health of securities firms in the wake of the unprecedented market movements.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 9 In response, the Federal Reserve issued a statement affirming its readiness to serve as a source of liquidity to support the economic and financial system.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve underscored its commitment to providing liquidity by conducting open market operations in a high-profile manner and earlier than usual.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 10 The Federal Reserve also communicated with market participants to support efforts to coordinate a market response (Greenspan, 1994).
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: What is remarkable about this episode is the relatively limited amount of liquidity extended by the Federal Reserve:  In the immediate aftermath of the crash, it temporarily injected through open market operations about $12 billion, which at the time was a notable but not exceptional amount.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because the Federal Reserve acted promptly (within a day) to prevent the financial system from seizing up, banks were not as reluctant to lend their funds to securities firms as they presumably would have been in the absence of a stabilizing action from the central bank.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, the Fed did not need to lend directly to the banks to encourage them to lend to the securities firms that needed funds to clear their customers' accounts.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Confidence was restored, and the fear of crisis subsided quickly.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The ability of the Federal Reserve to provide liquidity was also vital following the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001, which disrupted payment, settlement, and communication systems needed to transfer funds among financial institutions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Unable to receive funds for their normal operations, many of these institutions turned to the central bank.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve responded by injecting a considerable amount of liquidity into the system, both through discount window loans (which soared from around $200 million in the days immediately before the attacks to a maximum of $46 billion) and repurchase agreements (which jumped from $25 billion to a peak of more than $80 billion).
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Further, the Federal Reserve helped facilitate the provision of dollar liquidity abroad by arranging swap lines with foreign central banks.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thanks to these steps, credit continued to flow through the system during the episode, and serious macroeconomic consequences were avoided.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The final episode of financial instability I want to discuss is the market turbulence of the past few months.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Concerns originating in the subprime-mortgage sector sparked a pullback in risk-taking in a variety of markets.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As investors sought safety and liquidity, the issuance and trading of structured financial products slowed sharply or, in some cases, completely ceased; some asset-backed commercial paper could not be rolled over; yields in the Treasury bill market fluctuated considerably; and spreads in interbank funding markets rose to unusually high levels.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To prevent these problems from turning into a severe credit crunch for households and corporations alike, the Federal Reserve used several tools to inject liquidity into the system.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In particular, on August 10, the Federal Reserve announced that it would conduct open market operations necessary to promote trading in the interbank market at close to the target federal funds rate and noted that the discount window was available as a source of funding.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: On August 17, the Federal Reserve Board approved a reduction of 50 basis points in the discount window's primary-credit rate and announced changes in practices to allow the provision of term financing to depository institutions in solid financial condition for as long as thirty days.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Also, to help address the heightened safe-haven demands for Treasury securities, the Federal Reserve announced a temporary reductionââfrom 100 basis points to 50 basis pointsââin the minimum fee for borrowing securities from the System Open Market Account.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although market functioning has certainly not yet returned to normal, and while it is still too early to judge their ultimate success, these actions, along with the policy easing decided at the September FOMC meeting, have helped improve conditions in several short-term funding markets and instill confidence in investors that liquidity would be available if needed.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Policy Issues As I have just recounted, the Federal Reserve has been able to reduce the negative macroeconomic consequences of bouts of financial instability by providing liquidity to markets and institutions at times of need.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The provision of liquidity should thus be seen as a key tool for the Federal Reserve in its quest to achieve its statutory objectives of maximum sustainable employment and price stability.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The episodes I reviewed here also suggest that the more quickly liquidity can be provided when financial instability occurs, the more effective it may be.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I mentioned earlier, the Federal Reserve's quick response to the stock market crash of 1987 is noteworthy because it meant that only a small amount of liquidity, and no direct lending, was needed to restore normal market conditions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although the provision of liquidity is undoubtedly a useful tool, it is not without potential costs.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Improperly managed, it can lead to increased incentives for banks to take on excessive riskââthat is, it can create another form of moral hazard.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That additional moral hazard will worsen, rather than enhance, the stability of the financial system.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The risk of moral hazard increases if the central bank is perceived to be lending frequently to insolvent financial institutions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That concern, however, is addressed in the United States by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act of 1991, which establishes certain constraints on the Federal Reserve's ability to lend to troubled institutions, and by the guiding principle for the operation of the Federal Reserve's primary-credit facility, namely, to lend only to sound institutions and on good collateral.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 11 The need to limit moral hazard by not lending to insolvent institutions indicates that central banks must have information sufficient to determine whether an institution with access to the discount window is indeed healthy.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That consideration is one reason that central banks benefit from having some supervisory responsibility for institutions with access to the discount window (Mishkin, 1994; Bernanke, 2007).
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moral hazard could also arise when a central bank lends in response to liquidity problems, but I would argue that the risk of that happening might be lower than in the case of lending to troubled institutions.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: I have in mind situations in which markets become impaired for exogenous reasons.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In those circumstancesââwhen financial institutions that are otherwise perfectly solid are at risk of failure because market infrastructures are disrupted or, more generally, when financial instability originates outside the banking sectorââan intervention by the Federal Reserve would certainly be beneficial, and the creation of perverse incentives would probably be limited.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The traditional recommendation for the prevention of financial crises goes back to Thornton (1802) and Bagehot (1873), who argued that, during a panic, the central bank should be a lender of last resort that lends freely at a penalty rate.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Charging a penalty rate is another way to limit the possible moral hazard arising from liquidity provisions because it gives institutions an incentive to maintain liquidity sufficient to avoid borrowing at a high rate.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, the Federal Reserve's standing facility charges an interest rate above the target federal funds rate for exactly that reason (Madigan and Nelson, 2002).
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Thornton-Bagehot criterion is an important principle, but central banks must also determine the appropriate penalty rate to apply under the circumstances.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, when financial instability originates outside of the banking sector, liquidity made available to banks may allow them to channel funds to the part of the financial system that has seized up, thereby helping the recovery of that sector.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, that mechanism seems to have been at work during the Penn Central bankruptcy episode.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, if banks must pay a substantial penalty rate to acquire the extra liquidity, they may find it unprofitable to extend loans to the troubled sector.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In such circumstances, the central bank may judge that a lower penalty rate for borrowing at the discount window is warranted for a time.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Lowering the discount rate may also help underscore the central bank's intent to provide adequate liquidity to promote the functioning of financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve took just such an action on August 17 of this year, when it lowered the rate for primary credit by 50 basis points.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: When even depository institutions in sound financial condition are constrained in their access to funding because of information problems or operational disruptions, open market operations may be incapable of providing reserves to the specific banks in need of funding.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Having a discount facility at its disposal provides a central bank with a more targeted tool for coping with financial disturbances without promoting inflationary tendencies.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: But wouldn't lending at a reduced rate exacerbate moral hazard?
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: That seems to me to be unlikely so long as two fundamental principles are observed.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, any such lending should be temporary and implemented only in the highly unusual circumstance in which systemic risk is clearly present; that restriction should prevent market participants from expecting such lending to become a normal part of doing business (Brimmer, 1989).
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, commercial banksââto the extent that they lend out the funds obtained from the central bankââshould remain responsible for their own credit judgments, even in extreme situations.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conclusion The Congress has given the Federal Reserve a dual mandate to achieve both price stability and maximum sustainable employment.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve's role as a provider of liquidity to cope with episodes of financial instability has been, and will continue to be, critical to its success in achieving this mandate.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: How best to perform that role is something that both academics and policymakers will continue to think about for a long time.
speech_title: Financial Instability and the Federal Reserve as a Liquidity Provider
speech_venue: At the Museum of American Finance Commemoration of the Panic of 1907, New York, New York
