speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The key measures were the House Concurrent Resolution 133, in 1975; the Federal Reserve Reform Act of 1977; and the Full Employment and Balanced Growth Act of 1978 (the Humphrey-Hawkins Act).
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Gary Stern, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, and Janet Yellen, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, were the other members of the subcommittee.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic projections were first published in 1979 to fulfill the Board's legislated requirement to report on "prospects for the future."
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The projection period of the first three releases each year will cover the current year and the subsequent two years.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The fourth release each year will add a year to the projection horizon.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, the first three sets of projections in 2008 will be for the period 2008 through 2010, whereas the fourth set of projections will extend to 2011.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Participants will no longer provide projections for the growth of nominal GDP.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These now seem relatively less useful to the public, given participants' projections for real GDP growth and overall inflation.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The range for each variable in a given year includes all participants' projections, from lowest to highest, for that variable in the given year.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The central tendencies exclude the three highest and three lowest projections for each variable in each year.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A Board staff paper discussing the historical forecasting record of the Federal Reserve and other institutions will be released on November 20, simultaneously with the release of the expanded projections.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The historical data we will provide on forecast errors will starkly illustrate this point.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I thought it might be useful to start this session with a few thoughts on some of the issues facing central banks as they deal with the consequences of the recent turbulence in financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: 1 This list is not comprehensive:  I have concentrated on the issues associated with our roles as monetary policy makers and providers of liquidity--and even in that category I cannot address all the issues in the short time allotted.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Like every other period of financial turbulence, this one has been marked by considerable uncertainty.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Central banks, other authorities, and private-market participants must make decisions based on analyses made with incomplete information and understanding.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The repricing of assets is centered on relatively new instruments with limited histories--especially under conditions of stress; many of them are complex and have reacted to changing circumstances in unanticipated ways; and those newer instruments have been held by a variety of investors and intermediaries and traded in increasingly integrated global markets, thereby complicating the difficulty of seeing where risk is coming to rest.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Operating under this degree of uncertainty has many consequences.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: One is that the rules and criteria for taking particular actions seem a lot clearer in textbooks or to many commentators than they are to decisionmakers.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, the extent to which institutions are facing liquidity constraints as opposed to capital constraints, or the moral hazard consequences of policy actions, are inherently ambiguous in real time.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Another consequence of operating under a high degree of uncertainty is that, more than usually, the potential actions the Federal Reserve discusses have the character of "buying insurance" or managing risk--that is, weighing the possibility of especially adverse outcomes.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The nature of financial market upsets is that they substantially increase the risk of such especially adverse outcomes while possibly having limited effects on the most likely path for the economy.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Moral Hazard Central banks seek to promote financial stability while avoiding the creation of moral hazard.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: People should bear the consequences of their decisions about lending, borrowing, and managing their portfolios, both when those decisions turn out to be wise and when they turn out to be ill advised.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, however, in my view, when the decisions do go poorly, innocent bystanders should not have to bear the cost.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In general, I think those dual objectives--promoting financial stability and avoiding the creation of moral hazard--are best reconciled by central banks' focusing on the macroeconomic objectives of price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Asset prices will eventually find levels consistent with the economy producing at its potential, consumer prices remaining stable, and interest rates reflecting productivity and thrift.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Such a strategy would not forestall the correction of asset prices that are out of line with fundamentals or prevent investors from sustaining significant losses.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Losses were evident early in this decade in the case of many high-tech stocks, and they are in store for houses purchased at unsustainable prices and for mortgages made on the assumption that house prices would rise indefinitely.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, lowering interest rates to keep the economy on an even keel when adverse financial market developments occur will reduce the penalty incurred by some people who exercised poor judgment.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: But these people are still bearing the costs of their decisions and we should not hold the economy hostage to teach a small segment of the population a lesson.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The design of policies to achieve medium-term macroeconomic stability can affect the incentives for future risk-taking.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To minimize moral hazard, central banks should operate as much as possible through general instruments not aimed at individual institutions.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Open market operations fit this description, but so, too, can the discount window when it is structured to make credit available only to clearly solvent institutions in support of market functioning.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve's reduction of the discount rate penalty by 50 basis points in August followed this model.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: It was intended not to help particular institutions but rather to open up a source of liquidity to the financial system to complement open market operations, which deal with a more limited set of counterparties and collateral.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The Effects of Financial Markets on the Real Economy Related developments in housing and mortgage markets are a root cause of the financial market turbulence.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Expectations of ever-rising house prices along with increasingly lax lending standards, especially on subprime mortgages, created an unsustainable dynamic, which is now reversing.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In that reversal, loss and fear of loss on mortgage credit have impaired the availability of new mortgage loans, which in turn has reduced the demand for housing and put downward pressures on house prices, which have further damped desires to lend.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: We are following this trajectory closely, but key questions for central banks, including the Federal Reserve, are, What is happening to credit for other uses, and how much restraint are financial market developments likely to exert on demands outside the housing sector?
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Some broader repricing of risk is not surprising or unwelcome in the wake of unusually thin rewards for risk taking in several types of credit over recent years.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: And such a repricing in the form of wider spreads and tighter credit standards at banks and other lenders would make some types of credit more expensive and discourage some spending, developments that would require offsetting policy actions, other things being equal.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Some restraint on demand from this process was a factor I took into account when I considered the economic outlook and the appropriate policy responses over the past few months.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: An important issue now is whether concerns about losses on mortgages and some other instruments are inducing much greater restraint and thus constricting the flow of credit to a broad range of borrowers by more than seemed in train a month or two ago.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In general, nonfinancial businesses have been in very good financial condition; outside of variable-rate mortgages, households are meeting their obligations with, to date, only a little increase in delinquency rates, which generally remain at low levels.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Consequently, we might expect a moderate adjustment in the availability of credit to these key spending sectors.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the increased turbulence of recent weeks partly reversed some of the improvement in market functioning over the late part of September and in October.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Should the elevated turbulence persist, it would increase the possibility of further tightening in financial conditions for households and businesses.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Heightened concerns about larger losses at financial institutions now reflected in various markets have depressed equity prices and could induce more intermediaries to adopt a more defensive posture in granting credit, not only for house purchases, but for other uses a well.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Liquidity Provision and Bank Funding Markets Central banks have been confronting several issues in the provision of liquidity and bank funding.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: When the turbulence deepened in early August, demands for liquidity and reserves pushed overnight rates in interbank markets above monetary policy targets.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The aggressive provision of reserves by a number of central banks met those demands, and rates returned to targeted levels.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In the United States, strong bids by foreign banks in the dollar-funding markets early in the day have complicated our management of this rate.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: And demands for reserves have been more variable and less flexible in an environment of heightened uncertainty, thereby adding to volatility.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the Federal Reserve is limited in its ability to restrict the actual federal funds rate within a narrow band because we cannot, by law, pay interest on reserves for another four years.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, the term interbank funding markets have remained unsettled.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This is evident in the much wider spread between term funding rates--like libor--and the expected path of the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This is not solely a dollar-funding phenomenon--it is being experienced in euro and sterling markets to different degrees.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Many loans are priced off of these term funding rates, and the wider spreads are one development we have factored into our easing actions.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the behavior of these rates is symptomatic of caution among key marketmakers about taking and funding positions, and this is probably impeding the reestablishment of broader market trading liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Conditions in term markets have deteriorated some in recent weeks.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The deterioration partly reflects portfolio adjustments for the publication of year-end balance sheets.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Our announcement on Monday of term open market operations was designed to alleviate some of the concerns about year-end pressures.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The underlying causes of the persistence of relatively wide-term funding spreads are not yet clear.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Several factors probably have been contributing.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: One may be potential counterparty risk while the ultimate size and location of credit losses on subprime mortgages and other lending are yet to be determined.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Another probably is balance sheet risk or capital risk--that is, caution about retaining greater control over the size of balance sheets and capital ratios given uncertainty about the ultimate demands for bank credit to meet liquidity backstop and other obligations.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Favoring overnight or very short-term loans to other depositories and limiting term loans give banks the flexibility to reduce one type of asset if others grow or to reduce the entire size of the balance sheet to maintain capital leverage ratios if losses unexpectedly subtract from capital.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, banks may be worried about access to liquidity in turbulent markets.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Such a concern would lead to increased demands and reduced supplies of term funding, which would put upward pressure on rates.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This last concern is one that central banks should be able to address.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve attempted to deal with it when, as I already noted, we reduced the penalty for discount window borrowing 50 basis points in August and made term loans available.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The success of such a program lies not in loans extended but rather in the extent to which the existence of this facility helps reassure market participants.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In that regard, I think we had some success, at least for a time.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: But the usefulness of the discount window as a source of liquidity has been limited in part by banks' fears that their borrowing might be mistaken for accessing emergency loans for troubled institutions.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This "stigma" problem is not peculiar to the United States, and central banks, including the Federal Reserve, need to give some thought to how all their liquidity facilities can remain effective when financial markets are under stress.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Conclusion In response to developments in financial markets, the Federal Reserve has adjusted the stance of monetary policy and the parameters of how we supply liquidity to banks and the financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: These adjustments have been designed to foster price stability and maximum sustainable growth and to restore better functioning of financial markets in support of these economic objectives.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: My discussion today was intended to highlight some of the issues we will be looking at in financial markets as we weigh the necessity of future actions.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: We will need to assess the implications of these developments, along with the vast array of incoming information on economic activity and prices, for the future path of the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As the Federal Open Market Committee noted at its last meeting, uncertainties about the economic outlook are unusually high right now.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In my view, these uncertainties require flexible and pragmatic policymaking-- nimble is the adjective I used a few weeks ago.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In the conduct of monetary policy, as Chairman Bernanke has emphasized, we will act as needed to foster both price stability and full employment.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: These are my views and are not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Financial Markets and Central Banking
speech_venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The focus of my brief remarks this evening will be the Charlotte region and how the area and the economy have changed since I regularly visited my grandparents here some four-and-a-half decades ago.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, though, I would like to share a few thoughts on the U.S. economy and the considerations that we at the Federal Reserve will be weighing as we prepare for our policy meeting on December 11, less than two weeks from now.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the monetary policy making arm of the Federal Reserve System, last met on October 30-31.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: At that meeting, the Committee cut its target for the federal funds rate, the key policy interest rate, by 25 basis points (1/4 of a percentage point), following a cut of 50 basis points in September.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic growth in the period leading up to the October meeting had proven quite strong, as confirmed by this morningâs figures on third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP).
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: At its meeting, however, Committee members took the view that tightening credit conditions--the product of ongoing stresses in financial markets--and some intensification of the correction in the housing sector were likely to restrain economic activity going forward.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Specifically, growth appeared likely to slow significantly in the fourth quarter from its rapid third-quarter rate and to remain sluggish in early 2008.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Committee expected that economic growth would thereafter gradually return to a pace approaching its long-run trend as the drag from housing subsided and financial conditions improved.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Inflation was seen as edging down next year, approaching rates consistent with price stability; however, the Committee remained concerned about the possible effects of higher energy costs and the lower foreign exchange value of the dollar, especially the risk that they might lead to an increase in the publicâs long-term inflation expectations.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: How has the economic picture changed in the month since that meeting?
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As is often the case, the incoming economic data have been mixed.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the market for residential real estate, indicators of construction and home sales have continued to be weak.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In contrast, the labor market remained solid in October, with some 130,000 new jobs added to private-sector payrolls and the unemployment rate remaining at 4.7 percent.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Claims for unemployment insurance have drifted up a bit in recent weeks, although, on average, they have remained at a level consistent with moderate expansion in employment.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will, of course, have the labor market report for November next week, and in the coming days we will continue to draw on anecdotal reports, surveys, and other sources of information about employment and wages.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Continued good performance by the labor market is important for maintaining the economic expansion, as growth in earnings helps to underpin household spending.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: With respect to household spending, the data received over the past month have been on the soft side.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Committee will have considerable additional information on consumer purchases and sentiment to digest before its next meeting.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I expect household income and spending to continue to grow, but the combination of higher gas prices, the weak housing market, tighter credit conditions, and declines in stock prices seem likely to create some headwinds for the consumer in the months ahead.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Core inflation--that is, inflation excluding the relatively more volatile prices of food and energy--has remained moderate.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the price of crude oil has continued its rise over the past month, a rise that will be reflected in gasoline and heating oil prices and, of course, in the overall inflation rate in the near term.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, increases in food prices and in the prices of some imported goods have the potential to put additional pressures on inflation and inflation expectations.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The effectiveness of monetary policy depends critically on maintaining the publicâs confidence that inflation will be well controlled.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: We are accordingly monitoring inflation developments closely.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The incoming data on economic activity and prices will help to shape the Committeeâs outlook for the economy; however, the outlook has also been importantly affected over the past month by renewed turbulence in financial markets, which has partially reversed the improvement that occurred in September and October.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors have focused on continued credit losses and write-downs across a number of financial institutions, prompted in many cases by credit-rating agenciesâ downgrades of securities backed by residential mortgages.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The fresh wave of investor concern has contributed in recent weeks to a decline in equity values, a widening of risk spreads for many credit products (not only those related to housing), and increased short-term funding pressures.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: These developments have resulted in a further tightening in financial conditions, which has the potential to impose additional restraint on activity in housing markets and in other credit-sensitive sectors.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Needless to say, the Federal Reserve is following the evolution of financial conditions carefully, with particular attention to the question of how strains in financial markets might affect the broader economy.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In sum, as I have indicated, we will be receiving a good deal of relevant information in the coming days.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In making its policy decision, the Committee will have to judge whether the outlook for the economy or the balance of risks has shifted materially.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In doing so, we will take full account of the implications for the outlook of both the incoming economic data and the ongoing developments in the financial markets.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic forecasting is always difficult, but the current stresses in financial markets make the uncertainty surrounding the outlook even greater than usual.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: We at the Federal Reserve will have to remain exceptionally alert and flexible as we continue to assess how best to promote sustainable economic growth and price stability in the United States.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Charlotte and the Carolinas : Personal Connections Iâd like now to speak a bit about Charlotte and the region from a personal as well as an economic perspective.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: My family has a long connection with Charlotte.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: My maternal grandparents, originally immigrants from Eastern Europe, moved here from Connecticut when my mother was a teenager, and she finished high school here.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: My parents met while attending different campuses of the University of North Carolina--my father at UNC-Chapel Hill, my mother at UNC-Greensboro (then a womenâs college).
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I was raised from early childhood in the small town of Dillon, South Carolina, about two hours from here.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: My family settled in Dillon because my paternal grandfather bought a drug store there in 1941, and my father and his brother followed in his footsteps as town pharmacists.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In Dillon, a town that was always very short of the more regular kind of doctor, my father and uncle were popularly known as Dr. Phil and Dr. Mort, and the prescriptions they dispensed were often accompanied by their free advice on maintaining good health.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I often visited my maternal grandparentsâ home on Cumberland Avenue in Charlotte, sometimes with my parents and sometimes on my own, and I have many fond memories of those visits.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: A short walk from their home was a park where my grandfather often took me to feed the ducks that lived on a lake there.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The name of that spot--Freedom Park--was sufficiently like my grandparentsâ surname--Friedman--for me as a small child to conclude that it was actually called Friedman Park.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I was suitably impressed by the honor the city authorities had apparently given my grandparents.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Grandpa Friedman taught me to play chess when I was five or six; he let me win at first, but after a few years I was no longer a pushover, and the games became very, very serious.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Grandma Friedman was a wonderful cook, and if you dig deep enough into the archives of the Charlotte Observer, you will find a large photo of a much younger me under the headline, âBen Loves Grandmaâs Blintzes,â together with her recipe for that dish.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Unfortunately, my grandmother died when I was thirteen, and when my grandfather came to live with us in Dillon, the regular trips to Charlotte ended.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I am pleased to say, though, that my connection to this city has since been re-established, as my parents have retired to Charlotte, and my brother (a lawyer in town) and his family live here, too.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: So I still feel like an honorary Charlottean as well as a Carolinian.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In my periodic visits to the Carolinas, I have been enormously impressed by the social and economic changes that have emerged in what has aptly been called the New South.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: This transformation has not been easy.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In Dillon in the 1960s, I attended a segregated public school; but I did have African-American friends, and one of them was instrumental in persuading me to attend Harvard University--a critical step, as it turned out, in my life and career.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Now, in Dillon, Charlotte, and elsewhere in the Carolinas, I see increasing cooperation among people of different races and backgrounds to achieve common civic and economic goals.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Transformation of the Economy in the Carolinas Economically speaking, Carolinians have faced the same challenge confronting many other parts of the country, that is, to replace jobs lost in old-line manufacturing industries by creating jobs in services such as health care and hospitality while simultaneously adapting to globalization and advancing technology.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Here as elsewhere, the Carolinas have met this challenge through education and by building on regional strengths.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As Iâve stressed on previous occasions, the quality of the workforce is the single most important factor in an economyâs success.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In a rapidly changing world, economically valuable skills can be maintained only through learning that extends beyond traditional schooling to encompass training and re-training well into the middle years of life.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: North Carolina offers a good example of these trends.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the past decade, the state has lost about one-third of the manufacturing jobs it had at the beginning of the decade--a loss of about 250,000 jobs.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: About 60 percent of the losses occurred in the textile and apparel industries.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the textile mills in particular, employment across the state is down two-thirds from the level of ten years ago.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the furniture industry, which accounts for the largest share of the remaining job losses in North Carolina manufacturing, employment in the state has dropped from 82,000 in 1999 to less than 51,000.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Charlotte area itself has experienced a number of plant closings, including the 2003 shutdown of the Pillowtex plant in nearby Kannapolis.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: There is, of course, another side to the coin of economic change here.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Despite losing an average of 25,000 manufacturing jobs each year over the past decade, North Carolina has managed a net increase of 44,000 jobs per year in total nonfarm employment over the same period.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Those two numbers together imply that, on average, North Carolina has enjoyed an annual net gain of 69,000 nonmanufacturing jobs.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The largest net increases have been in education and health care, professional and business services, and the leisure and hospitality sector.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, like many other vibrant regions of the country, the Charlotte area has grown by developing a high-productivity service economy.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, what happened to the former Pillowtex site itself is a good metaphor for the transformation under way in the region.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Though the loss of manufacturing jobs is painful, the ongoing development of the Pillowtex site as the North Carolina Research Campus illustrates this regionâs ability to shift resources from industries that are shrinking to those that are expanding The North Carolina Research Campus is a public-private, 350-acre life sciences hub near Charlotte that includes partnerships with Duke University, the University of North Carolina, the North Carolina Community College System, and other institutions of higher education.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: This is one high-profile example, but the transformation has also been happening in less dramatic fashion through the development of hundreds of smaller businesses throughout the region.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even within the manufacturing sector, a number of firms--typically smaller operations with relatively few employees--have begun to exploit nontraditional niches.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some recent examples of emerging industrial operations across the state include primary metal manufacturing, machinery production, and the manufacture of nonwoven fabrics (Employment Security Commission of North Carolina, 2007).
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: That last category includes a remarkably wide variety of engineered fabrics, ranging from those used to make doctorsâ and nursesâ operating-room garb to some used in roofing materials; those products are especially interesting because they represent a small but fast-growing segment of specialty textiles within the broader textile industry.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The transformation of this region has been aided by its reputation as a desirable location in which to live and work.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Census data and statistics from interstate moving companies indicate a heavy flow of people moving into Charlotte from other states, including large numbers of educated workers.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Overall, the area has gained an average of 39,000 net new residents every year since 1997.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: (You probably feel that you see all those people every day in traffic.)
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Without a doubt, Charlotteâs status as one of the preeminent financial centers of the country lies behind much of the inflow.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importance of Charlotte as a Financial Services Center Charlotteâs roots as a financial center stretch back two centuries.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: From 1800 to 1848, the city was the center of U.S. gold production, and a branch of the U.S. Mint operated here from 1837 to 1913.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: More recently, North Carolinaâs legal framework has been important to the growth of the banking system.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because the state had long allowed in-state branch banking, homegrown banks here had a head start when interstate banking became possible--first regionally, in the mid-1980s, and then nationally with the 1994 passage of the Riegle-Neal Interstate Banking and Branching Efficiency Act (Hills, 2007).
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: North Carolinaâs early adoption of branch banking is a good example of a âfirst moverâ gaining a strategic advantage.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The banking statutes allowed banks in North Carolina to become larger than their counterparts in other states and helped them develop expertise in running larger branch networks.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The result has been a rapid increase in the size of banks located in the state: In 1970, only three banks from the entire South, including two from North Carolina, were among the fifty largest U.S. banks ranked by assets, today, three of the top ten U.S. banks are headquartered in Charlotte alone (Hills, 2007).

speaker: Bernanke
text: One of the key advantages of Charlotte and other metropolitan centers in North Carolina has been the ability to attract and retain educated workers: Among adults aged 25 or older, 31 percent in metro centers hold at least a bachelorâs degree, versus 17 percent in rural areas (U.S. Census Bureau, 2006).

speaker: Bernanke
text: In some cases, growing urban areas like Charlotte are the beneficiaries of a positive dynamic: The cityâs modern, service-oriented economy attracts skilled and educated workers; the presence of a skilled workforce attracts new firms to the area and also promotes the development of amenities such as high-end restaurants and cultural activities; these opportunities and amenities then attract additional highly skilled workers.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Challenge of Education in North Carolina Cities like Charlotte will probably continue to attract highly educated and skilled workers from other areas of the country, but improving the skills of local workers--especially those displaced by industries in decline--remains critical for both urban and rural areas in the state.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Four-year institutions play an important role in meeting that challenge, but they are not the sole means for developing workforce skills.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, in the 2004-05 school year, the North Carolina Community College System served nearly 780,000 students in fifty-eight institutions.

speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The average community college student in the state is thirty years old and likely working while attending school (North Carolina Community College System, 2006).
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because they offer education closely tailored to employer demands in the local workplace, community colleges in North Carolina, as elsewhere, play an essential role in training and retraining workers.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, they do so at a relatively low cost.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In general, we must move beyond the view that education is something that takes place only in K-through-12 schools and four-year colleges, as important as those are.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Education and skills must be provided flexibly and to people of any age.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will close my comments on education with a pitch for financial literacy.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
speech_venue: At the presentation of the Citizen of the Carolinas Award, Charlotte Chamber of Commerce, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In todayâs complex financial marketplace, a basic understanding of financial tools and markets and an appreciation of the need to budget, save, invest, and borrow wisely are critical to the financial health of every individual.

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Branch has active partnerships with organizations involved in financial literacy and economic education, including among others Jump$tart, Junior Achievement, LifeSmarts, Communities in Schools, the North Carolina Council on Economic Education, and the North Carolina Bankers Association.
speech_title: National and regional economic overview
