speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, given PCE inflation of about 1-1/2 percent to 2 percent, the âtrueâ inflation rate faced by consumers might well be less than 1 percent.
speech_title: The Federal Reserveâs Enhanced Communication Strategy and the Science of Monetary Policy
speech_venue: To the Undergraduate Economics Association, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, Massachusetts

speaker: Kroszner
text: In my remarks today, I would like to explore the role of information in the development of new financial products and then draw some lessons about risk management and regulation.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In particular, I will examine the role that investment in information gathering, processing, and evaluating plays in supporting the price discovery process and how such investment can lead toward a tendency to greater standardization as markets for innovative financial products mature.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Examples from both history and current experience will help to illustrate this tendency with respect to loan work-outs and restructurings.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: I will then conclude by considering how a regulatory approach that encourages transparency and sound risk management, such as Basel II, can be valuable in fostering a robust environment for the introduction of innovative financial products.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Experimentation and Learning in New Instrument Development Typically, when a new product is being developed, there is an initial experimentation phase in which market participants learn a great deal about the productâs performance and risk characteristics.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This phase involves gathering and processing information and modeling the performance of the product in various scenarios and under different market conditions.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: It may then take time for market participants to understand what, exactly, they need to know to value a product.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: During the early phases, a fair amount of due diligence is appropriate, given the greater uncertainty associated with innovative products.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The investment in gathering, processing, and evaluating information then, as I will discuss, often leads to greater standardization of products and contract terms, which can enhance liquidity of products as their markets mature.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the initial experimentation phase, the terms and characteristics of a new product are adjusted in response to market acceptance--or lack thereof.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: During this period, market participants are seeking and providing information so that they can properly value the product, judge its potential for risk and return, assess its market acceptance and liquidity, and determine the extent to which the risks of the product can be hedged or mitigated.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: When a productâs track record is not well established, there should be a strong market demand for information in order to facilitate price discovery.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Price discovery is the process by which buyersâ and sellersâ preferences, as well as any other available market information, result in the âdiscoveryâ of a price that will balance supply and demand and provide signals to market participants about how most efficiently to allocate resources.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This market-determined price will, of course, be subject to change as new information becomes available, as preferences evolve, as expectations are revised, and as costs of production change.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In order for this process to work most effectively, market participants must utilize information relevant to value that product.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, searching out and using relevant sources of information--as well as determining what information is relevant--has its own costs.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: To underscore the last point, with new instruments, it may not even be clear exactly what information is needed for price discovery--that is, some market participants may not know what they do not know and they may therefore terminate the information-gathering stage prematurely, unwittingly bearing the risks and costs of incomplete information.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Price Discovery Due diligence is an important part of the price discovery process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The due-diligence process allows market participants to âtrust but verifyâ market-provided information through a range of activities, from assessing risks and exposures through stress-testing to assessing the enforceability of the contracts that define the legal relationship among originators, sponsors, investors, and guarantors.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The due diligence is complemented by risk-management structures that allow participants to interpret, understand, and act appropriately in response to the information in the market.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recently we have seen how a lack of information and inadequate due diligence and risk management have created problems in the market for certain structured finance products.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Let me focus a moment on structured investment vehicles, or SIVs.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: SIVs have been created with a variety of terms and characteristics--for example, different underlying assets, different levels of liquidity support or guarantees, and various triggers that require the forced sale of assets or liquidation of the structure.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Although SIVs or similar vehicles have existed for many years, many recent SIV structures involved a much higher level of complexity of the underlying credit risks, legal structures, and operations.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This complexity--and the lack of information about where the underlying credit, legal, and operational risks resided--made these products more difficult and costly to value than many investors originally thought.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Investors suddenly realized that they were much less informed than they assumed and, not surprisingly, they pulled back from the market.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have seen similar problems in the subprime residential mortgage-backed securities market and the related derivatives markets.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The lack of long historical data on the performance of these instruments, and their correlations with other assets and instruments, made it difficult to assess their overall risk-return profile, especially in times of stress.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, in the subprime residential mortgage-backed securities market, many market participants were willing to proceed without conducting robust due diligence and without establishing appropriate risk-management structures and processes.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: They did not follow âtrust but verify,â that is, they instead accepted the investment-grade ratings of these securities as substitutes for their own risk analysis.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ratings keyed to expected default or credit loss do not adequately capture the full range or magnitude of risks to which a product may be subject, including--as we have seen most dramatically--market liquidity risks.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, some originators may not have demanded sufficient information about the purchased assets underlying these structures and therefore may not have fully appreciated the credit risk of the assets and the consequential risk that the structures would come back on balance sheet when the assets defaulted.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: When the problems in the subprime mortgage market began to emerge and delinquencies exceeded rating agency estimates and the defaults predicted by limited historical data, we had moved beyond our past experience with these instruments.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Information was not readily available about the extent to which the economic context had changed, or even whether underlying loans would or could be modified to prevent default.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: When ratings were downgraded, investors lost confidence in the quality of the ratings and hence the quality of the information they had about subprime investments.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Lack of information, a disrupted price-discovery process, and a stressed environment led to a reassessment of risk, not only in the subprime market but also in the residential mortgage market across the board.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, this is not the first time that participants in a market for an innovative product have suffered losses.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the early 1990s, participants in the collateralized mortgage obligation (CMO) market and the markets for structured notes and certain types of interest rate derivatives did not have adequate information about the potential volatility and prepayment risk involved.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consequently, market participants did not appropriately model these risks and suffered significant losses when market interest rates rose sharply in the mid-1990s.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: As in the case of the residential mortgage-backed securities market today, the general market reaction was a flight away from these instruments.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, over time, the market was restored as market participants came to better understand the risks and as standardized methods were developed to measure the risks and model the value of these instruments under alternative scenarios.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Increased information and standardized pricing conventions, such as the use of option-adjusted spreads, moved these instruments from the experimentation and learning phase to the phase of broad market acceptance.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: When market participants realize that they do not have the information necessary for proper valuation of risks, the price-discovery process can be disrupted, and market liquidity can become impaired.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: A significant investment in information gathering, processing, and evaluation may be necessary to revive the price discovery process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This revival is likely to take time and the market may not look the same when it re-emerges.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Let me describe in a bit more detail the ways in which these investments will take place and hence why recovery of price discovery may be a gradual process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, market participants will likely need to collect more-detailed data in a more systematic manner in order to better understand the nature and risks of the instruments and their underlying assets.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, investments in enhanced systems to warehouse and model data related to these instruments will facilitate a better understanding of their risks, particularly under stress conditions.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, investors need to ensure that they have the so-called human capital expertise--that is, the people--to understand, interpret, and act appropriately on the results of the modeling and analysis of the information gathered.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The pay-off from these investments will be a greater understanding of risks and greater ability to value the instruments.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Development of Greater Standardization in a Market Another consequence of information investments is a tendency towards greater standardization of many of the aspects of an instrument, which can help to increase transparency and reduce complexity.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: As was demonstrated in the CMO market, as the market gains information about a product and develops a level of confidence in that information, the product tends to become increasingly standardized.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Standardization in the terms and in the contractual rights and obligations of purchasers and sellers of the product reduces the need for market participants to engage in extensive efforts to obtain information and reduces the need to verify the information that is provided in the market through due diligence.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Reduced information costs in turn lower transaction costs, thereby facilitating price discovery and enhancing market liquidity.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Also, standardization can reduce legal risks because litigation over contract terms can result in case law that applies to similar situations, thus reducing uncertainty.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The benefits of the development of standardization for enhancing the liquidity of financial markets have a long history.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: One particularly clear example dates back to the development of exchange-traded commodities futures contracts in the mid-1800s.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The standardization of the futures markets improved the flow of information to market participants, reducing transaction costs and fostering the emergence of liquid markets.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the early days of the Chicago Board of Trade, in the mid-1850s, standardization took the form of creating âgradesâ or quality categories for commodities such as wheat, allowing for the fungibility of grains stored in elevators and warehouses, and breaking the link between ownership rights and specific lots of a physical commodity.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Traders no longer needed to verify that a certain quantity of grain was of a sufficiently high grade because the exchange established a system of internal controls in the form of grain inspectors and a self-regulatory system to arbitrate disputes.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The grain inspectors charged a set fee to certify the quality of the grain for any receipt traded at the board, a system with parallels to the mechanisms employed today by the rating agencies.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In effect, standardization and related controls reduced tradersâ information requirements and, thus, their transaction costs.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In 1865, the Chicago Board of Trade standardized the delivery dates for the contracts, thus fostering the emergence of liquid markets in which traders could readily hedge the risk of price changes in the commodities and contracts.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: A final step toward standardization came years later with the adoption of the clearinghouse for the exchange as the common counterparty to all of the contracts traded on the exchange.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: With a central counterparty, the costs and uncertainties of failures and restructurings were significantly reduced, thereby reducing work-out costs and enhancing liquidity of the contracts traded on the exchange.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The benefits of standardization can be realized not only on organized exchanges but also in over-the-counter markets.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In more recent times, for example, the creation of the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement for over-the-counter swaps and derivatives contracts has brought about the benefits of standardization while also allowing for product flexibility and customization.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The ISDA master agreement provides standard definitions and a general outline for the contract but allows latitude in customizing terms.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The master agreement also sets forth a template for workout procedures if a counterparty defaults, allowing parties to the agreement to adjust their risk-management strategies in light of the agreed-upon work-out process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This standardization reduces uncertainty about the instruments, which lowers transaction costs and facilitates price discovery and market liquidity.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The examples from the long- and more recent- past may hold some valuable lessons for how improvements in standardization could help to address some of the challenges in the subprime market.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Uncertainty about the work-out process and the options that are available, for example, could be contributing to the difficulties in reviving price discovery and liquidity in the market for subprime residential mortgage-backed securities.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Part of the valuation challenge is gauging the extent of the difficulties that borrowers will have in making payments and being able to stay in their homes given the reduction in house price appreciation--or actual declines in some areas--and the large number of interest rate resets coming on many adjustable-rate mortgages.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: From now until the end of next year, monthly payments for an average of roughly 450,000 subprime mortgages per quarter are scheduled to undergo their first interest rate reset.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, tightening credit conditions as reported in the Federal Reserveâs Senior Loan Officer Opinion Surveys on Bank Lending Practices suggest that refinancing may become more difficult.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Lenders and servicers generally would want to work with borrowers to avoid foreclosure, which, according to industry estimates, can lead to a loss of as much as 40 percent to 50 percent of the unpaid mortgage balance.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Loss mitigation techniques that preserve homeownership are typically less costly than foreclosure, particularly when applied before default.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Borrowers who have been current in their payments but could default after reset may be able to work with their lender or servicer to adjust their payments or otherwise change their loans to make them more manageable.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is imperative that we work together as a financial services community to look for ways to help borrowers address their mortgage challenges, particularly for those who may have fewer alternatives, such as lower-income families.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve and other regulators have been active in encouraging lenders and servicers to take a proactive approach to work with borrowers who may be at risk of losing their homes.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, the agencies have issued statements underscoring that prudent workout arrangements that are consistent with safe and sound lending practices are generally in the long-term best interest of both the investor and the borrower and have had numerous meetings with interested parties to foster the development and implementation of work-out arrangements.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Given the substantial number of resets from now through the end of 2008, I believe it would behoove the industry to go further than it has to join together and explore collaborative, creative efforts to develop prudent loan modification programs and other assistance to help large groups of borrowers systematically.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am not suggesting a one-size-fits-all approach, but a bottom-up approach designed to appropriately balance the needs of all parties.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Getting to borrowers who have been making payments but are at risk of falling behind before they actually do become delinquent, for example, can help to preserve work-out and refinancing options.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some industry participants and consumer groups have begun to work collaboratively to develop loan-modification templates, standards, and principles that can help to streamline the work-out and modification process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This can reduce transaction costs and potentially provide timely relief to a wider range of borrowers.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: A systematic approach to loan modifications would likely reduce some of the uncertainties in the market for such subprime mortgage-backed securities, helping to restore price-discovery and liquidity.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This would help to ease the tightening of credit conditions in the market.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am privileged to serve as a board member of NeighborWorks America, a national nonprofit that partners with the HOPE NOW Alliance.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: This alliance is developing ways to facilitate the flow of information between servicers and distressed borrowers and to work toward clarification of loan-modification procedures.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Increased standardization and certainty could also benefit investors in the mortgage market by improving information flows and the price-discovery process, thereby improving market liquidity while at the same time helping to avoid foreclosures and promoting sustainable homeownership.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: A Regulatory Environment That Encourages Sound Risk Management and Transparency Recent market events have underscored the need for better market information about new products, robust due diligence to verify that information, and risk-management strategies to utilize the information in management decisionmaking.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The supervisory agencies and the industry both are addressing the need for improved risk management in light of the market disruptions
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The newly adopted Basel II capital framework for large internationally-active banking organizations, for example, is an important advance that encourages the types of investment in information I discussed earlier.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Basel II framework is comprised of three pillars.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Pillar 1 requires information gathering and robust modeling techniques to better take into account the risks of different types of instruments and securities than under the traditional Basel I framework.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: It also provides incentives for more robust risk management in connection with certain higher-risk activities, such as securitization and other off-balance-sheet activities.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Pillar 2 emphasizes the further stress testing and analysis of the data in conjunction with an ongoing evaluation of the institutionâs capital adequacy in light of its risks through the internal capital adequacy assessment process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: Pillar 3 reflects the need for better information through investments in data gathering and analysis that are reflected in enhanced public disclosures and regulatory reporting.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: More-comprehensive and more-transparent information allows investors to better understand the banking organizationâs risk profile and thus reduces transaction costs and facilitates price discovery and market liquidity.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: The three pillars of Basel II promote precisely the three types of investment in information discussed earlier that facilitate the price discovery process.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition to supervisory initiatives, industry leadersâ efforts to influence the adoption of sound practices and codes of conduct can efficiently and effectively facilitate market-correcting behaviors.
speech_title: Innovation, Information, and Regulation in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Philadelphia Fed Policy Forum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

speaker: Kohn
text: This panel is dealing with an important topic--in effect, the design and functioning of monetary policy committees.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Monetary policy decisions are judgment calls, informed by forecasts and discussions about how the economy is likely to evolve, alternative possibilities, and potential responses to policy actions.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The question is how to bring the best possible judgments to bear on these questions.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Besley, Meads and Surico's contribution is to ask whether certain characteristics of the policymakers matter for how they vote on the monetary policy committee.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) at the Bank of England, they find heterogeneous views among voters, but no systematic differences based on whether the MPC member is an insider--that is part of the hierarchy at the Bank--or an outsider appointed for a short term just to the MPC; whether the person comes from an academic background; or whether that person has worked at the Treasury.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I found the piece well done and interesting, and I have only a few comments before moving on to some questions and observations about the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sparked by reading this research.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: My first comment is that I'm not surprised by the results.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The MPC has a well-defined objective given by the government.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, members may differ about the precise time frame in which to meet that objective, but these distinctions should be small relative to the importance of the overall objective.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, at every policy meeting, each member of the MPC is operating with the same information from the staff, and before the quarterly meetings that precede an Inflation Report, the members have sat through a number of discussions covering all aspects of the forecast.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Everyone should be equally familiar with the key issues and analysis.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, dissent is accepted, indeed encouraged in some respects, by insiders as well as outsiders, reducing any differences in incentives facing the two groups.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, some aspects of the paper raised questions in my mind about the robustness of the results.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For one, the authors, in testing for differences in policy preferences, assume everyone has the same forecast, thus eliminating one channel through which different backgrounds may manifest themselves.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The MPC does go through an extensive internal process when producing its forecast, which as I just noted, may mitigate the differences among members.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Still, some of the differences in policy choices probably reflect underlying differences in forecasts, not just differences in Taylor-rule parameters.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Certainly, the minutes of the MPC meetings suggest divergence in how members view the outlook, and the Inflation Report routinely notes differences in views about the central tendency forecasts.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Small differences, especially if sustained over time, could well have a substantial effect on voting patterns.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In practice, policy decisions are likely to depend on more than the modal forecast used by the authors, such as the degree of uncertainty, the risks around the central tendency, and a weighting of the costs to public welfare from missing the forecast on one side or another.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In this regard, the Inflation Reports also note that members may have different views about the balance of risks.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I don't know how the authors could go about testing whether the backgrounds of MPC members are systematically related to differences in forecasts or in risk assessments, but surely these are important possibilities.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I was also struck by the finding that the output gap did not play a significant role in policy decisions.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: As the paper notes, the MPC takes account of the gap in its inflation forecast, but the results suggest members give no independent weight to deviations of output from potential.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: On the surface, this may suggest that either the MPC has faced only demand shocks--unlikely given the rise in energy prices--or it is not really a flexible inflation targeter.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, figure 1, column 3, indicates that many MPC members have significantly negative coefficients on the output gap.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I suspect the reality is that members rely on much more than the projected output gap to judge the future balance of demand and potential supply, but the econometric results on the output gap suggest the need for further explanation.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, the authors find that the change in the policy rate at the last meeting matters for each person's vote at the current meeting.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: It is not clear why the decision to change rates at the last meeting should affect judgments on the appropriate policy at the current meeting, independent of the outlook.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Perhaps the dissenters believe they've made their point and unless they feel especially strongly they don't need to dissent again, but the rationale for this variable should probably be explored further.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The purpose of bringing outsiders onto the policy committee of the Bank of England is to assure that a variety of views will be considered in the policy debate.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I'll spend the rest of my time addressing how this works at the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I'll do this in the form of questions about the personnel and functioning of the FOMC, with my tentative answers.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Does it matter who is on the FOMC other than the Chairman?
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: My answer is yes, and I think I have reasons other than simple self-esteem.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, the Committee looks to the Chairman to provide strong leadership.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The Chairman's special role is partly legal and structural--as the chair of the Board and the Committee and as the Committee's representative in front of Congress where the FOMC is held accountable for its actions.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the Committee is so large--in effect nineteen people--that strong leadership is required to construct a policy position that can command a substantial majority and to present a coherent rationale for that policy to the public.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But in my experience, the other members of the Committee are also important for good policy.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Effective Chairmen cannot operate independently of the sentiment on the Committee; ultimately, the authority of the Chairman rests on his ability to persuade the other members of the Committee that the choices they are making under his leadership will accomplish their objectives.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The better the collection of individuals he needs to persuade, the better the policy is likely to be.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Individual members can exert considerable influence over time through the cogency of their arguments, and having a variety of perspectives on the Committee will strengthen this process.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, all FOMC members play important roles in explaining policy decisions to the public, and how they present their views can influence public attitudes, perceptions, and expectations.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Are there insider/outsider types of distinctions on the FOMC?
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Although the process by which people come onto the Committee leads naturally to considerable diversity, the insider/outsider distinction does not apply cleanly to the FOMC.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Board members of course are appointed by the President with the approval of the Senate.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The members of the Board are almost always outsiders--the appointment of a staff member, like myself, is very rare.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And Board members typically come from a variety of backgrounds, including top-notch academic economists, but also bankers and others with experience in the financial arena, and occasionally business people.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: We are appointed for fixed terms, encouraging independent views.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Reserve Bank presidents owe their appointments to both the board of directors of their regional Reserve Bank and the Board of Governors in Washington.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Presidents can be either insiders--long-time staff members--or outsiders with relevant experience in academia, public policy, or the financial sector.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Once appointed, a president can serve until retirement at age 65 or for a minimum of ten years, affording scope for maintaining their individual views.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, FOMC members try to find consensus under the leadership of the Chairman, and neither Governors nor presidents dissent very often.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Presidents have tended to dissent a little more than Governors.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The greater number of dissents by presidents might reflect a number of factors.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For one, presidents have their own staffs, which can help support alternative views in preparing for a meeting.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Board members share a common staff with the Chairman, and, being in the same building, perhaps have a greater opportunity to influence and be influenced by the Chairman.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In this regard, Bank presidents may act like "outsiders" more readily than Board members.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, Bank presidents tend to be longer tenured than Board members, and can contribute the institutional memory one might expect from "insiders" when Board membership turns over rapidly.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: FOMC members recognize the degree of uncertainty around their judgments.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Unless they perceive that a serious misjudgment is being made, they expect, given common objectives, that when they prefer another policy and their analysis later proves correct, the Committee is likely to move in their direction in time to forestall problems developing.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And they may see their influence on policy as greater over time if they are usually part of the consensus.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, they could perceive that a series of close votes could create uncertainty about policy and the direction of the institution.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The absence of dissents should not be taken as indicating that alternative views are not expressed at FOMC meetings.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Often these are manifest in participants' forecasts.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Because we are such a large and geographically separated Committee, the FOMC, unlike the MPC, does not attempt to arrive at a common forecast, and the dispersion of individual forecasts illustrates the range of views.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, participants' projections in October of gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 2008 differed by one full percentage point and differences were still a half a percentage point for 2010.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Participants had alternative views about current developments affecting the economy and about its long-run growth properties, and they argued their points in the meeting.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, all but one of the voting members was able to agree that the action taken that day was consistent with moving the economy toward meeting the Committee's objectives.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Do you need to be a monetary policy expert to contribute?
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The Committee is strengthened by having people with a wide variety of backgrounds, including those whose principal area of expertise of lies outside of monetary economics.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: To some extent, the range of backgrounds on the FOMC reflects the need for expertise to carry out the non-monetary policy responsibilities of the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Any monetary policy committee needs to have a number of people on it that fully understand and can deal readily with the model behind policy deliberations, and who have an awareness of the lessons of monetary policy history.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But other types of expertise also are valuable.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Policy works through financial markets, and those with that background contribute to understanding how policy impulses are being transmitted to savers and spenders.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Experience in private industry is valuable for gathering and interpreting information from many business sources that we bring to FOMC deliberations.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Any member needs to understand the basic framework to have influence on the debate.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But you don't need to be a monetary policy expert.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Those who come on the Committee with policy credentials can be very effective immediately.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But judgment and experience count.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Noneconomists can become very effective as they learn the lingo and the framework.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The large size of the Committee and long tenure of members allows time and space for this expertise to develop.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: One of the most difficult aspects of policymaking is recognizing what you don't know, perhaps because the world is no longer conforming to your models.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: A high level of monetary policy expertise is not necessarily a good guide to who will possess that skill.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Conclusion The proof of the pudding is in the eating.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Since the late 1970s in the United States and since the establishment of the MPC in the United Kingdom, economic performance in both countries has, on balance, been good.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: A number of factors have contributed to this result, but the respective monetary policy committees must have played some role.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, in the United States, the leadership of Chairmen Volcker, Greenspan, and Bernanke has been critical to the results, but I believe a diverse and independent minded group of policymakers has contributed as well, and it is important to maintain this mix and quality.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Could the functioning of the FOMC be improved?
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Certainly, and Chairman Bernanke has moved to further utilize the diverse views of the FOMC members, while maintaining the leadership necessary to keep this diverse group headed in the appropriate direction.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
