text: The views expressed here are my own and not necessarily shared by other members of the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Expertise and Macroeconomic Policy, Comments on "Insiders versus Outsiders in Monetary Policy-Making," by Timothy Besley, Neil Meads, and Paolo Surico
speech_venue: At the American Economic Association Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Good communication is essential to successful central banking.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: It is critical to preserving the democratic accountability and public legitimacy of central banks that, for good reasons, have been granted a high degree of insulation from short-run political pressures.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And good communication strengthens the effectiveness of good policy, largely because expectations are so important to the choices that households and businesses make about spending and saving and about prices and wages, as well as to the asset prices that help shape those choices.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Private decisions are more likely to reinforce the achievement of central bank objectives if decisionmakers understand the goals of the central bank, its evaluation of the forces bearing on the economy, and its possible responses to economic shocks.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Good communication is a complement to good policy, not a substitute for it.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Ultimately, central banks are judged on the outcomes for the economy--how well they meet their objectives.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: No amount of well-designed communication can counter the effects of consistently deficient analysis or poorly judged policy choices.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But clear explanations and public frameworks can themselves help to promote good policy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Feedback from the market is more useful to central banks when the market understands the central bank's reasoning, strategy, and objectives, even if market participants don't agree with the central bank's outlook.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And the discussions and decisions on how to frame the public presentation of policy can lead to improvements in internal deliberations.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Among the most important criteria for judging the effectiveness of communications and transparency, then, is whether or not they impede making the best possible policy decisions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Transparency should not be allowed to inhibit the free give and take and the testing of ideas at meetings that are so important to reaching good decisions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And communication must deal with the diversity of views on the policy committee; that diversity is a strength of policy committees, but it can make it challenging to arrive at a clear, consistent public explanation of a policy decision, because policymakers can arrive at the same policy position based on different rationales.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Good communication must also take into account uncertainty.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Understandably, market participants want to know what is going to happen next--to the economy and to policy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But we cannot say more than we know, and we should strive to avoid giving people the impression that we know more than we do.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I'll touch on a number of these themes as I review recent Federal Reserve communications.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Before I do, I have one last comment: Our communication strategy is a work in process--we are constantly looking for additional steps that could reasonably be expected to improve public understanding and policy effectiveness.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: However, we move slowly in changing what we say in part because ill-conceived communication policy has the power to harm the economy, and, even if that harm were to be realized, the policy could be difficult to alter.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Enhanced Economic Projections As already noted, I believe that the additional information in the enhanced projections the FOMC announced in November should be a substantial step forward in increasing public understanding of monetary policy decisions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: 2 The enhanced projections give more information about the FOMC's medium-term outlook for the economy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: That's particularly important, because the lags in the effect of policy on economic activity and prices mean that policy decisions are necessarily based on a view of the likely path for the economy over several years, relative to the Federal Reserve's legislated objectives of maximum employment and stable prices.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In that regard, one of the most significant aspects of the initiative is the lengthening of the forecast horizon from 1-1/2 to 2 years previously to about 3 years.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Shorter-term forecasts tend to be dominated by the interpretation of how recent shocks to the economy will play out.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: By lengthening the projection horizon, FOMC members will also be giving a sense of their assessment of a number of important structural characteristics of the economy that influence the conduct of policy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, given the starting point for the outlook, the forecasts will trace out a path for the economy to preserve or reestablish maximum employment and price stability that will reflect FOMC participants' views of the relative variation in output and inflation that is possible in the short run.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, FOMC participants' projections of growth and unemployment in the third year of their forecasts will be influenced significantly by their interpretation of  maximum sustainable growth and resource utilization, given their understanding of the likely growth of productivity and structure of labor markets.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And our projections for inflation in year three will depend importantly on our sense of what inflation rate is consistent with our mandates for employment and price stability.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: That projection, along with the path to year-three inflation, should help the public differentiate short-term shocks to price stability from the longer-term price trends it should use for planning purposes.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Over time, as actual inflation tends toward the year-three forecasts, inflation expectations may well become even more firmly anchored than they are today.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In another change, the Committee included total consumer inflation in its forecasts along with the core measure it had been using.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: We have always recognized that "price stability" was not intended to apply to a subset of prices that people paid.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: However, we have also found that excluding volatile food and energy prices generally gives a better sense of underlying inflation pressures that are likely to persist and dominate total inflation over time.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Hence, core inflation has been the most useful guide to the factors affecting policy when our forecast horizon was relatively short.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Because the final year or so of the longer horizon is heavily influenced by our longer-term objectives, a more comprehensive measure is now also useful and appropriate.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: FOMC members will be making their forecasts quarterly, thereby adding two rounds to the semiannual forecasts keyed to our monetary policy reports and Chairman Bernanke's testimonies.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Economic circumstances, and thus the appropriate path for policy, can change rapidly, and we will continue to address those changes in our policy announcements and the minutes for our meetings.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the increased frequency of forecasts will give us more opportunities to place such changes in the context of our medium-term outlook.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The forecasts themselves are each Committee member's assessment of the most likely outcome for the economy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: From time to time, however, policy decisions must take account of less likely, but especially important, potential outcomes.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: A significant contribution of the enhanced forecasts is to report more regularly and systematically on Committee members' views on the degree of uncertainty in the medium-term outlook and whether the risks to the most likely forecasts are skewed in any particular direction.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Both elements can influence Committee actions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Uncertainty arises not only from future economic shocks, but also from our incomplete knowledge of the structure of the economy and of the full characteristics of recent economic developments that had not been anticipated.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: When, as now, the FOMC believes that uncertainty is high, it may need to give greater weight to new information and be readier to revise its forecasts.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Policy decisions may also take into account the substantial risk that the economy will turn out differently than the most likely forecast, especially when that alternative is seen as having unusually large costs in terms of public welfare.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The enhanced forecasts will be accompanied by a narrative derived from the forecast submissions and the discussion of those forecasts at the meeting.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: This narrative will give the Committee an opportunity to tell the story behind the forecast--the most important forces it sees as bearing on the outlook and on the risks around the outlook, extending and expanding on the discussion in the minutes.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: This explanation, as much as the forecasts themselves, may well be most useful to the public in interpreting new data and developments and their implications for the economy and policy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The narrative will regularly include Committee members' take on why reality has deviated from the expectations embodied in past forecasts--often a key to understanding and anticipating policy actions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In the FOMC's discussion of communications, we considered, but did not adopt, a number of proposals at this time, and I thought it might be useful for me to briefly address a few of these, while keeping in mind my previous comment that we are constantly reviewing our communication strategy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: As noted previously, our longer-term forecasts of inflation are presumably influenced by our individual assessments of what inflation rate would be acceptable and consistent with fulfilling our congressional mandates, but we chose not to ask each participant for an explicit numerical definition of price stability.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: We believed that the steps we were taking would provide additional information that could help clarify how we viewed price stability that at the same time would allow us to remain consistent with giving information about how we expected to fulfill our dual mandate.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I expect that our new projections will provide some of the benefits of an explicit target in better anchoring inflation expectations while not giving up any flexibility to react to developments that threaten high employment.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: As we gain experience with the enhanced forecasts, we will continue to evaluate how best to promote stability of both prices and employment.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: When FOMC participants make their forecasts, each individual assumes "appropriate" monetary policy--that is, the policy that is most likely to foster the achievement of our objectives.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Forecasts made under such an assumption should better reveal the participants' views of the underlying structural parameters of the economy--the best possible tradeoffs between inflation and output stability in the short run and longer-term price and output trends--than would be made assuming an externally derived path for rates, such as the path implicit in market interest rates.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: If the markets' path for appropriate policy were at odds with my judgment about appropriate policy, I would have to write down a forecast whose path or end points were not consistent with what I believed were our best efforts to achieve our objectives.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The FOMC decided against reporting a range or histogram for participants' assumptions about appropriate policy, because it was concerned about the potential for unintended consequences of such a publication.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Specifically, it worried about a tendency for the public to infer more of a commitment to following the implied path than would be appropriate for good policy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In that circumstance, deviating from the path would risk market instability, and concerns about such dynamic responses would complicate already difficult policy choices.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, over time, market participants might learn how little weight they should give any published average of "appropriate" policies, but the learning process could take time and be costly, and we would not be assured of a successful outcome.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Recent FOMC Communication Communication in a period of market turmoil as we have experienced in the past several months poses special challenges.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The situation has been changing rapidly, taking unexpected twists and turns.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Every episode of financial turmoil is different, which greatly complicates the analysis of how the financial situation is likely to evolve in the current circumstances, how lenders and borrowers might react, and how spending and prices could be affected.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Central bankers, like everyone else, necessarily are operating with incomplete information about the state of the financial system, and some of the day-to-day information they are getting is colored by the perspective of the people giving it.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: With everyone looking for clues as to underlying conditions, central bank communications will be scrutinized especially closely, with the risk of unanticipated and unwelcome reactions; a frequently debated question within the central bank is whether a given statement will reassure market participants or alarm them.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: At any given point, the FOMC must make judgments about an appropriate policy and its communication based on what it knows at the time and thinks, given that information, it can anticipate for the future.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Because of the uncertainty and fluidity of the situation, the FOMC needs to be aware of the high odds of unanticipated developments as it formulates and discusses policy; however, market participants and other observers also must keep the same caveats in mind as they interpret what the FOMC is saying.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In many respects, our recent communication has been driven by the necessity to announce and explain unusual actions we have taken.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Examples of this are the reduction in the penalty on the primary discount rate in August and the inauguration of a Term Auction Facility in December.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, we've tried to adhere to certain principles in our communications over this period.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: First, we have tried to provide more information than usual to reduce uncertainty and clarify our intentions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: This effort is particularly noticeable with respect to open market operations--beginning in August, we have been especially forthcoming about the operations we were undertaking to manage actual or potential disturbances in money markets.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, we have attempted to let people know when our views of the macroeconomic situation had changed materially between FOMC meetings.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For instance, we issued a FOMC statement about the changing balance of risks on August 17 and Chairman Bernanke delivered a speech in late November after market conditions had deteriorated again.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And third, we have tried to be open in our balance-of-risks portion of our announcement about our perceptions of the shifting degree of uncertainty in the outlook caused by the recent turmoil.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In both September and December we said that the uncertainty was so great that we couldn't usefully characterize the balance of risks; at the end of October, when markets looked as though they were settling down and spillovers beyond the housing sector might be limited, we thought we could characterize "rough balance."
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Because the situation has been so fluid and so uncertain in its effects, the speeches of individual FOMC participants have given varied interpretations of the developments and their implications for policy.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The resulting dispersion of messages has bothered market participants seeking clear, unambiguous guidance about the views of the central bank.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The public should understand that the FOMC members do not coordinate schedules and messages, and that members' views are likely to be especially diverse when, as in the current situation, circumstances are changing quickly and are subject to many different analyses.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The diversity of views on the Committee is one of its strengths and vital to arriving at sound decisions.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: As I noted in the introduction to this talk, sound decisions are the most important contributions we can make to further the accomplishment of our public policy objectives.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I'm sure that the communications of the Federal Reserve, like all human endeavors, can be improved.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: We will be learning from our own experiences and those of our sister central banks, as well as from discussions such as this one organized by the National Association for Business Economics.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: These views are my own and not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The policy regarding enhanced projections was announced in Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (2007), press release, Nov. 14 .
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Also, the new policy was discussed in a speech given by Chairman Bernanke that day (Ben S. Bernanke, 2007, "Federal Reserve Communications," speech delivered at the Cato Institute 25th Annual Monetary Conference, Washington, Nov. 14).
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: And the first set of projections under the new policy was prepared in conjunction with the Oct. 30-31, 2007, FOMC meeting and released in the minutes of that meeting (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 2007, press release, Nov. 20 ).
speech_title: Recent and Prospective Developments in Monetary Policy Transparency and Communications:  A Global Perspective
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics Session, Allied Social Science Associations Annual Meeting, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since late last summer, the financial markets in the United States and in a number of other industrialized countries have been under considerable strain.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The turmoil has affected the prospects for the broader economy, principally through its effects on the availability and terms of credit to households and businesses.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Financial market conditions, in turn, have been sensitive to the evolving economic outlook, as investors have tried to assess the implications of incoming economic information for future earnings and asset values.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These interactions have produced a volatile situation that has made forecasting the course of the economy even more difficult than usual.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In my remarks today I will provide some perspective on recent developments in the economy and financial markets, focusing on conditions in the United States.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will then discuss the Fedâs recent policy actions and our plans for addressing the economic and financial challenges ahead.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Housing, the Subprime Mortgage Market, and the Financial Turmoil As you will recall, the U.S. economy experienced a mild recession in 2001.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: During the ensuing recovery, above-trend growth was accompanied by rising rates of resource utilization, particularly after the expansion picked up steam in mid-2003.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, the civilian unemployment rate declined from a high of 6.3 percent in June 2003 to 4.4 percent in March 2007.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the economy approached full employment, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the monetary policymaking arm of the Federal Reserve System, was faced with the classic problem of managing the mid-cycle slowdown--that is, of setting policy to help guide the economy toward sustainable growth without inflation.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: With that objective, the FOMC implemented a sequence of rate increases, beginning in mid-2004 and ending in June 2006, at which point the target for the federal funds rate was 5.25 percent--a level that, in the judgment of the Committee, would best promote the policy objectives given to us by the Congress.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The economy continued to perform well into 2007, with solid growth through the third quarter and unemployment remaining near recent lows.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indicators of the underlying inflation trend, such as core inflation, showed signs of moderating.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the situation was complicated by a number of factors.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Continued increases in the prices of energy and other commodities, together with high levels of resource utilization, kept the Committee on inflation alert.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But perhaps an even greater challenge was posed by a sharp and protracted correction in the U.S. housing market, which followed a multiyear boom in housing construction and house prices.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indicating the depth of the decline in housing, according to the most recent available data, housing starts and new home sales have both fallen by about 50 percent from their respective peaks.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In all likelihood, the housing contraction would have been considerably milder had it not been for adverse developments in the subprime mortgage market.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since early 2007, financial market participants have been focused on the high and rising delinquency rates of subprime mortgages, especially those with adjustable interest rates (subprime ARMs).
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Currently, about 21 percent of subprime ARMs are ninety days or more delinquent, and foreclosure rates are rising sharply.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although poor underwriting and, in some cases, fraud and abusive practices contributed to the high rates of delinquency that we are now seeing in the subprime ARM market, the more fundamental reason for the sharp deterioration in credit quality was the flawed premise on which much subprime ARM lending was based: that house prices would continue to rise rapidly.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: When house prices were increasing at double-digit rates, subprime ARM borrowers were able to build equity in their homes during the period in which they paid a (relatively) low introductory (or âteaserâ) rate on their mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Once sufficient equity had been accumulated, borrowers were often able to refinance, avoiding the increased payments associated with the reset in the rate on the original mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, when declining affordability finally began to take its toll on the demand for homes and thus on house prices, borrowers could no longer rely on home-price appreciation to build equity; they were accordingly unable to refinance and found themselves locked into their subprime ARM contracts.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Many of these borrowers found it difficult to make payments at even the introductory rate, much less at the higher post-adjustment rate.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The result, as I have already noted, has been rising delinquencies and foreclosures, which will have adverse effects for communities and the broader economy as well as for the borrowers themselves.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: One of the many unfortunate consequences of these events, which may be with us for some time, is on the availability of credit for nonprime borrowers.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Ample evidence suggests that responsible nonprime lending can be beneficial and safe for the borrower as well as profitable for the lender.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, even as delinquencies on subprime ARMs have soared, loss rates on subprime mortgages with fixed interest rates, though somewhat higher recently, remain in their historical range.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some lenders, including some who have worked closely with nonprofit groups with strong roots in low-to-moderate-income communities, have been able to foster homeownership in those communities while experiencing exceptionally low rates of default.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Unfortunately, at this point, the market is not discriminating to any significant degree between good and bad nonprime loans, and few new loans are being made.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although subprime borrowers and the investors who hold these mortgages are the parties most directly affected by the collapse of this market, the consequences have been felt much more broadly.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I have already referred to the role that the subprime crisis has played in the housing correction.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the way up, expansive subprime lending increased the effective demand for housing, pushing up prices and stimulating construction activity.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the way down, the withdrawal of this source of demand for housing has exacerbated the downturn, adding to the sharp decline in new homebuilding and putting downward pressure on house prices.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The addition of foreclosed properties to the inventories of unsold homes is further weakening the market.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, the losses in the subprime mortgage market also triggered a substantial reaction in other financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At some level, the magnitude of that reaction might be deemed surprising, given the small size of the U.S. subprime market relative to world financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Part of the explanation for the outsized effect may be that, following a period of more-aggressive risk-taking, the subprime crisis led investors to reassess credit risks more broadly and, perhaps, to become less willing to take on risks of any type.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors have also been concerned that, by further weakening the housing sector, the problems in the subprime mortgage market may lead overall economic growth to slow.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, part of the explanation for the far-reaching financial impact of the subprime shock is that it has contributed to a considerable increase in investor uncertainty about the appropriate valuations of a broader range of financial assets, not just subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, subprime mortgages were often combined with other types of loans in so-called structured credit products.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These investment products, sometimes packaged with various credit and liquidity guarantees obtained from banks or through derivative contracts, were divided into portions, or tranches, of varying seniority and credit quality.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, through financial engineering, a diverse combination of underlying credits became the raw material for a new set of financial assets, many of them garnering high ratings from credit agencies, which could be matched to the needs of ultimate investors.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The complexity of structured credit products, as well as the difficulty of determining the values of some of the underlying assets, led many investors to rely heavily on the evaluations of these products by credit-rating agencies.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, as subprime mortgage losses rose to levels that threatened even highly rated tranches, investors began to question the reliability of the credit ratings and became increasingly unwilling to hold these products.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Similar concerns arose in the market for asset-backed commercial paper (ABCP).
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this market, various institutions established special-purpose vehicles to issue commercial paper to help fund a variety of assets, including some private-label mortgage-backed securities, mortgages warehoused for securitization, and other long-maturity assets.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors had typically viewed the commercial paper backed by these assets as quite safe and liquid.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the concerns about mortgage-backed securities and structured credit products more generally (even those unrelated to mortgages) led to great reluctance on the part of investors to roll over ABCP, particularly at maturities of more than a few days, leaving the sponsors of the various investment vehicles scrambling for liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Those who could not find new funding were forced to sell assets into a highly illiquid and unreceptive market.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importantly, investorsâ loss of confidence was not restricted to securities related to subprime mortgages but extended to other key asset classes.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, the secondary market for private-label securities backed by prime jumbo mortgages has also contracted, and issuance of such securities has dwindled.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 Even though default rates on prime jumbo mortgages have remained very low, the experience with subprime mortgages has evidently made investors more sensitive to the risks associated with other housing-related assets as well.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Other types of assets that have seen a cooling of investor interest include loans for commercial real estate projects and so-called leveraged loans, which are used to finance mergers and leveraged buyouts.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although structured credit products and special-purpose investment vehicles may be viewed as providing direct channels between the ultimate borrowers and the broader capital markets, thereby circumventing the need for traditional bank financing, banks nevertheless played important roles in this mode of finance.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Large money-center banks and other major financial institutions (which I will call âbanks,â for short) underwrote many of the loans and created many of the structured credit products that were sold into the market.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Banks also supported the various investment vehicles in many ways, for example, by serving as advisers and by providing standby liquidity facilities and various credit enhancements.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the problems with these facilities multiplied, banks came under increasing pressure to rescue the investment vehicles they sponsored--either by providing liquidity or other support or, as has become increasingly the norm, by taking the assets of the off-balance-sheet vehicles onto their own balance sheets.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Banksâ balance sheets were swelled further by non-conforming mortgages, leveraged loans, and other credits that the banks had extended but for which well-functioning secondary markets no longer existed.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even as their balance sheets expanded, banks began to report large losses, reflecting the sharp declines in the values of mortgages and other assets.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, banks too became subject to valuation uncertainty, as could be seen in their share prices and other market indicators such as quotes on credit default swaps.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The combination of larger balance sheets and unexpected losses also resulted in a decline in the capital ratios of a number of institutions.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Several have chosen to raise new capital in response, and the banking system retains substantial levels of capital.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, on balance, these developments have prompted banks to become protective of their liquidity and balance sheet capacity and thus to become less willing to provide funding to other market participants, including other banks.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result, both overnight and term interbank funding markets have periodically come under considerable pressure, with spreads on interbank lending rates over various benchmark rates rising notably.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We also see considerable evidence that banks have become more restrictive in their lending to firms and households.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: More-expensive and less-available credit seems likely to impose a measure of financial restraint on economic growth.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The recent developments in U.S. and foreign financial markets will stimulate considerable review and analysis in the months and years to come.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Around the world, legislatures, regulators, supervisors, accounting boards, central banks, and others with responsibility for oversight of the financial system are already hard at work trying to distill the lessons to be drawn from this experience and their implications for policy.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Many in the private sector, including banks, credit-rating agencies, and the investment community, are likewise actively reviewing and responding to these developments.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some of the areas that will draw scrutiny are the appropriate use of credit ratings by investors, banks, and supervisors; the need for enterprise-wide, better-integrated risk-management techniques in large financial institutions; the appropriateness of accounting rules governing asset valuation and the use of off-balance-sheet vehicles; and weaknesses in the originate-to-distribute model and in the design of structured credit products, among many others.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the longer term, the response of the public and private sectors to this experience should help create a stronger financial system.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserveâs Response Fortunately, after a number of years of strong earnings, most financial institutions entered the current episode in good financial condition.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, notwithstanding the effects of multi-billion dollar write-downs on the earnings and share prices of some large institutions, the banking system remains sound.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nevertheless, the market strains have been serious, and they continue to pose risks to the broader economy.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve accordingly has taken a number of steps to help markets return to more orderly functioning and to foster its macroeconomic objectives of maximum sustainable employment and price stability.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Broadly, the Federal Reserveâs response has followed two tracks: efforts to support market liquidity and functioning and the pursuit of our macroeconomic objectives through monetary policy.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To help address the significant strains in short-term money markets, the Federal Reserve has taken a range of steps.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, on August 17, the Federal Reserve Board cut the discount rate--the rate at which it lends directly to banks--by 50 basis points, or 1/2 percentage point, and it has since maintained the spread between the federal funds rate and the discount rate at 50 basis points, rather than the customary 100 basis points.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 The Fed also adjusted its usual practices to facilitate the provision of discount window financing for as long as thirty days, renewable at the request of the borrower.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Loans through the discount window differ from conventional open market operations in that the loans can be made directly to individual banks.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In contrast, open market operations are arranged with a limited set of dealers of government securities.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, whereas open market operations involve lending against government and agency securities, loans through the discount window can be made against a much wider range of collateral.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The changes to the discount window were designed to assure banks of the availability of a backstop source of liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although banks borrowed only moderate amounts at the discount window, they substantially increased the amount of collateral they placed with Reserve Banks.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This and other factors suggest that these changes to the discount window facility, together with the statements and actions of the FOMC, had some positive influence on market conditions.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, as a tool for easing the strains in money markets, the discount window has two drawbacks.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, banks may be reluctant to use the window, fearing that markets will draw adverse inferences about their financial condition and access to private sources of funding--the so-called stigma problem.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, to maintain the federal funds rate near its target, the Federal Reserve Systemâs open market desk must take into account the fact that loans through the discount window add reserves to the banking system and thus, all else equal, could tend to push the federal funds rate below the target set by the FOMC.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The open market desk can offset this effect by draining reserves from the system.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the amounts that banks choose to borrow at the discount window can be difficult to predict, complicating the management of the federal funds rate, especially when borrowings are large.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address the limitations of the discount window, the Federal Reserve recently introduced a term auction facility, or TAF, through which prespecified amounts of discount window credit can be auctioned to eligible borrowers.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As I will discuss in greater detail in a moment, our intention in developing the TAF was to provide a tool that could more effectively address the problems currently affecting the interbank lending market without complicating the administration of reserves and the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In December, the Fed successfully auctioned $40 billion through this facility and, as part of a coordinated operation, the European Central Bank and the Swiss National Bank lent an additional $24 billion.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These two central banks obtained the dollars from the Federal Reserve through currency swaps (essentially, two-way lines of credit in which each central bank agrees to lend the other up to a fixed amount in its own currency).
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
