text: As part of the same coordinated action, the central banks of the United Kingdom and Canada conducted similar operations in their own currencies.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On January 4, the Federal Reserve announced that we will auction an additional $60 billion in twenty-eight-day credit through the TAF, to be spread across two auctions that will be held later this month.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: With these actions and the passage of the year end, term premiums in the interbank market and some other measures of strains in funding markets have eased significantly, though they remain well above levels prevailing before August last year.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Based on our initial experience, it appears that the TAF may have overcome the two drawbacks of the discount window, in that there appears to have been little if any stigma associated with participation in the auction, and--because the Fed was able to set the amounts to be auctioned in advance--the open market desk faced minimal uncertainty about the effects of the operation on bank reserves.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The TAF may thus become a useful permanent addition to the Fedâs toolbox.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 TAF auctions will continue as long as necessary to address elevated pressures in short-term funding markets, and we will continue to work closely and cooperatively with other central banks to address market strains that could hamper the achievement of our broader economic objectives.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although the TAF and other liquidity-related actions appear to have had some positive effects, such measures alone cannot fully address fundamental concerns about credit quality and valuation, nor do these actions relax the balance sheet constraints on financial institutions.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Hence, they cannot eliminate the financial restraints affecting the broader economy.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Monetary policy (that is, the management of the short-term interest rate) is the Fedâs best tool for pursuing our macroeconomic objectives, namely to promote maximum sustainable employment and price stability.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although economic growth slowed in the fourth quarter of last year from the third quarterâs rapid clip, it seems nonetheless, as best we can tell, to have continued at a moderate pace.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recently, however, incoming information has suggested that the baseline outlook for real activity in 2008 has worsened and the downside risks to growth have become more pronounced.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, the demand for housing seems to have weakened further, in part reflecting the ongoing problems in mortgage markets.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, a number of factors, including higher oil prices, lower equity prices, and softening home values, seem likely to weigh on consumer spending as we move into 2008.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Financial conditions continue to pose a downside risk to the outlook for growth.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Market participants still express considerable uncertainty about the appropriate valuation of complex financial assets and about the extent of additional losses that may be disclosed in the future.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the whole, despite improvements in some areas, the financial situation remains fragile, and many funding markets remain impaired.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Adverse economic or financial news has the potential to increase financial strains and to lead to further constraints on the supply of credit to households and businesses.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I expect that financial-market participants--and, of course, the Committee--will be paying particular attention to developments in the housing market, in part because of the potential for spillovers from housing to other sectors of the economy.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A second consequential risk to the growth outlook concerns the performance of the labor market.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Last weekâs report on labor-market conditions in December was disappointing, as it showed an increase of 0.3 percentage point in the unemployment rate and a decline in private payroll employment.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Heretofore, the labor market has been a source of stability in the macroeconomic situation, with relatively steady gains in wage and salary income providing households the wherewithal to support moderate growth in real consumption spending.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It would be a mistake to read too much into any one report.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, should the labor market deteriorate, the risks to consumer spending would rise.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even as the outlook for real activity has weakened, there have been some important developments on the inflation front.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Most notably, the same increase in oil prices that may be a negative influence on growth is also lifting overall consumer prices and probably putting some upward pressure on core inflation measures as well.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Last year, food prices also increased exceptionally rapidly by recent standards, further boosting overall consumer price inflation.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus far, inflation expectations appear to have remained reasonably well anchored, and pressures on resource utilization have diminished a bit.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, any tendency of inflation expectations to become unmoored or for the Fedâs inflation-fighting credibility to be eroded could greatly complicate the task of sustaining price stability and reduce the central bankâs policy flexibility to counter shortfalls in growth in the future.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Accordingly, in the months ahead we will be closely monitoring the inflation situation, particularly as regards inflation expectations.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Monetary policy has responded proactively to evolving conditions.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, the Committee cut its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points at its September meeting and by 25 basis points each at the October and December meetings.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In total, therefore, we have brought the funds rate down by a percentage point from its level just before financial strains emerged.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve took these actions to help offset the restraint imposed by the tightening of credit conditions and the weakening of the housing market.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, in light of recent changes in the outlook for and the risks to growth, additional policy easing may well be necessary.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Committee will, of course, be carefully evaluating incoming information bearing on the economic outlook.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Based on that evaluation, and consistent with our dual mandate, we stand ready to take substantive additional action as needed to support growth and to provide adequate insurance against downside risks.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Financial and economic conditions can change quickly.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consequently, the Committee must remain exceptionally alert and flexible, prepared to act in a decisive and timely manner and, in particular, to counter any adverse dynamics that might threaten economic or financial stability.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Jumbo mortgages are those mortgages for which the principal value does not conform to the limit set annually by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac for loans they will purchase; the amount for 2008 is $417,000.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Jumbo loans are thus a type of ânonconformingâ loan.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Prime loans are those made to borrowers with good credit records.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The discount rate is also known as the primary credit rate.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Before making the TAF permanent, however, we would seek public comment on its design and utility.
speech_title: Financial Markets, the Economic Outlook, and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the Women in Housing and Finance and Exchequer Club Joint Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In my remarks today, I would like to consider the rationale for greater flexibility in monetary policy during periods of financial disruptions.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Before doing so, however, I would like to make not just one, but two important disclaimers.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, as usual, my remarks reflect only my own views and are not intended to reflect those of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) or of anyone else associated with the Federal Reserve System.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: And second, my comments today should not be viewed as suggesting what policy actions I would be likely to advocate at the next FOMC meeting; rather, my purpose here is to discuss at a general level what can be said about the appropriate framework for monetary policy when we face a financial disruption of the sort that we have seen recently.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: I have two reasons for making the second disclaimer.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, in some circumstances, the appropriate near-term path for policy rates can be highly uncertain and may well evolve right up until the time of the meeting, depending on the implications of the incoming data.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, as I noted in a speech in late November, I think there is too much focus on what decision will be made about the federal funds rate target at the next FOMC meeting (Mishkin, 2007e).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: What is important for pricing most financial assets is the path of monetary policy, not the particular action taken at a single meeting.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For these reasons, I hope the recent enhancements to the Federal Reserveâs communication strategy--especially the greater prominence of the macroeconomic projections of FOMC participants--will help shift attention toward our medium-term objectives and our approach in meeting these objectives.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In particular, the Congress has given the Federal Reserve a specific mandate (often referred to as the dual mandate) of fostering the objectives of price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, when the economy faces a disruption in financial markets, monetary policy must aim at balancing the risks to both economic growth and inflation.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the remainder of this speech, I will elaborate a bit further about why financial market disruptions can pose significant risks to the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Then I will explain how the science of monetary policy can help provide a conceptual framework for a systematic approach to managing these risks, and I will briefly discuss how that framework can be useful for understanding the course of Federal Reserve policy over the past few months.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Financial Disruptions and Macroeconomic Risk Before considering the appropriate policy response to strains in financial markets, it is essential to consider the sources of these strains and the potential consequences for the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In general, the U.S. financial system is an efficient mechanism for channeling funds to individuals or corporations with worthy investment opportunities, because the financial markets are highly competitive and provide strong incentives for collecting and processing information.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although financial markets and institutions deal with large volumes of information, some of this information is by nature asymmetric; that is, one party to a financial contract (typically the lender) has less accurate information about the likely distribution of outcomes than does the other party (typically the borrower).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: 2 Historically, banks and other financial intermediaries have played a major role in reducing the asymmetry of information, partly because these firms tend to have long-term relationships with their clients.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Recent years have witnessed the development of new types of financial institutions and of new markets for trading financial products, and these innovations have had the potential (not always realized) to contribute to the efficient flow of information.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The continuity of this information flow is crucial to the process of price discovery--that is, the ability of market participants to assess the fundamental worth of each financial asset.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: During periods of financial distress, however, information flows may be disrupted and price discovery may be impaired.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result, such episodes tend to generate greater uncertainty, which contributes to higher credit spreads and greater reluctance to engage in market transactions.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I noted in another recent speech, financial disruptions are associated with two distinct types of risk: valuation risk and macroeconomic risk (Mishkin, 2007d).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Valuation risk refers to the extent that market participants become more uncertain about the returns on a specific asset, especially in cases where the security is highly complex and its underlying creditworthiness is relatively opaque.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In recent months, for example, this type of risk has been central to the repricing of many structured credit products, as investors have struggled to understand how potential losses in subprime mortgages might filter through the various layers of securities linked to these loans.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: While valuation risk is relevant for individual investors, monetary policymakers are concerned with macroeconomic risk.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In particular, strains in financial markets can spill over to the broader economy and have adverse consequences on output and employment.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, an economic downturn tends to generate even greater uncertainty about asset values, which could initiate an adverse feedback loop in which the financial disruption restrains economic activity; such a situation could lead to greater uncertainty and increased financial disruption, causing a further deterioration in macroeconomic activity, and so on.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the academic literature, this phenomenon is generally referred to as the financial accelerator (Bernanke and Gertler, 1989; Bernanke, Gertler, and Gilchrist, 1996, 1999).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The quality of balance sheets of households and firms comprise a key element of the financial accelerator mechanism, because some of the assets of each borrower may serve as collateral for its liabilities.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The use of collateral helps mitigate the problem of asymmetric information, because the borrowerâs incentive not to engage in excessive risk-taking is strengthened by the threat of losing the collateral: If a default does occur, the lender can take title to the borrowerâs collateral and thereby recover some or all of the value of the loan.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, a macroeconomic downturn tends to diminish the value of many forms of collateral, thereby exacerbating the impact of frictions in credit markets and reinforcing the propagation of the adverse feedback loop.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Risk Management and the Science of Monetary Policy Given that a financial market disruption can pose significant risks to the macroeconomy, risk management is crucial in formulating the appropriate response of monetary policy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Unfortunately, most existing studies of optimal monetary policy have completely abstracted from considerations of macroeconomic risk, because these studies use specific formulations or approximations which imply that the design of the optimal monetary policy does not depend on the magnitude or direction of uncertainty facing the economyââan implication referred to as certainty equivalence.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To elaborate on these issues, itâs necessary for me to proceed at a somewhat more technical level, but I promise to use plain English again later in the speech.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In particular, the standard textbook approach to analyzing optimal monetary policy utilizes a linear-quadratic (LQ ) framework, in which the equations describing the dynamic behavior of the economy are linear and the objective function specifying the goals of policy is quadratic .
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, in light of the dual mandate, monetary policy is often characterized as seeking to minimize a loss function comprising the squared value of the inflation gap (that is, actual inflation minus desired inflation) and the squared value of the output gap (that is, actual output minus potential output).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Under these assumptions, the optimal policy is certainty equivalent: This policy can be characterized by a linear time-invariant response to each shock, and the magnitude of these responses does not depend on the variances or any other aspect of the probability distribution of the shocks.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In such an environment, optimal monetary policy does not focus on risk management.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, when financial market participants and wage and price setters are relatively forward-looking, the optimal policy under commitment is characterized by considerable inertia.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, the actual course of monetary policy over the past quarter-century has typically been very smooth in the United States as well as in many other industrial economies.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the Federal Reserve has usually adjusted the federal funds rate in increments of 25 or 50 basis points (that is, 1/4 or 1/2 percentage point) and sharp reversals in the funds rate path have been rare.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Numerous empirical studies have characterized monetary policy using Taylor-style rules in which the policy rate responds to the inflation gap and the output gap; these studies have generally found that the fit of the regression equation is improved by including a lagged interest rate that reflects the smoothness of the typical adjustment pattern.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: While an LQ framework may provide a reasonable approximation to how monetary policy should operate under fairly normal circumstances, this approach is less likely to be adequate for thinking about monetary policy when the risk of poor economic performance is unusually high.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, the dynamic behavior of the economy may well exhibit nonlinearities, at least in response to some shocks (Hamilton, 1989; Kim and Nelson, 1999; and Kim, Morley, and Piger, 2005).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, the use of a quadratic objective function does not reflect the extent to which most individuals have strong preferences for minimizing the incidence of worst-case scenarios.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, given that the central bankâs ultimate goal should be to maximize the public welfare, I believe that the design of monetary policy ought to reflect the publicâs preferences, especially with respect to avoiding particularly adverse economic outcomes.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Most of the quantitative studies of optimal monetary policy have also assumed that the shocks hitting the economy have a time-invariant Gaussian distribution, that is, a classical bell curve with symmetric and well-behaved tails.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In reality, however, the distribution of shocks hitting the economy is more complex.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In some instances, the uncertainty facing the economy is clearly skewed in one direction or another; again, this is likely when there are significant financial disruptions.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve often reports on our judgments regarding the degree of skewness and the associated economic costs by giving assessments of the âBalance of Risksâ in the press releases that are issued following FOMC meetings.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, at least in some circumstances, the shocks hitting the economy may exhibit excess kurtosis, commonly referred to as tail risk because the probability of relatively large disturbances is higher than would be implied by a Gaussian distribution.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In that light, one element of the recent enhancements to the Federal Reserveâs communication strategy is that FOMC participants now provide assessments of the relative degree of uncertainty.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, in the âSummary of Economic Projectionsâissued in late November, FOMC participants indicated that the degree of uncertainty regarding the economic growth outlook was relatively high compared to the average degree of uncertainty over the past two decades.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: This account could be interpreted as a statement that the Committee perceived the tail risk as unusually large.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: With a nonquadratic objective function (consistent with the importance of uncertainty for the course of monetary policy) as well as nonlinear dynamics and non-Gaussian shocks, optimal monetary policy will also be nonlinear and will tend to focus on risk management.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Policy in this setting tends to respond aggressively when a large shock becomes evident; for this reason, the degree of inertia in such cases may be markedly lower than in more routine circumstances.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, as I will argue, I believe that financial disruptions of the sort that have been experienced in recent months tend to have highly nonlinear effects on the economy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, compared with the standard case, optimal policy may well involve much more rapid adjustmentââa pattern that I will refer to as policy flexibility .
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Formal models of how monetary policy should respond to financial disruptions are unfortunately not yet available, and this is an area of research that I plan to pursue with Board staff.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, I do have some thoughts about what a systematic framework should look like, and I would like to share them with you without going into any further technical details.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: A Risk-Management Framework for Dealing with Financial Disruptions Although the assumptions behind the LQ framework might be reasonable during normal times, financial disruptions are likely to produce large deviations from these assumptions, making it especially important to adopt a more flexible framework for analyzing the behavior of a central bank that practices risk management.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: What factors come into play with special vigor during financial disruptions?
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, financial disruptions are likely to lead to highly nonlinear behavior because the cost and availability of credit can shift suddenly.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, even though linear approximations of the financial accelerator mechanism have typically been used in recent quantitative studies, this mechanism is, in fact, highly nonlinear (Levin, Natalucci, and ZakrajÅ¡ek, 2004).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, because financial disruptions, if severe enough, raise the probability of particularly adverse outcomes, the standard approach of employing a quadratic approximation of the objective function may not be sufficiently accurate to convey the extent to which policymakers seek to avoid such outcomes in maximizing the publicâs welfare.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In light of these risk-management considerations, how should monetary policy respond to financial disruptions?
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Periods of financial instability are characterized by valuation risk and macroeconomic risk.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Monetary policy cannotââand should notââaim at minimizing valuation risk, but policy should aim at reducing macroeconomic risk.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: By cutting interest rates to offset the negative effects of financial turmoil on aggregate economic activity, monetary policy can reduce the likelihood that a financial disruption might set off an adverse feedback loop.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The resulting reduction in uncertainty can then make it easier for the markets to collect the information that facilitates price discovery, thus hastening the return of normal market functioning.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: To achieve this result most effectively, monetary policy needs to be timely, decisive, and flexible.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, timely action is crucial when an episode of financial instability becomes sufficiently severe to threaten the core macroeconomic objectives of the central bank.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In such circumstances, waiting too long to ease policy could result in further deterioration of the macroeconomy and might well increase the overall amount of easing that would eventually be needed.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, monetary policy must be at least as preemptive in responding to financial shocks as in responding to other types of disturbances to the economy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: When financial markets are working well, monetary policy can respond primarily to the incoming flow of economic data about production, employment, and inflation.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: When a financial disruption occurs, however, greater consideration needs to be given to indicators of market liquidity, credit spreads, and other financial market measures that can provide information about sharp changes in the magnitude of tail risk to the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, policymakers should be prepared for decisive action in response to financial disruptions.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In such circumstances, the most likely outcomeââreferred to as the modal forecastââfor the economy may be fairly benign, but there may be a significant risk of more severe adverse outcomes.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In such circumstances, the central bank may prefer to take out insurance by easing the stance of policy further than if the distribution of probable outcomes were perceived as fairly symmetric around the modal forecast.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, in such circumstances, these policy actions should not be interpreted by the public or market participants as implying a deterioration in the central bankâs assessment of the most likely outcome for the economy, but rather as an appropriate form of risk management that reduces the risk of particularly adverse outcomes.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Third, policy flexibility is crucial throughout the evolution of a financial market disruption.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: During the onset of the episode, this flexibility may be evident from the decisive easing of policy that is intended to forestall the contractionary effects of the disruption and provide insurance against the downside risks to the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, it is important to recognize that financial markets can also turn around quickly, thereby reducing the drag on the economy as well as the degree of tail risk.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, the central bank needs to monitor credit spreads and other incoming data for signs of financial market recovery and, if necessary, take back some of the insurance; thus, at each stage of the episode, the appropriate monetary policy may exhibit much less smoothing than would be typical in other circumstances.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, while policymakers may need to react aggressively to financial market information that indicates a significant shift in macroeconomic risks, monetary policy would typically move back toward a more incremental approach once the risks to the macroeconomy have returned to more usual levels.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Risk Management and the Anchoring of Inflation Expectations An important proviso to my discussion thus far involves the other part of the dual mandate, price stability.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: A central bank must always be concerned with inflation as well as growth.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I have emphasized in an earlier speech about inflation dynamics, the behavior of inflation is significantly influenced by the publicâs expectations about where inflation is likely to head in the long run (Mishkin, 2007a).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Therefore, preemptive actions of the sort I have described here would be counterproductive if these actions caused an increase in inflation expectations and the underlying rate of inflation; in other words, the flexibility to act preemptively against a financial disruption presumes that inflation expectations are well anchored and unlikely to rise during a period of temporary monetary easing.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, as I have argued elsewhere, a commitment to a strong nominal anchor is crucial for both aspects of the dual mandate, that is, for achieving maximum employment as well as for keeping inflation under control (Mishkin, 2007b).
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: How can a central bank keep inflation expectations solidly anchored so it can respond preemptively to financial disruptions?
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The central bank has to have earned credibility with financial markets and the public through a record of previous actions to maintain low and stable inflation.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, the central bank needs to clearly indicate the rationale for its policy actions.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Policymakers also need to monitor information about underlying inflation and longer-run inflation expectations, and if the evidence indicates that these inflation expectations have begun rising significantly, the central bank should be prepared to hold steady or even raise the policy rate.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserveâs Recent Monetary Policy Decisions The framework I have outlined here can be useful in understanding the rationale for the recent decisions of the Federal Reserve and our policy approach going forward.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Yesterday, Chairman Bernanke provided a detailed discussion of economic and financial developments and of the Federal Reserveâs policy strategy, so here I will just relate some key points of his discussion to the major themes that I have emphasized today.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, we are proceeding in a timely manner in countering any developments that might threaten economic or financial stability.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The FOMC has not been basing its decisions solely on the incoming flow of economic data; for example, the sequence of interest rate cuts was initiated last fall even though growth in the gross domestic product had been quite strong in the third quarter.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Rather, our policy approach has reflected the rapid deterioration of financial market conditions, which has contributed to a worsening of the economic outlook and the emergence of pronounced downside risks to economic growth and employment.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, in my view, the Federal Reserve has been acting and will continue to act decisively , in the sense that our policy strategy reflects the evolution of the balance of risks and not simply a change in the modal outlook for the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The disruption in financial markets poses a substantial downside risk to the outlook for economic growth, and adverse economic or financial news has the potential to cause further strains.
speech_title: Monetary Policy Flexibility, Risk Management, and Financial Disruptions
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In that light, the Federal Reserveâs policy strategy is aimed at providing insurance to help avoid more severe macroeconomic outcomes.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Third, because we recognize that financial and economic conditions can change quickly, the Federal Reserve is prepared to respond flexibly to incoming information.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, in making its decisions, the Federal Reserve also gives careful consideration to the outlook and risks associated with the second aspect of our dual mandate, namely, price stability.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because longer-run inflation expectations appear to have remained reasonably well anchored, in my view, the easing of the stance of policy in response to deteriorating financial conditions seems unlikely to have an adverse impact on the outlook for inflation.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nonetheless, we will continue to monitor incoming data on inflation and inflation expectations, especially given the potential risks to price stability that are associated with the rapid increase in energy prices and the depreciation of the dollar.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: In short, the FOMC will determine the future course of monetary policy in light of the evolution of the macroeconomic outlook and the balance of risks to our objectives of maximum employment and price stability.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conclusions The monetary policy that is appropriate during an episode of financial market disruption is likely to be quite different than in times of normal market functioning.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: When financial markets experience a significant disruption, a systematic approach to risk management requires policymakers to be preemptive in responding to the macroeconomic implications of incoming financial market information, and decisive actions may be required to reduce the likelihood of an adverse feedback loop.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: The central bank also needs to exhibit flexibility--that is, less inertia than would otherwise be typicalâânot only in moving decisively to reduce downside risks arising from a financial market disruption, but also in being prepared to take back some of that insurance in response to a recovery in financial markets or an upward shift in inflation risks.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, while I have argued that monetary policy needs to be decisive and timely in responding to a financial market disruption, a lot of art as well as science is involved in determining the severity and duration of the disruption and the associated implications for the macroeconomy (Mishkin, 2007c).

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, a central bank may well be able to employ non-monetary toolsââsuch as liquidity provisionââto help alleviate the adverse impact from financial disruptions.
