speaker: Kohn
text: When, at the end of July, I accepted Tom Simpson's invitation to speak to you today on the economy and monetary policy, little did I realize the challenges I would face.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: For one, the economy and financial markets have taken some unexpected twists and turns over the intervening seven months, and we are still in the midst of a rapidly evolving and highly uncertain situation.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: For another, when we set the date, I had expected that Chairman Bernanke would have already given our Monetary Policy Report to the Congress , and I could simply develop some of the themes he had laid out.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: However, that testimony will be tomorrow, and I must emphasize that the views you are about to hear are my own and not necessarily shared by any of my colleagues on the Board or the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Several major developments are shaping current economic performance, the outlook, and the conduct of monetary policy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The most prominent of these developments is the contraction in the housing market that began in early 2006.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Both the prices and pace of construction of new homes rose to unsustainable levels in the preceding few years.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: For a time, the resulting correction was largely confined to the housing market, but the consequences of that correction have spread to other sectors of the economy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The financial markets are playing a key role in the transmission of the housing downturn to the rest of the economy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In the first half of 2007, investors became concerned about the likely performance of many subprime adjustable-rate mortgages made from late 2005 through early 2007.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Lenders turned away from subprime mortgages and some other investments as the magnitude of the losses on those mortgages began to emerge, as uncertainty about the ultimate size of the losses and who would bear them mounted, and as these experiences undermined confidence in a variety of other credit instruments, especially those with complex structures.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Those tendencies have intensified as risks of a spillover to the broader economy have risen.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The increase in expected losses along with the unwillingness of investors to fund some types of credits has led to pressures on banks and other financial intermediaries as well as on prices and liquidity in securities markets.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The result has been a substantial tightening in credit availability for many firms and households.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, continued sizable increases in the prices of food, energy, and other commodities have raised inflation.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: To some extent, those increases have resulted from strong demand in rapidly growing emerging-market economies, like China and India.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: But the increases likely also reflect conditions such as adverse weather in some parts of the world, the use of agricultural commodities to produce energy, and geopolitical developments that threaten supplies in some petroleum-producing centers.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The higher prices have eroded the purchasing power of household income, adding to restraint on spending.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In my remarks today I will trace the effects of these developments in more detail, discuss the response of monetary policy, and talk about the implications for the future path of the economy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Recent Economic and Financial Developments The pace of real economic activity stepped down sharply toward the end of last year and has remained sluggish in recent months.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Real gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have risen only slightly in the fourth quarter.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The contraction in the housing market continues to drag down economic growth.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Declines in real residential investment subtracted nearly 1 percentage point from the overall increase in real GDP in 2007.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Even so, the inventory of unsold new homes remains unusually high, because the demand for housing has fallen about as rapidly as the supply.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Problems in the subprime market have virtually cut off financing in this sector.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Prime jumbo mortgages are being made, but the lack of a secondary market has caused the spread between rates on these mortgages and on those that have been eligible for purchase by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to widen substantially.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Even the standards for conforming mortgages have been tightened of late.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Weak demand, in turn, is leading to widespread declines in the actual and expected prices of houses, further discouraging buyers.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Starts of new single-family homes continued to fall in January, dropping to fewer than 750,000 units--a level of activity more than 1 million units below the peak in early 2006.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Judging from the further decline in permits last month, additional cutbacks in construction are likely.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: It appears that the correction in the housing market has further to go.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: For the better part of the past two years, the trouble in the housing market was contained; however, over the past several months, the weakness appears to have spread to other sectors of the economy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Tighter credit, reductions in housing and equity wealth, higher energy prices, and uncertainty about economic prospects seem to be weighing on business and household spending.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Labor demand has softened in recent months.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Private nonfarm payrolls were little changed in January, and the unemployment rate moved up to 4.9 percent, on average, during December and January, after remaining around 4-1/2 percent from late 2006 through most of 2007.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The higher level of weekly claims for unemployment insurance suggests continued softness in employment this month.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Apart from the labor market, the hard data on economic activity in the first quarter are limited, but, on the whole, the data suggest economic activity has remained very sluggish.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Retail sales were up moderately in nominal terms in January, but after adjusting for the rise in prices of consumer goods, real spending on non-auto goods appears to have been little changed last month.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, unit sales of new motor vehicles weakened.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Total industrial production rose just 0.1 percent in January for a second consecutive month, and manufacturing output was unchanged.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Much of the other information about the current quarter has come in the form of surveys of business and consumers--and most all of it has been downbeat.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, I can still see a few bright spots.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: One is that the level of business inventories does not appear worrisome at present.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Another is that international trade continued to be a solid source of support for the economy through the end of last year.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The worsening financial conditions and slower growth in the United States have had some effect on the rest of the world, but the prospects for foreign growth remain favorable.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The most recent news on inflation--the January report on the consumer price index (CPI)--was disappointing.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Once again, total or headline CPI was boosted by a jump in energy prices and relatively large increases in food prices; last month's rise left the twelve-month change in the overall CPI at 4.3 percent--twice the pace a year ago.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the January increase of 0.3 percent in the CPI excluding food and energy was slightly higher than the average monthly rate in 2007.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, the twelve-month change in this measure of core inflation, at 2-1/2 percent, was still slightly below the rate one year earlier.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The recent readings on core inflation suggest that the higher costs of energy, a pickup in prices of imported goods, and, perhaps, the persistent upward price pressures in commodity markets may be passing through a bit to core consumer prices.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The Implications of Financial Stress for the Economic Outlook The recent evolution of U.S. financial markets is a complicated story, and a full consideration of how and why this episode of financial turmoil developed is a topic for another speech.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Today, I am going to focus on some key aspects of the situation in which we find ourselves and discuss their implications for the economy and for monetary policy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The pressures from the financial turmoil have been most intense for those financial intermediaries that have been exposed to losses on mortgages and other credits that are repricing, as well as for those institutions now required to bring onto their balance sheets loans that previously would have been sold into securities markets.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: As those intermediaries take steps to protect themselves from further losses and conserve capital, and as investors more broadly have responded to the evolving risks, spreads on household and business debt in securities markets have widened, the availability of bank credit has decreased, and equity prices have weakened.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition to the drying up of large portions of mortgage finance that I referred to previously, conditions have firmed on loans for a variety of other purposes.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Responses to our Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey in January showed that banks have tightened terms and standards for household and commercial mortgages, commercial and industrial loans, and consumer loans.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In corporate bond markets, spreads have been widening on both investment- and speculative-grade issues.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Lenders are demanding much higher risk premiums for commercial real estate loans.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: And equity prices have fallen substantially over the past seven months, reducing household wealth and increasing the cost of raising equity capital for businesses.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, the easing of monetary policy that I will be discussing in a minute has, quite deliberately, been intended to offset the effect of this tightening, resulting in some borrowers seeing lower interest rates.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: But financing costs have risen, on balance, for riskier credits, and almost all borrowers are dealing with more cautious lenders who have adopted more stringent standards.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Those financial market developments are, in many respects, a healthy correction to previous excesses.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: But, in some cases, they may represent an overreaction, or at least positioning for the small probability of very adverse economic conditions.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In any case, they have the potential to adversely affect household and business spending.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The recovery in financial markets is likely to be a prolonged process.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The length of the recuperation will depend importantly on the course of the economy, particularly on developments in the housing market.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: If the deterioration in the housing market were greater than expected in coming months, the losses borne by financial institutions would be even greater, and lenders might further reduce credit availability.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: More widespread macroeconomic weakness could make lenders more cautious and could cause the financial problems to spread further.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The recent problems of financial guarantors, with possible implications for municipal bond markets as well as for bank balance sheets, are an indication that the financial sector remains vulnerable.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Even in a more favorable economic environment, some time is likely to be required to restore the functioning and liquidity of a number of markets.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The collapse of the subprime mortgage market and subsequent problems in other areas of the financial markets have brought to light a number of deficiencies in the practice of financial intermediation that will take some time to correct.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Clearly, lending standards in the subprime mortgage market were too lax, particularly for riskier households.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Compounding the problem, those involved in moving the loans from originator to investor, including the credit rating agencies, failed to ensure that the quality of the underlying credit was accurately assessed and represented.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, some of the financial instruments developed in recent years were opaque, making it difficult for investors to price them correctly.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: And many did not fully appreciate and properly manage the risks involved in the maturity, credit, and liquidity transformations that were taking place in several sectors of the financial market.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: A number of markets will need to make institutional changes before they are likely to function smoothly again, and regulators will need to adapt their oversight to take account of the lessons learned.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In the end, we will have a safer system, but one with more bank intermediation, less leverage, and higher financing costs for many borrowers.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The Monetary Policy Response The Federal Reserve has responded to the unfolding situation by acting to improve the access of depository institutions to liquidity and by easing the stance of monetary policy substantially.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Problems in the subprime mortgage market had been evident by early 2007, but the disruptions took a far more serious turn last August when pressures spread to commercial banks both here and abroad.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Among other things, the disruption of markets for structured credits had the effect of bringing a good deal of financial intermediation back onto the balance sheets of banks.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Uncertain about the ultimate call on their lending capacity, the financial strength of some of their counterparties, and their own needs for liquidity, banks and other lenders became much more reluctant to extend credit in term funding markets.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve was created in large part to supply liquidity and calm markets in such situations, importantly by assuring banks of a backup source of funding through the discount window.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: To enhance the utility of the discount window and encourage its use, the Federal Reserve reduced the spread between the discount rate and the federal funds rate last August, and we made lending available explicitly on a term basis, rather than only overnight.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: However, banks were reluctant to use even this more attractive discount facility because they feared that their counterparties would see it as a sign of weakness, and pressures in term funding markets increased.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In December we introduced a new method for banks to borrow from the Federal Reserve against a broad range of collateral--the term auction facility (TAF).
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The TAF is an auction through which a fixed amount of lending is offered to the banking system, and it seems to have been successful in avoiding the "stigma" problem and in helping funding markets return to more normal functioning.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Markets were also aided by coordinated efforts to supply liquidity by several other central banks at the same time.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: As the deterioration in financial markets increasingly has threatened to hold down spending and employment, the FOMC has eased monetary policy, reducing the federal funds rate target by 2-1/4 percentage points since the turmoil erupted in August.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Those actions have been intended to counteract the effects on the overall economy of tighter terms and conditions in credit markets, the drop in equity and housing wealth, and the steep decline in housing activity.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Our objective has been to promote sustainable growth and maximum employment over time.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: But easier monetary policy will not forestall a period of economic weakness in the near term.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Experience teaches us that some time is likely to pass between a decline in interest rates and its positive effect on demand.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Once financial conditions change, time is required for individuals to recalibrate, and then execute, their spending decisions.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Lower interest rates will not stop, only cushion, the correction in housing markets.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Easier monetary policy will not--and should not--"bail out" lenders and other investors who made poor choices or failed to protect themselves against the remote, but potentially severe, contingency that house prices would decline or against the much more predictable repricing of credit and liquidity risk.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The adjustment in financial markets is part of the process that ultimately will restore credit allocation and market functioning to a sounder, more sustainable basis.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: What policy can do is attempt to limit the fallout on the economy from this adjustment.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Lower interest rates should support aggregate demand over time, even in the face of widespread contraction in the supply of credit.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Certainly, interest rates on loans will be lower than if policy had not been eased, and, if policy is eased sufficiently, they can be absolutely lower than before for many borrowers, which could well be necessary in an environment where standards and nonprice terms on access to credit are tighter.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Among other things, lower rates should facilitate the refinancing of mortgage loans, and they will hold down the cost of capital to business.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, reductions in interest rates will not help borrowers facing a cutoff of credit from lenders, but, in general, credit is still flowing from banks and other lenders.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Easier policy should also support asset prices--or at least cushion declines that otherwise would have occurred.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: And expected policy easing likely contributed to the drop in the foreign exchange value of the dollar, which is bolstering our exports.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The extent of the financial adjustment, as I mentioned previously, is itself highly dependent on how housing and the economy evolve.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Part of the rise in risk spreads, reduction in credit availability, and the declines in stock prices in the past few months reflect investor efforts to protect themselves against the potential for very adverse economic outcomes--that is, the exposures and losses that would accompany a persistent steep decline in house prices and a significant recession.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Of course, these actions--reducing exposures, tightening credit standards, demanding extra compensation for taking risk--themselves make these "tail risk" scenarios even more likely.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In circumstances like these, the decisions of policymakers must take account of not only the most likely course of the economy, but also the possibility of very unfavorable developments.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Doing so should reduce the odds on an especially adverse outcome not only by having policy a little easier than otherwise, but also by reassuring lenders and spenders that the central bank recognizes such a possibility in its policy deliberations.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Whether the Federal Reserve has done enough in this regard is a question this policymaker will be weighing carefully over coming months.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Even as we respond to forces currently weighing on real activity, we must also set policy to resist any tendency for inflation to increase on a sustained basis.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Allowing elevated rates of inflation to become entrenched in inflation expectations would be costly to reverse, constrain our ability to cushion further downward shocks to spending, and result over time in lower and less stable economic expansion.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Inflation expectations generally have appeared reasonably well anchored, giving the FOMC room to focus on supporting economic growth.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, as I will explain below, for a variety of reasons, I do not expect the recent elevated inflation rates to persist.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In my view, the adverse dynamics of the financial markets and the economy have presented the greater threat to economic welfare in the United States.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: But the recent information on prices underlines the need to continue to monitor the inflation situation very carefully.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The Outlook for Economic Activity and Inflation How long the adjustment in financial markets will take and the consequences of that adjustment for economic activity are subject to considerable uncertainty.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: In my view, the most likely scenario is one in which the economy experiences a period of sluggish growth in demand and production in the near term that is accompanied by some further increase in joblessness.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: New building activity will continue to decline until the overhang of inventories of unsold homes has been substantially reduced, and the demand side of the market is not likely to revive appreciably until buyers sense that price declines are abating and financing conditions for mortgages are improving.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Consumer spending will be damped by the effects on real incomes of a weak labor market and rising energy prices and by the effects of declines in the stock market and home prices on household wealth.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Business spending on capital equipment should be held down by slower sales and production and by caution in a very uncertain economic environment.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonresidential construction is likely to lose some momentum in the wake of both weak growth in overall economic activity and tighter credit.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Some modest offset to these areas of weakness should come from export demand, which should be boosted by the lagged effects of recent declines in the dollar and supported by still-solid growth abroad.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: By midyear, economic activity should begin to benefit from several factors.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: One is the fiscal stimulus package that the Congress recently enacted.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The rebates that households are scheduled to begin to receive in May should provide a temporary boost to consumption.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Although the timing and the magnitude of the spending response is uncertain, economic studies of the previous experience suggest that a noticeable proportion of households are quite sensitive to temporary cash flow.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The potential effects of the business incentives are perhaps more uncertain.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Although economic theory suggests that they should bring forward some capital spending, past experience has been mixed.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, the decline in residential investment should begin to abate later this year as the overhang of unsold homes is worked off, reducing what has been a significant drag on economic growth over the past two years.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, the declines in interest rates that began last summer should be supporting activity over coming quarters, and their effects should show through more clearly to improvements in economic activity as the stress in financial markets dissipates.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Although a firming in the growth of economic activity after midyear now appears the most likely scenario, the outlook is subject to a number of important risks.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Further substantial declines in house prices could cut more deeply into household wealth and intensify the problems in mortgage markets and for those intermediaries holding mortgage loans.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Financial markets could remain quite fragile, delaying the restoration of more normal credit flows.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: As observed in the minutes of its most recent meeting, the FOMC has expressed a broad concern about the possibility of adverse interactions among weaker economic activity, stress in financial markets, and credit constraints.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: I expect the run-up in headline inflation to be reversed and core inflation to edge lower over the next few years.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: This projection assumes that energy and other commodity prices will level out, as suggested by the futures markets.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, greater slack in the economy should reduce pressure on prices and wages.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Despite high resource utilization over the past couple of years and periods of elevated headline inflation, labor cost increases have remained quite moderate, and inflation expectations remain reasonably well anchored.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, policymakers must remain very attentive to the outlook for inflation.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: As I mentioned earlier, the recent uptick in core inflation may reflect some spillover of the higher costs of food, energy, and imports into core prices.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: And the prices of crude oil and other commodities have moved up further in recent weeks.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: A related concern is that inflation expectations might drift higher if the current rapid rates of headline inflation persist for longer than anticipated or if the recent easing in monetary policy is misinterpreted as reflecting less resolve among Committee members to maintain low and stable inflation over the medium run.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Persistent elevated inflation would undermine the performance of the economy over time.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Conclusion These have been difficult times for the U.S. economy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: The correction of excesses in sectors of the economy and financial markets has spilled over more broadly.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Growth has slowed, and unemployment has increased; both borrowers and lenders are facing problems, and the functioning of the financial markets has been disrupted.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, inflation has risen.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: I believe we will see a return to stronger growth, lower unemployment, lower inflation and improved flows in financial markets, but it probably will take a little while.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: And adverse risks to this most likely scenario abound:  Uncertainty could trigger an even greater withdrawal from risk-taking by households, businesses, and investors, resulting in more pronounced and prolonged economic weakness; events beyond our borders could continue to put upward pressure on inflation rates.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: But we should not lose sight of some fundamental strengths of our economy.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Our markets have proven to be flexible and resilient, able to absorb shocks, and quick to adapt to changing circumstances.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Those markets reward entrepreneurship and risk-taking, and many people are looking for opportunities to buy distressed assets and restructure and strengthen businesses to take advantage of the economic rebound that will occur.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Monetary policy has proven itself, under a wide variety of circumstances, very effective in recent decades in damping inflation when needed and in stimulating demand and activity when that has been appropriate.
speech_title: The U.S. Economy and Monetary Policy
speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: Our job at the Federal Reserve is to put in place those policies that will promote both price stability and growth over time.

speech_venue: At the University of North Carolina at Wilmington, Cameron School of Business' Business Week Program, Wilmington, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn

speaker: Mishkin
text: There can hardly be a better time to make the case for economic and financial literacy than right now.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Others have doubtless stood before an audience like you in years past and made the same case, but now we face a downturn in our housing industry fueled, at least in part, by unwise mortgage borrowing and, at times, abusive lending practices.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Improving consumers' knowledge of the home mortgage process will better equip them to avoid unsuitable mortgages in the future.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Our national economy has been strained by this housing slowdown and other forces, causing policymakers and others to debate what response is necessary.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Also, during this election season, we are reminded of the importance of economic issues.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Just a brief consideration of these three cases shows that a better-educated citizenry can not only contribute to a better functioning economy, but also to a more-effective government.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: On the first point, many lessons can be drawn from the downward swing in the housing industry, ranging from those that individual consumers can learn at the micro level, to those that financial companies can learn about investment and oversight.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In that regard, the Federal Reserve has proposed new rules to strengthen regulatory oversight and to protect consumers in the future, and we continue to assess this episode to determine what more can be done to help homebuyers and homeowners.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, one of the most effective ways to help consumers is to empower them with information.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: And this gets to our first case for economic and financial literacy: Improving consumers' economic decision making will enhance the effectiveness of new rules and regulations.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: And while we at the Federal Reserve are charged with regulatory duties, we certainly see the value of education and the positive impact it can have on the broader economy.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: While the current troubles in the housing industry stem from a number of causes, a better-informed citizenry would likely have resulted in more-prudent decision making and, consequently, less harm to the economy.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the matter of the national economy, here the call for economic education is based on the idea that a better-informed citizenry makes for better economic policymaking.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This is a subtle argument, but its logic is no less clear.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As my friend Alan Blinder, the noted Princeton economist and textbook author, as well as the former vice chairman of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, has said, an uneducated citizenry can lead to simplistic policy solutions, and those solutions are usually suboptimal.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: "The fact that the basic level of economic literacy in the country, indeed in the world, is so low," Alan has said, "is one of the things that leaves the political process so vulnerable to this malady."
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 1 Now, even Alan would admit that it's difficult to draw a direct line from economic literacy to economic policymaking, but politicians listen to their constituents at home, just as they are supposed to do.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: And at a time when our elected officials are confronted with a myriad of options to address a slowing economy, or when they consider the increasing fears about a globalizing economy, it's fair to ask whether they are getting good economic counsel from their constituents.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This is not to say that there is only one valid answer for these complicated questions, but it does mean that we get a better answer when we are all better informed.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Let me reinforce this point by sharing this quote from Ben Bernanke, Chairman of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors:
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Chairman Bernanke made those comments nearly two years ago, but the message is no less relevant today.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Let's now consider our third case for economic and financial literacy--the role of citizens as voters.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Americans elect a president every four years and we also send representatives and senators to Washington.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As is so often the case, the pundits and the opinion polls tell us that the top issues on voters' minds this year are those relating to the economy.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: What do the candidates have to say about how, if at all, the federal government should address the lagging national economy?
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: How about issues relating to trade?
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even issues that are not often described as economic--such as health care, education, and the environment--are informed by an understanding of economic principles.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: All these issues are better understood by an appreciation of tradeoffs, cost-benefit ratios, and opportunity cost, to name just a few core economic tools and principles.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, as we are so often told, people vote with their pocketbooks.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: And not only do they vote with their pocketbooks, they also make a lot of pocketbook decisions every day that have an impact on the health of the economy, such as whether to take on a particular mortgage, how much to save and invest, whether to lease or buy a car, and how to manage credit cards.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This brings us back to the importance of financial literacy.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The choices we make as individuals--as consumers, investors, and even voters--are linked to the broader economy in ways that we don't always appreciate.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, one thing is certain--we make better decisions if we are better informed, and the whole economy benefits.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: That's the promise of economic education--to get back to the title of this session--that it not only improves the lives of individual consumers, but that it also makes for more-effective policy and a better economy.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Delivering on that promise is the hard part, of course, but that's where the National Council comes in.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: We at the Federal Reserve are proud of our relationship with the National Council and with other educational organizations around the country, and we look forward to continuing this important work.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The task at hand is not easy, as all of you know, but the returns are high.
speech_title: The Importance of Economic Education and Financial Literacy
speech_venue: At the Third National Summit on Economic and Financial Literacy, Washington, D.C.
