speaker: Bernanke
text: This audience, the National Community Reinvestment Coalition, is certainly aware that mortgage delinquency and foreclosure rates have increased substantially over the past year and a half.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This increase reflects significantly, though not exclusively, a sharp deterioration in the performance of subprime mortgages, particularly those with adjustable-rate features.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the end of last year, more than one in five of the roughly 3.6 million outstanding subprime adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs) were seriously delinquent, meaning they were either in foreclosure or ninety days or more past due.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 That rate is about four times higher than it was in mid-2005.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Lenders initiated roughly 1-1/2 million foreclosures last year, up from an average of 950,000 in the preceding two years.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: More than one-half of the foreclosure starts in 2007 were on subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Behind these disturbing statistics are families facing personal and financial hardship and neighborhoods that may be destabilized by clusters of foreclosures.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These realities challenge us to find ways to prevent unnecessary foreclosures.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And, looking toward the future, they challenge us to ensure a regulatory environment that promotes responsible lending and sustainable homeownership.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I would like to briefly discuss how we arrived at where we are today.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Then I would like to share with you what the Federal Reserve is doing to reduce foreclosures, to protect aspiring homeowners from unfair and deceptive practices, and to equip them to choose wisely from among the often confusing array of mortgage options.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, I would like to highlight the new regulations we have proposed under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Origins of the Subprime Mortgage Turmoil Over the past quarter century, advances in information technology, the development of credit-scoring techniques, and the emergence of a large secondary market, among other factors, have significantly increased access to mortgage credit.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: From 1994 to 2006, subprime lending increased from an estimated $35 billion, or 4.5 percent of all one-to-four family mortgage originations, to $600 billion, or 20 percent of originations (Inside Mortgage Finance, 2007).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Responsible subprime lending expanded credit to borrowers with imperfect or limited credit histories.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: More renters became homeowners than would have otherwise.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Though few subprime mortgages are being written today, I believe responsible subprime lending has been helpful, and at some point will be again, in fostering sustainable homeownership.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, far too much of the lending in recent years was neither responsible nor prudent.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The terms of some subprime mortgages permitted homebuyers and investors to purchase properties beyond their means, often with little or no equity.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, abusive, unfair, or deceptive lending practices led some borrowers into mortgages that they would not have chosen knowingly.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The current crisis has many roots.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The drop in home prices in many once-hot markets is among the most significant.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In a recent survey, nearly 30 percent of homeowners reported that their houses decreased in value over the past year.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 The decline in home equity makes it more difficult for struggling homeowners to refinance and reduces the financial incentive of stressed borrowers to remain in their homes.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Mortgage performance data show a strong correlation between adverse house price changes and subsequent increases in mortgage delinquency and foreclosure (Avery, Brevoort, and Canner, 2007; Gerardi, Shapiro, and Willen, 2007).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors who purchased homes in the hope of price appreciation seem particularly likely to walk away from "underwater" mortgages.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, the role of investors in the housing market has increased markedly over time.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: According to data collected under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA), lending to non-owner-occupants has risen from about 5 percent of the home-purchase loans in the mid-1990s to about 17 percent of all purchases in 2005 and 2006 (Avery, Brevoort, and Canner, 2007).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Mortgage delinquencies are also tied to local economic conditions; notably, several midwestern states struggling with job losses and slow income growth have seen increased delinquencies.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The deterioration in underwriting standards that appears to have begun in late 2005 is another important factor underlying the current crisis.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A large share of subprime loans that were originated during this time featured high combined loan-to-value ratios and, in some cases, layers of additional risk factors, such as a lack of full documentation or the acceptance of very high debt-to-income ratios.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 2006, for example, the HMDA data suggest that nearly 40 percent of higher-priced home-purchase loans involved a piggy-back loan or second mortgage.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 Indeed, many defaults are occurring within the first few months of origination, well before payment resets occur on subprime ARM products.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Much of the weakening in underwriting standards appears to have happened outside of institutions regulated by the federal banking agencies.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The HMDA data for 2006 show that more than 45 percent of high-cost first mortgages were originated by independent mortgage companies, which are institutions that are not regulated by the federal banking agencies and that sell almost all of the mortgages they originate.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this instance, this originate-to-distribute model appears to have contributed to the breakdown in underwriting standards, as lenders often found themselves able to pass on the credit risk without much resistance from the ultimate investors.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For a number of years, rapid increases in house prices effectively insulated lenders and investors from the effects of weaker underwriting, providing false comfort.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Another concern is the substantial number of borrowers with subprime ARMs whose interest rates are scheduled to reset upward--about 1.5 million in 2008.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 4 The problem posed by resets is serious, but it may be mitigated somewhat by lower short-term interest rates and by the efforts of servicers, including those working with the Hope Now Alliance, to find solutions for borrowers facing resets, including interest-rate freezes (Hope Now Alliance Servicers, 2008).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, the FHASecure plan, which the Federal Housing Administration (FHA) announced late last summer, offers qualified borrowers who are delinquent because of an interest rate reset and who have some equity in the home the opportunity to refinance into an FHA-insured mortgage.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recently, the Congress and Administration temporarily increased the maximum loan value eligible for FHA insurance, which will allow more borrowers access to this program.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The current high rate of delinquencies and foreclosures is not confined to the subprime market.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 2007, about 45 percent of foreclosures were on prime, near-prime, or government-backed mortgages.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Across market segments, delinquencies are rising fastest on the more-complex loans originated over the past few years.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In part, that trend seems to be due to the fact that such loans were made to borrowers in weaker financial condition.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In some cases, borrowers may not have fully understood the details of their loans, including the potential for large payment increases.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Federal Reserve Responses Effective responses need to build on an informed understanding of this complex picture.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, as these problems in housing emerged and deepened, the Federal Reserve System engaged with a wide array of market participants--including lenders, community groups, servicers, consumer advocates, public officials, and other regulators--to properly diagnose the problems and work toward sustainable solutions.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve System alone, of course, cannot resolve all of the problems in the marketplace, but we have responded thus far through our regulatory, supervisory, research, and community affairs functions.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Regulation and Supervision As part of a periodic review of our regulations under HOEPA, the Federal Reserve Board in 2006 began a systematic look at changes in the mortgage industry.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Four public hearings held around the country confirmed evidence that we were gathering from other sources that the mortgage market was undergoing the significant changes with which we are all now familiar.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our concerns led us in 2006 and 2007 to issue, along with other federal and state regulators, a series of guidances to the institutions we supervise that covered nontraditional mortgage loans, subprime lending, and servicing practices.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Those were good steps, but we also recognized that many of the problems we were beginning to see were a result of actions by companies and individuals not subject to our supervisory oversight.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, we conducted an additional HOEPA hearing, focusing on four specific areas: assessment of repayment ability; low- and no-documentation lending; escrowing for taxes and insurance; and prepayment penalties.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result of a careful review of available data and information, we proposed new rules under our HOEPA authority in December, banning practices that we found to be unfair or deceptive.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Significantly, bans on such unfair or deceptive acts and practices would apply to the entire mortgage industry, not just to institutions directly regulated by the Board.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our goal was to produce clear and comprehensive rules to protect consumers from unfair practices while maintaining the viability of a market for responsible mortgage lending.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The rules would apply stricter regulations to higher-priced mortgage loans, which we have defined broadly so as to cover substantially all of the subprime market.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 5 The regulations would be enforceable by state and federal supervisory and enforcement agencies as well as by consumers themselves, who could recover statutory damages for violations above and beyond actual damages.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The proposed rules cover a range of practices.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, the rules would prohibit a lender from engaging in a pattern or practice of making higher-priced loans that the borrower cannot reasonably be expected to repay from income or from assets other than the house.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Of course, appropriate attention to the borrower's ability to repay is a fundamental feature of good underwriting.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, we found that the prevalence of "stated-income" lending led to many borrowers receiving mortgages that they could not afford.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consequently, we would require lenders to verify the income or assets they rely on to make credit decisions for higher-priced loans--standard industry practice, in fact, for most lending until quite recently.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Third, our proposal would require higher-priced loans to have an escrow account for real-estate taxes and hazard insurance.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This rule would help ensure that borrowers can afford their payments and avoid the cases in which borrowers, especially first-time borrowers, did not understand that the monthly principal and interest payment was not the only financial obligation associated with homeownership.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Escrowing has become standard practice in the prime market, and our proposal would make it standard practice for this part of the market, as well.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Fourth, the proposed rules would ban prepayment penalties in situations in which the borrower may be especially vulnerable.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, prepayment penalties would be prohibited where the borrower's debt-to-income ratio exceeds 50 percent and, when permitted, would be required to expire at least sixty days before a scheduled increase in the loan payment.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The rule would also ban prepayment penalties that could enable a "loan flipping" scheme, in which a lender or its affiliate refinances the lender's own loan at adverse terms for the borrower.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In seeking information and opinion about these four issues, the Board determined that additional problems needed to be addressed as well, and for all loans, not just higher-priced loans.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Among the practices addressed by our proposal is the use of yield spread premiums (YSPs).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 6 Many consumers use mortgage brokers to guide them through a complex process and shop for the best deal.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Unfortunately, consumers may believe that the broker has a responsibility to get them that best deal, which is not necessarily the case.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In fact, the design of YSPs may provide the broker a financial incentive to offer a loan with a higher rate.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consumers who do not understand this point may not shop to their best advantage.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Therefore, we would prohibit a lender, for both prime and subprime loans, from paying a broker an amount greater than the consumer agrees to in advance.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Brokers would also have to disclose their potential conflict of interest.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The combination of stricter regulation and better disclosure will not solve all the problems.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We do believe, however, that this proposal will give consumers much better information and raise their awareness of brokers' potential conflict of interest while reducing a broker's incentive to steer a consumer to a higher rate.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To protect consumers and promote competition, our proposal would also ban seven specific advertising practices deemed unfair or deceptive.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Under our rules, for example, mortgage originators would not be allowed to advertise a mortgage as having a "fixed" rate unless the advertisement also states clearly how long the rate or payment is fixed, and they could not advertise loans in one language but have important consumer disclosures in another.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The proposal would also require that consumers receive loan-specific Truth in Lending Act disclosures early in the application process, when they can use the information to shop more effectively.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The proposal also addresses certain practices in loan servicing that can cause problems for consumers, such as delays in posting payments to a consumer's account, and it acts to prohibit coercion of appraisers by lenders or brokers.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We believe these proposed rules will help protect mortgage borrowers from unfair and deceptive practices.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the same time, we did not want to create rules that were so open-ended or costly to administer that responsible lenders would pull out of the subprime market.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: So, our proposal is designed to protect consumers without shutting off access to responsible credit.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We anticipate vigorous discussion through the public comment process that ends on April 8, and we will, as always, carefully consider this input before issuing final rules.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition to regulations, strong uniform oversight of different types of mortgage lenders is critical to avoiding future problems.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Regulatory oversight of mortgage lending has become more challenging as the breadth and depth of this market has grown over the past decade.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Other changes, such as the increased role of nonbank mortgage lenders, have added complexity.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To achieve more uniformly effective supervision, the Federal Reserve, together with other federal and state agencies, launched a pilot program last summer to conduct reviews of selected nondepository lenders with significant subprime mortgage operations.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These reviews will evaluate the companies' underwriting standards as well as senior management oversight of compliance with state and federal consumer protection regulations and laws.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will take corrective or enforcement action as warranted.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We plan to use this joint project as a vehicle for strengthening cooperation and coordination among federal and state agencies.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Research and Community Affairs The Federal Reserve is addressing the foreclosure crisis in capacities other than that of a regulator, leveraging our strengths in research and data analysis, our regional presence, and the many contacts we have developed with local community groups, lenders, policymakers, and other stakeholders in this issue.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Community affairs officers at the Board and the twelve Reserve Banks work with Federal Reserve research economists to anticipate and, where possible, mitigate foreclosure problems.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: They share detailed reports and information that help community organizations, nonprofits, state regulators, and others identify regions and neighborhoods most vulnerable to foreclosure and respond accordingly.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For instance, NeighborWorks America recently used the Board's analyses to help identify geographic areas and neighborhoods in most critical need of $130 million in emergency funds provided by the Congress to increase mortgage counselor capacity.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Solid analysis of available information is critical to crafting appropriate policy remedies, and the Federal Reserve has invested considerable resources into such studies.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, a Federal Reserve Bank of Boston working paper has analyzed the factors that predict foreclosure, finding a particularly important role for declining house prices (Gerardi, Shapiro, and Willen, 2007).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia is conducting a five-year study of pre-purchase homeownership counseling.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: That study will provide important information on the benefits of counseling services in fostering sustainable homeownership and help us understand the long-term effects of financial-management skills on the credit worthiness of low- and moderate-income homebuyers.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition to this ongoing research, the Federal Reserve is supporting efforts to reach troubled borrowers and to raise awareness in communities about ways to prevent foreclosures.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since July, the community affairs offices across the Federal Reserve System have sponsored or cosponsored more than fifty events related to foreclosures, reaching more than 4,000 attendees including lenders, counselors, community development specialists, and policymakers.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: There is also work to be done in mitigating the impact of unavoidable foreclosures on consumers and communities.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Families who cannot sustain homeownership will need to find new places to live, highlighting the critical need for an adequate supply of affordable rental housing.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consumers going through foreclosure typically will see their credit scores drop, raising longer-term questions about their ability to rebound financially and perhaps pursue a more sustainable home purchase at some later point.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: High numbers of foreclosed homes in some communities also raise challenges, and perhaps opportunities.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because vacant homes, in particular, impose real costs on neighborhood and communities, forward-looking strategies to keep these homes occupied are important (Apgar and Duda, 2005).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some efforts are underway to prevent vacancies, as well as return vacant properties to active use; some of these efforts may also help preserve the supply of affordable housing in areas that have experienced shortages.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 7 The Federal Reserve has recently undertaken a joint effort with NeighborWorks America to help communities develop strategies for neighborhood stabilization.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion It is clear that rising home foreclosures and delinquencies significantly challenge many consumers and communities, and I hope I have conveyed today that the Federal Reserve is strongly committed to fully employing our authority, expertise, and resources to help alleviate their distress.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will continue to collaborate at the national, regional, and local levels with other stakeholders in the public, private, and nonprofit sectors to help to avoid preventable foreclosures and to address the consequences of the foreclosures that occur.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the longer term, through our regulations and oversight, we seek to promote responsible and sustainable lending that will allow more Americans to achieve their goal of homeownership.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Under the proposal, a "higher-priced mortgage loan" would have an annual percentage rate that exceeds the yield on comparable Treasury securities by 3 percentage points or more for first-lien loans or 5 percentage points or more for subordinate-lien loans.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A YSP is the present dollar value of the difference between the lowest interest rate the wholesale lenders would have accepted on a particular transaction and the interest rate the broker actually obtained for the lender.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This dollar amount is usually paid to the mortgage broker.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It may also be applied to other loan-related costs, but the Board's proposal concerns only the amount paid to the broker.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some promising examples of programs to address vacancies already exist.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, the Neighborhood Housing Services Redevelopment Corporation in Chicago has acquired hundreds of abandoned properties from such sources as the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the City of Chicago, bank foreclosures (that is, real estate owned), and private owners.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The properties are then rehabilitated and sold to owner-occupants.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In highly depressed housing markets, the worst-quality units are often demolished to mitigate safety hazards and reduce supply.
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, in Flint, Michigan, the Genesee County Land Bank acquires vacant properties through tax liens (see www.thelandbank.org).
speech_title: Fostering Sustainable Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Community Reinvestment Coalition Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The mortgage market has long been a source of strength in the U.S. economy, but it is facing significant challenges, especially in the subprime segment that serves consumers who have shorter or weaker credit records.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As of January 2008, the most recent month for which data are available, about 24 percent of subprime adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs) were ninety or more days delinquent, twice the level one year earlier.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 1 Roughly 190,000 foreclosures were started on these mortgages in the fourth quarter, up 11 percent from the previous quarter.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 The significance of the problems with subprime loan performance is evident in the unusually high rate of defaults within a few months of loan origination, known as early payment defaults.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In January 2008, nearly 9 percent of subprime ARMs originated in the previous six months were already ninety or more days delinquent, twice the rate of the year before and nearly four times the rate two years earlier.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These problems have many causes, but the role of abusive lending practices is of particular concern.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such practices have led many people into homeownership that they cannot sustain, and have had adverse effects on their neighbors and communities as defaults and foreclosures can lead to declines in the values of surrounding properties.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Practices that have hurt consumers have also undermined the confidence of investors and contributed to a virtual shutdown of the subprime market with consequences for other segments of the mortgage market.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result, it is difficult for many borrowers, especially in the subprime space, to obtain home loans.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The implications of diminished access to mortgage credit are of particular concern to the audience today, given that the subprime market was the source of home purchase loans extended to many in the Hispanic community.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These events have highlighted the shared interest of mortgage borrowers, their communities, lenders, and investors in protecting borrowers from abusive practices and preserving their choices.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Abusive loans that strip their equity or cause them to lose their homes must not be tolerated.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Protecting borrowers with responsible underwriting standards also protects the integrity and proper functioning of the mortgage market by increasing investor confidence.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Effective consumer protection produces a complementary benefit for consumers by making more capital available to meet their needs.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Similarly, systematic efforts to keep borrowers who may have trouble meeting their loan obligations in their homes on a sustainable basis, by providing more certainty to the market, can have the complementary benefit of ensuring the flow of capital for potential borrowers.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: With these principles in mind, I will discuss current initiatives to mitigate foreclosures.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Then I will spend most of my time discussing the Board's recent initiative in proposing new regulations that apply to all mortgage lenders, not just federally supervised banks, that are designed to prevent abuse, unfairness, and deception in residential mortgage lending.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The expansive scope of this proposal is essential to ensure that consumer protections convey across the mortgage market, regardless of whether a borrower receives a loan from a bank, an independent mortgage company, or through a mortgage broker.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Preventing Unnecessary Foreclosures Given the high cost of foreclosures to lenders and investors and the disruption and distress that foreclosure can cause to consumers, their families, and their communities, it is in everyone's interest to avoid foreclosures whenever other viable options exist.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: With large numbers of borrowers facing potential repayment problems, it is in the interest of borrowers and investors alike for the industry to develop prudent loan modification programs and other assistance to help borrowers on a systematic and sustainable basis.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As you know, there are various initiatives underway to help borrowers struggling with their mortgages.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: NeighborWorks America and the Homeownership Preservation Foundation offer financial counseling services through the Homeowners HOPE hotline.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Hope Now Alliance, a broad-based coalition of government sponsored enterprises, industry trade associations, counseling agencies, and mortgage servicers, is making efforts to find ways to help borrowers through loan modification plans.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Housing Administration has established the FHASecure plan to provide qualified borrowers who are delinquent because of an interest rate reset and who have some equity in the home the opportunity to refinance into an FHA-insured mortgage.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I have been an active proponent of such streamlined systematic approaches to reduce transactions costs and to help mitigate foreclosure risk, and I strongly encourage market participants to adopt and to implement these fast-track modification proposals as quickly as possible.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I applaud these efforts but also recognize that much more must be done.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Challenges remain, for example, with respect to ongoing constraints on servicing capacity to expedite work outs.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Servicers must undertake the investment to overcome the capacity challenges and provide transparent and timely measures of the results.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve has been working with financial institutions and community groups around the country to address the challenges posed by problem loans.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For instance, we have been providing community coalitions, counseling agencies, fellow regulators, and others with detailed analyses identifying neighborhoods at high risk of foreclosures.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: By understanding those areas with concentrations of subprime mortgages, delinquencies, and foreclosures, community leaders can better target their scarce resources to borrowers in need of counseling and other interventions that may help forestall foreclosure.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Communities are also working to find ways to address the challenges that foreclosed homes can present, such as decreased home values and vacant properties that can deteriorate from neglect.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Toward this end, the Federal Reserve has recently engaged in a partnership with NeighborWorks America to help identify strategies to help stabilize neighborhoods.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is essential that organizations with access to at-risk homeowners, particularly those who may have additional challenges, such as language barriers, engage in foreclosure prevention initiatives to help keep families in their homes and stabilize communities.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve has worked to support consumers by providing them with the information they need to understand and shop for banking products, as well as to file a complaint against a bank.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Many of these consumer education brochures are available in Spanish.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Importantly, we have just launched a Spanish-language version of the Federal Reserve Consumer Help Center to help better meet the needs of Spanish-speaking consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have seen a dramatic increase in the number of consumers contacting us since we launched this centralized call center and website in November 2007, and now we have the capability to reach even greater numbers by providing information and assistance to Spanish-speaking consumers at 888-851-1920.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Board's Proposal I will now focus on the Board's recent proposal for stricter regulations prohibiting abusive and deceptive practices in the mortgage market under authority of the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA).
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This proposal is intended to protect consumers and to preserve consumer choice by targeting protections to borrowers who face the most risk.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have also sought to ensure that these standards are clear for lenders to reduce unintended consequences for consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Though clear, the standards are intended to be not overly prescriptive, so as to preserve access to responsible credit while amply protecting consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our proposal is also comprehensive, covering most mortgage loans with certain protections and the entire subprime market with certain more specific regulations.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: While comprehensive, the proposal would focus protections where the risks are greatest and preserve consumers' access to responsible credit.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our effort to produce robust, clear, and comprehensive rules was based on a rigorous analysis of available qualitative and quantitative data.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have put this proposal out for public comment until April 8 and eagerly seek suggestions to be able to craft the best possible final rule.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Comprehensive Scope Let me say more about the comprehensive scope of this proposal.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: It would apply stricter regulations to higher-priced mortgage loans, which we have defined broadly, and it covers all types of mortgage lenders, unlike guidance that only applies to federally insured banks.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We were particularly interested in ensuring that protections remain strong over time as loan products and lending practices change.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our analysis of the data suggested that the troubles in the mortgage market generally arise not from a single practice in isolation, but instead from the complex ways that risk factors and underwriting practices can affect each other, sometimes called "risk layering."
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, we have proposed using a loan's annual percentage rate, or APR, to determine whether the loan is covered by stricter regulations.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 5 Because the APR is closely correlated to risk, the proposed protections would cover loans with higher risks rather than single out particular risk factors or underwriting practices.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: With the APR thresholds we have proposed, we expect that the new protections would cover the entire subprime mortgage market and the riskier end of the "near prime" market, the latter also known as the "alt-A" market.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Covering part of the alt-A market would anticipate possible actions by lenders to avoid restrictions on subprime loans priced near the threshold.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: It would also address real risks to consumers in the alt-A segment.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This segment grew very rapidly, and it layered risks, such as undocumented income, on top of other risks, such as nontraditional loan structures allowing borrowers to defer paying principal and interest.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, we have heard from commenters who have expressed concern that in the current market environment, the proposed trigger could cover the market too broadly, and we will carefully consider the issues they raise and other possible approaches to achieve our objective.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our public hearings and our analysis identified problems not just in higher-priced loans, but also in the broader mortgage market.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, our proposal addresses unfair or deceptive practices for the vast majority of mortgage loans secured by a consumer's primary home.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Areas targeted this broadly include broker steering, appraisal coercion, unwarranted servicing fees, and deceptive advertising.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I'll touch on broker steering toward the end of my remarks.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Robust Approach to Affordability Extending credit that borrowers can afford to repay is a fundamental pillar of responsible lending.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Across the whole range of higher-priced mortgage loans, our proposal offers three rules that, working in combination, would help ensure that borrowers can afford their payments.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, is a requirement that a lender maintain responsible underwriting practices that genuinely assess borrowers' ability to repay.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This general requirement would be complemented by a specific requirement to verify the income and assets of the borrower that are relied upon in making the loan.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A third rule would require lenders to escrow property taxes and homeowners insurance to help borrowers meet these obligations.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This robust approach to affordability would help ensure that the subprime market promotes sustainable homeownership.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Just as important, it would also help protect consumers from abusive refinancings that strip equity.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Clear lending standards have the further advantages of increasing investor confidence in the mortgage market and helping to revive the flow of credit to consumers with shorter or weaker credit records.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Assessment of Repayment Ability Now I want to discuss the major elements of our proposed regulations for higher-priced loans in a little more depth, starting with the requirement to assess repayment ability.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The regulations would prohibit a lender from engaging in a pattern or practice of making higher-priced loans based on the value of the borrower's house rather than on the borrower's ability to repay from income, or from assets other than the house.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This prohibition is intentionally broad to capture all risks to loan performance and the different ways that these risks can be layered.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, the proposal avoids prescribing quantitative underwriting requirements.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, the proposal would prohibit a pattern or practice of disregarding the ratio of applicants' income to their debt, but it does not prescribe a maximum ratio because the appropriate number depends heavily on other risk factors, which vary from loan to loan.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the same time, the proposal does offer specifics.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, it would create a presumption that a lender had violated the regulations if it engaged in a pattern or practice of failing to underwrite at the fully-indexed rate.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our proposed regulations would be more robust and comprehensive than the subprime guidance the agencies issued last year.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The regulations would apply to all mortgage lenders, including independent mortgage companies.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, the regulations would be legally enforceable by supervisory and enforcement agencies.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Just as important, the regulations, unlike the guidance, would be legally enforceable by consumers who could recover statutory and actual damages for violations.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The proposed requirement to assess repayment ability is intended to protect consumers from abusive practices while maintaining their access to responsible credit.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We recognize that satisfying both objectives at the same time is a challenge.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The proposed rule's potential for consumer actions, coupled with its careful avoidance of prescribing quantitative underwriting thresholds, could raise compliance and litigation risk.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In turn, this could raise the cost of credit for higher-risk borrowers or limit the availability of responsible credit.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is why we have proposed prohibiting a "pattern or practice" of disregarding repayment ability rather than attaching a risk of legal liability to every individual loan that does not perform.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some commentators have argued that the pattern or practice requirement creates a higher standard of proof that can make it more difficult and costly for consumers to pursue litigation.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have specifically sought comment on this provision and look forward to perspectives offered by the industry and consumer groups.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Income Verification When we looked closely at why so many borrowers had mortgages that they struggled to repay so soon after taking out the loan, the prevalence of "stated-income" lending was a clear culprit.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Substantial anecdotal evidence indicates that failing to verify income invited fraud.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, when we looked at the loan-level data we saw a clear correlation between "low-doc" or "no-doc" lending and performance problems, particularly early payment defaults.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is why we have proposed to complement a broad requirement to assess repayment ability with a specific requirement to verify the income or assets a lender relies on to make a credit decision.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We recognize that stated-income lending may have a proper place when not layered on top of too many other risks.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, we would target the verification requirement to higher-priced loans, including the higher-priced end of the alt-A market, where the risks of stated-income lending could be layered on top of too many other risks.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The proposal identifies standard documents that would be acceptable, such as W-2 forms.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some consumers may have access to only nonstandard documents and others, such as self-employed entrepreneurs, may have some difficulty documenting their income.

text: This rule is meant to preserve consumer choice by allowing the market to identify credible nontraditional documentation of consumer income--for example, check-cashing receipts.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: To help ensure that the proposal preserves access to credit for the full range of consumers, we have sought public comment on this issue.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Escrows for Taxes and Insurance Another part of our proposal for higher-priced loans--a requirement to escrow taxes and insurance--would also help ensure that borrowers can afford their payments.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Escrowing has become standard practice in the prime market, and the case for making it standard in the subprime market, too, appears compelling.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consumers with shorter or weaker credit histories may be less likely to appreciate the sizable burden that taxes and insurance can add to the cost of homeownership, or more vulnerable to being misled by payment quotes that leave out these amounts.
