speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, when we looked at the data, we saw in the unusually high level of early payment defaults possible evidence that the lack of escrows hurt consumers who did not have experience paying property tax and insurance bills.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have proposed to address the problem with a requirement to escrow taxes and insurance on higher-priced loans, accompanied by a limited allowance for opt-out.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We wanted the regulations to prevent irresponsible efforts to encourage borrowers to opt out.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

text: In this respect the proposal is intended to preserve consumer choice while protecting consumers from unaffordable mortgage obligations.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Prepayment Penalties Having discussed the rules that would promote affordability, I want to say a word about our proposed rule on prepayment penalties.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These penalties can take a toll on consumers who have riskier loans, and many consumers may not even be aware their loans have a penalty.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accordingly, we have proposed a ban on prepayment penalties in circumstances of a high degree of risk to the consumer, and we are also addressing transparency concerns.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

text: The proposed rule would ban prepayment penalties where they are most likely to prevent a consumer from refinancing a loan that has a particularly burdensome payment.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Specifically, a penalty would be prohibited where the borrower's debt-to-income ratio exceeds 50 percent, and a penalty would have to expire before a loan's payment could increase.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The rule would also ban prepayment penalties where they are more likely to be part of a "loan flipping" scheme--specifically, where a lender or its affiliate refinances the lender's own loan.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Banning penalties altogether could cause all borrowers, including those who do not prepay, to bear the full cost of investors' prepayment risk, which could raise questions of fairness, and it could reduce consumer choice.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We recognize there are differing views on this and look forward to gaining those perspectives through the comment process.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Steering I have so far discussed the elements of our proposal that would seek to ensure that underwriting practices and loan terms on higher-priced loans do not present unwarranted risks to consumers.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: There is another potential source of risk to consumers that I want to address that is related to "steering"--the risk that when they use the services of a mortgage broker, they do not appreciate the extent to which the broker's interests may diverge from the consumer's interests because of "yield spread premiums."

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, when a lender pays a broker for a loan that has a higher rate, that payment can create a conflict of interest between the broker and the consumer.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This conflict is problematic if the consumer does not know it exists or assumes, incorrectly, that the broker is obligated to put the consumer's interests first.
speech_title: Protecting Homeowners and Sustaining Homeownership
speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, we have proposed to prohibit a lender, for both prime and subprime loans, from paying a broker any more than the consumer had expressly agreed that the broker would receive.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speech_venue: At the National Association of Hispanic Real Estate Professionals Legislative Conference 2008, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: It's a genuine pleasure to address the Virginia Association of Economists here at Washington and Lee University on an important issue in monetary policy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some of you may be wondering about the meaning of my speech title--"Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones."
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Well, putting the "shm" before a word is a way to cast a bit of skepticism on it.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, if your friend tells you that you are "fancy, shmancy," then you might be overdressed for the occasion.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: And if you exclaim, "Email, shmemail!"
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: then you've just found your inbox overloaded.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, there's also a significant distinction between the expressions "shlemiel" and "shlimazel," but that's more-advanced material that I will defer until another speech.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although this speech has a somewhat humorous title, my remarks will address a serious and important topic, namely, how central banks promote the stability of prices and economic activity and how this policy framework is communicated to the public.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: More specifically, I will consider whether central banks should describe price stability in terms of a desired range of inflation outcomes--often referred to as a "comfort zone" for inflation--or in terms of a specific numerical value at which the inflation rate is expected to settle down over some reasonable time horizon.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: After a brief review of the academic literature regarding the level of inflation that best promotes longer-run economic growth and employment, I will discuss several conceptual issues regarding the pitfalls of comfort zones and the benefits of specifying a point objective for inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, I will move from theory to practice and consider the experiences of other major industrial countries.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: As usual, my remarks reflect only my own views and are not intended to reflect those of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) or of anyone else associated with the Federal Reserve System.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: What is the Optimal Level of the Inflation Rate?
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Research in monetary economics usually specifies monetary policy objectives in terms of stabilizing both inflation and economic activity.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 2 Those two goals are related:  Maintaining price stability promotes stronger economic activity in the long run.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: What do we mean by price stability?
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: A widely cited definition is that the inflation rate is sufficiently low so that households and businesses do not need to take inflation into account in making everyday decisions.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 3 Broadly speaking, I believe this definition of price stability is a reasonable one, and in practice, central banks around the world have chosen average levels of inflation between 0 and 3 percent as consistent with this criterion.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, this range can be narrowed a bit further by considering the implications of economic theory and empirical evidence about the average inflation rate that produces the best economic outcomes.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In particular, the literature on the optimal inflation rate not only bolsters the case for low inflation but also highlights the risks of maintaining an excessively low inflation rate.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Case for Low Inflation All economists agree that hyperinflations, such as the one in Germany in the 1920s, are particularly damaging due to the resulting distortion of economic incentives and the waste of valuable resources.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even rates of inflation far short of hyperinflation appear detrimental to economic performance, as evidenced by the double-digit inflation rates of the 1970s.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: And over the past decade or so, central bankers and academic economists have reached a remarkable degree of consensus about the desirability of low and stable inflation--and as you know, arriving at a consensus is quite rare for economists.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The average rate of inflation distorts the efficient allocation of resources through three main channels.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, because some firms face costs in changing their prices, a rise in the general price level tends to generate undesirable movements in relative prices, thereby leading to an inefficient allocation of resources.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: This relative price dispersion increases with inflation, and the desirability of minimizing these relative price distortions provides a key rationale for price stability.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, inflation is an implicit tax on capital.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In an imperfectly indexed tax system, inflation seriously distorts saving and investment because investment income is taxed on the basis of its nominal rather than inflation-adjusted or real value.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In those circumstances, price stability may considerably improve the efficiency of the economy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 5 Third, a higher average inflation rate tends to generate distortions by raising the cost of holding currency and other non-interest-bearing assets.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Can Inflation Be Too Low?
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: While the benefits of low inflation are now widely recognized, somewhat less attention has been given to the pitfalls of maintaining inflation rates very close to zero, so I will now discuss this issue in somewhat greater detail.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Specifically, if the average inflation rate is too low, then the economy faces a greater risk that a given adverse shock could distort labor markets, induce debt deflation, or cause monetary policy to become constrained by the zero lower bound on nominal interest rates.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: These risks imply that undershooting a zero inflation objective is potentially more costly than overshooting that objective by the same amount, and that setting the inflation objective at a rate a bit above zero provides some insurance against these risks.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Inflation at rates close to zero might create nonnegligible costs to the economy because firms may be relatively reluctant to cut nominal wages.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 7 Sticky nominal wages can prevent labor markets from reaching the optimal equilibrium.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, empirical evidence from Switzerland and Japan indicates that in an environment of deflation or very low inflation, downward nominal wage rigidities become less prevalent.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Keeping the average inflation rate close to zero increases the likelihood that the economy will experience occasional episodes of deflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Deflation can be particularly dangerous for an advanced economy, in which debt contracts often have long maturities.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: As described by Irving Fisher (1933), an episode of deflation can lead to "debt deflation," that is, a substantial rise in the real indebtedness of households and firms, because the nominal values of debt obligations are largely predetermined whereas the nominal values of household income and business revenue are falling together with the general price level.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 9 Indeed, the deterioration of the balance sheets of households and firms can result in financial turmoil that contributes to further deflation and greater macroeconomic instability.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: With a very low average inflation rate, monetary policy is also more likely to encounter circumstances in which short-term interest rates are constrained by the so-called zero lower bound on nominal interest rates.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 10 Specifically, investors will never choose to lend money at a negative nominal interest rate because they always have the option of simply holding cash at a zero interest rate; thus, nominal interest rates cannot fall below zero.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: A number of researchers in the Federal Reserve System and elsewhere have analyzed the implications of the zero lower bound in estimated dynamic rational expectations models.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 11 If the economy faces a large contractionary shock, the optimal monetary policy response is to push the short-term nominal interest rate below the level of expected inflation, thereby reducing real interest rates enough to mitigate the impact of the shock.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: But if the central bank has an inflation objective very close to zero, the zero lower bound can prevent the full implementation of this policy response, and hence the economy will tend to exhibit greater volatility of economic activity and inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In contrast, given shocks like those seen over the past several decades, an average inflation rate higher than about 1 percent substantially reduces the frequency with which the economy hits the zero lower bound.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: An inflation objective of about 2 percent implies that monetary policy is rarely constrained by the zero lower bound and thereby minimizes the adverse consequences for macroeconomic stability.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: These considerations provide the foundations for a broad consensus among academic economists and monetary policymakers around the world that the optimal inflation rate is in the range of about 1 to 3 percent; that is, an average inflation rate outside this range would be detrimental to longer-run health of the economy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In light of that consensus, it might seem natural to specify price stability in terms of a range of acceptable outcomes for inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, several present and past FOMC participants have used the term "comfort zone" and specified a 1 to 2 percent range, thereby providing valuable information regarding their views about what levels of inflation are consistent with the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Analytical Case for a Point Objective Nevertheless, while a "comfort zone" approach may seem appealing, analytical considerations reveal some disadvantages of that approach as well as some significant benefits of specifying and maintaining a point objective for inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Pitfalls of Comfort Zones In particular, I would like to highlight three specific pitfalls associated with the "comfort zone" approach.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, when the price stability objective is formulated in terms of an acceptable range of inflation outcomes, the policy implications may be difficult to interpret.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, if the comfort zone spans a range from 1 to 2 percent, does that mean that policymakers are equally comfortable with inflation rates of 1.1 percent and 1.9 percent?
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Furthermore, confusion about inflation objectives might make it harder for a committee of policymakers to decide on the appropriate course of monetary policy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: When one member advocates a more accommodative policy stance than other members, it may not be clear whether that reflects a more negative outlook for the economy or a greater willingness to allow inflation to settle in or near the top of the comfort zone.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, the comfort zone approach might lead to greater confusion in policy deliberations and hence produce a less effective decisionmaking process.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, framing price stability in terms of a comfort zone could lead to perverse expectations dynamics and thereby generate larger fluctuations in economic activity, especially if policymakers maintain a neutral stance regardless of where the inflation rate falls within the comfort zone.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: For instance, a negative shock to aggregate demand that brought inflation near the bottom end of the range might cause long-run expected inflation to fall, which would raise the real interest rate if the nominal interest rate remained unchanged.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: This rise in the real interest rate would exert a further drag that could exacerbate the adverse impact of the original negative shock on the economy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Similarly, a positive shock to aggregate demand that raised inflation to the upper end of the range might cause a rise in expected inflation and thus a decline in the real interest rate, which would provide further stimulus to the economy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The result would then be more pronounced swings in economic activity.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Third, if a central bank places a high degree of emphasis on the boundaries of the comfort zone, then these threshold effects imply nonlinearities in the conduct of monetary policy that are likely to produce less desirable economic outcomes (Orphanides and Wieland, 2000).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the stance of policy would remain roughly neutral in response to a shock that leaves inflation just below the upper end of the comfort zone, whereas a slightly larger shock that pushes inflation just above that boundary would cause an abrupt shift to a contractionary policy stance.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such a "stop-start" approach is likely to cause greater uncertainty in financial markets and would also tend to generate greater volatility of the macroeconomy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Benefits of Maintaining a Point Objective In contrast to the various pitfalls associated with comfort zones, there are a number of significant benefits to maintaining a point objective for inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, as I have emphasized in several previous speeches, communication plays a crucial role in the success of monetary policy (Mishkin, 2007b and 2007c).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: And in this regard, it seems virtually self-evident that communicating about a single numerical value for the inflation objective is more straightforward than communicating about an interval or range of numbers.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, regardless of whether the central bank has a point objective or a comfort zone, it is inevitable that the inflation rate will fluctuate in response to various shocks; that's why it is also crucial for policymakers to communicate clearly about the outlook for the macroeconomy and about the central bank's strategy for promoting the stability of prices and economic activity.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: An explicit point objective anchors inflation expectations more effectively than a comfort zone.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: If the comfort zone is considered to be a zone of indifference, then the inflation rate might well exhibit highly persistent fluctuations inside the zone, perhaps even looking like a random walk within that range.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In that case, if inflation drifts up to the top of the comfort zone, then the private sector could take the view that inflation might remain at that rate for an extended period of time, especially if policymakers are not taking any action to bring inflation back toward the midpoint of the range.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, the comfort zone might then generate somewhat larger fluctuations in longer-run inflation expectations, which would in turn tend to contribute to wider fluctuations in actual inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In contrast, with a transparent and credible point objective, longer-run inflation expectations will be firmly anchored at that rate.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even if policymakers are relatively indifferent about the level of inflation within a comfort zone, research on the optimal design of monetary policy indicates that they shouldn't be:  The central bank should actively seek to bring inflation back to the midpoint of its comfort zone, thereby minimizing the probability that inflation wanders outside the boundaries of that zone.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In effect, the optimal policy strategy takes into account the benefits of insurance, and hence the midpoint of the zone becomes the point objective for inflation (Mishkin and Westelius, 2006).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Empirical Case for a Point Objective Now let's turn to the international experience.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 13 As shown in table 1, a number of major industrial economies have adopted explicit inflation objectives  In 1990, the newly independent Reserve Bank of New Zealand became the first central bank to establish such an objective.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Many governments have followed in New Zealand's footsteps, and the inflation objectives have been variously expressed in the form of a point, a range with a preferred midpoint, or a comfort zone (that is, a range of indifference).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In some cases, the inflation objective was adopted in part as a way to lock in the benefits of recent disinflation and to prevent the return of adverse inflation outcomes.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: New Zealand, whose inflation performance in the 1970s and 1980s was the worst among the industrialized economies, is arguably one such example.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In other instances, inflation had already been kept low and stable for some time, and the adoption of an explicit inflation objective followed from extensive research and debate on issues such as the benefits of low and stable inflation, the presence of biases in the measurement of inflation, and the importance of central bank communications.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although the mix of reasons and circumstances that led to the adoption of an explicit inflation objective varies across economies, there is a remarkable degree of similarity in the characteristics of these policy frameworks, from which three broad conclusions can be drawn.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, there is a fairly general consensus among central banks throughout the world that the average inflation rate should be somewhere between about 1 percent and 3 percent.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, point objectives have proven more effective than ranges in anchoring inflation expectations.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Third, when the inflation objective is formulated in terms of a range, the implied degree of nonlinearity in the central bank's policy actions can be alleviated by placing increased emphasis on the midpoint of the range.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: New Zealand The monetary policy objective of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand is to "keep future CPI inflation outcomes between 1 and 3 per cent on average over the medium term."
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The narrowness of this range may seem surprising, especially given the historical volatility of inflation in New Zealand.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: After all, New Zealand is a small open economy with a large commodity-producing sector, and as a result the economy is particularly subject to external shocks that can have a relatively large impact on consumer prices.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In this context, the use of a narrow comfort zone would increase the odds that inflation would fall outside the band at certain times.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some observers have argued that such outcomes may undermine the public's trust in the central bank's ability to deliver inflation outcomes in line with its stated objective, and hence that the inflation band should be widened.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 14 Nevertheless, a wider band would hinder the anchoring of inflation expectations, which is pivotal to the successful pursuit of an explicit inflation objective.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: As the previous discussion has illustrated, expressing an inflation objective in terms of a range makes it more difficult for a central bank to anchor inflation expectations, especially in the absence of any explicit emphasis on the midpoint.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: A related issue is that the boundaries of the range may be seen as "hard edges," that is, inflation outcomes inside the range may be seen as qualitatively different from those outside the range.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The nonlinear policy reactions implied by this approach can lead to greater variations in interest rates, exchange rates, and output.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The international experience indicates that even when inflation bands with hard edges have been introduced, subsequent changes in the central bank's policy framework and communications have tended to soften the edges of the inflation band.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The experience of New Zealand is particularly instructive in this regard.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Reserve Bank Act requires that price stability be defined in a specific and public contract, negotiated between the Minister of Finance and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Under the act, the Governor of the Reserve Bank is personally accountable for keeping inflation in line with the stated objective.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: (Indeed, the Governor could be fired for failing to do so.)
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Since 1990, price stability has been defined in terms of a band for the inflation rate.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the following decade, the Reserve Bank treated this band as having hard edges, both in its conduct of policy and in its communications with the public; indeed, the boundaries of the inflation band were occasionally referred to as "electric fences" (Sherwin, 1999).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, it became increasingly evident that the Reserve Bank's vigorous attempts to keep inflation within the band tended to generate destabilizing fluctuations in nominal interest rates and undesirable outcomes for the broader macroeconomy.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Given the dissatisfaction with that approach, the Reserve Bank's mandate was refined significantly in 1997, namely, in seeking to keep inflation within the band, the Reserve Bank should avoid "unnecessary instability" in output, interest rates, and the exchange rate (Sherwin, 1999).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: This refinement allowed the Reserve Bank to lengthen the time horizon for achieving the inflation goal, thereby reducing the need to respond to transitory price fluctuations and providing greater flexibility in promoting the goal of macroeconomic stability.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: And since the edges of the inflation band have been softened, the Reserve Bank has placed greater emphasis on the policy actions needed to bring inflation toward the midpoint of the band over the forecast horizon.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: United Kingdom The desire to anchor inflation expectations more firmly led the United Kingdom to move from a range to a point objective for inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Three weeks after the United Kingdom departed from the European Exchange Rate Mechanism in the fall of 1992, the Chancellor of the Exchequer announced an inflation objective of 1 to 4 percent, which was to be achieved by the middle of 1997.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The use of a range for the inflation objective was interpreted by many as a way of limiting the extent of discretionary policy and of acknowledging the extent of imperfect control over inflation (Bernanke and others, 1999, p. 154).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The initial target range of 1 to 4 percent was often perceived as a range of indifference, which implied that inflation just outside the range would be viewed as qualitatively different from inflation just inside the range.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a consequence, inflation tended to stay near the upper border of the range.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Dissatisfaction with that outcome motivated the subsequent decision in mid-1997 to move to a framework with an explicit point objective of 2-1/2 percent, with deviations in either direction treated symmetrically.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: This modification of the policy framework was well received by financial markets and the general public, and surveys of households and professional forecasters indicated that inflation expectations converged fairly quickly to the Bank of England's point objective.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Euro Area and Canada The importance of anchoring expectations helps explain why other central banks that initially adopted an inflation objective stated in terms of a rangeââeven a narrow oneââincreasingly emphasized a single value in their communications or have replaced the range with a point objective.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, in May 2003 the European Central Bank (ECB) clarified that in implementing its mandate of price stability, monetary policy would be aimed at maintaining inflation "below, but close to, 2 percent in the medium term"  (European Central Bank, 2003).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: That clarification was welcomed by market participants and likely made it easier for the ECB to anchor inflation expectations.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a final example, consider the evolution of the monetary policy framework in Canada.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the late 1990s, this framework was well described as a range with relatively hard edges because statements by Bank of Canada officials had consistently indicated that the boundaries of the target zone (which ranged from 1 to 3 percent) were to be taken more seriously than the midpoint (Bernanke and others, 1999).
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the past decade, however, the conduct of monetary policy has evolved in the direction of placing greater emphasis on the midpoint, while the range has been used mainly as a communication device rather than as an objective in itself.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conclusion I have argued today that the science of monetary policy provides a strong rationale for framing the inflation goal in terms of a specific point objective rather than as a range or comfort zone.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: 17 First of all, I've argued inflation should be low but not too low.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, I've provided a brief review of lessons from economic theory that can inform policymakers in their choice of inflation objectives.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Third, I've outlined what we can learn from the practical experiences of other industrial economies; indeed, in recent years, a number of foreign central banks have moved toward emphasizing the midpoint of an inflation range or have provided a specific point objective for inflation.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Finally, you may have noticed that I haven't said much about the United States in this speech.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nevertheless, the issues that I've discussed today have potentially important implications for the ongoing process of refining the Federal Reserve's policy framework and of enhancing our communications.
speech_title: Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones
speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, as Chairman Bernanke has recently indicated, our communication strategy is "a work in progress," and the Federal Reserve "will continue to look for ways to improve the accountability and public understanding of U.S. monetary policymaking" (Bernanke, 2007).

speech_venue: At the Sandridge Lecture of the Virginia Association of Economists and the H. Parker Willis Lecture of Washington and Lee University, Lexington, Virginia

text: Over the past couple of decades, an extensive literature has analyzed the benefits of low average inflation in a so-called New Keynesian framework.

text: These studies generally start from a neoclassical model and incorporate two key features:  monopolistic competition and costly price adjustment.

text: Interestingly, the larger the burden coming from the interaction of inflation and the capital income tax, the more government tax revenues will fall when inflation is reduced.

text: Feldstein (1997, 1999) provides a quantitative assessment of the benefits of price stability based on the interaction of inflation and the tax system, showing that a lower average inflation rate stimulates investment by reducing the effective tax on capital income.

text: Because real money balances bear no interest, the opportunity cost of holding them is the nominal rate of interest.
