speaker: Warsh
text: Prologue A little more than a year ago, I began to recount a story--already long-in-the-making--of the transformation of financial institutions driven by abundant liquidity in global financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 2 In those early chapters, one could not help but worry about the inherent risks to financial markets and the economy when the gloss of confidence wears thin, causing me to wonder aloud: "What happens when liquidity falters?"
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 3 Let me briefly try to recount this tale over the last few quarters before offering some rough plot lines from which the balance of the story can be divined.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The sleepy complacency of a bygone era seemed rudely interrupted by a liquidity shock last August.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 4 A global margin call on virtually all leveraged positions began.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: As you know, the Federal Reserve found it necessary to begin to exercise its monetary muscles in unprecedented ways.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The seasons darkened, and the plot thickened.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: New structured products and old financial institutions evidenced increasing signs of weakness.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Some central banks, including the Federal Reserve, helped supply liquidity to where it was most in need.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial market turmoil, partly as a result, was periodically placed in abeyance.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Casualties of the liquidity contraction nonetheless appeared; some remained in the narrative for awhile, others were removed with great dispatch.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The narrative continued to morph through the first quarter of 2008.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Central banks, while generally more comfortable remaining behind the scenes, took center stage with new tools and policy prescriptions.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The script was rewritten so that product innovation flowed, but this time from the public authorities.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Many private market participants receded to the shadows of the stage, some anxiously anticipating intermission.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: What some originally read as a short story punctuated by a liquidity shock evolved into a longer narrative.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Credit is threatening to displace liquidity as the primary antagonist.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: A credit crunch, particularly for small businesses and consumers, poses meaningful downside risks to the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And market participants are struggling to assess the possibility that the narrative turns into a multi-act, macroeconomic drama.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In the remainder of my remarks, let me explore three of the most trenchant and overlapping plot lines, none of which seem to avail themselves readily to a speedy resolution.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: First, a striking loss of confidence is affecting financial market functioning.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Second, the business models of many large financial institutions are in the process of significant re-examination and repair.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Third, the Federal Reserve is exercising its powers to mitigate the effects of financial turmoil on the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: This third plot line, however necessary, will not, in and of itself, ensure a more durable return of trust to our financial architecture.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In my view, public liquidity is an imperfect substitute for private liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: That is, only when the other plot lines advance apace--meaning that significant, private financial actors return to their proper role at center stage--will credit market functioning and support for economic growth be fully restored.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And for that to happen, as I am confident it will, we will find that the financial markets and financial firms are outfitted quite differently.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Plot Line 1: Liquidity in Financial Markets As I advanced in prior remarks, liquidity is confidence.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Liquidity expands with confidence in the efficacy of our financial architecture.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: When information, securities, markets, and institutions work in a seamless fashion to intermediate the flow of funds between investors and borrowers, liquidity flourishes.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: When the confidence in the financial architecture is meaningfully impaired, liquidity flounders.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: A couple of examples highlight the dramatic change in liquidity that is gripping financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: First, consider structured product markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Recall the explosive growth in securitization markets in recent years.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 5 The loss in confidence in structured products was first evidenced last year in securities backed by subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Actual and projected credit losses began to mount across many housing-related assets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 6 Participants also lost confidence in the value provided through the securitization process itself.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Some highly structured products, such as collateralized debt obligations squared, vanished.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Yields on non-agency mortgage-backed securities and commercial mortgage-backed securities skyrocketed; and, in some cases, securitization markets simply shut down.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: All in all, this decline in confidence, while painful, is understandable.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investors and financial institutions became complacent in their abilities--and the ability of credit rating agencies--to evaluate credit risks of complex structured products.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And while the originate-to-distribute model entails legitimate principal-agent problems, investors did not demand or enforce safeguards.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Even many large, sophisticated financial institutions chose to retain super senior and AAA-rated tranches for their own accounts.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In so doing, they systematically erred in assessing the assets' risk profile.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, these products--born in times of massive liquidity--were often not well designed to ensure efficient workout arrangements should the abundant pools of liquidity retreat or should unexpected defaults emerge.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Next, consider short-term credit markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Many financial products, such as asset-backed commercial paper (ABCP), auction rate securities (ARS), interbank funding products, and repurchase agreements (RPs), were intended to be steady, supportive credit facilitators in a liquidity-rich environment.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In reality, these products involved a good deal of maturity mismatching and rollover risk.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: So, when liquidity retrenched, these markets experienced substantial disruptions.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: ABCP outstanding fell by a staggering $300 billion this past summer.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Issuance of ARS--long-term bonds that reissue and reprice at very short intervals--came to an abrupt halt.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And, the interbank funding and RP markets showed significant signs of strain.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Credit quality concerns alone do not appear, even now, sufficiently widespread to induce the depth of problems witnessed in financial markets during the past several months.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Some ARS that failed, for example, funded pools of federally guaranteed student loans.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I do not mean to suggest that counterparties themselves are blameless--many had been less than fully transparent.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Unclear disclosure by some financial institutions with respect to their off-balance-sheet commitments and liquidity support accentuated the uncertainty that is responsible for some of the poor market functioning.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: More fundamentally, in my view, funding market disruptions reflect a striking decline in confidence in the financial architecture itself.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Perhaps an analogue to banking systems without deposit insurance is appropriate: Depositors withdraw funds if they believe others will act similarly.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In short-term credit markets with minimal liquidity support, investors balk if they lose confidence in other investors' willingness to roll maturing paper.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Even when liquidity support exists, it may well prove insufficient to address market-wide concerns.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Many dealers of ARS, for example, withdrew their implicit liquidity support when failures became more frequent.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Even those ABCP programs purportedly with full explicit liquidity support were implicated in the turmoil.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: I hesitate to ascribe this loss in confidence simply to a change in animal spirits or to dismiss this occurrence as some kind of contagion.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: After all, a loss in confidence can be completely rational: Illiquidity forces issuers to sell assets into distressed markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: So, I argue, the functioning of short-term credit markets is invariably tied to changes in confidence of our financial architecture--on the way up and on the way down.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The arc of this narrative, thus, necessarily began some years ago.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Increasingly abundant confidence when things were advancing apace--unsustainably so, it turns out--gave rise to levels of liquidity that engendered complacency among investors and counterparties.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The financial architecture grew increasingly impervious to skeptics and dissenters, perpetuating insufficient transparency and under-informed risk-taking.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It was commonly believed that short-term, secured credit markets would perpetually remain open to finance high-quality assets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And the notion of liquidity risk management was anachronistic, or so it seemed.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Market participants now seem to be questioning the financial architecture itself.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The fragility of short-term credit markets is a powerful manifestation of that loss of confidence.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: There are some encouraging, early signs of repair, but regaining the confidence that markets require will take time, and perhaps uncomfortably to some, patience.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It may also require new forms of credit intermediation.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Plot Line 2: Transformation of Financial Institutions The rise and fall of liquidity is not only changing fund flows in financial markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It may also be transforming the business models of financial institutions themselves--no matter their size, regulatory structure, peer group, funding status, or geography.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The period that preceded the recent turmoil was marked by abundant liquidity, high transaction volumes, and remarkably low volatility.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: That environment proved exceptionally hospitable to significant profits across classes of financial institutions.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It also was supportive of high leverage, and correspondingly high returns on equity for financial intermediaries.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Of no less consequence, it drove a conflation of roles among commercial banks, investment banks, and asset managers.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The core functions of credit intermediation--creating, distributing, and owning risk--remained constant, but more institutions came to believe that there were inescapable synergies by operating across all three primary functions.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: From 2002 to mid-2007, many large financial institutions did just that, and to great effect--creating products by aggregating and reconstituting assets, distributing bespoke risks across institutional and retail channels, and retaining certain preferred positions for proprietary accounts.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: A changing paradigm of financial intermediation may well be on the horizon.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: From the market's perspective, financial institutions overproduced goods and services that now have to be warehoused or liquidated.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: From the perspective of financial institutions themselves, the old business models may be in the process of being upended.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And from the perspective of a dispassionate central banker, the contemporaneous changes in balance sheets and income statements by incumbent financial institutions--most notably, deleveraging and paring of business lines--are likely to prove highly consequential to the near-term outlook for the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Changing forms of financial intermediation are expected, given higher volatility and less leverage, in some cases building on old-fashioned banking products.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Commercial and thrift deposits, for example, backed by a loyal customer base, may offer greater franchise value.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Investment banks may reconfigure capital structures and core trading businesses to maximize benefits in a higher volatility environment.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Asset-gatherers, whether in the form of traditional money-management firms or hedge funds, that survive this time of testing may rely more on term funding and seek equity returns across beaten-down classes of structured and debt products.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And dependable, recurring revenues, even at lower levels, may warrant a premium valuation in the public markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The case for opportunistic capital is improving.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Some curative steps by incumbent financial institutions are in the offing.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial institutions should continue to reassess their sources and uses of funding, their risk-management systems, risk tolerance, and human capital.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Generally, they should not hesitate to pare their dividend and share repurchase programs.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And, they should raise new capital to strengthen their balance sheets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These actions, in my view, are important signs of strength, and will ensure that financial institutions thrive in the emerging financial architecture replete with new opportunities.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These actions will have concomitant benefits on real economic activity.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Plot Line 3: Federal Reserve's Policy Formulation The central bank's responsibility is not to individual firms but to financial markets, and only then, to the extent that financial market stresses affect the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Given the fragility evidenced in financial markets, and the toll it is taking on real activity, the Federal Reserve agreed to take center stage.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: This is a role for which we did not volunteer, but one in which we are prepared to serve.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The role has been thrust upon us by a loss of confidence in our existing financial architecture.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Hence, we should remain at center stage as long as is necessary, but no longer.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: The Fed responded aggressively to mitigate spillovers to the real economy, exercising some authorities for the first time in decades.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: To prevent more serious financial fallout, the Fed established and expanded various lending facilities to depository institutions and primary dealers.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: 7 Some facilities allow daily access to variable amounts of funding, and others provide access to a fixed amount of longer-term funding at pre-announced auction dates.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Still other facilities target action involving repurchase transactions with primary dealers.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These recently implemented measures appear to have reduced, to some extent, strains in the financial situation.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In particular, conditions in the RP market have improved.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: And, while Libor and commercial-paper spreads have remained elevated, they are below their year-end highs.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: In the corporate bond market, risk spreads have narrowed a bit in recent weeks and measures of secondary-market functioning are improved.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: While the adjustment process by financial intermediaries is showing signs of promise, the healing process is not likely to be linear.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: More consequentially, we should recognize that Fed-supplied liquidity is a poor substitute for private-sector-supplied liquidity.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: When liquidity flows among private-sector participants, the players can more judiciously assess risk and reward, more adroitly learn from the recent turmoil to strengthen the resiliency of credit intermediation, and more ably allocate capital to its most productive uses in the real economy.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, Fed-provided liquidity should not be mistaken for capital.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Volatility is generally a friend, not a foe, of market functioning.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: It should not be treated as an externality from which we suffer.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Volatility, absent destabilizing moves, should be allowed to effectuate change in the financial architecture of private markets.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Only then, I suspect, will a more robust recovery in market liquidity, investor confidence, and real economic activity be achieved.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: Of course, monetary policy continues to play an important role in the Federal Reserve's policy formulation.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: We have reduced the policy target rate by a cumulative 3 percentage points since August.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
text: These actions, together with significant actions to support liquidity, are intended to promote growth and mitigate downside risks to economic activity.
speech_title: Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens
speech_venue: At the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, New York

speaker: Warsh
