speaker: Kroszner
text: I am pleased to address the inaugural Community Reinvestment Fund (CRF) Annual Community Forum Series.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The development of sustainable capital sources through innovation is an important goal for the Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFI) industry.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Today's host, CRF, has played a pioneering role in the development of a secondary market for community development loans, a topic I spoke on more than a year and a half ago in Washington, D.C.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The financial markets have experienced much turbulence since that time.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The turmoil in the subprime mortgage market, in particular, has affected liquidity of the larger secondary markets.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Given the cautious state of financial markets, how can the CDFI industry enhance the attractiveness of CDFI investments to private capital?
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The markets have changed, but the core ideas I raised in my previous remarks are more relevant than ever.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: There is a striking parallel with the challenges for the re-emergence of the subprime mortgage market and the adoption of innovations in the community development investments market.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: To overcome the unease of the current financial markets and attract a new source of capital, new market entrants must make particular efforts to reduce the uncertainty associated with their investment opportunities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: For the CDFI industry, the challenges that need to be addressed are improving information about these products, developing models of risk and pricing, and standardizing these contracts.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Addressing these issues will be critical to jump-start sustainable private CDFI investments as well as to revive the subprime mortgage market.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Growth of Community Development Finance and Current Challenges The Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) was enacted more than 30 years ago in response to deteriorating economic conditions in urban areas, particularly in lower-income and minority communities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The CRA served as a catalyst in attracting innovative public and private investment capital into low- and moderate-income communities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consider the following: In 1991, 2,000 community development corporations (CDCs) built 300,000 units and 17 million square feet of commercial space.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: In 2006, 4,600 CDCs built 1.2 million units and 126 million square feet of commercial space.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Today, there are more than 600 CDFIs with more than $19 billion in assets and with more than $20 billion of finance activities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The CRF has issued three rated securities within the past six years totaling almost $200 million, opening the door to institutional investors and expanding the marketplace.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The migration toward sustainable mainstream capital sources is important in light of budgetary challenges facing governmental and philanthropic funding sources.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: For CDFIs to expand the scope and volume of their financing activities, they need to develop new products and innovations that tap more predictable sources of funding.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accessing the broad depth of the capital markets as a self-sustaining funding source for community development would yield enhanced benefits, such as more-efficient delivery of capital, greater funding and underwriting discipline, and reduced finance costs.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, a real challenge is building a bridge between the two very different worlds of capital markets and community development.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The former requires strict market discipline, a rich set of data to assess risk and pricing, and standardization.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The latter, community development, however, has a commitment to individuals and communities that have been left out of the economic mainstream and uses products tailored to their unique circumstances.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: These two worlds, however, can be brought together; and that has begun to happen, particularly around the challenges I will discuss in greater detail.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Importance of Data for New Products and Proper Risk Modeling When a new product is being developed, there is an initial experimentation phase in which market participants learn a great deal about the product's performance and risk characteristics.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: This phase involves gathering and processing information and modeling the performance of the product in various scenarios and under different market conditions.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: It may then take time for market participants to understand what, exactly, they need to know to value a product.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: During the early phases, a fair amount of due diligence is appropriate, given the greater uncertainty associated with innovative products.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the initial experimentation phase, the terms and characteristics of a new product are adjusted in response to market acceptance--or lack thereof.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: During this period, market participants are seeking and providing information so that they can properly value the product, judge its potential for risk and return, assess its market acceptance and liquidity, and determine the extent to which the risks of the product can be hedged or mitigated.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: To do this, market participants must perform due diligence, a process to gather and assess relevant sources of information to evaluate that product.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Due diligence is critical because market participants must trust but verify the market-provided information.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Potential purchasers, for example, might engage in various activities, ranging from assessing risk exposures through stress testing to assessing the enforceability of contracts that define the requirements of investors, trustees, guarantors, and originators.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have recently seen how a lack of information and insufficient due diligence have created problems in the market for subprime residential mortgage-backed securities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Many investors appear not to have demanded sufficient information about these investment vehicles, or perhaps did not carefully evaluate the information that was available.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Instead, they may have simply accepted or trusted credit ratings as a substitute for their own risk analysis, and not verified enough.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result, subprime delinquencies and defaults exceeded expectations.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Lack of information, a stressed financial environment, and disparate contract obligations led to a general lack of liquidity in the subprime market, which later spread to the broader market for mortgage securities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Investors in new and innovative products have suffered losses before.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the early 1990s, for example, participants engaged in the collateralized mortgage obligation (CMO) market and in certain types of interest rate derivatives that did not have adequate information about the potential volatility and prepayment risk involved.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consequently, market participants did not appropriately model these risks and suffered significant losses when market interest rates rose sharply in the mid-1990s.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: As in the case of today's market for residential mortgage-backed securities, the general market reaction was a flight away from these instruments.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, over time, the market was restored as market participants came to better understand the risks and as standardized methods were developed to measure the risks and model the value of these instruments under alternative scenarios.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Increased information and standardized pricing conventions, such as the use of option-adjusted spreads, moved these instruments from the experimentation and learning phase to broad market acceptance.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: When market participants realize that they do not have the information necessary for proper valuation of risks, market liquidity can become impaired, such as in the CMO market in the 1990s and in the subprime market recently.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: A significant investment in information gathering, processing, and evaluation may be necessary to revive markets.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: This process will likely take time.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, more-detailed data will need to be collected in a more systematic manner in order to better understand the nature and risks of the instruments and their underlying assets.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, investments will need to be made to warehouse and model data related to these instruments, which will enhance the understanding of risks, particularly under stress conditions.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, investments in human capital expertise--that is, in people so that they can better understand, interpret, and act appropriately on the results of the modeling and analysis of the information gathered--will also need to be made.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Finally, sellers may respond by reducing complexity and by improving the quality of the underlying assets, increasing transparency, or both.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ultimately, the payoff from these activities will be a greater understanding of risks and greater ability to value the instruments.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: For innovations in the community development investment markets, it will also likely take time for these markets to mature because of the time and cost to systematically collect data and for investors to understand these new instruments.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: To accelerate the development of these markets, however, some key issues will need to be addressed.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, how will the CDFI industry organize itself to generate and collect this data?
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, who is poised to lead efforts in setting standards for industry data?
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Finally, who and how will the intellectual capital be developed to model and structure these new instruments?
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: There should also be consideration of existing standards from established products that parallel developing ones, such as the adoption of best practices for both mortgage securitizations and community development securitizations.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: I do want to acknowledge that there have been many notable accomplishments in pioneering community development investments.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, there is a growing secondary market for community development loans; community development venture capital has grown 100 percent since 2002 to more than $800 million in assets under management in 2004; since 2002, the New Markets Tax Credit Program has issued $16 billion in allocations, with a growing sophisticated market for investments and trading of the tax credit equity.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am pleased that the Federal Reserve Banks have played an active role as a convener on these topics and in the dissemination of best practices and policy.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: I enjoyed sharing my thoughts on the topic of the development of the secondary markets for community development loans at a forum that was hosted last year by the Board of Governors and the Federal Reserve Banks of San Francisco and New York.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: For these markets to grow significantly, however, there must be continued dialogue and exchange between market participants to collect these data uniformly from the beginning to the culmination of these deals so that performance data are captured.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Standardization in Developing Markets These data should be collected with consideration toward improving standardization of many of the aspects of the product, which can help to increase transparency, improve efficiency, and reduce uncertainty.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, the recovery of the CMO market was aided by improved information and modeling, which increased confidence, especially as products became increasingly standardized.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Standardization in the terms and in the contractual rights and obligations of purchasers and sellers of the product reduces, but does not eliminate, the need for market participants to engage in extensive efforts to obtain information and reduces the need to verify the information that is provided in the market through due diligence.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Reduced information costs, in turn, lower transaction costs, thereby facilitating price discovery and enhancing market liquidity.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Also, standardization can reduce legal risks because litigation over contract terms can result in case law that applies to similar situations, thus reducing uncertainty .
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The benefits of the development of standardization for enhancing the liquidity of financial markets have a long history.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: One particularly clear example dates back to the development of exchange-traded commodities futures contracts in the mid-1800s.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The standardization of the futures markets improved the flow of information to market participants, reducing transaction costs and fostering the emergence of liquid markets.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the mid-1850s, the market for grain did not enjoy the very deep liquidity we see in today's market.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the time, Chicago was facing competition from exchanges in Minneapolis and St. Louis and from some in Europe that had created innovative structures to make markets more liquid.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: To create a liquid market for grain trading, buyers and sellers of grain needed a way of systematically analyzing the different kinds of grain that came into the exchange from different sources.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, the market needed a way to "grade the grain."
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The market created special silos that combined grain from a number of sources.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Buyers no longer bought a silo of grain from one source; a silo, for example, of "Winter Wheat Number 2" would be graded in a way that allowed buyers to know exactly what they were getting.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Standardization and related controls reduced traders' information requirements and, thus, their transaction costs.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Board of Trade established minimum quality standards based on the need for market participants to evaluate the reliability of promises of future deliveries of grain to the buyer.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: In 1865, the Chicago Board of Trade standardized the delivery dates for the contracts, thus fostering the emergence of liquid markets in which traders could readily hedge the risk of price changes in the commodities and contracts.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Buyers and sellers of grain ultimately became members of the exchange, supported by an underpinning of standardized measures of grain quality and minimum standards for exchange members.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: This example of how standardization helped jump-start a marketplace may provide insights regarding the current challenges in the subprime markets as well as the development of the community development investment market.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: As of January 2008, the most recent month for which data are available, about 24 percent of subprime adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs) were 90 or more days delinquent, twice the level one year earlier.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: 3 Roughly 190,000 foreclosures were started on these mortgages in the fourth quarter, up 11 percent from the previous quarter.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: 4 The cost of foreclosures is high for lenders, investors, communities and causes severe disruption and distress to individuals and families.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: With the continuing high rates of foreclosure and the high costs associated with foreclosures, it is in the interest of lenders, investors, and borrowers to develop prudent loan modification programs to help borrowers on a larger scale and at sustainable levels.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Efforts to streamline or standardize the loan modification process could lower transaction costs, provide timely relief for distressed borrowers, and reduce uncertainties in the market for subprime mortgage-backed securities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Industry and consumer groups are exploring loan modification templates, clarification of accounting rules, automated electronic platforms, and standards to streamline the loan modification process.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Hope Now Alliance--a broad-based coalition of government-sponsored enterprises, industry trade associations, counseling agencies, and mortgage servicers--is making efforts to find ways to help borrowers through loan modification plans.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Board has also sought to ensure clear lending standards through stricter regulations prohibiting abusive and deceptive practices in the mortgage market under the authority of the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA).
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: This proposal is intended to protect consumers and to preserve consumer choice by targeting protections to borrowers who face the most risk.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Under HOEPA, the Board is considering changes that would stem abusive practices by addressing the following: a requirement to assess repayment ability, a requirement to escrow taxes and insurance, a ban on prepayment penalties in certain circumstances, a prohibition on a lender paying a broker more than the consumer had expressly agreed that the broker would receive, and a ban on specific advertising practices deemed unfair or deceptive.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Clarifying lending standards will increase investor confidence in the mortgage market and help to revive the flow of credit to consumers, particularly those with shorter or weaker credit histories.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: These lessons learned from standardization challenges facing the subprime market may be helpful as the community development industry considers ways to reduce uncertainty to enhance the attractiveness of CDFI investments.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The wide variety of investment activities of the CDFI industry is a formidable challenge to standardization.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The industry encompasses rental housing and commercial real estate and small business finance and has disparate origination channels that range from small non-profit intermediaries to large financial institutions.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: A more recent development in the over-the-counter markets may be informative.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Over-the-counter derivative products are multifaceted and designed to be customized to the unique needs of market participants.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: To standardize these products, while maintaining their unique features, the International Swaps and Derivatives Association created a master agreement that not only provided standard definitions and a general outline for the contract, but also provided latitude to include customized terms.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: The master agreement also sets forth a template for workout procedures if a counterparty defaults, allowing parties to adjust risk-management strategies based on the work-out arrangements.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ultimately, the standardization provided by the master agreement reduces uncertainty about the instruments, lowers transaction costs, and facilitates price discovery and market liquidity.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Similarly, the community development investments field may consider the benefits of standardizing some type of master agreement that captures key structural provisions and that incorporates the flexibility to include customized terms of the underlying transactions.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would also encourage the CDFI industry to explore the possibility of some type of organized marketplace for its investments, whether it is an online platform or an added component of an existing marketplace, or some other similar initiative.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusion To achieve a more dynamic marketplace for community development investments, the CDFI industry should continue to dialogue and to strengthen bridges with mainstream financial market participants.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: To reduce uncertainty around community development investments, the CDFI industry must collect and provide uniform data so that appropriate risk and pricing models can be developed and must also make efforts to standardize these contracts.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conversely, capital providers must strengthen working relationships with the CDFI industry to develop a richer understanding of the finance activities and unique risks and strengths of these investment opportunities.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: As these two seemingly disparate worlds of the capital markets and the community development industry address these challenges together, a powerful source of sustainable private capital can be tapped to fund an equally powerful spectrum of community investments.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am confident that the expertise and dedication found in the community development industry can move the industry in the right direction to address these obstacles as well as to expand the flow of capital to low- and moderate-income communities and individuals.
speech_title: Developing Sustainable Capital for Community Investments
speech_venue: At the Community Reinvestment Fund First Annual Forum, Minneapolis, Minnesota

speaker: Bernanke
text: President Bollinger, Dean Hubbard, Co-Chairman Kravis, and distinguished guests, I am very pleased to be here and especially honored to receive the Columbia Business School's Distinguished Leadership in Government Award.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This evening I would like to offer a few thoughts on mortgage markets and the recent increase in the pace of delinquencies and foreclosures.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: My particular focus will be on geographic variation in mortgage performance and how that variation can help us better understand and prevent foreclosures.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will also discuss some initiatives taken by the Federal Reserve to address the foreclosure crisis as well as other policies that might be used to strengthen mortgage and housing markets.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Geographic Variation in Loan Mortgage Performance As my listeners know, conditions in mortgage markets remain quite difficult, and mortgage delinquencies have climbed steeply.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The sharpest increases have been among subprime mortgages, particularly those with adjustable interest rates:  About one quarter of subprime adjustable-rate mortgages are currently 90 days or more delinquent or in foreclosure.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 Delinquency rates also have increased in the prime and near-prime segments of the mortgage market, although not nearly so much as in the subprime sector.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a consequence of rising delinquencies, foreclosure proceedings were initiated on some 1.5 million U.S. homes during 2007, up 53 percent from 2006, and the rate of foreclosure starts looks likely to be yet higher in 2008.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Not all foreclosure starts result in the borrower's loss of the home; sometimes the borrower is able to make up the missed payments or other arrangements are made with the lender.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But, given the number of borrowers in distress and the weakness of the general housing market, the share of foreclosure initiations that ultimately result in the loss of the home seems likely to be higher in the current episode than customarily has been the case.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Many foreclosures are not preventable.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Investors, for example, are unlikely to want to hold onto a property whose value has depreciated significantly, and some borrowers--perhaps because they were put into an inappropriate loan or because personal circumstances have changed--cannot realistically sustain homeownership.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, if a foreclosure is preventable, and the borrower wants to stay in the home, the economic case for trying to avoid foreclosure is strong.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because foreclosures impose high costs, including legal and administrative costs as well as the costs of leaving the property vacant for a possibly extended period, both the borrower and the lender often are better off avoiding foreclosure.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, it is important to recognize that the costs of foreclosure may extend well beyond those borne directly by the borrower and the lender.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Clusters of foreclosures can destabilize communities, reduce the property values of nearby homes, and lower municipal tax revenues.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: At both the local and national levels, foreclosures add to the stock of homes for sale, increasing downward pressure on home prices in general.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the current environment, more-rapid declines in house prices may have an adverse impact on the broader economy and, through their effects on the valuation of mortgage-related assets, on the stability of the financial system.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, finding ways to avoid preventable foreclosures is a legitimate and important concern of public policy.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To determine the appropriate public- and private-sector responses to the rise in mortgage delinquencies and foreclosures, we need to better understand the sources of this phenomenon.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In good times and bad, a mortgage default can be triggered by a life event, such as the loss of a job, serious illness or injury, or divorce.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, another factor is now playing an increasing role in many markets:  declines in home values, which reduce homeowners' equity and may consequently affect their ability or incentive to make the financial sacrifices necessary to stay in their homes.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the principle that a picture is worth a thousand words, Federal Reserve staff, using detailed, county-by-county information on mortgage performance, have developed a series of "heat maps," which summarize the incidence of serious mortgage delinquencies across the nation as well as some of the key drivers of loan performance.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the examples will make clear, the figures (with the exception of one map depicting house price changes) use warmer colors--orange and red--to show counties for which the factor being considered has a higher value or change.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Lower values or changes (again, with the exception of that one map) are indicated by shades of green.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Yellow indicates areas where the factor under consideration has a moderate value or change.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nationally, as of the fourth quarter of 2007, the rate of serious delinquency, as measured by credit records, stood at 2 percent of all mortgage borrowers, up nearly 50 percent from the end of 2004.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 The fourth quarter of 2004 is a useful benchmark, because general economic conditions were fairly normal and the lax underwriting that emerged later was not yet evident.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Figure 1 shows the national patterns of serious mortgage delinquency in 2004, which, again, I am taking as representative of a relatively normal period, with orange and red indicating the highest rates of delinquency and greens indicating the lowest.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 2004, the areas of the country with the highest rates of serious delinquency included significant portions of the Southeast; parts of the Midwest, most notably Ohio and Indiana; portions of the Rocky Mountain region; and Texas, Oklahoma, and areas in the Mississippi valley.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In contrast, many parts of the country experienced exceptionally good loan performance at that time, including most of the West Coast, New England, and much of southern Florida.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, conditions in some areas changed greatly in a relatively short period of time.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Figure 2 shows the pattern of delinquency rates as of the last quarter of 2007.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Many of the areas that exhibited elevated delinquency rates in 2004 continued to show relatively high rates of delinquency in 2007.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But some areas that had low rates in 2004 experienced high rates three years later.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Figure 3 makes this point more sharply by showing the pattern of increases in delinquency rates between 2004 and 2007, with the largest increases shown in red.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The strong regional pattern is evident in the figure.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although many parts of the country have seen significant increases in mortgage delinquencies and foreclosures, a number of areas--such as California, parts of Nevada, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, portions of the upper Midwest, and New England--have been particularly hard hit.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The regional pattern of the recent rise in mortgage delinquencies and foreclosures requires explanation.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Again, we can use heat maps to examine the underlying relationships across geographic regions between changes in mortgage delinquency rates and factors identified as driving loan performance.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, the change in the unemployment rate in a county can be used as a proxy for disruptions in family incomes and subsequent financial stress.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Figure 4 shows changes in average annual unemployment rates across counties between 2004 and 2007, with counties indicated in red experiencing increases or only slight decreases in joblessness.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 The data suggest that increases in unemployment rates account for at least some of the recent increases in mortgage delinquencies.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Parts of New England, states in the Great Lakes region--including Minnesota, Michigan, and Wisconsin--and a number of other states, such as Nevada, show both increased mortgage delinquencies and notable increases in unemployment rates.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the behavior of unemployment does not seem sufficient to explain the increased delinquency rates in other areas, including California, Florida, and portions of Colorado, where mortgage delinquencies increased during a period in which unemployment generally decreased.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Another important determinant of loan performance, identified by research at the Federal Reserve and elsewhere, is changes in house prices.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 4 Figure 5 shows the regional pattern of changes in house prices between 2006 and 2007, with unchanged prices and price declines indicated in red.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 5 The figure shows that Florida, California, Nevada, Michigan, and parts of Arizona and Colorado experienced decreases in house prices between the fourth quarter of 2006 and the fourth quarter of 2007 (a pattern which has continued and intensified in 2008).
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 6 As I noted, sharp declines in house prices, and thus in homeowners' equity, reduce both the ability and incentive of homeowners, particularly those under financial stress for other reasons, to retain their homes.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Other factors affect foreclosure rates, and once again the heat maps can give us a visual impression.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Figure 6 shows the share of home purchases by non-owner occupiers--investors or purchasers of vacation homes, for example--during 2005 and 2006.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 7 Again, there is some correlation with the increase in delinquencies and foreclosures, as purchases by non-owner occupiers were relatively high in the West, Southwest, and in Florida.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Figure 7 shows the incidence of junior liens (or piggyback loans), often an indicator of little borrower equity at the time of purchase.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The greater use of these mortgages in the West and East Coasts presumably reflects higher house prices in those regions; again, the geographical pattern suggests that the use of piggyback loans may also have contributed to the recent rise in delinquencies and foreclosures.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: What are the implications of these relationships, particularly the linkage of mortgage payment problems and falling house prices?
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Loan servicers are used to dealing with mortgage delinquencies related to life events such as unemployment or illness, with the most common approaches being a temporary repayment plan or the folding of missed payments into the principal balance.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: A widespread decline in home prices, by contrast, is a relatively novel phenomenon, and lenders and servicers will have to develop new and flexible strategies to deal with this issue.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In some cases, when the source of the problem is a decline of the value of the home well below the mortgage's principal balance, the best solution may be a write-down of principal or other permanent modification of the loan by the servicer, perhaps combined with a refinancing by the Federal Housing Administration or another lender.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be effective, such programs must be tightly targeted to borrowers at the highest risk of foreclosure, as measured, for example, by debt-to-income ratio or by the extent to which the mortgage is "underwater."
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Finding the right balance--particularly the need to avoid programs that give borrowers who can make their payments an incentive to default--is difficult.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But realistic public- and private-sector policies must take into account the fact that traditional foreclosure avoidance strategies may not always work well in the current environment.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's Homeownership and Mortgage Initiatives I would like to say a few words about the Federal Reserve's efforts to strengthen homeownership and reduce preventable foreclosures.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's decisions regarding monetary policy and our efforts to increase financial stability affect housing and mortgage markets, of course.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But, as an organization with a national presence in the form of regional Federal Reserve Banks and their Branches, we are also working to address these issues more directly.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We are collaborating with other regulators, community groups, policy organizations, lenders, and public officials to identify ways to prevent unnecessary foreclosures and their negative effects on local economies.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our efforts have taken a variety of forms.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, we have employed economic research and analysis, a particular strength of the Federal Reserve, to increase the sum of knowledge about mortgage and housing issues.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, we are providing community leaders with detailed analyses identifying neighborhoods at high risk of foreclosures, analogous to the heat maps I showed you this evening.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: 9 These analyses have helped community organizations better focus their scarce resources, such as deciding where to target counseling services or other intervention efforts.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: A Federal Reserve System work group has prepared overviews of the current state of knowledge about housing and mortgage markets, and further research is currently under way to fill in the most important analytical gaps.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, we are collaborating with interested parties across the country, taking advantage of our national presence and our existing relationships with local lenders, community groups, government officials, and other stakeholders, to take practical steps to address the causes and consequences of foreclosures.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, I mentioned earlier the destabilizing effects foreclosures have on neighborhoods, resulting from factors such as decreased home values and deterioration of vacant properties from neglect.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To help address this problem, the Federal Reserve is joining in a partnership with the nonprofit NeighborWorks America to develop materials, tools, and training programs to help communities and others acquire and manage vacant properties.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The goal is to support the provision of affordable rental housing and new homeownership opportunities in low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Federal Reserve Banks and Branches have also hosted numerous meetings and workshops to bring together local officials, lenders, community groups, and others to try to find ways to reduce the incidence of foreclosures and mitigate their economic and social effects.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Third, we are engaged with mortgage servicers to understand impediments they may face when modifying loans or offering other alternatives to foreclosure.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Servicers still report difficulty connecting with troubled borrowers, and we have supported efforts to encourage borrowers to contact their lenders or housing counselors.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Working with the Hope Now alliance and independently, we have encouraged the industry to increase their efforts to work with troubled borrowers, to develop guidelines and templates for reasonable standardized approaches to various loss-mitigation techniques, and to adopt uniform reporting standards, such as those sponsored by Hope Now.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Clear disclosures of loan modifications will not only make it easier for regulators, the mortgage industry, and homeowners to assess the effectiveness of foreclosure-prevention efforts, but they will also foster greater transparency, and hence greater confidence, in the securitization market.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Prospectively, we are committed to promoting an environment that supports the homeownership goals of creditworthy borrowers.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To this end, the Federal Reserve Board has proposed new regulations to better protect consumers from a range of unfair or deceptive mortgage lending and advertising practices.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To help ensure that the rules are broadly enforced, we are engaging in a program with other federal and state agencies to conduct consumer compliance reviews of nondepository lenders and mortgage brokers.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These reviews are targeting underwriting standards, risk-management strategies, and compliance with consumer protection laws and regulations.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve also is continuing its long-standing practice of providing educational and information resources to help consumers make informed personal financial decisions, including choosing the right mortgage.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Through their community affairs offices, Federal Reserve Banks are working to establish foreclosure-mitigation resource centers on their websites to be used by small municipalities, housing counselors, and community groups.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: For consumers who have questions about banking procedures and rules or who believe they may have been treated unfairly by their lender, the Federal Reserve Consumer Help Center directs queries to the various regulatory agencies so that a consumer has only one call to make to ask questions or file complaints.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Congress can take an important step by moving quickly to reconcile and enact legislation permitting the Federal Housing Administration (FHA) to increase its scale and improve its management of risks.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Such legislation could help the FHA reach a wider range of borrowers and develop appropriate underwriting and pricing methodologies to deal with any increase in credit risk.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Giving the FHA greater latitude to set underwriting standards and risk-based premiums for mortgage refinancing, as well as more flexibility in product development, would allow it to help still more troubled borrowers.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Separately, the government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs)--Fannie Mae and Freddie Macââcould do more.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recently, the Congress expanded Fannie Mae's and Freddie Mac's role in the mortgage market by temporarily increasing the limits on the sizes of the mortgages they can accept for securitization.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, because the GSEs have resolved some of their accounting and operational problems, their federal regulator, the Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight, has lifted some of the constraints that it had imposed on them.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, now is an especially appropriate time for the GSEs to move quickly to raise significant new capital, which they will need to take advantage of these new securitization and investment opportunities, to provide assistance to the housing markets in times of stress, and to do so in a safe and sound manner.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the GSEs expand their role in housing markets, the Congress should move forward on GSE reform legislation, which includes strengthening the regulatory oversight of these companies.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the Federal Reserve has testified on many occasions, it is very important for the health and stability of our housing finance system that the Congress provide the GSE regulator with broad authority to set capital standards, establish a clear and credible receivership process, and define and monitor a transparent public purpose--one that transcends just shareholder interests--for the accumulation of assets held in their portfolios.
speech_title: Mortgage Delinquencies and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion The realtor's mantra is "location, location, location," and, as I have discussed this evening, local variation in housing and mortgage markets is considerable.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This variation is useful for understanding the sources of the increase in mortgage delinquencies and foreclosures, and it should be taken into account as servicers and policymakers consider how best to avoid preventable foreclosures.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Most Americans are paying their mortgages on time and are not at risk of foreclosure.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But high rates of delinquency and foreclosure can have substantial spillover effects on the housing market, the financial markets, and the broader economy.

speech_venue: At the Columbia Business School's 32nd Annual Dinner, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Therefore, doing what we can to avoid preventable foreclosures is not just in the interest of lenders and borrowers.
