speaker: Kroszner
text: I am delighted to be here today at this impressive conference.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: I thank my hosts, President Rosengren and his staff at the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, for the invitation.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: I also thank President Rosengren for providing such interesting and informative introductory remarks.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Over the next two days, you will be having a number of discussions on specific aspects of operational risk and the advanced measurements approaches (AMA) for calculating risk-based capital requirements under Basel II.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, I can probably best contribute to this conference by offering a broader perspective about risk management and Basel II, using examples from the field of operational risk management.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: I will discuss the implementation of Basel II, including enhancements to the framework being undertaken by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in light of recent market events, as well as a proposal to implement in the United States a less complex version of the Basel II framework, known as the standardized approach.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Background I believe focusing on risk management today is certainly topical, given some of the risk management challenges that financial institutions have faced over the past year.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recent market events have shown that a number of institutions have not maintained satisfactory risk management practices; however, we also can point to many examples of sound risk management practices during the recent disruptions.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Individual institutions are responsible for maintaining sound risk management practices.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: But supervisors, of course, also have a role to play both in promoting effective risk management  and offering incentives for bankers to make improvements to their practices.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: There are a number of methods supervisors use to that end--some informal, some formal--including speeches, one-on-one discussions, supervisory guidance, onsite examinations, formal supervisory actions, and regulations.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: One substantial initiative that seeks to improve risk management practices at banking organizations is Basel II.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Importance of Basel II As you all know, banking activities must be supported by both sound risk management and strong capital levels.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, even where robust internal controls are in place, the potential for losses from fraud can never be fully eliminated, meaning that institutions need to hold sufficient capital to offset unexpected losses.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Determining the right level of capital to hold for fraud and other elements of operational risk is not necessarily easy, as many of you here can attest.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: But the AMA is designed to make that determination more risk sensitive and more accurate.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this manner, Basel II represents a major step forward in banking regulation.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: While the existing Basel I capital regime was a significant advance when introduced in 1988, it has become outdated for large, internationally active banking organizations.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Retaining Basel I for these institutions would have widened the gap between their regulatory capital requirements and their actual risk profiles.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is one reason why the Federal Reserve supports Basel II so strongly.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: With regard to credit risk, the advanced approaches of Basel II improve regulatory capital measures by requiring banks to distinguish among the credit quality of individual borrowers.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Generally speaking, banks holding riskier credit exposures are required to hold more capital.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Similarly, the AMA framework requires a more systematic approach for assessing the operational risk to which a bank is exposed and ties an explicit regulatory risk-based capital requirement to these exposures.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Under Basel I, this charge was indirect and embedded in credit and market risk measures.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In contrast, under the AMA, banks with higher levels of operational risk--such as those more heavily involved than others in activities that have elevated loss potential from fraud, business disruption, or systems failure--generally should have higher capital requirements.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: By establishing a much more refined approach that requires banks to hold capital commensurate with the actual risks of their exposures and activities, Basel II should lead institutions to make better decisions about assuming, retaining, and mitigating risks.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Not only does Basel II establish more risk-sensitive and meaningful regulatory capital requirements, it also encourages ongoing improvements in banks' risk management practices.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The U.S. final rule for Basel II includes extensive system and process requirements and U.S. supervisors have high standards for banks seeking to qualify.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: One reason for such high standards is that the framework will only function as intended if Basel II banks have solid risk management infrastructures and robust quantification methods on which to base capital requirements.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Another reason for such high standards is that the risk management improvements in Basel II offer broader safety and soundness benefits, beyond those associated with capital requirements.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Risk Management and the AMA There are strong linkages between the AMA and supervisory expectations for sound management of operational risk.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The AMA builds upon the longtime best practices of banks to develop techniques for identifying, measuring, and attributing capital for operational risk.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: I commend those of you here today who have made strides in improving operational risk management, and heartily encourage you to maintain your efforts.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Supervisors have been working actively with bankers to improve operational risk management and help bankers move toward qualification under AMA.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: A good example is the research and analysis conducted by my colleagues here at the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston:  their useful papers have covered such topics as estimating operational risk loss distributions, evaluating various measurement techniques, and analyzing the reputational impact of operational risk losses.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Supervisors have also conducted a series of loss-data collection exercises in which many of you have participated.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: More generally, I think supervisory attention on operational risk management has provided support to risk managers striving to improve practices within their organizations.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The AMA has specific qualification requirements that are intended to bring about risk management improvements.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, institutions are required to categorize operational risk losses by event type, which promotes identification of the underlying risk drivers of each category.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The AMA also requires consistent comprehensive operational risk capture, which promotes an enterprise-wide assessment across all business units within an entire organization.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, qualifying for the AMA requires strong senior management and board oversight of the entire process.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In designing AMA requirements, supervisors decided against creating a mandated, standard treatment and instead allowed for considerable flexibility.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Allowing more flexibility lets banks create an AMA reflective of their organization, and it promotes innovation in AMA approaches.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: But that flexibility makes banks more responsible for creating a solid and robust process rather than simply providing inputs to a supervisory-determined formula.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Operational risk management is a relatively new field, and a number of challenges remain, such as collecting sufficient and relevant data and developing appropriate modeling techniques to capture low probability events of high severity.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Naturally, validating the techniques used in the AMA is also very important, as with any quantitative models.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Pillar 2 and Pillar 3 While Pillar 1 minimum capital requirements are very important, people sometimes forget that Basel II has three pillars of equal significance.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Under Pillar 2, banks are required to have an internal capital adequacy assessment process (ICAAP), subject to rigorous supervisory review.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The bank's ICAAP should ensure that the bank is holding enough overall capital to support its entire risk profile, and it should provide a cushion against the potential impact of periods of financial or economic stress.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In its ICAAP, for example, an institution may choose a solvency standard for overall capital adequacy that is higher than the 99.9 percent implied by the AMA--for example, a solvency standard of 99.95 or 99.97 associated with a certain credit rating.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: As most of you know, estimating capital needs in the tail of a loss distribution becomes more and more difficult the farther out one goes, so simply "scaling" the AMA measure will likely not suffice for truly assessing capital adequacy against a higher solvency standard.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: More broadly, one of the supervisory expectations surrounding the ICAAP is that institutions should understand the limitations of models and conduct stress testing and scenario analysis to provide greater information about potential losses and capital needs.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Even good models have their limits--such as incomplete data or assumptions that have not been tested across business cycles--and need to be supported by more qualitative measures and sound judgment.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Put another way, Pillar 2 is not just about using "one number," but requires institutions to develop a robust process to evaluate the full range of potentially adverse outcomes that could affect capital adequacy.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: This process certainly includes considering the potential for operational risk losses becoming correlated with losses in other risk areas.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recent events provide ample evidence that underestimating the potential for concurrent losses in multiple risk areas can put pressure on capital levels.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Pillar 3 plays an important role in providing greater information on banks' risk profiles and their ability to manage them.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition to disclosing their capital requirements for operational risk under the AMA, banks will have to provide a description of their AMA process, including their measurement approaches and relevant internal and external factors considered.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: They will also have to provide information about the use of insurance to mitigate operational risk.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a strong believer in market discipline and the importance of information in market transactions, I believe Pillar 3 will improve bank disclosures about risk profiles and enhance discussions between bankers and market participants about risk-management practices.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Next Steps with Basel II Implementation In the United States, Basel II has been an official regulation for just over a month.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: But the full implementation process will take time.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: While I believe that expeditious application of Basel II will have significant benefits, it is of the utmost importance that the implementation be undertaken thoughtfully and deliberately.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: As you know, following a successful four-quarter parallel run, a banking organization would have to progress through three transitional periods--each lasting at least one year--before being able to fully implement Basel II.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: A banking organization would need approval from its primary federal supervisor to move into each of the three transition periods.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, we recognize the substantial work that bankers have undertaken over the past several years to prepare themselves for Basel II, and we think that preparation will pay off.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, before setting a parallel run target start date, we strongly recommend that banks conduct a sober and frank self-appraisal of their current state as well as their ability to meet requirements of the final rule.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Systems development can take time, for example, and it is important to make sure that these systems function appropriately.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: As stated in the final rule, and as the U.S. agencies articulated several years ago, a key instrument in the qualification process is a bank's implementation plan.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: This written implementation plan, approved by a bank's full board of directors, is a detailed and tangible representation of how the bank complies, or intends to comply, with the rule's qualification requirements.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our hope is to provide a bit more information in the next month or so about our expectations for these plans, so I will only provide high-level comments here.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: One important part of a credible implementation plan is a thorough assessment of how the bank intends to address the gaps it has identified between its existing practices and the qualification requirements set forth in the rule for the advanced approaches that cover all consolidated subsidiaries.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The implementation plan also must include objective, measurable milestones--including delivery dates--and a target date when the bank expects its advanced approaches to be fully operational.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The bank must establish and maintain a sound, comprehensive planning and governance process to oversee implementation efforts, and it must demonstrate to the full satisfaction of its supervisor that it meets the qualification requirements.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Because the implementation plan (including the gap analysis) is the only requirement to enter parallel run, the agencies have high expectations for its overall quality and the reasonableness of the approach taken by the banks in assessing their current state.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The large, internationally active banks subject to the final rule on a mandatory basis--the core banks--have until October 1 st of this year to adopt an implementation plan and have it approved by their board of directors.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: This deadline for submission of plans by core banks is intended to ensure that the board of directors will provide the necessary resources and oversight and prevent delays in implementation efforts.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, banks may always submit their plans earlier.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Once they have adopted an implementation plan, banks have ample time to fully meet the qualification requirements, since the final rule allows a bank up to 36 months before it would have to exit parallel run and enter the first transition period.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: As with all things, however, waiting until the last possible moment leaves little margin for error.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Again, as supervisors, we understand that banks face challenges in implementing Basel II, and we stand ready to assist bankers as they work to meet the high standards we expect.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: For one, we have already engaged in a number of discussions with bankers to address their questions on certain aspects of the final rule.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In that effort, supervisory staffs of all the U.S. agencies are working together to ensure that we give consistent messages to bankers, and we intend to maintain such cooperation among the agencies throughout the implementation process.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have also been preparing our examiners to assess banks' practices during the qualification process.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this manner, we have been working to ensure that qualification is done thoroughly, fairly, and consistently.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Enhancements to the Basel II Framework One of the substantial benefits of the Basel II framework is its overall flexibility and adaptability to new practices, instruments, and circumstances.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is, Basel II provides a robust structure within which to integrate new information and enhanced risk management practices as needed.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: As such, the Basel II framework is well suited to address some of the current challenges seen with the current Basel I framework.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, the new framework's credit risk capital charges for mortgages vary with the underlying riskiness of the exposures unlike Basel I.  Basel II also takes into account off-balance sheet exposures much better than the Basel I framework.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Just as lessons learned from recent events can help bankers improve risk management practices, they can also help supervisors further increase the effectiveness of the Basel II framework.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, members of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision recently announced plans to strengthen the resiliency of the framework based on the lessons we have learned over the past year.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Basel Committee's plans to enhance aspects of Basel II are entirely consistent with what we have done in the past with regulatory capital rules upon receiving new information and represent good supervisory practice.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: These proposals to enhance the resiliency of the Basel II framework are fully consistent with one of its key objectives--improving risk management--and should in no way interfere with institutions' efforts to meet the process and system requirements in the U.S. final rule.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Basel Committee's enhancements, which it outlined in an April 16 press release, 2 are intended to improve Basel II's ability to make the banking system more resilient to financial shocks.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: For one, the Committee will revise the framework to establish higher capital requirements for certain complex structured credit products, such as so-called "resecuritizations" or collateralized debt obligations (CDOs) of asset-backed securities, which have been the source of many losses during the recent market disturbances.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: There are also plans to strengthen the capital treatment of liquidity facilities extended by banks to support off-balance sheet vehicles such as asset-backed commercial paper conduits.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Furthermore, the Committee will strengthen the capital requirements in the trading book, given the large growth in trading-book assets and the wide range of instruments held there, some of them quite complex and less liquid.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The current value-at-risk based treatment for assessing capital for trading book risk is limited in its ability to capture extraordinary events that can affect many complex and less liquid exposures.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Committee is working with the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) on an interim treatment for certain instruments held in the trading book, such as complex securitizations, and will conduct further analysis to determine a suitable longer-term approach.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Committee plans to issue Pillar 2 guidance in a number of areas to help strengthen banks' practices and help them better prepare for financial shocks that could affect capital adequacy.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Areas under consideration include proper asssessment of the risks from off-balance sheet exposures and securitizations, as well as the need to address reputational risk and apply proper stress testing.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: These efforts relating to Pillar 2 are certainly in line with my earlier comments that bankers must understand the limitations of their more formal risk models, and think creatively to ensure that they have captured all risks and addressed them appropriately.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Going forward, the Committee will monitor Basel II minimum requirements and capital buffers to evaluate their appropriateness.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: It will also assess banks' internal capital management processes and associated risk management practices.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: This oversight will be particularly important given some of the breakdowns in risk management at institutions over the past year and the associated pressures on capital ratios.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Committee is also working to promote better disclosures by banking organizations under Pillar 3.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Standardized Approach in the United States As a final point, I would like to mention that U.S. agencies plan, fairly soon, to publish for public comment a set of proposed rules that would provide an optional capital framework--known as the standardized approach--for those banks not subject to the advanced approaches of Basel II.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The proposed standardized approach would help increase risk sensitivity and foster competitive equity.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Since we have not yet formally issued the proposed rules for public comment, I will provide just a brief overview on aspects of the proposal that the agencies have already discussed publicly.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The proposed U.S. standardized approach will be based on the approach of the same name in the international Basel II framework, modified in some areas to suit the U.S. banking system.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The standardized approach would enhance risk sensitivity by increasing the number of risk-weight categories to which a bank would assign credit exposures.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: It also would increase capital requirements for certain off-balance sheet exposures, such as liquidity commitments, and allow for broader recognition of credit risk mitigants, such as collateral and guarantees.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, the approach will include a specific capital requirement for operational risk.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Banks not required to adopt the Basel II advanced approaches are facing a choice about whether to opt-in to them.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some of these banks may be sophisticated institutions that exhibit sound risk management, but they might not wish to undertake the extensive effort to meet the advanced approaches of Basel II.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The agencies recognize that such institutions should be afforded an alternative to more-risk-sensitive capital requirements, one not as complex as the advanced approaches.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, the proposal is being developed as an optional risk-based capital framework for all banking organizations not required to adopt the Basel II advanced approaches.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: We plan to retain our existing Basel I-based regulatory capital framework for those banks that would prefer to remain under that regime.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: I encourage all interested parties to review and comment on this proposal once it has been issued.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: We are keenly aware of the need for capital requirements to make sense from a standpoint that considers safety, soundness, and competitiveness; we recognize that a one-size-fits-all approach is probably not the best for our banking system, in light of our wide range of institutions.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: We remain sensitive to the principle that if we have multiple regulatory capital frameworks they must work together to support the safety and soundness of our entire banking system without artificially creating competitive inequalities.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusion My remarks today have focused on the risk management aspects of Basel II, with particular emphasis on operational risk.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Events of the past year have shown that institutions should never let their guard down when it comes to risk management.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: Even though most of the high-profile losses during the past year have--so far--stemmed from market and credit risks, one should not, therefore, assume that less attention should be paid to operational risk management.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Basel II capital framework is a positive step forward through its combination of more risk-sensitive capital requirements with strong incentives for improved risk management.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this manner, we expect Basel II to make the U.S. banking industry more resilient in the face of future financial turbulence and generally more safe and sound.
speech_title: Risk Management and Basel II
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston AMA Conference, Boston, MA
