text: But if ever a demonstration of the value of doing so were needed, the recent episode certainly provides it.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Perhaps the biggest challenge facing public pension systems is inadequate funding.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Even by current measures of liability, which themselves may not be fully revealing, last year about three-fourths of public pension systems were underfunded, and about one-third were funded at less than 80 percent.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Lengthening life expectancies and tight public budgets are making existing pension promises ever more difficult to keep--and the problem is significantly magnified if promised health benefits are included.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The funding situation puts systems under a great deal of pressure to reach for higher returns by investing in riskier assets.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But as has been so clearly and forcefully demonstrated over the past year, there is no free lunch with risk-taking: The price is volatility, the extent of which should be well disclosed and the implications of which should be well understood.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The generally high weight on equity and real estate investments in the typical public pension fund portfolio has increased in recent years.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Part of that exposure has come from increased investment in private equity, real estate investment trusts, and hedge funds.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, some funds have allocated 25 percent or more of their portfolios to these "alternative" categories.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: With exposures like those, public pension systems should maintain formal risk-management procedures that are independent of the selection and evaluation of managers and that are carefully designed to minimize conflicts of interest that can weaken the risk-management function.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: I mentioned earlier that current measures of pension liabilities might be less than fully revealing.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Why might that be so?
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The chief reason is that public pension benefits are essentially bullet-proof promises to pay.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: We all have read about instances in which benefits were lost when a private-sector pension sponsor declared bankruptcy and terminated the plan.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: In the public sector, that just hasn't happened, even when the plan sponsor has run into serious financial difficulty.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: For all intents and purposes, accrued benefits have turned out to be riskless obligations.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: While economists are famous for disagreeing with each other on virtually every other conceivable issue, when it comes to this one there is no professional disagreement: The only appropriate way to calculate the present value of a very-low-risk liability is to use a very-low-risk discount rate.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: However, most public pension funds calculate the present value of their liabilities using the projected rate of return on the portfolio of assets as the discount rate.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: This practice makes little sense from an economic perspective.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: If they shift their portfolio into even riskier assets, does the value of the liabilities backed by their taxpayers go down?
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Financial economists would say no, but the conventional approach to pension accounting says yes.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Unfortunately, the measure of liabilities that results from this process has a real consequence: It pushes the burden of financing today's pension benefits onto future taxpayers, who will be called upon to fund the true cost of existing pension promises.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Another challenge that everyone involved in public pensions faces is the issue of transparency.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Unlike private pension funds, public pension systems do not account for liabilities in a standardized way.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, public employees, taxpayers, municipal bond investors, credit rating agencies, and other market participants have a hard time comparing funding levels across systems and over time.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: What steps can pension funds take to improve transparency and help clarify their long-run challenges?
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Ideally, they would disclose a standardized measurement of funding status, using consistent and appropriate measures of liability.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: They might also disclose how their asset allocation affects the volatility of the returns on their assets and how their funding ratios and cash flow might be affected by various outcomes in the financial markets.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Such practices almost surely would be welcomed externally.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: But they might also pay dividends internally, because the funds might find that the information about the volatility built into their systems changes their views about the amount of risk they want to shoulder.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Public pension funds hold more than $3 trillion in assets and cover nearly 20 million workers and retirees.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Those funds are clearly vital to the business of state and local governments across the country as well as to the public employees they cover.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The potential improvements I have touched on today--adhering to best practices with regard to risk management and grappling with some of the difficult structural issues that currently face public pension systems--would help strengthen public pension systems and should minimize the risks to public employees, the governments that employ them, and the taxpayers that finance them both now and in the future.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Paul Smith , David Wilcox , and Joyce Zickler, of the Board's staff contributed to the preparation of these remarks.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: The views expressed are my own and do not necessarily represent the views of other members of the Board or the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Kohn
text: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (2008), " The April 2008 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices " (April).
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems Annual Conference, New Orleans, Louisiana

speaker: Warsh
text: Thanks in no small measure to the scores of professionals long found in the four walls of the Federal Reserve System--and ample access to information--the Fed possesses both the commitment and resources to tackle these policy challenges.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: And, by virtue of the Fed's institutional credibility, bequeathed to today's Federal Open Market Committee by its predecessors, the policy response tends to be as highly anticipated as it is consequential.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But in affirming our formidable assets, it is similarly not my intention to suggest that we have devised error-free policies to painlessly and smoothly achieve agreed-upon objectives.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: On Monetary Policyâ¦Today The Fed is not omniscient.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Neither are our tools uniquely and perfectly suited to ensure that the ills of yesterday do not recur.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Nor can we guarantee that our policy response alone will set the economy on a steady and obvious path to unequalled prosperity.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: We run serious risks if we overstate our knowledge or overplay our hand.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Look no further than the financial wizards in the financial sector recently who were convinced that risks were manageable and returns exponential.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Milton Friedman reminded us long ago, and Edmund Phelps more recently, of the "consequences of conceit."
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 2 For all that has been learned about the practice of monetary policy, we must be mindful of the dangers of purporting to know more than we do about the relationship between central bank policies and the real economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Humility, thus, is a particularly important attribute for a central banker, particularly when financial markets and financial intermediaries--through which the effects of monetary policy flow to the real economy--find themselves at a crossroads.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Starting in August, my fellow Fed policymakers and I persistently subjected ourselves to the age-old dialectic in determining the breadth and depth of our policy response: What do we know?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: What do we think we know--that is, what do we suspect?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: And, perhaps most important, in light of various forms of uncertainty: What should we do about it?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The more we asked ourselves these questions during this period of extraordinary tumult, the more we recognized the need to broaden our policy response beyond monetary policy's blunt traditional tool.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Changes in the policy rate affect many sectors, not just those that seem out of balance.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Charlie Munger, the under-heralded partner of the "Oracle of Omaha," Warren Buffett (perhaps comprising the finest investment team of the last half-century), believes that economics remains a rather insular field of practice.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: He seems to delight in accusing the economics profession of suffering from "Man with a Hammer Syndrome."
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: He recounts, "[T]o the man with only a hammer, every problem looks pretty much like a nail."
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 3 I suspect Munger feels similarly about the orthodoxy of monetary policy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Consistent with Munger's admonition, the Fed saw it necessary to expand our toolkit beyond the proverbial hammer of the policy rate in the last nine months.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: And as I discussed in remarks last month, the Fed's nontraditional policy response included the use of innovative liquidity tools to counter the market turmoil and improve the functioning of financial and credit markets.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 4 In my remarks today, I would like to discuss the use of the hammer--the setting of the federal funds rate--particularly in extraordinary times.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Of course, determining the proper level of the federal funds rate is rarely simple, given typical imprecision on key economic variables and relationships.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: It is far more challenging still when the financial architecture is in the early stages of redesign, the economy is adjusting to the aftermath of a credit bubble (witnessed most acutely in the housing markets), and inflation risks are evident.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve has employed the hammer with considerable force in the last nine months, lowering the federal funds rate by 3-1/4 percentage points, with wide-ranging implications for the economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Of substantial import, we have filled the toolkit with other implements to provide liquidity and improve the provisioning of credit during the turmoil.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But now, policymakers may be well served encouraging a new financial architecture to emerge, aided, in part, by the actions we have taken.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Even if the economy were to weaken somewhat further, we should be inclined to resist expected, reflexive calls to trot out the hammer again.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Policy actions should reinforce the notion with stakeholders that further hammering needs to be done, but it needs to be accomplished by the financial institutions themselves in retooling their businesses and rebuilding the credit channel to help ensure a stronger, more durable economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Private financial institutions should raise substantial capital, reconstitute business models, and take other actions to reinvigorate the principal transmission channel of monetary policy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: These private efforts are critical to improving market functioning, and until this process is more advanced, the economy is unlikely, in my view, to return to sustainable trend-rate growth.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: We at the Fed have taken action to help foster this curative process to improve the real economy, but market participants will ultimately determine its speed and success.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: On Monetary Policyâ¦Generally The Fed is charged with promoting price stability and maximum sustainable employment.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Stakeholders advocate various strategies for achieving these objectives.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In recent years, most central banks have elected to adjust the policy rate in response to changing economic conditions to achieve their goals.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: A key question for central bankers under this approach: What level of the policy rate would bring real activity in line with its potential?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In gauging this value, a central banker seeks to be forward-looking because monetary policy influences real activity with considerable lag.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The same consideration applies to assessing the effect of policy actions on inflation.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: For analytical purposes only, let's assume that we are in a world where inflation is running well within acceptable levels and that the central bank and stakeholders have ultimate conviction it will remain as such.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This, of course, smacks of the old joke about economists and can-openers.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 5 I'll revisit this heroic assumption later in my remarks.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But with the assumption in mind, monetary policy can focus on the real side of the economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The Taylor rule provides a convenient rule-of-thumb for setting monetary policy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 6 The rule posits that the appropriate setting of the real federal funds rate incorporates three components.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The first component is the economy's natural rate of interest.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This is the real federal funds rate consistent with output equal to potential, on average, over the medium- to long-run.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: If policymakers set the real federal funds rate at this level, the Fed would be neither artificially boosting nor restricting the real economy over long periods.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Holding the federal funds rate at the natural rate, however, may yield an undesirably slow return of real activity to normal, particularly if shocks have a persistent effect on aggregate demand and supply.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: To expedite the process, the Taylor rule adds a second component to the real federal funds rate, one that purports to be proportional to the size of the current output gap.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: By setting the real federal funds rate below the natural rate when resource utilization is loose--and, correspondingly, above the natural rate when resource utilization is tight--policy purports to help move the real economy back to normal at a speedier pace.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The third component responds to the gap between actual inflation and its desired rate, pushing real rates up when inflation is too high and pushing rates down when inflation is too low.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The Taylor rule provides a reasonable description of actual monetary policy behavior on average over the past 20 years.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The reasonably good macroeconomic performance of this period suggests that central banks should pay some heed to its prescriptions.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: By design, however, the Taylor rule focuses largely on what can be observed in real-time, without accounting for some factors that influence monetary policy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: For example, policymakers may try to peer, however imperfectly, into the future when setting the federal funds rate rather than responding solely to the current state of the economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Some central bankers find this more forward-looking approach to be particularly appealing when financial market prices and other high-frequency indicators suggest that the economy is poised to change direction markedly.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: To implement a forward-looking strategy, a policymaker could seek to forecast the average level of the real federal funds rate consistent with the economy either approximating or expeditiously returning to potential.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Such a neutral rate thus might equilibrate the real economy over the next two or three years.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Then, in our hypothetical example where inflation is stable at desired levels, the neutral rate would be a sufficient guide for monetary policy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 7 The wisdom of emphasizing a forward-looking strategy over the Taylor rule approach may depend in part on policymakers' forecasting acumen.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: To estimate the neutral rate, central bankers must forecast how the forces affecting aggregate demand and supply will reconcile during the forecast period.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, policymakers must project how changes in the federal funds rate--past and anticipated--will interact with asset prices, credit provision, and real-side variables.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Under the best of circumstances, these forecasts are subject to meaningful uncertainty.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Thus, peering into the future and acting on what we think we see will invariably lead to some mistakes, certainly with the benefit of hindsight.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Ignoring the future altogether, however, hardly seems the wisest course.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, the Taylor rule approach does not remove uncertainty.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Consider the natural rate of interest, a key element in the rule.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This rate depends on many things--worldwide saving and investment propensities, the achievable trend growth rate of the economy, the natural rate of unemployment, and the state of financial markets and financial intermediation.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Some of these factors may be measurable; others can only be estimated indirectly.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: And many of these estimates demand a judgment about the path of non-monetary policy factors that will almost assuredly change over time.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, policymakers need to grapple with uncertainty from error in real-time estimates of real gross domestic product and estimates of potential output.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The key for policymakers, of course, is to recognize these uncertainties that, if misunderstood or miscalculated, could lead to policy errors.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Munger, the proud non-economist, recounts another lesson born of his investment career that I find particularly heartening in considering the calculation of the neutral rate: Avoid the error of false precision.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 8 Most monetary policy frameworks, while fiercely debated in the academy, tend to suffer from a common and unavoidable weakness--relying on provisional estimates in a complex and uncertain world.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This weakness argues in favor of being persistently inquisitive in search of a keener understanding of the economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This consideration applies to the making of monetary policy in normal times; in times of turmoil, the case for humility is stronger.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: On Monetary Policyâ¦in Times of Financial Market Turmoil The Fed sets monetary policy to support the real economy through several important channels.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In times of financial market turmoil, policymakers like me are especially focused on disruptions in the so-called credit channel.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: After all, much of the Fed's policy prescriptions are carried out through financial intermediaries--commercial banks, investment banks, others--to affect the real economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: When the economy is operating below-trend, so long as financial markets are functioning well, a lower federal funds rate can encourage lending by financial institutions to bolster the real economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 9 Hence, the Fed typically establishes the federal funds rate in anticipation of a customary market response, returning output to potential within a reasonable period, as well as to achieve its price objectives.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In normal times, then, the neutral rate is equivalent to the real federal funds rate that incorporates typical transmission effects and normal market functioning.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Thus, subject to the qualifications I raised in the prior section, changes in the federal funds rate have a reasonably well-understood impact on the real economy, at least most of the time.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: What about the role of the federal funds rate when the real economy is performing smartly but financial markets are functioning with exceptionally low volatility, and liquidity and credit spreads are extremely narrow?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In these periods, the relationship between the federal funds rate and real activity is more difficult to decipher.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: If abundant credit availability is perpetuated by investor overconfidence, I would submit, policymakers may need to target a higher federal funds rate than otherwise to help the economy attain a sustainable equilibrium.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: That is, a federal funds rate that is satisfactory in times of normal market functioning may turn out be lower than required to ensure that the economy performs at potential through the horizon.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Making that judgment represents an important, but difficult task for policymakers.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: And how about when the real economy is operating below-trend in large part because financial markets are impaired, many financial intermediaries are undercapitalized, and risk and liquidity premiums are large and especially volatile?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: What happens when banks and other financial institutions that stand between the Fed and the real economy restrict the supply of credit beyond that implied by higher premiums or, potentially, economic fundamentals?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Should markedly higher doses of monetary medicine (read: lower rates) be proffered to compensate fully for the reduced efficacy of the transmission channels?
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial turmoil lowers real activity expected to accompany a given level of the federal funds rate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Such a development is equivalent to a fall in the neutral rate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But policymakers should recognize that financial market turmoil is not a garden-variety shock to output.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: It is different than, say, a demand shock caused by a change in exports.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial market turmoil can lower output growth and limit the efficacy of the transmission mechanism concurrently.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The federal funds rate, I maintain, will generally need to be lowered, and by more than in normal circumstances, to achieve an operative monetary policy rate that helps to restore the economy expeditiously to equilibrium.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But policymakers need to think carefully about two issues: the degree of reduction in the federal funds rate and the pace at which the rate returns to normal.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The prudence of these moves in the funds rate may ultimately depend on one's diagnosis of what ails the real economy, the risk to that diagnosis, expected benefits of changes in wealth and the cost of capital to businesses and households, and the effect of a lower federal funds rate on the sum of credit availability to the real economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Of no less importance, it may depend on policymakers' judgment on tradeoffs with other critical policy objectives.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: More on that to come.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The differing nature of these infrequent episodes of financial turmoil makes it difficult to place great confidence in available econometric evidence.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Almost by definition, there are few historical precedents that might usefully guide forecasts of aggregate demand and supply.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: My favorite saw of this period has it about right: If you have seen one financial crisis, you have seen one financial crisis.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: So, by necessity, policymakers must make judgments about how the crisis will unfold.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Economics, and the conduct of monetary policy, after all, is not physics.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 10 At least it isn't yet.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Still, a strong case for a forward-looking approach to monetary policy in these episodes seems compelling.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Waiting for the effects of the turmoil to reveal themselves in spending and production data before policy action, as in an unadjusted Taylor rule approach, could risk prolonged weakness.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: On Monetary Policyâ¦in Times of Inflation Risks Up to this point, I focused almost exclusively on the conduct of monetary policy in a non-inflationary environment.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But we cannot assume inflation concerns away.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Determining appropriate policy necessarily involves more than figuring out the neutral real federal funds rate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This reality is especially obvious at present.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Inflation has been elevated for some time and prices of commodities are surging.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: I find these trends particularly vexing at a time when global demand growth, most likely, has slowed.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Concerns about price stability and concerns about the real economy may conflict with one another in the short run.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: These short-run tensions arise, for example, if shocks to energy prices hit the economy, boosting overall inflation while simultaneously weakening output and employment.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In the medium and long run, the Fed's dual objectives are not in conflict.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Investment, productivity, and real economic growth fare best in an environment of low and stable inflation.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Central banks that ignore this lesson invariably pay a substantial cost, both economic and reputational.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: My ode to humility would not be complete without acknowledging our imperfect understanding of the mooring of inflation expectations.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Survey measures suggest that long-run inflation expectations have remained quite stable since the mid-1990s.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This stability is due, in substantial measure, to our predecessors' success in bringing inflation under control after the 1970s.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: We cannot be certain, however, about the durability of this legacy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: If a central bank enjoys a high degree of credibility with its stakeholders, the anchoring of inflation expectations gives policymakers some scope for supporting real activity in the face of adverse shocks.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But, such a strategy poses risks.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: If the Fed were deemed too accommodative for too long, credibility could be undermined, threatening to create a persistent inflation problem that would have to be corrected, no doubt at great cost.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The public could mistakenly see the stance of policy as a sign that our commitment to long-term price stability has wavered.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: That is not a perception we will countenance.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The inflation news since last summer offers little solace.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Oil prices are near record levels, food prices have risen rapidly, prices for a wide range of commodities are up, and dollar depreciation is among the causes pushing up import prices.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Some indicators of expected long-run inflation have also risen.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Given changes in investor preferences for risk-free assets amid the market turmoil, I take less signal from the seemingly satisfactory signals derived from spreads between Treasury securities and comparable Treasury inflation-protected securities.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: No fair recitation of inflation risks, however, should neglect the seeming steady state of core inflation.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: It is running at about the same pace as a year ago, and wage growth appears unlikely to accelerate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Moreover, if commodity prices level out as markets expect, prospects seem decent for a gradual moderation in inflation over time.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Nonetheless, futures markets assessments of these prices have been wrong for awhile.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: As a result, a benign forecast for inflation carries considerable upside risk.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: On Monetary Policyâ¦in Times of Possible Paradigm Shift We should be reminded that a country's macroeconomy is established by the microeconomic decisions of millions of individuals on the front lines of real business and consumption.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Adaptation, dynamism, and flexibility are watchwords of a successful economy, but they test the capability of public authorities to encourage, measure, and incorporate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Here again, Munger, my preferred investment pro, offers a final lesson applicable to the crafting of monetary policy: Resist the tendency to overweight what can be counted and thereby underweight factors that are more important.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 11 If the flexibility and resiliency of our labor, product, and capital markets change materially--resulting from some new policy consensus on trade policies, tax policies, or regulatory policies--the economy's potential would assuredly be affected.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: These changes are hard to incorporate into monetary policy, but that should not distract us from their importance.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: No surprise, then, that the determination of the proper level of the real federal funds rate continues to be subject to considerable debate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The Fed, of course, is not the only monetary policy maker of consequence in a globally integrated economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Our counterparts, particularly among our major trading partners, bring their own prudential policy prescriptions to bear based on their judgments on the contours of their real economies, financial markets, and inflation risks.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: We should expect nothing else.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Some argue that a new paradigm of global economic growth is at hand and that traditional engines of growth like the United States are stalling, but the effects on the world's other major economies will be of little consequence.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Whether the economies of the rest of the world have successfully decoupled from the United States is a judgment we will have to leave to the economic historians.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: What I do believe, however, is that our financial markets at the center of this turmoil have not decoupled, not even a little bit.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In fact, our financial institutions and financial markets have never been more integrated.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Policy differences, thus, should not be taken lightly.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Conclusion In my judgment, the changes in credit availability during the past six years have less to do with the prevailing stance of policy and more to do with changes in financial markets and financial intermediaries.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Returning the economy to equilibrium requires actions more befitting than changes in the federal funds rate alone.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The lending facilities created and employed by the Fed are likely proving useful in this regard.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Increasing liquidity by having a central bank lower the federal funds rate can reduce the risk of a more severe financial crisis, but is imperfectly suited to compensate for declines in liquidity arising from retrenchment in the financial sector for long periods.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: 12 As policymakers, we strive to distill truths about how the conduct of monetary policy, the transmission mechanism of financial markets, and other determinants--domestic and foreign--affect real economic activity.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In my remarks today, I tried to expound not only on what we know, but also on what we don't.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Successful economies are dynamic and flexible.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Their citizens respond to changes in policy preferences, financial conditions, and global forces.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Central bankers must seek a better understanding of an economy's changing fundamentals, distilling lessons learned and aspiring to reduce monetary policy to a science.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In the interim, the art of monetary policy rightly will predominate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The opinions I am expressing are my own and do not necessarily correspond with those of my colleagues on the Board of Governors or the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Nellie Liang and Dave Reifschneider , of the Federal Reserve Board's staff, provided valuable contributions to these remarks.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

text: Kevin Warsh (2008), " Financial Market Turmoil and the Federal Reserve: The Plot Thickens ," speech delivered at the New York University School of Law Global Economic Policy Forum, New York, April 14.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times

speaker: Warsh
text: A physicist, a chemist, and an economist are shipwrecked on a desert island.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Starving, they find a case of canned vegetables washed up on the beach, but they cannot locate a can opener.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The physicist says: "I've got it.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: We find a rock and propel it at the lid of the can at, oh, 40 meters per second at an angle of 82 degrees."
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The chemist thinks for awhile and responds: "No, let's weaken the can's seams with an acid made from decaying leaves, and then heat the can until the internal pressure is enough to burst it open."
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The economist merely shakes his head at his compatriots and says in a condescending tone: "Gentlemen, gentlemen, I have a much more elegant solution.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Let's assume we have a can-opener..." Return to text 6.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: John Taylor, professor and confidante, originally presented the construct for what later became known as the Taylor rule at a Carnegie-Rochester conference in the early 1990s; see John B. Taylor (1993), " Discretion versus Policy Rules in Practice ," Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy , vol.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The real funds rate prescribed by the Taylor rule also would not depend on inflation, obviously, if inflation were at its desired level.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This does not mean, however, that a Taylor rule policy would replicate the neutral rate.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: While the neutral rate depends in part on current resource utilization, it also depends on all of the other factors influencing the trajectory for the real economy.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Thus, the two approaches can sometimes suggest quite different policies, even if inflation is not an issue.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: That said, both the Taylor rule and the forward-looking strategy will tend to prescribe similar movements in the real funds rate over the course of the business cycle.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: See Munger (2003) in footnote 3.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: This is due in part to an increase in the value of financial institution balance sheets and collateral that can be pledged to back loans.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Kevin Warsh (2007), " The End of History? "
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times

speaker: Warsh

speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: In my view, only when private financial agents resume their role as the primary source of liquidity in markets will proper credit market functioning and support for economic growth be restored.
speech_title: The Federal Funds Rate in Extraordinary Times
speech_venue: At the Exchequer Club Luncheon, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
