speaker: Kohn
text: An economic model of inflation is an indispensable input to monetary policy deliberations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: A model in the Phillips curve tradition remains at the core of how most academic researchers and policymakers--including this one--think about fluctuations in inflation; indeed, alternative frameworks seem to lack solid economic foundations and empirical support.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: But the modern Phillips curve differs substantially from versions in use several decades ago; policymakers and academics alike are now attuned to the importance of expectations, the possibility of structural change, and the uncertainty that surrounds our understanding of the dynamics of wage and price adjustment.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the link between inflation and resource utilization often emphasized in a Phillips curve framework accounts for only a modest part of inflation fluctuations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: My comments today will focus on how the lessons from recent research on the Phillips curve are helping me think about the influence of fluctuations in the prices of commodities, such as oil, on the outlook for inflation and the appropriate policy responses to such developments.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Policy Objectives and a Framework for Analyzing Inflation Fluctuations The Federal Reserve has been charged with the pursuit of price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Price stability is uniquely in the control of the central bank over long periods, and it is a prerequisite for the economy performing efficiently over time.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The welfare costs of inflation result from many factors:  the potential costs to households and firms that result from efforts to insure themselves against inflation or from confusion regarding real and nominal prices; distortions to the financial system related to inflation; imperfect indexation of the taxation, especially of capital income, and the related distortions to economic activity; and the costs associated with a slow adjustment of nominal prices and wages.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The costs of inflation imply that central banks should aim for low measured inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, many of the costs of inflation--such as those associated with misconceptions regarding inflation, efforts to insure against inflation, and distortions to the financial system--are associated with the rate of change in the entire set of prices of goods and services facing households or firms, suggesting that measured inflation should be gauged by the rate of change in a broad set of prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Accordingly, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has been emphasizing that it gauges price stability over the long-term by the behavior of the overall personal consumption expenditures price index.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The economic framework that helps me think about fluctuations in inflation is based on the substantial body of research on models of price dynamics that has been developed over the past five decades.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: At its heart, the framework is based on the importance of sluggish adjustment in (some) nominal wages and prices to changing economic conditions.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: This sluggishness undoubtedly reflects a number of factors, which include the costs of adjusting some nominal prices and wages, imperfect information regarding shifts in economic conditions, and learning by firms and households about the structure of the economy, including the setting of monetary policy.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Regardless of its source, the presence of sluggish nominal adjustment brings to the fore three key elements driving wage and price dynamics: inflation expectations, supply shocks, and resource utilization.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Because some prices and wages are adjusted only infrequently, both firms and households anticipate the future erosion of real prices and wages by incorporating the expectations they have for inflation into their current price settings and wage demands.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, inflation expectations play a critical role in the formation of monetary policy.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the tendency of some prices to adjust very quickly to changing circumstances in conjunction with sluggish adjustment in other prices and wages implies that large, sharp price movements, such as a change in the price of oil, lead to relative price distortions throughout the economy; these distortions imply that relative price shocks have important implications for the functioning of the economy.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 2 Finally, fluctuations in resource utilization, through their effects on the costs of production and on firms' desired markups over these costs, are a significant determinant of price and wage decisions.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The link from resource utilization to inflation provides a major channel through which monetary policy settings influence inflation: Adjustments in the policy interest rate bring about changes in resource utilization, which then influence current and expected inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Inflation Forecasting and Commodity Price Shocks The economic outlook is the prime focus of monetary policy.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Because the stance of policy influences economic activity and inflation only with a lag, policymakers must adjust policy to minimize the costs from fluctuations in activity and inflation in the future.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The Phillips curve framework is an important input into the forecast for inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: I will focus specifically on how a shock to the price of oil affects the inflation outlook within this framework.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: This topic is especially salient of late--commodities prices in general, and perhaps most glaringly the price of oil, have risen sharply over the past year; indeed, oil prices have risen sharply for more than four years.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Consider a sharp rise in the price of oil that primarily reflects a shift in the balance between demand and supply in the global market for oil.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 3 In the first instance, higher oil prices lead to an increase in the overall level of consumer prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: When thinking about the outlook for future inflation, it is useful to distinguish between oil and other prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The most significant factor determining oil prices is the current and prospective balance between demand and supply.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The aggregate behavior of most other prices, consisting of a large set of nominal prices and wages that adjust slowly, is driven by the factors that enter the Phillips curve--inflation expectations, resource utilization, and supply shocks (in this case, a shock to the price of oil).
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: In a forecasting context, the Phillips curve framework motivates reduced-form regressions of the rate of inflation for consumer prices excluding food and energy against proxies for each key factor.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Lagged values of inflation typically proxy for inflation expectations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The deviation of output from potential or of the unemployment rate from its sustainable rate serves as a proxy for resource utilization.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: And changes in relative prices for energy, food and imports are traditionally included as measures of supply shocks.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 4 This type of regression is among the most useful tools for forecasting inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, its forecast record is far from spotless, and hence I consider the forecasts from such regressions as just one input that helps inform my outlook for inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The results of such exercises imply that, over recent history, a sharp jump in oil prices appears to have had only modest effects on the future rate of inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: This result likely reflects two factors.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: First, commodities like oil represent only a small share of the overall costs of production, implying that the magnitude of the direct pass-through from changes in such prices to other prices should be modest, all else equal.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, inflation expectations have been well anchored in recent years, contributing to a muted response of inflation to oil price shocks.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: But the anchoring of expectations cannot be taken as given; indeed, the type of empirical exercises I have outlined reveal a larger effect of the price of oil on inflation prior to the last two decades, a period in which inflation expectations were not as well anchored as they are today.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Of course, oil prices have jumped repeatedly in recent years.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The (relatively) continuous rise in energy prices since 2003 has been a surprise to me and to most others, as least as best as I can gauge by looking at prices that have been embedded in futures contracts over this period.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: These contracts currently suggest that the price of oil will flatten out in the period ahead.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Nonetheless, repeated increases in energy prices and their effect on overall inflation have contributed to a rise in the year-ahead inflation expectations of households, especially this year.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Of greater concern is that some measures of longer-term inflation expectations appear to have edged up since last year.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Any tendency for these longer-term inflation expectations to drift higher or even to fail to reverse over time would have troublesome implications for the outlook for inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The Structural Phillips Curve, Commodity Price Shocks, and Monetary Policy The central role of inflation expectations implies that policymakers must look beyond this type of reduced-form exercise for guidance.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: After all, the lags of inflation in reduced-form regressions are a very imperfect proxy for inflation expectations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: As emphasized in Robert Lucas's critique of reduced-form Phillips curves more than 30 years ago, s tructural models are needed to have confidence in the effect of any shock on the outlook for inflation and economic activity.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The importance of structural relationships as inputs to the monetary policy process poses a challenge; for instance, there are many "structural" models of nominal price and wage adjustment, each of these models emphasizes different frictions or imperfections and therefore can have different policy implications, and empirical work has reached different conclusions regarding the merits of alternative models.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 7 As a result, policymakers must look to lessons that are common across alternative specifications and base policy on our current understanding of the most likely important structural factors.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Fortunately, I think that many of the models of nominal price and wage adjustment imply similar conclusions regarding the influence of commodity prices on the inflation outlook and the appropriate response of monetary policy.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: I will again focus on a sharp jump in the price of oil, reflecting supply and demand in the market for oil.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Because many nominal prices and wages are costly and slow to adjust, the efficient allocation of resources is impeded during a transition period in which relative price signals are distorted.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, the prices of energy-intensive goods need to rise relative to those of less-energy-intensive goods, but this adjustment follows a gradual and asynchronous pattern.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Similarly, the equilibrium real wage--the relative price of labor--will tend to be depressed by an oil price shock due to the accompanying adverse movements in the terms of trade and reduction in labor productivity, but the needed wage or price adjustments proceed gradually.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 8 An efficient monetary policy should attempt to facilitate the needed economic adjustments so as to minimize distortions to economic efficiency on the path to achieving, over time, its dual objectives of price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: In particular, an appropriate monetary policy following a jump in the price of oil will allow, on a temporary basis, both some increase in unemployment and some increase in price inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: By pursuing actions that balance the deleterious effects of oil prices on both employment and inflation over the near term, policymakers are, in essence, attempting to find their preferred point on the activity/inflation variance-tradeoff curve introduced by John Taylor 30 years ago.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 10 Such policy actions promote the efficient adjustment of relative prices:  Since real wages need to fall and both prices and wages adjust slowly, the efficient adjustment of relative prices will tend to include a bit of additional price inflation and a bit of additional unemployment for a time, leading to increases in real wages that are temporarily below the trend established by productivity gains.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: I should emphasize that the course of policy I have just described has taken inflation expectations as given.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: In practice, it is very important to ensure that policy actions anchor inflation expectations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: This anchoring is critical:  As demonstrated by historical experiences around the world and in the United States during the 1970s and 1980s, efforts to bring inflation and inflation expectations back to desirable levels after they have risen appreciably involve costly and undesirable changes in resource utilization.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 11 As a result, the degree to which any deviations of inflation from long-run objectives are tolerated to allow the efficient relative price adjustments that I have described needs to be tempered so as to ensure that longer-term inflation expectations are not affected to a significant extent.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Global Demand, Trending Commodity Prices, and Monetary Policy My remarks so far have concentrated on the factors guiding the monetary policy response to a shock in the prices of commodities like oil that stems from a shifting balance of supply and demand in the specific market for these commodities.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Some might think that this focus misses the point in the current context, for at least two reasons.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: First, it has been suggested that the run-up in the prices of a broad range of commodity prices reflects, in part, global excess demand rather than sector-specific forces.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: And second, some have suggested that important commodity prices, like that of oil, may be on a more significant upward trend than is currently embedded in futures prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: It seems highly likely that, over the period since 2003, the rise in commodity prices has reflected strong global economic growth as well as some sector-specific factors, such as geopolitical tensions and other disruptions to the supply of oil.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 12 In this regard, I share the views expressed by Chairman Bernanke at this conference two days ago in which he discussed a range of factors that have likely influenced relative commodity prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the fact that rising relative commodity prices have likely reflected many factors does not, by itself, change the analytical framework that I used to frame policy deliberations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: As I highlighted at the beginning of my remarks, the most important drivers of inflation in the model of inflation dynamics I use are relative price shocks, inflation expectations, and the balance between aggregate demand and supply in the United States, as measured by some notion of resource utilization.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: If a shift in global demand affects both commodity prices and the demand for U.S. goods, the model I have in mind accounts for these influences on inflation through relative price shocks and resource utilization.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: For example, the rise in the price of oil this year has lowered consumption demand by pinching households' real incomes and likely damped the growth in labor productivity by trimming energy input; both of these factors have probably contributed to a lower equilibrium real wage, as I described earlier.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: If the impact on demand from these factors was accompanied by stronger global demand that boosted demand for U.S. goods generally, the forecasts of inflation would need to take this into account.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: In any event, resource utilization has been slackening, judging from the rise in the unemployment rate and the slow pace of economic growth in the United States, on average, over the past six to nine months.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Some have suggested that the price of oil is on a more significant upward trend than currently appreciated.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: 14 Such an unanticipated shift in trend would not be embedded in the anticipated rate of change in slowly adjusting nominal prices and wages, implying that an adjustment period with distortions to relative prices would follow.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, there would likely be upward pressure on overall inflation during this period, reflecting the slow response of the rate of change in some nominal prices to the new trend in the price of oil.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: This tendency for higher overall inflation could risk a rise in inflation expectations.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: An appropriate monetary policy response would share many of the characteristics I discussed earlier.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: In particular, bringing overall inflation immediately back to the low rate consistent with price stability could be associated with a much higher rate of unemployment for a short time.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: It may be efficient to allow some adjustment period in which both overall inflation exceeds its desired low level and the unemployment rate is higher than its long-run sustainable level; as before, setting policy in a manner that balances the undesirable effects of a shock to the system on both inflation and employment will tend to be more efficient than setting policy so as to deliver more extreme outcomes in either inflation or unemployment.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: However, two additional considerations are likely important when considering a shift in trend.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: First, developments in inflation expectations following a significant shift in the relative price trend of a commodity like oil should be monitored carefully, as our understanding of changes in long-run inflation expectations is limited and shifts in trends are infrequent, potentially implying a greater chance of confusion between relative price trends and overall inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, it is very important to remember that the costs of inflation in excess of the low rate of measured inflation consistent with price stability over any extended period are significant and reflect a broad range of factors.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: As I emphasized earlier, economic research into the many costs of inflation has suggested that these costs are associated with the rate of change in a broad set of prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, a trend in any individual relative price should not, in itself, lead to a change in the desirable rate of measured inflation over the long run.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Summary To reiterate, the Phillips curve framework is one important input to my outlook for inflation and provides a framework in which I can analyze the nature of efficient policy choices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: In the case of a shock to the relative price of oil or other commodities, this framework suggests that policymakers should ensure that their actions balance the deleterious economic effects of such a shock in the short run on both unemployment and inflation.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Of course, the framework helps to define the short-run goals for policy, but it doesn't tell you what path for interest rates will accomplish these objectives.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: That's what we wrestle with at the FOMC and is perhaps a subject for a future Federal Reserve Bank of Boston conference.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

text: The views expressed are my own and not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Board of Governors or the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Relative price shocks act like supply shocks in the Phillips curve framework for two reasons.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: First, some prices are sluggish and others are flexible, and the Phillips curve framework focuses on the adjustment of sluggish prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Second, prices are more likely to adjust to very large shocks, and the skewness on the distribution of relative price disturbances can fluctuate substantially, giving rise to shocks to the Phillips curve.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: Ball and Mankiw (1995) discuss these issues and argue that the second type of relative price shock is quantitatively very important.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: The rise in a broad range of commodity prices, as has occurred from time to time recently, would not affect the basic analysis which rests on the contrasting behavior of flexible and sluggishly adjusting prices.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's 53rd Annual Economic Conference, Chatham, Massachusetts

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the simultaneous rise in many commodity prices might suggest that strong global aggregate demand is playing an important role, which would affect the appropriate setting for monetary policy.
speech_title: Lessons for Central Bankers from a Phillips Curve Framework

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am delighted to be here today to help open this important conference.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: I thank my hosts, President Pianalto and her staff at the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, for the invitation.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: This year's conference explores a confluence of consumer-related finance issues in the context of the current difficulties in the mortgage markets.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In my remarks today, I would like to discuss the key role of consumer credit in our economy and describe how information disclosure and protecting consumers can work to facilitate and promote the efficient functioning of markets for such credit.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Good information is essential to achieving well-functioning markets.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consumers, equipped with the right information at the right time, can make the choices most appropriate to their individual circumstances and desires.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: For consumers to make the most meaningful use of the relevant information, such information should be accessible and understandable.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In turn, businesses rely on consumers through their choices to signal their desires and preferences in order to produce the products that consumers want.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: If consumers are not well informed, it is difficult for them to be effective in conveying to businesses what they most want and in rewarding those businesses that do produce such products.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Good information in a marketplace thus not only empowers consumers to make better choices but also helps competition work more effectively to provide the products consumers most desire.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: There are challenges in ensuring that the appropriate information is provided to help markets function efficiently.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Product suppliers may not always provide needed information or present it in a format that enables meaningful comparison across competing products.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consumers must also have the financial skills to evaluate the information effectively.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, even in the presence of good information, practices can emerge that offer little benefit to consumers and, in some cases, may cause harm.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In such cases, improved disclosure alone may be insufficient to address these issues.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Rules can establish standards that promote increased certainty and restrain abusive practices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the same time, such rules need to be implemented in a careful and informed manner so that the potential benefits of such rules are not offset by unintended consequences or the imposition of unnecessary costs.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The challenge to policymakers is to strike the right balance--that is, to find ways to empower and protect consumers without diminishing access to credit and hindering future innovation.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: With these principles in mind, I will briefly describe some of the key steps that the Federal Reserve is undertaking to strike this balance in the area of consumer regulation to protect consumers and provide them with the information they need, and when they need it, to make sound decisions.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Credit and the Economy Credit is the lifeblood of the American economy.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Whether it is to finance an education, purchase an automobile or home, or simply bridge short-term differences in the timing between our income and expenses, virtually all of us rely on credit at various points in our lives.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accordingly, choosing the right type of credit with the most appropriate terms and conditions is important to each of us.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve has an important role to play in this regard, as it has been given a mandate by the Congress to help ensure that the costs and terms of credit use are both transparent and understandable and to protect consumers from unfair and deceptive lending acts and practices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In our role as a supervisor of banking institutions, the Federal Reserve also seeks to ensure that lending is undertaken in a safe and sound manner.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Credit is not only important to each of us as individuals; it also plays a central role in the working of our economy.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Today's economy relies on consumer spending as an engine of growth--it accounts for about 70 percent of the gross domestic product.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Credit is an important underpinning to such spending.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Overall, evidence from the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances shows that about three-quarters of all households carry some debt.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 About three-quarters of automobile purchases are currently either financed or leased, and about 95 percent of home purchases involve a mortgage.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The use of revolving credit is similarly widespread; about 75 percent of consumers hold credit cards.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The annual transaction volume on general-purpose credit card accounts reached nearly $1.8 trillion in 2006, and our latest information suggests that consumers owed nearly $1 trillion on revolving credit accounts of all types.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Because consumer credit plays a central role in the economy, the Federal Reserve has a macroeconomic interest in facilitating the efficient functioning of consumer credit markets.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Role of Credit The prudent use of credit by households provides a number of important economic benefits.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, for many families, credit allows for easier and timelier purchase of assets and goods, such as homes, educations, and automobiles and other consumer durables that can generate savings in cost and time and improve employment and income-generating opportunities.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 3 By facilitating such investment-oriented spending, credit enables consumers to save and consume at times that meet their needs.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, the purchase of an automobile, which many are only able to do using credit, can expand employment opportunities, which, in turn, can lead to higher incomes.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Access to consumer credit also enables many entrepreneurs to finance the start-up or expansion of small businesses, a large source of employment in the United States.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, a robust consumer credit market facilitates the growth of consumer durables industries (e.g., computers, autos, and appliances) in which new technologies, mass production, and economies of scale have historically created employment growth and new wealth.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is simply hard to imagine the pace of development in the automobile and appliance industries in the twentieth century without the availability of credit to purchase their output.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, the lack of well-developed credit markets has been found to be an impediment to economic growth and prosperity.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 4 Even in a well-developed economy such as ours, innovation in credit markets over the past two decades or so has expanded credit availability to lower-income households and increased options for middle-income consumers as well.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, from an economy-wide perspective, credit provides an important outlet for the savings of consumers through the financial intermediation process.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ultimately, the source of funds for consumers who borrow is other consumers who have savings they hold in deposit accounts, life insurance and pension reserves, or portfolios of securities that include bonds, stocks, and mutual fund shares.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Efficient markets for household credit are part of a well-functioning system of financial intermediation that allocates savings to the most productive uses.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The developments in credit markets have generally benefited consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, some of these developments have increased the complexity of our choices and made mistakes potentially more costly.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 6 A key challenge is to find ways to improve consumers' ability to identify products that are suitable to their needs without diminishing the benefits market innovations can provide and without reducing future access to credit.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: One important way this challenge can be met is by improving the information available to consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Central Role of Information Information is critical to the efficient functioning of markets.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 7 A central tenant of economics is that markets are more competitive, and therefore more efficient, when accurate and complete information is available to both consumers and product suppliers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accurate and complete information about credit terms and prices is essential for households to make sound judgments about the use of credit.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Information disclosure improves consumers' ability to compare products and to choose those products that will help them meet their personal goals.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: To be effective, disclosures must give consumers information about credit pricing and important terms at a time when it is relevant, and in language consumers can easily understand.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The information must also be presented in a format that allows consumers to pick out and use the information that is most important to them.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Effective disclosures give consumers information they notice, understand, and can use.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Better credit-term disclosures permit better-informed credit decisions and lead to more-intense competition among creditors.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In a nutshell, effective disclosure empowers consumers to choose wisely and enhances competition.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In some circumstances, the disclosure rules can facilitate efficient market outcomes by establishing guidelines to improve information flows and establishing uniform standards for how information is provided.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, since enactment of the Truth in Lending Act of 1968, which requires uniform disclosure of the cost of credit and other key lending terms, consumer awareness of and sensitivity to interest rates in credit decisions has increased.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 8 Evidence also suggests that these disclosures have improved competition and helped consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 9 The prohibition of the provision of misleading or erroneous information can also help to improve competitive outcomes.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: To evaluate the effectiveness of disclosures, we must know what consumers understand, what information they use, and how they use the information in making decisions.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In designing rules, we need to take consumers' actual behavior and understanding into consideration.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result, the Federal Reserve has been using consumer testing to address the considerable challenge of making disclosures effective.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: As mentioned, consumers increasingly face more-diverse and more-complex financial products, including nontraditional mortgages and credit cards with multiple and complex features.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Given this complexity, we are mindful of the challenges of information overload and seek to design disclosures that are not only accurate, but also clear and concise, so that they are meaningful and useful to consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Numerous pages of fine print may provide the comprehensive descriptions that lawyers may prefer, but they can also be confusing, or provide limited value, to consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We increasingly rely on feedback from surveys and testing from actual consumers to determine the information they need to make informed choices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this regard, we recently completed several rounds of consumer testing for credit card disclosures.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: That testing has been essential to our effort to redesign and improve them.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have also begun using consumer testing of mortgage disclosures to help develop more-effective disclosures around product features and other terms that consumers need to know.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Limitations of Disclosure Protections When consumers are fully aware of and understand product terms and features, they are better positioned to make the right choices and achieve the outcomes most appropriate to their given circumstances, as well as give the signals and rewards to businesses that produce the products and services consumers most value.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, some product features and contract terms may be so complex that they are not readily understood.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In some instances, even small misunderstandings, misjudgments, or the challenge of focusing on the most essential features of a product can lead to serious problems down the road.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: This is one reason why financial education and literacy efforts are essential to enabling consumers to navigate our complex consumer financial marketplace.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Problems can arise if competition does not ensure that relevant information on some terms or product features is provided in a timely and comprehensible way.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: 10 Moreover, product terms or features can sometimes emerge that offer little or no benefit to the vast majority of consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Double-cycle billing, for example, is a practice in the credit card industry that is so complex that few consumers can fully understand the implications of this practice, even in the presence of full disclosure.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Generally speaking, institutions using this practice assess interest not only on the balance for the current billing cycle, but also on the balance for the preceding billing cycle.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Board has conducted extensive consumer testing of various ways to describe this balance computation method and found that disclosures are not successful in helping consumers understand it.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In such cases, improving information disclosure alone may not adequately address the issue.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consequently, the goal of consumer protection may be most effectively realized, weighing the potential costs and benefits, if certain product features are modified by rule or prohibited outright rather than disclosed.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Current Challenges and the Federal Reserve's Regulatory Proposals In today's vast and complex consumer finance marketplace, we face the challenge of ensuring that disclosures for consumer credit remain effective in light of the growing complexity of consumer credit products and terms.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We also face the challenge of identifying when restrictions and prohibitions are appropriate to ensure meaningful consumer protection and do not involve unintended consequences that could ultimately reduce consumer welfare.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: With the increased complexity of mortgage loans and credit cards in recent years, for example, there has been great concern about the need for more-effective disclosure and increased consumer protection in these transactions.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve has undertaken extensive efforts to gain insight into industry practices and consumer experiences to understand how to improve disclosures when possible and to enhance consumer protections where needed.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: With respect to mortgage lending, we have been working to finalize the rules under the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act that we proposed in December.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In developing this proposal, we gained valuable insight through public hearings, discussions with industry and consumer groups, input from our Consumer Advisory Council, and other sources.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The amendments we have proposed would better protect consumers from a range of unfair or deceptive mortgage lending and advertising practices that have been the source of considerable concern and criticism.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our proposal includes key protections for higher-priced mortgage loans secured by a consumer's principal dwelling.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Specifically, the proposal addresses concerns about underwriting and lenders' consideration of the borrower's ability to make the scheduled payments, including verifying the income and assets that lenders rely upon in making the loan.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The proposal also addresses concerns about prepayment penalties and the impact on consumers when lenders fail to establish escrow accounts for taxes and insurance.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We are working toward issuing final regulations in July.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: For credit cards, the Federal Reserve has employed a two-step strategy toward improving consumer protection.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our first step was the Board's proposal to substantially revise and improve credit card disclosures under the Truth in Lending Act.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have done extensive consumer testing to determine the type of information and its format that consumers find most useful in shopping for and choosing a credit card.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We issued this proposal last year, and we are still carefully considering the public comment letters received on that proposal, many of which contain suggestions for how we might further improve the disclosures.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We believe that this proposal will result in credit card disclosures that are significantly more effective for today's complex products.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Testing disclosure forms and formats with credit card users is crucial to ensuring that the disclosures are understandable and useful to consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Effective disclosures can help to empower consumers and enhance the competition because consumers find it easier to comparison shop.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We are continuing to use consumer testing as we work toward issuing final rules by year-end.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: This extensive consumer testing--and the thousands of public comments generated by our 2007 credit card proposal--suggested that disclosures might not provide sufficient consumer protection with regard to certain practices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, in May we took the next step in our ongoing effort to enhance protections for consumers who use credit cards by proposing rules under the Federal Trade Commission Act to prevent financial harm to consumers from specific practices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: We proposed rules that go beyond disclosure and could require financial institutions to make changes to their business models and to alter some practices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Board has worked jointly with the Office of Thrift Supervision and the National Credit Union Administration in drafting and issuing a proposal intended to prevent financial harm to consumers from specific practices that the agencies find to be potentially abusive.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Among other things, the proposed rules would address the following:
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The rules also prohibit a practice associated with the issuance of some subprime credit cards, in which most of the credit limit is used for security deposits and high fees imposed at account opening before the consumer actually receives the card.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition to rules for credit cards, our proposal also addresses potentially abusive practices in connection with banks' payment of overdrafts to ensure that consumers have a choice of obtaining overdraft protection and receive information related to its service and costs.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusion A robust, innovative, and competitive consumer finance market is crucial to a healthy economy and, as I described earlier, can provide significant benefits to consumers.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such a market works most effectively and brings the greatest benefits when consumers are well-informed and are not subject to abusive practices.
speech_title: Protecting Consumers in the Credit Marketplace
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Community Development Policy Summit, Cleveland, Ohio

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve is working diligently to best use its authorities to provide both creditors and consumers with rules that strike the right balance between ensuring that consumers receive useful information at an appropriate time and restricting certain practices, while at the same time minimizing the risk of unintended consequences and the imposition of unnecessary costs that could reduce the benefits of a vital consumer finance marketplace.
