speaker: Bernanke
text: It is my pleasure to be here today to help dedicate this state-of-the-art facility.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: President Hoenig, I commend you and your staff, as well as the designers and builders, of this impressive structure.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: It will serve Kansas City and the entire 10th District well.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Permit me to start with a bit of history that I hope will underscore the crucial role played by the regional Reserve Banks.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: When the Federal Reserve was created in 1913, it was the nation's third attempt at a central bank.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: The First Bank of the United States, chartered in 1791, and the Second Bank of the United States, chartered in 1816, did not last.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: They both failed to gain the trust of a public fearful of concentrated power.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address this concern, the creators of the Federal Reserve crafted a plan for a central bank with a unique structure: what some have called a decentralized central bank.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: An independent federal agency in Washington, D.C., the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System oversees 12 regional Banks, which serve as the operating arms of the System and blend public and private elements.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importantly, the presidents of the Reserve Banks participate, along with the Washington-based Board members, in the monetary policy deliberations of the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: The presidents bring a wealth of knowledge acquired from their regional contacts.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, in making policy, we are able to view the economy not just from a Washington perspective, or a Wall Street perspective, but also from a Main Street perspective.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: This system has served the central bank and the nation well for nearly a century.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Last night I attended a dinner with the Bank's current directors as well as many former members of the Bank's board.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nationally, 278 private citizens--including business people, bankers, nonprofit executives, and community, agricultural and labor leaders--serve on the boards of our 12 Banks and their Branches.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: These individuals provide us with extensive and current information about economic conditions from a unique local perspective.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Often, they provide an early warning of shifting economic conditions before they show up in official government statistics.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: I commend them for their service to both the central bank and our nation.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Here in Kansas City, and in all of our Districts, the Bank and Branch directors have played an important role since the Federal Reserve's inception.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you might expect, at last night's dinner, we talked to some degree about the Bank's history, our current challenges, and the future.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: In preparing for this event, I read a little bit about the dedication ceremony for the previous Kansas City Fed headquarters at 925 Grand Boulevard.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: One of my predecessors as Chairman, William P.G.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Harding, spoke at its dedication on November 16, 1921, and I am happy to follow in his footsteps.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Considering the Federal Reserve's history, this location is a most appropriate site for a Federal Reserve Bank, with its new neighbor being the National World War I Museum at Liberty Memorial.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Those who have an appreciation of U.S. history know that the Federal Reserve played an important role in support of the funding of the First World War and that the war forced the early Federal Reserve to contend with an uncertain global environment with wide-ranging monetary and economic ramifications.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has faced many such challenges since its founding, and the System has evolved in response.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Ours must be a dynamic institution if it is to successfully fulfill its mission in a changing financial and economic landscape.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: When the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City opened in 1914, it operated out of leased office space before moving to the building it is now vacating.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the more than nine decades since, the world has changed dramatically, especially in the areas of banking and finance; however, the Federal Reserve's purpose, mission, and goals remain unchanged.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: And while the Bank's former home on Grand Boulevard served it well, today we celebrate the opening of a building that will well serve this country, and this region.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Looking at the Federal Reserve more broadly, while we must continue to change, we also must recognize that one of the Federal Reserve's key strengths continues to be the strong regional connections fostered by the Reserve Banks.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: To quote from the Federal Reserve Board's first annual report, published on January 15, 1915: "It should never be lost to sight that the Reserve Banks are invested with much of the quality of a public trust.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: They were created because of the existence of certain common needs and interests, and they should be administered for the common welfare--for the good of all."
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: In that spirit, let us use this ceremony to recognize the Federal Reserve's unique structure with roots that are broad and deep in the region.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: To echo comments Tom Hoenig made at the groundbreaking on this site three years ago, let us dedicate this Bank to the service of our nation, this great city of Kansas City, and the other important cities, towns, and rural regions in the heart of America that define the 10th Federal Reserve District.
speech_title: Dedication of the New Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Building
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Kansas City, Missouri

speaker: Bernanke
text: Improving the performance of our health-care system is without a doubt one of the most important challenges that our nation faces.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In recent decades, improvements in medical knowledge and standards of care have allowed people to live healthier, longer, and more productive lives.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: New medical technologies and treatments promise more and better to come.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: From a social point of view, we hope as many people as possible benefit from these advances.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But health care is not only a scientific and social issue; it is an economic issue as well.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The decisions we make about health-care reform will affect many aspects of our economy, including the pace of economic growth, wages and living standards, and government budgets, to name a few.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: By any measure, the health-care sector represents a major segment of our economy.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Spending on health-care services currently exceeds 15 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP).
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, health-care spending is the single largest component of personal consumption--larger than spending on either housing or food.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importantly, health care also has long been, and continues to be, one of the fastest-growing sectors in the economy: Over the past four decades, this sector has grown, on average, at a rate of about 2-1/2 percentage points faster than the GDP.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Should this rate of growth continue, health spending would exceed 22 percent of GDP by 2020 and reach almost 30 percent of GDP by 2030.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Health-related spending is also a large and growing share of government budgets.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Last year, health care accounted for about one-quarter of total federal spending.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) projects that, under current policies, health spending will account for almost one-half of all federal non-interest outlays by 2050.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the public interest in these issues testifies, the stakes associated with health-care reform, both economic and social, are very high.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But we must keep in mind that, for all its problems, the U.S. health-care system also has many strengths.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We must take care that we do not lose what is good about our system as we try to address the significant concerns that certainly exist.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the remainder of my remarks, I will discuss three key challenges for health-care reform.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These challenges are, in short, the issues of access, quality, and cost.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Challenges for Health-Care Reform Access Access to health care is the first major challenge that health-care reform must address.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 2006, a total of 47 million Americans, or almost 16 percent of the population, lacked health insurance.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although the federal and state governments spent more than $35 billion to finance uncompensated care in 2004, the evidence nonetheless indicates that uninsured persons receive less health care than those who are insured and that their health suffers as a consequence.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Per capita expenditures on health care for uninsured individuals are, on average, roughly half those for fully insured individuals.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 People who are uninsured are less likely to receive preventive and screening services, less likely to receive appropriate care to manage chronic illnesses, and more likely to die prematurely from cancer--largely because they tend to be diagnosed when the disease is more advanced.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 4 One recent study found that uninsured victims of automobile accidents receive 20 percent less treatment in hospitals and are 37 percent more likely to die of their injuries than those who are insured.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Quality The second key challenge is improving the quality of health care.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The quality of medical research, training, and technology in the United States is generally very high.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the quality of health care is determined not only by, say, technological advances in preventing and treating disease but also by our ability to deliver the benefits of those advances to patients.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For maximum impact, advances in medical knowledge must be widely disseminated and consistently and efficiently implemented.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But evidence suggests a disturbing gap between the quality of health services that can be provided in principle and the quality of health services that actually are provided in practice.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, in 2000, the Institute of Medicine issued a landmark report that concluded that up to 98,000 Americans died each year in hospitals as a result of medical errors.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 6 Many of the errors identified by the report--for example, errors caused by adverse drug events, improper transfusions, wrong-site surgery, and mistaken patient identity--could have been prevented if hospitals had adopted appropriate safety systems.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although hospitals have implemented a number of new safety practices since the time of that report, the scope for improving patient safety remains large.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Inconsistent use of best practices by doctors and hospitals is also surprisingly widespread.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, numerous studies have pointed to the lack of adherence to evidence-based guidelines for the treatment of heart attacks.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, it has long been well established that restoring blood flow to the heart and using aspirin, beta blockers, and ACE inhibitors at the appropriate times significantly reduce deaths resulting from heart attacks.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 8 Yet studies show that the dissemination of these treatments occurred only slowly.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 9 More widespread application of evidence-based medicine could help health-care workers make better use of the medical knowledge they already have to improve patients' outcomes.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although some patients do not receive the care they need, others receive more (and more expensive) care than necessary.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Research on geographic variation in health-care practices and costs confirms this point.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, Medicare expenditures per eligible recipient vary widely across regions, yet areas with the highest expenditures do not appear to have better health outcomes than those with the lowest expenditures; indeed, the reverse seems to be true.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Cost This observation brings me to a third important challenge for health-care reform: controlling costs.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The problem here is not only the current level of health-care spending (U.S. spending exceeds that of most other industrial countries) but, to an even greater degree, the continued rapid growth of that spending.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Per capita health-care spending in the United States has increased at a faster rate than per capita income for a number of decades.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Should that trend continue, as many economists predict it will, the share of income devoted to paying for health care will rise relentlessly.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A piece of wisdom attributed to the economist Herbert Stein holds that if something cannot go on forever, it will stop.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At some point, health-care spending as a share of GDP will stop rising, but it is difficult to guess when that will be, and there is little sign of it yet.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although the high cost of health care is a frequently heard complaint, it is important to note that a substantial portion of the cost increases that we have seen in recent decades reflects improvements in both the quality and quantity of care delivered rather than higher costs of delivering a given level of care.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, new technologies, despite greatly adding to cost in many cases, have also yielded significant benefits in the form of better health.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: People put great value on their health, and it is not surprising that, as our society becomes wealthier, we would choose to spend more on health-care services.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, although quantifying the economic value of improved health and greater expected longevity is difficult, most researchers who have undertaken an exercise of this type find that, on average, the health benefits of new technologies and other advances have significantly exceeded the economic costs.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: That said, the evidence also suggests that the cost of health care in the United States is greater than necessary to allow us to achieve the levels of health and longevity we now enjoy.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I have already mentioned research that finds large regional differences in the cost of treating a given condition, with high-cost areas showing no better results.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The slow diffusion of the use of aspirin and beta blockers for treating heart-attack patients shows that cheap, effective treatments are not always used, potentially leading to higher costs and worse outcomes.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, because insurance companies and the government play such prominent roles in financing health care, patients and doctors have far less incentive to consider the extra costs of optional tests or treatments.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But, as we all know, although testing and treatment decisions may be undertaken on the presumption that "someone else will pay," the public eventually pays for all these costs, either through higher insurance premiums or higher taxes.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The effects of high health-care costs on government budgets deserve special note.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the United States, a large and growing portion of both federal and state expenditures is for subsidized health insurance.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 1975, federal spending on Medicare and Medicaid was about 6 percent of total non-interest federal spending.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Today, that share is about 23 percent.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because of rising costs of health care and the aging of the population, the CBO projects that, without reform, Medicare and Medicaid will be about 35 percent of non-interest federal spending in 2025.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 12 This trend implies increasingly difficult tradeoffs for legislators and taxpayers, as higher government spending on health-care spending will, of necessity, require reductions in other government programs, higher taxes, or larger budget deficits.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Rapid increases in health spending also portend increasingly difficult access to health services for people with lower incomes.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 13 As health spending continues to outpace income, health insurance and out-of-pocket payments will become increasingly unaffordable.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 14 One way that society has addressed this problem in the past has been to expand government subsidies for health spending.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Medicare Part D program, which assists seniors with the costs of prescription drugs, is an example.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, to continue limiting the effects of rising medical costs on household budgets, the government may have to absorb an increasing proportion of the nation's total bill for health care, putting even greater pressure on government budgets than official projections suggest.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Taking on these challenges will be daunting.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because our health-care system is so complex, the challenges so diverse, and our knowledge so incomplete, we should not expect a single set of reforms to address all concerns.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Rather, an eclectic approach will probably be needed.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, we may need to first address the problems that seem more easily managed rather than waiting for a solution that will address all problems at once.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thinking About Solutions In health-care reform, it is certainly easier to pose questions than to provide answers.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, even putting aside the scope and technical complexities of the problems we face, the types of reforms we choose will depend importantly on value judgments and the tradeoffs made among social objectives.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Such choices are appropriately left to the public and their elected representatives.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consequently, I will have little to say here regarding specific proposals.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, I will suggest a few questions and considerations that those seeking reform might wish to keep in mind.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Regarding access, one important consideration is that people who are uninsured are not all alike.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: They include people who have low incomes, people who may not be poor but have costly pre-existing health conditions, those whose employers do not offer group health insurance and who cannot afford to buy insurance in the more-expensive nongroup market, and people who are eligible for Medicaid or other programs but for some reason have not enrolled.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some people who can afford health insurance do not purchase it, presumably because they do not anticipate having significant medical expenses.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Broadening access to health care may thus require us to consider a mix of policies.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The following are some of the questions with which we will have to wrestle.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, should enrollment in a health insurance program be mandated, or at least strongly encouraged, for example, through tax incentives?
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Supporters argue that mandates lead to better risk pooling and prevent those who could afford insurance but choose not to buy it from "free-riding" on the public safety net.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Opponents argue that mandates infringe on what should be an individual choice and may require a substantial government budgetary commitment to help those who cannot afford insurance on their own to meet the mandate.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, should we continue to rely on employer-provided health insurance as the key element of our system?
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The employees of large companies in particular typically constitute a good risk-sharing pool, allowing insurance to be provided at a lower overall cost.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the dominance of the insurance market by employer-provided plans means that the market for individual and small-group policies is underdeveloped and that the cost of such coverage is very high.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Employer-based systems also reduce the portability of health insurance between jobs, which reduces labor mobility and the efficiency of the labor market as well as creating a burden for those changing jobs.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Third, to help people with costly pre-existing conditions, should we impose requirements on insurance companies to accept all applicants and mandate the conditions that must be covered?
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Doing so would help some people obtain coverage, but the resulting increases in insurance premiums might exclude others.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: An alternative approach would be to promote bare-bones, high-deductible policies that are affordable and attractive to healthy people while offering government help to those who need coverage for costly conditions.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Finally, to what extent are we willing to use public funds to reduce the number of those who are uninsured, for example, by providing subsidies to low-income people not covered by Medicaid or to people, such as the self-employed, who find it difficult to obtain affordable coverage in the non-group market?
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: How would we finance additional spending?
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For instance, would we consider limiting the employers' tax exemption for the cost of employee health insurance?
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The issue of access to health care, though difficult politically, is in some sense the technically least complex of the three challenges I have identified; it is mostly about financing, and possibly regulation, rather than about medicine.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Of course, access to health care is closely entwined with the other issues, notably the issue of cost.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, restraining the growth of health-care costs would increase the number of people who can afford insurance coverage.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the second challenge, improving the quality of health care, a number of private and public initiatives have been undertaken in recent years.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These include programs to monitor hospitals' performance in ensuring patient safety and adherence to best practices; greater efforts to identify and disseminate best practices, as determined from clinical trials; and public and private initiatives to increase the use of information technology in health care.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Researchers are also examining how the structure of health-care delivery systems affects the quality of care.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, some evidence suggests that vertically integrated systems like that of the Veterans Administration are quicker to adopt health information technology and have been more successful in applying it.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some instances of initiatives that aim to encourage quality through financial incentives or disincentives--so-called pay-for-performance--have begun to emerge.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Examples include accreditation practices that require hospitals to comply with established standards and best practices, and the recent decision that Medicare will not cover costs caused by certain medical errors.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Efforts to improve the quality of health care are a vital component of comprehensive reform and are likely to yield high social returns.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Additional research and experimentation can help us address difficult questions such as how best to measure quality and cost-effectiveness in health-care delivery and how to give doctors and hospitals incentives to adopt best practices and improved information technologies.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The solutions we choose for access and quality will interact in important ways with the third critical issue--the issue of cost.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Greater access to health care will improve health outcomes, but it almost certainly will raise financial costs.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Increasing the quality of health care, although highly desirable, could also result in higher total health-care spending.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, increased patient screening may avoid more serious problems and thus be cost-saving, but it could also identify problems that might otherwise have gone untreated--a good outcome, certainly, but one that increases overall spending.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These are certainly not arguments against increasing access or improving quality.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: My point is only that improving access and quality may increase rather than reduce total costs.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: From the economist's perspective, the question of whether we are spending too much on health care cannot ultimately be answered by looking at total expenditures relative to GDP or the federal budget.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Rather, the question, whatever we spend, is whether we are getting our money's worth.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In general, good information and appropriate incentives are necessary to allocate resources efficiently.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In health care, the necessary information should include not only the clinical effectiveness of certain tests or courses of treatment but also their cost-effectiveness.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the regional comparison of health-care costs illustrates, cost-effective approaches may be at least as useful as more costly approaches in delivering good health outcomes.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Knowledge of the costs of alternative approaches is likely to be insufficient by itself.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Patients, doctors, and hospitals must also be given incentives for choosing cost-effective approaches.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the questions of how to structure incentives and monitor performance are hotly debated.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, advocates of "consumer-driven" health care argue that, given appropriate information and incentives, patients--or in some cases, private insurers acting on their behalf--can effectively impose at least some degree of market discipline on health-care providers.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Others see an inevitable role for government in setting standards of care and in measuring performance.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Professional associations, hospitals, medical researchers, and other stakeholders may also have a role to play.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the heart of the debate are the fundamental social questions of how we determine when various medical services are worth their cost and how we measure and reward good performance by providers.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Rising health spending increases stress on both private and public budgets, and thus stakeholders in both spheres are aiming to reduce costs.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Cost-saving reforms in the private sector will inevitably reverberate in the public sector and vice versa.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, the shift toward managed care in the private sector also resulted in more managed care in the public sector.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Similarly, innovations in public insurance programs, such as the introduction of reimbursement by diagnosis-related groups in Medicare, changed the way private insurance payments were structured.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 15 Our health-care system is, de facto, a private-public partnership; as a result, governments should not view health-care costs narrowly as a budgetary issue.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Rather, they should consider how the totality of government intervention in the health-care market--including tax policies, insurance regulation, and the structure of Medicare and Medicaid--affect the sector as a whole.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The best way to reduce the fiscal burdens of health care is to deliver cost-effective health care throughout the entire system.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion Let me conclude by restating a point I made at the beginning: As we focus on the problems of our health system, it is easy to forget that much is good about it.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our health system has produced innovations in basic science, in the understanding and diagnosing of disease, and in pharmacology and medical technology.
speech_title: Challenges for Health-Care Reform
speech_venue: At the Senate Finance Committee Health Reform Summit, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These advances have resulted in more-effective treatments and significant reductions in mortality across a wide spectrum of diseases.
