speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the years, the Federal Reserve has significantly increased the transparency of monetary policy making.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, starting in 1979, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has included economic projections of the FOMC participants in each semiannual Monetary Report to Congress .
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Since 1994, the FOMC has publicly announced changes in its target for its policy instrument, the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Most recently, the FOMC extended the horizon for its projections in October 2007 and is now publishing these projections four times a year.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Has the Federal Reserve gone far enough?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Or would further advances in transparency be useful?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I will argue here that the science of monetary policy suggests that the Federal Reserve can indeed go further in enhancing its communication strategy, and that doing so would produce important benefits in economic performance and democratic accountability.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I will also outline a specific proposal of my own and address a few concerns that some might have with elements of this proposal.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Before proceeding, I would like to emphasize that my remarks today reflect only my own views and not necessarily those of anyone else on the Board of Governors or the FOMC.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, this disclaimer has even more meaning now since, as many of you know, I will be leaving the Federal Reserve Board at the end of August and returning to Columbia University.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: What Are the Key Scientific Principles for Monetary Policy Communication?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: To think about what kind of central bank communication is desirable, let's begin by considering some key scientific principles regarding the objectives of monetary policy and the benefits of central bank transparency.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Objectives of Monetary Policy The modern science of monetary policy is based on the idea that the central bank's objective is to maximize the economic well-being of the households in the economy (Mishkin 2007d).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Broadly speaking, this objective can be expressed in terms of two components:  minimizing the deviations of inflation from its optimal rate and minimizing the deviations of real economic activity from its so-called natural rate, which is the efficient level determined by the productive potential of the economy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, this analytical formulation of the objectives of monetary policy captures the essential mission of the Federal Reserve System, as summarized by the Federal Reserve's dual mandate to promote price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 3 By the way, I believe that the Federal Reserve's role as the lender of last resort is also crucial for fostering the stability of the financial system, but I will not elaborate further on that today.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Policymakers, academic economists, and the general public broadly agree that maintaining a low and stable inflation rate significantly benefits the economy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, low and predictable inflation simplifies the savings and retirement planning of households, facilitates firms' production and investment decisions, and minimizes distortions that arise because the tax system is not completely indexed to inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, I interpret the available economic theory and empirical evidence as indicating that a long-run average inflation rate of about 2 percent, or perhaps a bit lower, is low enough to facilitate the everyday decisions of households and businesses while also alleviating the risk of debt deflation and other pitfalls of excessively low inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The rationale for promoting maximum sustainable employment is also fairly obvious:  Recessions weaken household income and business production, and unemployment hurts workers and their families.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I have outlined elsewhere, these two objectives are typically complementary and mutually reinforcing:  that is, done properly, stabilizing inflation contributes to stabilizing economic activity around its sustainable level, and vice versa.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nevertheless, it's important to note a fundamental difference between the objectives of price stability and maximum sustainable employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: On the one hand, the long-run average rate of inflation is solely determined by the actions of the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 7 On the other hand, the level of maximum sustainable employment is not something that can be chosen by the Federal Reserve, because no central bank can control the level of real economic activity or employment over the longer run.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 8 In fact, any attempt to use stimulative monetary policy to maintain employment above its long-run sustainable level would inevitably lead to an upward spiral of inflation with severe adverse consequences for household income and employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Recent research has also emphasized the challenges of making contemporaneous "real-time" assessments of the level of maximum sustainable employment, because this level cannot be directly observed and can be inferred only with considerable uncertainty.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, in making these assessments, monetary policy makers need to draw on a wide range of indicators from labor, product, and financial markets.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Benefits of Central Bank Communication A central element in successful monetary policy is the establishment of a nominal anchor.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Why is this so important?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The expectations for inflation of households and firms are a key factor in determining the actual behavior of inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 10 In the absence of a firm nominal anchor, these expectations may wander as the private sector revises its assessment of the rate at which inflation is likely to settle, and those movements in expectations for future inflation can generate pressure on the current inflation rate.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: By establishing a transparent and credible commitment to a specific numerical inflation objective, monetary policy can provide a firm anchor for long-run inflation expectations, thereby directly contributing to the objective of low and stable inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 11 Additionally, the presence of a firm nominal anchor gives the central bank greater flexibility to respond decisively to adverse demand shocks.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Such a commitment helps ensure that an aggressive policy easing is not misinterpreted as signaling a shift in the central bank's inflation objective and thereby minimizes the possibility that inflation expectations could move upward and lead to a rise in actual inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: A strong nominal anchor can be especially valuable in periods of financial market stress, as we have been experiencing recently, when prompt and decisive policy action may be required to minimize the risk of a severe contraction in economic activity that could exacerbate uncertainty and financial market stress.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 12 Thus, the establishment of an explicit numerical inflation objective can play an important role in promoting financial stability as well as the stability of employment and inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: More broadly, it should be noted that central bank transparency contributes importantly to democratic accountability and economic prosperity.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 13 In particular, in a democratic society, the central bank has a responsibility to provide the public and its elected representatives with a full and compelling rationale for monetary policy decisions.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Clarification of the central bank's objectives and policy strategies also reduces economic and financial uncertainty and thereby facilitates efficient decisionmaking by households, businesses, and financial market participants.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: How Has Federal Reserve Communication Been Enhanced?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Federal Reserve has been a pioneer in a number of aspects of central bank communication, many of which I have mentioned at the beginning of these remarks.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Now I would like to discuss some of the main aspects of the enhancements to the FOMC's communication strategy that were announced in November.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: First, the forecast horizon for the FOMC's economic projections now covers three calendar years instead of only two years.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the projections released after the past meeting extend to 2010.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Second, the Committee now publishes these projections four times a year rather than twice a year.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Third, the projections now include a forecast of overall consumer price inflation, as measured by the price index for personal consumption expenditures (PCE), a broad price index that corresponds closely to the price stability objective in the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: These forecasts of overall inflation complement the ongoing forecasts the Committee provides of the so-called core version of the PCE price index, which excludes the prices of food and energy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 14 Fourth, the release of the projections now includes a narrative describing FOMC participants' views of the principal forces shaping the outlook and the sources of risks to that outlook.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I indicated last November, I believe that these enhancements provide important information that will contribute to the public's understanding of our objectives and the rationale for our policy actions and hence will facilitate the decisionmaking of households and businesses.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As reported last week in conjunction with the minutes of the latest FOMC meeting, the projections for overall PCE inflation at a three-year horizon (which is currently 2010) fell in a range of 1.6 percent to 2.1 percent, and the central tendency of these projections was 1.8 percent to 2 percent.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 16 Each FOMC participant's projection is made under the assumption of "appropriate" monetary policy--that is, the path of policy calibrated to achieve outcomes for economic activity and inflation that are, in the eyes of each participant, most consistent with the objectives of price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For that reason, the longer-run inflation projections provide information about each FOMC participant's assessment of the long-run inflation rate that best promotes those dual objectives--what I have referred to as the "mandate-consistent inflation rate."
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 17 The increased information that these projections convey regarding FOMC participants' views of the mandate-consistent inflation rate, combined with the FOMC's continuing commitment to keeping inflation low and stable, should help anchor inflation expectations and actual inflation more firmly.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The longer-run projections of output growth and unemployment are heavily influenced by FOMC participants' assessments of the sustainable rates of output growth and employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result, these projections can provide the public with useful information regarding the FOMC's estimates of the sustainable rate of output growth (often referred to as potential output growth) and of the sustainable unemployment rate (often referred to as the natural rate of unemployment).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Providing projections for the short run as well as for the longer run encourages FOMC participants to think in terms of desirable paths for inflation and output, a discipline that economic research suggests will produce better policy outcomes.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: These projections also are useful in enabling the FOMC to explain its policy decisions and strategies more fully in the context of its medium-term objectives for economic activity and inflation as well as the risks to those objectives.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As a result, the public and the Congress can better assess whether our forecasts of the economy are reasonable and whether we are pursuing a policy that is consistent with achieving the dual mandate of price stability and maximum sustainable employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The result should be increased accountability that is consistent with basic democratic principles.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Is There Room for Further Improvement?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Although the enhancements to the FOMC's communication strategy last November have been a major step forward, I believe that there is some room for further improvement.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conceptual Considerations As a conceptual matter, the three-year horizon of the projections may not be long enough to provide sufficient clarity about the views of FOMC participants regarding the mandate-consistent inflation rate, the sustainable growth rate of output, or the natural rate of unemployment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, these projections do not establish a transparent and credible commitment to a specific numerical inflation objective and hence do not provide a sufficiently firm nominal anchor.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In my view, the length of the forecast horizon is particularly relevant at the current juncture in considering the projections for output growth and unemployment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because of the recent adverse shocks to the economy--including turmoil in financial markets and the sharp increase in the prices of oil--output growth in recent quarters has fallen below potential, and the unemployment rate is, as best as I can judge, above the natural rate.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Similarly, sharp increases in the prices of many commodities have driven inflation above rates consistent with price stability.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even under appropriate monetary policy, Committee forecasts of inflation, output growth, and unemployment might not settle at their respective long-run rates within the three-year horizon, obscuring Committee participants' views about these key parameters.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This problem may currently be somewhat less acute for the current set of inflation projections, because inflation is projected to moderate to about 2 percent or below by the end of the projection period.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Nevertheless, to the extent that some slack in economic activity is projected to persist through 2010, that slack might well induce a modest further decline in inflation, implying that policymakers' projections for inflation in 2010 might be a bit higher than their assessments of the mandate-consistent inflation rate.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Empirical Evidence My discussion of room for improvement relative to the Federal Reserve's current communication strategy has been theoretical.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: There is, fortunately, evidence from a number of countries that have adopted an explicit numerical goal for inflation, including Canada, New Zealand, Sweden, and the United Kingdom.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 18 And there is also evidence from the experience of the European Central Bank (ECB), which has not adopted an explicit numerical goal but has provided a fairly precise verbal description of its commitment to keeping inflation "below, but close to, 2 percent in the medium term."
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Over the past several years, empirical work that has drawn on this international experience has found some significant benefits in anchoring inflation expectations by establishing an explicit inflation objective.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, let's take a look at three figures from a recent paper by Beechey, Johannsen, and Levin.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 20 Figure 1 depicts the long-run inflation expectations from surveys of professional forecasters in the euro area and in the United States.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Inflation expectations in both economies are relatively well anchored.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The lines on the left for the euro area are extremely flat, with only tiny and occasional deviations from the ECB's inflation goal of keeping inflation just below 2 percent over the medium run.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In the United States, inflation expectations as measured by the mean or median forecast in the Survey of Professional Forecasters are also quite fixed at around 2-1/2 percent for consumer price index (CPI) inflation, but those in other surveys move around somewhat more.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, there is substantially greater disagreement in long-run inflation forecasts for the United States than for the euro area.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As shown in figure 2 , the standard deviation of U.S. inflation forecasts at each survey date is higher than the standard deviation of corresponding euro area inflation forecasts.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, the degree of dispersion in the views of individual forecasters has gradually declined towards negligible levels for the euro area but not for the United States.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: One obvious interpretation of these patterns is that professional forecasters in the United States are less certain about the Federal Reserve's longer-term inflation goal.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: That uncertainty may also explain differences in the behavior of inflation compensation as implied by the gap between nominal and real yields on long-term bonds.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Figure 3 depicts far-forward inflation compensation (that is, the one-year-forward rate nine years ahead) for the United States and the euro area.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Inflation compensation, sometimes referred to as "breakeven inflation," reflects not only inflation expectations but also a premium that compensates for uncertainty about inflation outcomes at the specified horizon.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Evidently, far-forward inflation compensation for the euro area displays much smaller fluctuations than for the United States, consistent with greater stability of inflation expectations and a lower degree of uncertainty about longer-run inflation outcomes.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Moreover, regression analysis confirms that U.S. far-ahead forward inflation compensation exhibits statistically significant responses to surprises in macroeconomic data releases--consistent with the view that market participants are continuously revising their views about the longer-run outlook for U.S. inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In contrast, euro-area inflation compensation does not respond significantly to economic news.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: One concern might be that these benefits in anchoring inflation expectations could come at the expense of the performance of output growth.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, the empirical evidence suggests that central banks with explicit inflation goals do not have worse output performances than central banks, such as the Federal Reserve, that have not specified an explicit numerical goal for inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In addition, the international experience suggests that an explicit inflation goal does not imply that these central banks place more emphasis on stabilizing inflation to the detriment of stabilizing output.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Figure 4 plots the standard deviation of headline inflation (measured as the quarter-on-quarter change at an annual rate) against the standard deviation of the unemployment gap as estimated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Note that the United States appears near the top of the graph, as the country with the highest volatility of unemployment gaps.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 23 Moreover, a number of researchers have shown that the response of policy interest rates to economic activity and inflation in the United States and euro area is quite similar, suggesting that the Federal Reserve and the ECB place similar weights on inflation and activity.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: This overview of the evidence should not be viewed as suggesting that the steps that the FOMC has taken to improve its communications over the past couple of decades or the more recent enhancements last fall have provided no benefits.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Rather, this analysis supports the view that some room for further improvement still remains.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: A Proposal In light of these considerations, I would like to suggest several specific modifications to the Federal Reserve's current communication strategy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: It is reasonable to ask a few questions about whether these proposed changes would be feasible or desirable adjustments to the Federal Reserve's communication strategy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Would This Proposal Be Consistent with the Dual Mandate?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some commentators have worried that establishing a specific numerical inflation objective might lead to an overemphasis on controlling inflation and not enough concern about stabilizing real economic activity.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: My proposal is, however, consistent with the dual mandate, because it has the advantage of being less likely to be misinterpreted as a commitment to control inflation within a tight range over short horizons, since it only involves a consensus on the mandate-consistent inflation rate and an agreement not to change it without scientific justification.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: By so doing, this proposal should enhance the ability of monetary policy to stabilize fluctuations in economic activity, and therefore support the dual objectives provided to the Federal Reserve by congressional legislation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: One lesson from the experiences of foreign central banks with explicit inflation objectives is that such a goal is indeed consistent with a dual mandate for stable prices and maximum employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Some of the central banks that have explicit inflation objectives have mandates that specifically include other objectives such as output stabilization and financial stability.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the regulations governing the Norwegian central bank specifically state that monetary policy should contribute to stable developments in output and employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Similarly, the Reserve Bank of Australia aims at encouraging strong and sustainable economic growth while ensuring that consumer inflation is consistent with the explicit numerical objective over the medium run.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Even at central banks where the inflation objective appears to be the primary goal, policymakers do acknowledge that the stability of economic activity is also an important objective.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For instance, Charles Goodhart, a former member of the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), has emphasized that the MPC aims at stabilizing both inflation and real economic activity and that its monetary policy strategy is quite similar to that of other central banks such as the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 26 Moreover, as I noted earlier, the empirical evidence is consistent with this view:  Central banks with explicit inflation objectives do not have worse outcomes for output growth and do not appear to be favoring inflation stabilization at the expense of output stabilization.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Should the Inflation Objective Be Stated as a Specific Numerical Value Rather Than a Range?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Establishing a specific numerical value for the inflation objective is a crucial aspect of my proposal.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As discussed in my recent speech with the whimsical title of "Comfort Zones, Shmumfort Zones," publishing a range of values for the inflation objective has a number of undesirable features.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 27 For example, when the price stability objective is formulated in terms of an acceptable range of inflation outcomes, the policy implications may be difficult to interpret and may make it harder for a committee of policymakers to decide on an appropriate course of monetary policy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Describing inflation objectives in terms of a comfort zone could also lead to perverse expectations dynamics that leads to larger fluctuations in economic activity.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 28 Moreover, the uncertainty associated with long-run inflation under a zone could affect the perceived long-term real interest rates faced by households and firms through differential effects on the expectations of different agents, a pitfall that seems particularly plausible given the dispersion in professional forecasters' long-run expectations for U.S. inflation, as shown in figure 2.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, one important lesson from the international experience is that point objectives have proven more effective than ranges in anchoring inflation expectations.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 30 And even in cases where the inflation objective is formulated in terms of a band, emphasizing the midpoint of that band helps allay concerns that the central bank will only take aggressive policy actions at the edges of the band.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In light of these considerations, many foreign central banks have taken steps to move away from an inflation objective that is expressed as a range and have moved toward an objective that is expressed as a single numerical value, as does my proposal here.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, the Bank of England initially announced an inflation objective in terms of a range from 1 percent to 4 percent for the Retail Price Index excluding mortgage interest payments (RPIX), but this range was perceived as a band of indifference that implied the Bank would be equally satisfied with inflation outcomes anywhere within the range.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Perhaps partly as a result, inflation expectations and realized inflation tended to remain close to the top of the range.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, the objective subsequently was modified to a point target of 2-1/2 percent for RPIX inflation, where inflation above or below that value was viewed as being equally undesirable.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Inflation expectations converged quickly to this new rate in surveys of both households and professional forecasters, and the move was favorably received both by the public and by financial markets.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In another instructive example, the ECB had initially emphasized a broad objective of keeping inflation below 2 percent over the medium term, but in May 2003, the ECB clarified that policy would be aimed at maintaining inflation below, but close to, 2 percent.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: That clarification was welcomed by market participants and likely contributed to the firm anchoring of long-run inflation expectations.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Would This Proposal Be Misinterpreted as Establishing a Goal for Maximum Employment?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: As I have emphasized, a central bank can determine the long-run average inflation rate but cannot choose the maximum sustainable level of employment, which is determined by the underlying structure of the real economy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, one might worry whether providing longer-horizon projections for output growth and employment as well as inflation might be mistakenly interpreted as establishing specific--and ultimately infeasible--goals for real economic activity.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I do not believe this potential pitfall poses a substantial risk.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because monetary policy determines the inflation rate in the long run, agreement on the mandate-consistent inflation rate among FOMC members can only lower uncertainty about future inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In contrast, differences in the long-run projections for output growth and unemployment across FOMC participants are inevitable, as these factors are outside of the Committee's control and inherently uncertain given our understanding of economic fluctuations.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The ongoing dispersion in long-run projections for output growth and unemployment that is a feature of my proposal would help underscore that these projections are assessments of potential output growth and the natural rate of unemployment and should not be viewed as numerical objectives chosen by the FOMC.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Could the Numerical Inflation Objective Be Modified if Appropriate?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: One might be concerned about whether the numerical inflation objective could be subsequently adjusted for sound economic reasons.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, I would again draw on the experience from other central banks and point out that changing the technical specification of the inflation goal has been very well received elsewhere.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: For example, in late 2003, the inflation target of the Bank of England was switched from a 2-1/2 percent target for RPIX inflation to a 2 percent target for the CPI.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 32 Despite some concerns both from the public and the Bank about the change, it appears to have been implemented with few problems.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, figure 5 shows the distribution of professional forecasters' medium- to long-range inflation projections in the United Kingdom in the fourth quarter of 2001, the first quarter of 2004, and the second quarter of this year.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: These expectations were initially clustered relatively tightly around the inflation objective of a 2-1/2 percent rate but moved to the new value of 2 percent within a few months of the announced change and have remained firmly anchored since then, especially compared with the dispersion in views regarding the longer-term outlook for U.S. inflation (Gürkaynak, Levin, and Swanson, 2008).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Similarly, as I mentioned earlier, the ECB also clarified its inflation objective, and this change was implemented smoothly.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Would This Proposal Provide a Sufficient Degree of Commitment to the Nominal Anchor?
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: By stating its intention not to modify the mandate-consistent inflation rate without a clear technical rationale, I believe that the FOMC would provide a firm nominal anchor that would not differ much in practice from some alternative commitment to a specific numerical inflation objective.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In explaining this view, I want to draw on some conversations with my son, who is currently enrolled in law school, and to take advantage of the opportunity to demonstrate my erudition by using a bit of Latin.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: (As you may know, I've already demonstrated my command of Yiddish in another recent speech.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In this instance, the relevant legal term is stare decisis , which means "to stand by things decided."
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: 34 This concept plays a crucial role in the functioning of our legal system:  When the Supreme Court makes a decision in any given case, the reasoning behind that decision serves as a precedent that guides all subsequent legal considerations, except for particular circumstances in which the Supreme Court finds compelling reasons for modifying or overturning a prior decision.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The approach that I have recommended here would operate in a roughly similar way.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Because the consensus on the mandate-consistent inflation rate would be very transparent, the FOMC would not be inclined to modify that consensus value except for sound economic reasons; hence, this proposal would be sufficient to provide a firm anchor for long-run inflation expectations.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Conclusion While the recent enhancements of the Federal Reserve's communication strategy have been beneficial, I believe that the science of monetary policy indicates that the FOMC needs to go even further.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, I have suggested that the FOMC should lengthen the horizons of its projections, reach a consensus on a specific numerical value for the mandate-consistent inflation rate, and indicate that this consensus value would be modified only for good scientific reasons.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: I have argued that moving in this direction would improve economic outcomes by anchoring inflation expectations more firmly while allowing sufficient flexibility to ensure that monetary policy would continue to be fully consistent with our dual mandate of price stability and maximum employment.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, once I return to academia at the end of next month, I will no longer be participating in any official consideration of these issues.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: However, I hope that the views that I have expressed today will be useful in contributing to the continuing evolution of the Federal Reserve's communication strategy.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Further details on the experiences of these countries--as well as other economies that have adopted explicit numerical inflation objectives--may be found in Mishkin and Posen (1997), Bernanke and others (1999), and Mishkin and Schmidt-Hebbel (2001, 2007).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: See ECB (2003, p. 6).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Indeed, the experience of other central banks confirms that establishing a specific numerical value for the inflation objective can be viewed as a technical issue that does not necessarily require any new legislation, but, of course, this depends on the political system in each country.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: In Sweden, for example, the government announced in 1991 that low inflation was an overriding political goal, but the Riksbank's January 1993 announcement of an explicit inflation objective did not coincide with any legislative action (Giavazzi and Mishkin, 2006).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: The Riksbank stated an inflation goal accompanied by a two-year start-up period, so that the goal was to become operational in January 1995.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications

speaker: Mishkin
text: Soon after the initial announcement by the Riksbank, various changes to its legislative mandate were proposed.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Many of these were adopted in 1999, when a new constitution and new Riksbank Act came into effect.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Similarly, the Reserve Bank of Australia announced a numerical inflation objective in 1993, and this objective was formalized about three years later when the government and governor issued a joint "Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy" (see Fraser, 1993; Reserve Bank of Australia and the Treasurer of Australia, 1996; and Reserve Bank of Australia, 2008).
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: And in Chile, the law establishes broad objectives for the Central Bank of Chile, but the Bank itself has elaborated that its mandate for price stability is to be interpreted at aiming for a 3 percent inflation rate at a two-year horizon (see Central Bank of Chile, 2007).

speaker: Mishkin
text: Gürkaynak, Levin, and Swanson (2008) examined far-ahead forward inflation compensation and found significant effects of news for the United States but not for Sweden or the United Kingdom; Gürkaynak, Levin, Marder, and Swanson (2007) obtained consistent results for Canada and Chile, and Beechey, Johannsen, and Levin (2008) found no significant effects of news on far-ahead forward inflation compensation for the euro area.

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Of course, this evidence is only suggestive, because differences in economic structure may account for some of these differences; for example, most of the countries with explicit inflation objectives are small and relatively open economies that might be expected to have higher volatility of both unemployment and inflation.
speech_title: Whither Federal Reserve Communications
speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: It should also be noted that the U.S. economy is closer to the center of the pack instead of an outlier when the volatility of the real economy is measured in terms of output gaps rather than unemployment gaps.

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

text: See Smets and Wouters (2005) and Christiano, Motto, and Rostagno (2007).

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: FOMC participants would work toward reaching this consensus about mandate-consistent inflation using the overall inflation rate, as measured by PCE inflation, to be consistent with the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Overall and core (excluding changes in the prices of food and energy) inflation rates are likely to be at similar rates at a horizon of five or more years.

text: At a given point in time, the yield on a bond with a specific maturity is determined by the views of the "marginal investor" who is indifferent between buying and selling that bond.

speech_venue: At the Peterson Institute for International Economics, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Thus, if financial market participants have heterogenous views about the central bank's inflation objective, the identity of the marginal investor might vary systematically over time in ways that influence the evolution of long-term bond yields.

speaker: Mishkin
text: Another pitfall is that if a central bank places a high degree of emphasis on the boundaries of a range, then these threshold effects imply nonlinearities in the conduct of monetary policy that are likely to produce less desirable economic outcomes; see Orphanides and Wieland (2000).

speaker: Warsh
text: Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework :
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: On behalf of the Federal Reserve, I am pleased to join Secretary Paulson and my fellow bank supervisors today.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial markets continue to show the ill effects of turmoil triggered by mortgage losses.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The real economy is underperforming in terms of growth and job creation, a result in part of financial strains.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: And financial institutions themselves are affected by the generalized pullback in liquidity and deteriorating credit quality.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Nearly one year after the onset of financial market distress, many financial institutions have retreated from certain business lines, limited their participation in markets for some financial products, delevered their balance sheets, and taken other actions aimed at balance sheet repair.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: These developments are both necessary and expected.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: But, the path to a new financial market architecture, however uneven and improvised, will not only be marked by the forces of retrenchment.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The path should equally, in my view, be distinguished by the creative impulses that drive product and market innovation.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: It is perhaps too convenient to denigrate the attributes of dynamism and ingenuity, particularly late in economic cycles, when the forces of innovation can disappoint and weaken the real economy.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Policymakers and market participants alike should recognize that innovation--in our product markets, labor markets, and yes, our financial markets--is likely to prove a necessary net contributor to economic growth in the coming period.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: We should also be reminded that financial innovation need not be equated with product complexity.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: While some take comfort in the presumption that global economies have decoupled, I would note that our global financial markets are more integrated than ever.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial products successfully developed in a single geography often can be readily exported to another; readily, that is, if the new product export befits investor preferences and policymakers remove barriers to their adoption.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Today's introduction of the Treasury Covered Bond Framework may be illustrative of the benefits of product innovation in globally connected financial markets.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Treasury's discussions with market participants suggest that a covered bond framework may attract investor interest and facilitate greater access to mortgage credit.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: High-quality assets might be financed if banks are allowed to manage pools of loans, substituting new loans into the pool as others become delinquent.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Newly issued covered bonds backed by high quality mortgage loans and issued by strong financial institutions may find a growing investor base in the United States.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve has long accepted a broad range of high-quality collateral from depository institutions at its discount window.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Highly rated, high-quality covered bonds would generally fall within that broad range as eligible collateral.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Private lenders also are likely to find such bonds attractive as collateral for credit extensions.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: Financial innovation, properly understood, can increase the diversity of funding sources, improve the distribution of risks, and provide incentives to monitor such risks--all helping to promote economic growth.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Warsh
text: The Federal Reserve seeks to encourage new and innovative sources of funding, and will continue to work with other policymakers and market participants to accomplish this important objective.
speech_title: Remarks on covered bond framework
speech_venue: At the U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Conference on Covered Bond Framework, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In choosing the topic for this year's symposium--maintaining stability in a changing financial system--the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City staff is, once again, right on target.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although we have seen improved functioning in some markets, the financial storm that reached gale force some weeks before our last meeting here in Jackson Hole has not yet subsided, and its effects on the broader economy are becoming apparent in the form of softening economic activity and rising unemployment.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Add to this mix a jump in inflation, in part the product of a global commodity boom, and the result has been one of the most challenging economic and policy environments in memory.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's response to this crisis has consisted of three key elements.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, we eased monetary policy substantially, particularly after indications of economic weakness proliferated around the turn of the year.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: In easing rapidly and proactively, we sought to offset, at least in part, the tightening of credit conditions associated with the crisis and thus to mitigate the effects on the broader economy.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: By cushioning the first-round economic impact of the financial stress, we hoped also to minimize the risks of a so-called adverse feedback loop in which economic weakness exacerbates financial stress, which, in turn, further damages economic prospects.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: In view of the weakening outlook and the downside risks to growth, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has maintained a relatively low target for the federal funds rate despite an increase in inflationary pressures.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: This strategy has been conditioned on our expectation that the prices of oil and other commodities would ultimately stabilize, in part as the result of slowing global growth, and that this outcome, together with well-anchored inflation expectations and increased slack in resource utilization, would foster a return to price stability in the medium run.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this regard, the recent decline in commodity prices, as well as the increased stability of the dollar, has been encouraging.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: If not reversed, these developments, together with a pace of growth that is likely to fall short of potential for a time, should lead inflation to moderate later this year and next year.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nevertheless, the inflation outlook remains highly uncertain, not least because of the difficulty of predicting the future course of commodity prices, and we will continue to monitor inflation and inflation expectations closely.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: The FOMC is committed to achieving medium-term price stability and will act as necessary to attain that objective.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: The second element of our response has been to offer liquidity support to the financial markets through a variety of collateralized lending programs.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: I have discussed these lending facilities and their rationale in some detail on other occasions.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 Briefly, these programs are intended to mitigate what have been, at times, very severe strains in short-term funding markets and, by providing an additional source of financing, to allow banks and other financial institutions to deleverage in a more orderly manner.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have recently extended our special programs for primary dealers beyond the end of the year, based on our assessment that financial conditions remain unusual and exigent.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will continue to review all of our liquidity facilities to determine if they are having their intended effects or require modification.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: The third element of our strategy encompasses a range of activities and initiatives undertaken in our role as financial regulator and supervisor, some of which I will describe in more detail later in my remarks.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Briefly, these activities include cooperating with other regulators to monitor the health of individual financial institutions; working with the private sector to reduce risks in some key markets; developing new regulations, including new rules to govern mortgage and credit card lending; taking an active part in domestic and international efforts to draw out the lessons of the recent experience; and applying those lessons in our supervisory practices.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Closely related to this third group of activities is a critical question that we as a country now face: how to strengthen our financial system, including our system of financial regulation and supervision, to reduce the frequency and severity of bouts of financial instability in the future.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this regard, some particularly thorny issues are raised by the existence of financial institutions that may be perceived as "too big to fail" and the moral hazard issues that may arise when governments intervene in a financial crisis.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, in March the Federal Reserve acted to prevent the default of the investment bank Bear Stearns.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: For reasons that I will discuss shortly, those actions were necessary and justified under the circumstances that prevailed at that time.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, those events also have consequences that must be addressed.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, if no countervailing actions are taken, what would be perceived as an implicit expansion of the safety net could exacerbate the problem of "too big to fail," possibly resulting in excessive risk-taking and yet greater systemic risk in the future.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Mitigating that problem is one of the design challenges that we face as we consider the future evolution of our system.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: As both the nation's central bank and a financial regulator, the Federal Reserve must be well prepared to make constructive contributions to the coming national debate on the future of the financial system and financial regulation.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: Accordingly, we have set up a number of internal working groups, consisting of governors, Reserve Bank presidents, and staff, to study these and related issues.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: That work is ongoing, and I do not want to prejudge the outcomes.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, in the remainder of my remarks today I will raise, in a preliminary way, what I see as some promising approaches for reducing systemic risk.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will begin by discussing steps that are already under way to strengthen the financial infrastructure in a manner that should increase the resilience of our financial system.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City's Annual Economic Symposium, Jackson Hole, Wyoming

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will then turn to a discussion of regulatory and supervisory practice, with particular attention to whether a more comprehensive, systemwide perspective in financial supervision is warranted.
speech_title: Reducing Systemic Risk
