speaker: Bernanke
text: I am very pleased to join you at this conference.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As an economist, but also as a former professor, one-time school board member, spouse of a teacher, and parent of two young adults pursuing higher education, I am always glad to have an opportunity to speak about the importance of education to our nation's economy and our society.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This morning I am especially pleased to highlight the past and continuing importance of the nation's historically black colleges and universities.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Given my audience, I may be "preaching to the choir," so to speak, on this topic, but I trust that you will appreciate the sermon.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Education is vital to our prosperity.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It fundamentally supports advances in productivity, upon which our ability to generate continuing improvement in our standard of living depends.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As our economy becomes more and more technologically advanced and globally interconnected, the skills, knowledge, and analytical ability that education develops are becoming ever more crucial to each individual's success.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A substantial body of research demonstrates that investments in education--higher education, certainly, but also lifelong education, from preschool to mid-career training and adult education--pay high rates of return both to individuals and to our society as a whole.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, the benefits of education are more than economic.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: By providing us with a broader view of the world, education helps each of us become the most complete person we can be.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Research suggests that more-highly-educated individuals are happier on average, make better personal financial decisions, suffer fewer spells of unemployment, and enjoy better health.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Educated individuals also are more likely to participate in civic affairs, volunteer their time to charities, and subscribe to personal values--such as tolerance and an appreciation of cultural differences--that are increasingly crucial for the healthy functioning of our diverse society.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Given our responsibilities at the Federal Reserve as a central bank and financial institution regulator, we see financial education in particular as a vital part of our mission.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In our increasingly complex financial marketplace, choosing a credit card, saving for education and retirement, and buying a home now require more financial savvy than ever before.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To help meet these needs, the Federal Reserve supports a variety of programs and initiatives to increase financial literacy.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the regional level, many of our economic education specialists offer training seminars to help educators teach economic and personal finance topics in their classrooms.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In general, higher education is one of the strong points of the U.S. educational system.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We must work diligently to maintain the quality of our educational system where it is strong and strive to improve it where it is not.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, we must find ways to move more of our students, especially minorities and those from disadvantaged backgrounds, into education after high school.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The historically black colleges and universities have long played a vital role in this regard.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: They have proud record of accomplishment, dating back to 1837 with the founding of what is now Cheyney University of Pennsylvania.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Slavery and segregation cast long dark shadows on our nation's history and our society, and the historically black colleges and universities served as beacons of knowledge in the darkness.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Today, they are no longer the only places a young African American woman or man can obtain an education, but they are very fine choices for many students, and not just African Americans--indeed, 90 four-year and 13 two-year institutions enroll more than 300,000 students, including more than 50,000 who are not African Americans.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In 2006, these institutions conferred more than 30,000 undergraduate degrees and nearly 9,000 advanced degrees.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: They have maintained their relevance by building on their tradition of educational excellence and by harnessing the loyalty and support of alumni.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: There are indeed many distinguished alumni of HBCUs, including media personality and philanthropist Oprah Winfrey, professor and Nobel Prize-winning author Toni Morrison, former U.S.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Surgeon General David Satcher, Brown University President Ruth J. Simmons, and Major General Dennis Via, among many others.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I wish you a very successful conference.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: You have much to celebrate and, doubtless, much to discuss as you strive to find ways to carry the rich heritage of the historically black colleges and universities into the future.
speech_title: Remarks on historically black colleges and universities
speech_venue: At the 2008 National Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week Conference, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I appreciate the opportunity to comment on these three papers.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: 1 They illuminate the sources and effects of the current financial market turmoil, and I learned a considerable amount from reading them and thinking about their implications.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Instead of providing detailed comments on each paper, I'd like to draw out the relationships among them and, in the process, comment a little on the papers and their implications.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: To foreshadow:  I will be highlighting the role of leverage--in the household sector and in financial intermediaries--as a critical factor in understanding the buildup of excesses and their unwinding.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: At the beginning of the chain of causation is the housing cycle in the United States.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Chip Case points out the difference between this housing cycle and others over past decades and asks why the difference developed.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One culprit he identifies is changes in the financial system that affected the way that mortgage credit is made available to borrowers.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: A key element of these changes, and one that accounts for a good part of the subsequent effects of the financial system and the economy, is the rise in leverage in housing finance.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As Case notes, for several years, mortgage indebtedness rose substantially relative to the value of owner-occupied housing.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The willingness of lenders to tolerate--or, in some cases, encourage--huge increases in loan-to-value ratios added to the demand for housing, especially by people who normally might not have had the savings to enter the market, and contributed to the rise in home prices.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One reason for the loosening of standards was the expectation that house prices would continue to rise--and even more certainly that they could not fall in all regions at the same time, supporting diversification through securitization.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Rising prices would enable lenders to recoup their funds even if the borrower was unable to service the loan, mostly because the borrower would be able to obtain extra cash through refinancing.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Expectations of house price appreciation facilitated and interacted with the increasing complexity of mortgage securities, including multiple securitizations of the same loan, which made it virtually impossible for ultimate lenders to monitor the creditworthiness of borrowers--a task they, in effect, had outsourced to credit rating agencies.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The absence of investor caution and due diligence was especially noticeable for the highest-rated tranches of securitized debt.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Elevated leverage in housing markets has meant that as prices have fallen, lenders have had to absorb an unusually high proportion of the losses.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As Case points out, foreclosures by lenders have added to the downward pressure on those prices.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Conceptually, such price declines moving down the demand curve for housing services could accelerate and cushion the adjustment in activity necessitated by previous overbuilding.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I am encouraged that Case finds the pace of declines abating in a number of markets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: However, partly owing to the feedback of price declines on lenders, mortgage conditions have tightened some since the late spring readings he is using for his conclusion, and in my view, the jury is still out on whether housing prices are close to finding a bottom.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The heavy involvement of financial intermediaries in amplifying the housing boom and the subsequent economic effects of the bust brings me to the Morris and Shin paper, which raises a host of important issues related to the systemic aspects of financial intermediation and the lessons from the recent turmoil.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As they emphasize, one of the important lessons has been the greater-than-expected vulnerability of secured financing when intermediaries are engaged in maturity, credit, and liquidity transformation.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Recall that the turmoil first came onto the balance sheets of the banks through the collapse of the asset-backed commercial paper market last fall before it affected the funding of investment banks through the triparty repurchase agreement market.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The new vulnerability results importantly from the extension of secured short-term financing to increasingly illiquid and riskier long-term assets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As uncertainty about the liquidity and creditworthiness of those assets--especially related to mortgage-backed securities--was called into question, lenders became more concerned about the possibility that they might end up owning the underlying assets, and they raised haircuts or simply refused to roll over loans.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Clearly, as Morris and Shin point out, what we have learned about various risks implies the need for intermediaries to build greater liquidity and capital buffers in good times, as well as to improve their abilities to manage their risks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: And those larger buffers would help to offset the moral hazard that may have been created through the expansion of our liquidity facilities.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Getting the micro-prudential piece right--having each institution adequately protected--would go a long way toward making the whole system more robust and resilient.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But Morris and Shin would go further; they would impose additional requirements on institutions to take account of the externalities for the system created when common shocks impair markets and credit availability by provoking widespread actions to preserve shareholder value.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: They would do this through a higher liquidity requirement and through the imposition of a leverage ratio on investment banks, which is already in place for commercial banks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I agree with the authors, and with Chairman Bernanke, that we need to consider the level of buffers that is appropriate to ameliorate systemic risk.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, a host of difficult judgments are inherent in how we establish such a system, and I'll raise just a few on a very general level.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One set concerns the size of the buffers.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: How far into the tail should intermediaries be required to insure themselves?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Shouldn't the Federal Reserve take some of the liquidity tail risk to facilitate intermediation of illiquid credits, as was intended at our founding?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the larger the regulatory tax, the more likely it is that activity will migrate to unregulated sectors in an environment of fluid and free capital movements.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: How can we gain better assurance of systemic stability when we are unlikely to be able to continuously extend the reach of regulation, and will it be sufficient to deepen the moats around the core institutions?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In this regard, the leverage ratio gives incentives to move some activities away from regulated institutions.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: A second question is, How we can structure these requirements and other aspects of regulation to damp, rather than reinforce, the natural procyclical tendencies of the financial system?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Among the challenges will be encouraging firms and supervisors to comfortably allow buffers to be eroded in bad times.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Interestingly, prompt corrective action under the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act of 1991 was intended, in part, to induce an element of countercyclical behavior by banks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: It gives banks an incentive to build excess capital--on both a risk-based and leverage ratio basis--in good times to avoid prompt corrective action when circumstances are less favorable.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Now that we are in the latter state of the world, a study of how commercial banks are viewing capital ratios, including the leverage ratio, could inform consideration of the Morris and Shin proposal.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Morris and Shin paper also provides a framework for thinking about the Federal Reserve's credit facilities.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: On page 9, they note that liquidity makes borrowers feel more robust and lenders less likely to withdraw, raising the odds for a more stable equilibrium for the entire system.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: That is exactly what we have been trying to do with our various discount lending facilities.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The assurance of the availability of liquidity to sound institutions against good collateral should counter the greater uncertainty and risk aversion that have impaired normal arbitrage and intermediary functions by making those institutions more willing to extend credit and take positions in the process of making markets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: It should also assure other creditors of those institutions that illiquid markets will not impede the repayment of their loans, and therefore make them more willing to keep lending.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: A number of markets remain disrupted and illiquid.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But I believe that they would have been even more illiquid and the risk of disruptive runs even greater without our various facilities; that's certainly what market participants are telling us.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Jan Hatzius is trying to gauge the combined effects on spending of the losses generated by the effects of the decline in housing prices outlined in the Case paper and the impulse for deleveraging in the financial sector inherent in the processes discussed by Morris and Shin.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: To restore capital ratios depleted by mortgage losses and to raise those ratios even further in order to reduce leverage to safer levels demanded by counterparties, banks and other lenders need to reduce assets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: They do so by tightening terms and standards across a broad array of credit--and we have seen this behavior reflected in our surveys of bank lending officers and in various spreads and other measures of risk perceptions, risk aversion, and reduced supply of credit at benchmark interest rates.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In the current circumstances, some of the tightening we have seen has been in anticipation of possible adverse events in the economy and in confidence toward the financial sector.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: These types of actions not only move up the demand-for-credit curve, but they also bolster profits going forward to cover potential write-offs and to attract new equity capital.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Pressures on profits arise not only from write-offs, but also because some sources of earnings, like securitization of mortgages or leveraged loans, are no longer available.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In the steady state, lenders will get greater returns for taking risk than they did two years ago, intermediaries will be less leveraged and better capitalized, and the financial system will be more robust and resilient to shocks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The transition to the new steady state, however, as lenders deleverage and protect themselves against various downside risks, involves some overshooting--making terms and standards tighter than will be necessary over the long run.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: This story is completely consistent with the one told in the Hatzius paper, which relies mostly on quantity relationships to gauge the possible effects on gross domestic product (GDP).
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: My instinct has been to go from the actual and expected indicators of tightening supply, such as the instrumental variables used in the paper, directly to estimates of the effects of that supply shift on GDP.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Measures of flows would fall out of that exercise, but not be its focus.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: And I have questions about the stability and reliability of the debt-GDP relationship used in the forecasts at the end of the paper.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But I will admit that we are in uncharted waters here, and the navigators shouldn't discard any potential information about the location of the shoals.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The message of the paper is that restraint on credit supplies is likely to persist because intermediaries have some way to go to rebuild their balance sheets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The process of adjustment to a safer, more resilient financial system is going to take a while.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I agree with this observation.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The views I express are my own and not necessarily those of other members of the Board of Governors.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The three papers discussed and their authors are as follows: (1) "Financial Regulation in a System Context," by Stephen Morris and Hyun Song Shin, professors of economics at Princeton University; (2) "Beyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn," by Jan Hatzius, chief U.S. economist at Goldman Sachs; and (3) "The Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?"
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: by Karl Case, professor of economics at Wellesley College.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Information about the 2008 Fall Conference on the Brookings Papers on Economic Activity is available at the Brookings website .
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: At the beginning of the chain of causation is the housing cycle in the United States.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Chip Case points out the difference between this housing cycle and others over past decades and asks why the difference developed.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One culprit he identifies is changes in the financial system that affected the way that mortgage credit is made available to borrowers.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: A key element of these changes, and one that accounts for a good part of the subsequent effects of the financial system and the economy, is the rise in leverage in housing finance.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As Case notes, for several years, mortgage indebtedness rose substantially relative to the value of owner-occupied housing.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The willingness of lenders to tolerate--or, in some cases, encourage--huge increases in loan-to-value ratios added to the demand for housing, especially by people who normally might not have had the savings to enter the market, and contributed to the rise in home prices.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One reason for the loosening of standards was the expectation that house prices would continue to rise--and even more certainly that they could not fall in all regions at the same time, supporting diversification through securitization.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Rising prices would enable lenders to recoup their funds even if the borrower was unable to service the loan, mostly because the borrower would be able to obtain extra cash through refinancing.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Expectations of house price appreciation facilitated and interacted with the increasing complexity of mortgage securities, including multiple securitizations of the same loan, which made it virtually impossible for ultimate lenders to monitor the creditworthiness of borrowers--a task they, in effect, had outsourced to credit rating agencies.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The absence of investor caution and due diligence was especially noticeable for the highest-rated tranches of securitized debt.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Elevated leverage in housing markets has meant that as prices have fallen, lenders have had to absorb an unusually high proportion of the losses.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As Case points out, foreclosures by lenders have added to the downward pressure on those prices.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Conceptually, such price declines moving down the demand curve for housing services could accelerate and cushion the adjustment in activity necessitated by previous overbuilding.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I am encouraged that Case finds the pace of declines abating in a number of markets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: However, partly owing to the feedback of price declines on lenders, mortgage conditions have tightened some since the late spring readings he is using for his conclusion, and in my view, the jury is still out on whether housing prices are close to finding a bottom.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The heavy involvement of financial intermediaries in amplifying the housing boom and the subsequent economic effects of the bust brings me to the Morris and Shin paper, which raises a host of important issues related to the systemic aspects of financial intermediation and the lessons from the recent turmoil.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As they emphasize, one of the important lessons has been the greater-than-expected vulnerability of secured financing when intermediaries are engaged in maturity, credit, and liquidity transformation.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Recall that the turmoil first came onto the balance sheets of the banks through the collapse of the asset-backed commercial paper market last fall before it affected the funding of investment banks through the triparty repurchase agreement market.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The new vulnerability results importantly from the extension of secured short-term financing to increasingly illiquid and riskier long-term assets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As uncertainty about the liquidity and creditworthiness of those assets--especially related to mortgage-backed securities--was called into question, lenders became more concerned about the possibility that they might end up owning the underlying assets, and they raised haircuts or simply refused to roll over loans.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Clearly, as Morris and Shin point out, what we have learned about various risks implies the need for intermediaries to build greater liquidity and capital buffers in good times, as well as to improve their abilities to manage their risks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: And those larger buffers would help to offset the moral hazard that may have been created through the expansion of our liquidity facilities.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Getting the micro-prudential piece right--having each institution adequately protected--would go a long way toward making the whole system more robust and resilient.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But Morris and Shin would go further; they would impose additional requirements on institutions to take account of the externalities for the system created when common shocks impair markets and credit availability by provoking widespread actions to preserve shareholder value.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: They would do this through a higher liquidity requirement and through the imposition of a leverage ratio on investment banks, which is already in place for commercial banks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I agree with the authors, and with Chairman Bernanke, that we need to consider the level of buffers that is appropriate to ameliorate systemic risk.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, a host of difficult judgments are inherent in how we establish such a system, and I'll raise just a few on a very general level.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One set concerns the size of the buffers.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: How far into the tail should intermediaries be required to insure themselves?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Shouldn't the Federal Reserve take some of the liquidity tail risk to facilitate intermediation of illiquid credits, as was intended at our founding?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the larger the regulatory tax, the more likely it is that activity will migrate to unregulated sectors in an environment of fluid and free capital movements.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: How can we gain better assurance of systemic stability when we are unlikely to be able to continuously extend the reach of regulation, and will it be sufficient to deepen the moats around the core institutions?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In this regard, the leverage ratio gives incentives to move some activities away from regulated institutions.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: A second question is, How we can structure these requirements and other aspects of regulation to damp, rather than reinforce, the natural procyclical tendencies of the financial system?
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Among the challenges will be encouraging firms and supervisors to comfortably allow buffers to be eroded in bad times.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Interestingly, prompt corrective action under the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Improvement Act of 1991 was intended, in part, to induce an element of countercyclical behavior by banks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: It gives banks an incentive to build excess capital--on both a risk-based and leverage ratio basis--in good times to avoid prompt corrective action when circumstances are less favorable.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Now that we are in the latter state of the world, a study of how commercial banks are viewing capital ratios, including the leverage ratio, could inform consideration of the Morris and Shin proposal.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Morris and Shin paper also provides a framework for thinking about the Federal Reserve's credit facilities.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: On page 9, they note that liquidity makes borrowers feel more robust and lenders less likely to withdraw, raising the odds for a more stable equilibrium for the entire system.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: That is exactly what we have been trying to do with our various discount lending facilities.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The assurance of the availability of liquidity to sound institutions against good collateral should counter the greater uncertainty and risk aversion that have impaired normal arbitrage and intermediary functions by making those institutions more willing to extend credit and take positions in the process of making markets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: It should also assure other creditors of those institutions that illiquid markets will not impede the repayment of their loans, and therefore make them more willing to keep lending.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: A number of markets remain disrupted and illiquid.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But I believe that they would have been even more illiquid and the risk of disruptive runs even greater without our various facilities; that's certainly what market participants are telling us.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Jan Hatzius is trying to gauge the combined effects on spending of the losses generated by the effects of the decline in housing prices outlined in the Case paper and the impulse for deleveraging in the financial sector inherent in the processes discussed by Morris and Shin.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: To restore capital ratios depleted by mortgage losses and to raise those ratios even further in order to reduce leverage to safer levels demanded by counterparties, banks and other lenders need to reduce assets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: They do so by tightening terms and standards across a broad array of credit--and we have seen this behavior reflected in our surveys of bank lending officers and in various spreads and other measures of risk perceptions, risk aversion, and reduced supply of credit at benchmark interest rates.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In the current circumstances, some of the tightening we have seen has been in anticipation of possible adverse events in the economy and in confidence toward the financial sector.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: These types of actions not only move up the demand-for-credit curve, but they also bolster profits going forward to cover potential write-offs and to attract new equity capital.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Pressures on profits arise not only from write-offs, but also because some sources of earnings, like securitization of mortgages or leveraged loans, are no longer available.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In the steady state, lenders will get greater returns for taking risk than they did two years ago, intermediaries will be less leveraged and better capitalized, and the financial system will be more robust and resilient to shocks.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The transition to the new steady state, however, as lenders deleverage and protect themselves against various downside risks, involves some overshooting--making terms and standards tighter than will be necessary over the long run.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: This story is completely consistent with the one told in the Hatzius paper, which relies mostly on quantity relationships to gauge the possible effects on gross domestic product (GDP).
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: My instinct has been to go from the actual and expected indicators of tightening supply, such as the instrumental variables used in the paper, directly to estimates of the effects of that supply shift on GDP.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Measures of flows would fall out of that exercise, but not be its focus.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: And I have questions about the stability and reliability of the debt-GDP relationship used in the forecasts at the end of the paper.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But I will admit that we are in uncharted waters here, and the navigators shouldn't discard any potential information about the location of the shoals.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The message of the paper is that restraint on credit supplies is likely to persist because intermediaries have some way to go to rebuild their balance sheets.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The process of adjustment to a safer, more resilient financial system is going to take a while.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â
speech_venue: At the Brookings Panel on Economic Activity, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: I agree with this observation.
speech_title: Comments on âFinancial Regulation in a System Context,â âBeyond Leveraged Losses: The Balance Sheet Effects of the Home Price Downturn,â and âThe Central Role of House Prices in the Financial Crisis: How Will the Market Clear?â

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, financial systems in the United States and in much of the rest of the world are under extraordinary stress, particularly the credit and money markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The losses suffered by many banks and nonbank financial firms have both constrained their ability to lend and reduced the willingness of other market participants to deal with them.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Great uncertainty about the values of financial assets, particularly more complex and opaque assets, has made investors extremely reluctant to bear credit risk, resulting in further declines in asset prices and a drying up of liquidity in a number of funding markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
