speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even secured funding has become expensive and difficult to obtain, as lenders worry about their ability to sell collateral in illiquid markets in the event of default.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, many securitization markets, such as the secondary market for private-label mortgage-backed securities, remain closed or impaired.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Considerable experience in both industrialized and emerging economies has shown that severe financial instability, together with the associated declines in asset prices and disruptions in credit markets, can take a heavy toll on the broader economy if left unchecked.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For this reason, the Federal Reserve, the Treasury, and other agencies are committed to restoring market stability and are working assiduously to ensure that the financial system is able to perform its critical economic functions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recent actions by the Congress have given the Treasury new tools and resources to address the stressed conditions of our financial markets and institutions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has also been granted a new authority, the ability to pay interest on bank reserves, which will allow us to expand our lending as needed to support the system while better managing the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These tools will provide important additional support for the government's efforts to strengthen financial markets and the economy.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Let me briefly review recent financial developments.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the heels of nearly a year of stress in credit markets, investors' and creditors' concerns about funding and credit risks at financial firms intensified over the summer as mortgage-related assets deteriorated further, economic growth slowed, and uncertainty about the economic outlook increased.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As investors and creditors lost confidence in the ability of certain firms to meet their obligations, their access to capital markets as well as to short-term funding markets became increasingly impaired and their stock prices fell sharply.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Among the companies that experienced this dynamic most forcefully were the government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs), Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; the investment bank Lehman Brothers; and the insurance company American International Group (AIG).
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve believes that, whenever possible, such difficulties should be addressed through private-sector arrangements--for example, by raising new equity capital, as many firms have done, by negotiations leading to a merger or acquisition, or by an orderly wind-down.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Government assistance should be provided with the greatest reluctance and only when the stability of the financial system, and thus the health of the broader economy, is at risk.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In those cases when financial stability is threatened, however, intervention to protect the public interest may well be justified.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac present cases in point.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve had long warned about the systemic risks posed by these companies' large portfolios of mortgages and mortgage-backed securities, as well as the problems arising from the conflict between shareholders' objectives and the government's goals for the two firms.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Given the scale of losses in their portfolios, raising enough new capital from private investors was infeasible.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The firms' size and their government-sponsored status precluded a merger with, or acquisition by, another company.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To avoid unacceptably large dislocations in the mortgage markets, the financial sector, and the economy as a whole, the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) put Fannie and Freddie into conservatorship and the Treasury, drawing on authorities recently granted by the Congress, made financial support available.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve, acting in a consultative role, worked closely with FHFA in evaluating the GSE portfolios and capital positions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Based on the joint findings of the agencies, we supported FHFA's decision to place the companies into conservatorship as necessary and appropriate, given their conditions and systemic importance.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The government's actions appear to have stabilized the GSEs, although like virtually all other firms they are experiencing effects of the current crisis.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nonetheless, we already have seen benefits of their stabilization in the form of lower mortgage rates, which should help the housing market.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The difficulties at Lehman and AIG raised somewhat different issues.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Like the GSEs, both companies were large and complex and deeply embedded in our financial system.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In both cases, as the firms approached default, the Treasury and the Federal Reserve sought private-sector solutions, but none was forthcoming.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Attempts to organize a consortium of private firms to purchase or recapitalize Lehman were unsuccessful.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: With respect to public-sector solutions, we determined that either facilitating a sale of Lehman or maintaining the company as a free-standing entity would have required a very sizable injection of public funds--much larger than in the case of Bear Stearns--and would have involved the assumption by taxpayers of billions of dollars of expected losses.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even if assuming these costs could be justified on public policy grounds, neither the Treasury nor the Federal Reserve had the authority to commit public money in that way; in particular, the Federal Reserve's loans must be sufficiently secured to provide reasonable assurance that the loan will be fully repaid.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Such collateral was not available in this case.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recognizing that Lehman's potential failure posed risks to market functioning, the Federal Reserve sought to cushion the effects by implementing a number of measures, including substantially broadening the collateral accepted by the Fed's Primary Dealer Credit Facility (PDCF) and Term Securities Lending Facility (TSLF) to ensure that the remaining primary dealers would have uninterrupted access to funding.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the case of AIG, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury judged that a disorderly failure of AIG would have severely threatened global financial stability and the performance of the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: That judgment reflected our assessment of prevailing market conditions, AIG's central role in a number of markets other firms use to manage risks, and the size and composition of AIG's balance sheet.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To avoid the default of AIG, the Federal Reserve was able to provide emergency credit that was judged to be adequately secured by the assets of the company.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To protect U.S. taxpayers and to mitigate the possibility that lending to AIG would encourage inappropriate risk-taking by financial firms in the future, the Federal Reserve further ensured that the terms of the credit extended to AIG imposed significant costs and constraints on the firm's owners, managers, and creditors.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: AIG's difficulties and Lehman's failure, along with growing concerns about the U.S. housing sector and economy, contributed to extraordinarily turbulent conditions in global financial markets in recent weeks.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Equity prices have fallen sharply, the cost of short-term credit, where such credit has been available, has spiked, and liquidity has dried up in many markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: One money market fund's losses forced it to "break the buck"--that is, the value of its assets fell below par--an event that triggered extensive withdrawals from a number of money market funds.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Those funds responded to the surge in redemptions by attempting to reduce their holdings of commercial paper and large certificates of deposit issued by banks.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some firms that could not roll over maturing commercial paper drew on back-up lines of credit with banks just as the banks were finding it even more difficult to raise cash in the money markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the same time, a marked increase in the demand for safe assets--a flight to quality and liquidity--resulted in a further drop in the value of mortgage-related assets and sent the yield on Treasury bills down to a few hundredths of a percent.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Developments during the summer pressured not only nonbank financial firms, but also a number of depository institutions, including Washington Mutual (WaMu) and Wachovia.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In recent weeks, these two institutions suffered deposit outflows and reduced access to wholesale funding.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Office of Thrift Supervision, WaMu's regulator, closed that company and appointed the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) as receiver; the FDIC immediately sold the institution to JPMorgan Chase.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the case of Wachovia, to avoid serious adverse effects on economic conditions and financial stability, the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the President and on the recommendation of the Federal Reserve and FDIC, authorized the FDIC to use its funds to facilitate the sale of that company's banking operations without loss to creditors.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Both Citicorp and Wells Fargo have offered to buy the company and negotiations are continuing.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Most importantly, however, in either case all depositors and creditors of Wachovia are fully protected, and depositors and other customers will experience no interruption in banking services.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: By potentially restricting future flows of credit to households and businesses, the developments in financial markets pose a significant threat to economic growth.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury and the Fed have taken a range of actions to address the very tight funding conditions that now prevail.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, the Treasury implemented a temporary guarantee program for balances held in money market mutual funds, helping to stem the outflows from these funds and thus reducing their need to sell assets into already distressed markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has taken a number of steps, including putting in place a temporary lending facility that provides financing for banks to purchase high-quality asset-backed commercial paper from money market funds.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed has also significantly increased the quantity of funds it auctions to banks and has accommodated heightened demands for funding from banks and primary dealers; as of last Wednesday, our various lending facilities, including our securities lending program, were providing more than $800 billion of liquidity to the financial system.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address dollar funding pressures worldwide, we have significantly expanded reciprocal currency arrangements (so-called swap agreements) with foreign central banks.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These agreements enable the foreign central banks to provide dollar funding to financial institutions in their jurisdictions, which helps to improve the functioning of dollar funding markets globally.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, this morning the Federal Reserve announced a new facility that will help provide liquidity to term funding markets by purchasing three-month commercial paper and asset-backed commercial paper directly from eligible issuers.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The expansion of Federal Reserve lending is helping financial firms cope with reduced access to their usual sources of funding.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recently, however, our liquidity provision had begun to run ahead of our ability to absorb excess reserves held by the banking system, leading the effective funds rate, on many days, to fall below the target set by the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This problem has largely been addressed by a provision of the legislation the Congress passed last week, which gives the Federal Reserve the authority to pay interest on balances that depository institutions hold in their accounts at the Federal Reserve Banks.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve announced yesterday that it will pay interest on required reserve balances at 10 basis points below the target federal funds rate, and pay interest on excess reserves, initially at 75 basis points below the target.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Paying interest on reserves should allow us to better control the federal funds rate, as banks are unlikely to lend overnight balances at a rate lower than they can receive from the Fed; thus, the payment of interest on reserves should set a floor for the funds rate over the day.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: With this step, our lending facilities may be more easily expanded as necessary.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: So long as financial conditions warrant, we will continue to look for ways to reduce funding pressures in key markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic activity had shown signs of decelerating even before the recent upsurge in financial-market tensions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As has been the case for some time, the housing market continues to be a primary source of weakness in the real economy as well as in the financial markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the slowdown in economic activity has spread outside the housing sector.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Private payrolls have continued to contract, and the declines in employment, together with earlier increases in food and energy prices, have eroded the purchasing power of households.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This sluggishness of real incomes, together with tighter credit and declining household wealth, is now showing through more clearly to consumer spending.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, since May, real consumer outlays have contracted significantly.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Meanwhile, in the business sector, worsening sales prospects and a heightened sense of uncertainty have begun to weigh more heavily on investment spending as well.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The intensification of financial turmoil and the further impairment of the functioning of credit markets seem likely to increase the restraint on economic activity in the period ahead.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even households with good credit histories are now facing difficulties obtaining mortgage loans or home equity lines of credit.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Banks are also reducing credit card limits, and denial rates on automobile loan applications reportedly are rising.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Businesses, too, are confronting diminished access to credit.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, disruptions in the commercial paper market and tightening of bank lending standards have made it more difficult for businesses to obtain the working capital they need to meet everyday operating expenses such as payrolls and inventories.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: All told, economic activity is likely to be subdued during the remainder of this year and into next year.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The heightened financial turmoil that we have experienced of late may well lengthen the period of weak economic performance and further increase the risks to growth.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To support growth and reduce the downside risks, continued efforts to stabilize the financial markets are essential.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve will continue to use the tools at its disposal to improve market functioning and liquidity.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Inflation has been elevated, reflecting the steep increases in the prices of oil, other commodities, and imports that occurred earlier this year, as well as some pass-through by firms to consumers of their higher costs of production.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, more recently, the prices of oil and other commodities, while remaining quite volatile, have fallen from their peaks, and prices of imports show signs of decelerating.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, expected inflation, as measured by consumer surveys and inflation-indexed Treasury securities, has held steady or eased.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These recent developments, together with economic activity that is likely to fall short of potential for a time, should lead to rates of inflation more consistent with price stability.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Still, the inflation outlook remains highly uncertain, in part because of the extraordinary volatility of commodity prices.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will need to continue to monitor price developments closely.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Overall, the combination of the incoming data and recent financial developments suggests that the outlook for economic growth has worsened and that the downside risks to growth have increased.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the same time, the outlook for inflation has improved somewhat, though it remains uncertain.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In light of these developments, the Federal Reserve will need to consider whether the current stance of policy remains appropriate.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The intensification of the financial crisis in recent weeks made clear that a more powerful and comprehensive approach involving the fiscal authorities was needed to solve these problems.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On that basis, the Secretary of the Treasury, with the support of the Federal Reserve, went to the Congress to ask for a substantial program aimed at stabilizing our financial markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, last week the Congress passed and the President signed the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This legislation provides important new tools for addressing the distress in financial markets and thus mitigating the risks to the economy.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The act adds broad, flexible authorities to buy troubled assets, to provide guarantees, and to directly strengthen the balance sheets of individual institutions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, the legislation establishes a new Troubled Asset Relief Program, or TARP, under which the Treasury is authorized to purchase as much as $700billion of troubled mortgages, mortgage-related securities, and other financial instruments from financial firms that are regulated under U.S. law and have significant operations in the United States.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The act also raises the limit on deposit insurance at banks and credit unions from $100,000 to $250,000 per account, a step that should reinforce depositors' confidence in the security of their funds and thus help to stabilize depository institutions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And, as I mentioned, the act provides the Federal Reserve the authority to pay interest on reserves, which will allow us to better manage the federal funds rate as we provide liquidity to the markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will begin exercising that authority this week.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The TARP's purchases of illiquid assets from banks and other financial institutions will create liquidity and promote price discovery in the markets for these assets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This in turn will reduce investor uncertainty about the current value and prospects of financial institutions, enabling banks and other institutions to raise capital and increasing the willingness of counterparties to engage.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: More generally, increased liquidity and transparency in pricing will help to restore confidence in our financial markets and promote more normal functioning.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: With time, strengthening our financial institutions and markets will allow credit to begin flowing again, supporting economic growth.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The interests of taxpayers are carefully protected under this program.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, the Congress has required extensive controls and oversight to ensure that the allotted funds are used appropriately and effectively.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, the $700 billion allocated by the legislation is not an authorization to spend but rather an authorization to purchase financial assets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury will be a patient investor and will likely hold these assets for an appreciable period of time.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Eventually, however, some assets will mature, and the Treasury will choose to sell others to private investors.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Financially, in the long run, the taxpayer may come out either ahead or behind in this process; in light of the many uncertainties, no assurances can be given.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the ultimate cost of the program to the taxpayer will certainly be far less than $700 billion.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Third, and most important, restoring the normal flow of credit is essential for economic recovery.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: If the TARP promotes financial stability, leading ultimately to stronger economic growth and job creation, it will have proved a very good investment indeed, to everyone's benefit.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be sure, there are many challenges associated with the design and implementation of the TARP, including determining which assets will be purchased and how prices will be determined.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury, with the advice and cooperation of the Federal Reserve, is working to address these challenges as quickly as possible.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It is unlikely that a single method will be used for acquiring assets; inevitably, some experimentation will be necessary to determine which approaches are most effective.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importantly, the legislation that created the TARP does provide sufficient flexibility to allow for different approaches to solving the problem--subject, of course, to the close oversight that will ensure that the program's funds are used in ways that are in the interest of taxpayers.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These are momentous steps, but they are being taken to address a problem of historic dimensions.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In one respect, however, we are fortunate.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have learned from historical experience with severe financial crises that if government intervention comes only at a point at which many or most financial institutions are insolvent or nearly so, the costs of restoring the system are greatly increased.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This is not the situation we face today.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Congress and the Administration chose to act at a moment of great stress, but one at which the great majority of financial institutions have sufficient capital and liquidity to return to their critical function of providing new credit for our economy.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The steps being taken now to restore confidence in our institutions and markets will go far to resolving the current dislocations in the markets.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I believe that the bold actions taken by the Congress, the Treasury, the Federal Reserve, and other agencies, together with the natural recuperative powers of the financial markets, will lay the groundwork for financial and economic recovery.
speech_title: Current Economic and Financial Conditions
speech_venue: At the National Association for Business Economics 50th Annual Meeting, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Over the past year, the Federal Reserve has actively used all its powers and authorities to try to help our economy through this difficult time.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And central banks around the world have consulted closely and cooperated in unprecedented ways to reduce strains in financial markets and to bolster our economies.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will continue to do so.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, clearly the time had come for a more comprehensive and broad-based solution.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: History teaches us that government engagement in times of severe financial crisis often arrives very late, usually at a point at which most financial institutions are insolvent or nearly so.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Waiting too long to act has usually led to much greater direct costs of the intervention itself and, more importantly, magnified the painful effects of financial turmoil on households and businesses.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: That is not the situation we face today.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Fortunately, the Congress and the Administration have acted at a time when the great majority of financial institutions, though stressed by highly volatile and difficult market conditions, remain capable of fulfilling their critical function of providing new credit for our economy.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Congress's prompt and decisive action in passing the financial rescue legislation made possible the critical steps that have been announced this morning.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I also find it heartening that we are seeing not just a national, but a global response to the crisis, commensurate with its global nature.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, this past weekend, the finance ministers and central bankers of the Group of Seven industrialized countries announced a set of principles embodying a comprehensive approach to dealing with the crisis.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The steps we are taking today are fully consistent with those principles.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As in all past crises, at the root of the problem is a loss of confidence by investors and the public in the strength of key financial institutions and markets, which has had cascading and unwelcome effects on the availability of credit and the value of savings.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The actions today are aimed at restoring confidence in our institutions and markets and repairing their capacity to meet the credit needs of American households and businesses.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The voluntary equity purchase program will strengthen financial institutions' capacity and willingness to lend.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The guarantee of the senior debt of all FDIC-insured depository institutions and their holding companies will restore the confidence of these institutions' creditors and reinvigorate the crucial inter-bank lending markets.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Additionally, the Federal Reserve is pressing forward with its facility to provide a broad backstop for the commercial paper market, so vital to the functioning of our businesses.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Policymakers here and around the globe have taken a series of extraordinary steps.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Americans can be confident that every resource is being brought to bear: historical understanding, technical expertise, economic analysis, and political leadership.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I am not suggesting the way forward will be easy.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But I strongly believe that the application of these tools, together with the underlying vitality and resilience of the American economy, will help to restore confidence to our financial system and place our economy back on a path to vigorous, healthy growth.
speech_title: Remarks
speech_venue: At the President's Working Group Market Stability Initiative Announcement, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I am pleased once again to share a meal and some thoughts with the Economic Club of New York.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will focus today on the economic and financial challenges we face and why I believe we are well positioned to move forward.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The problems now evident in the markets and in the economy are large and complex, but, in my judgment, our government now has the tools it needs to confront and solve them.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our strategy will continue to evolve and be refined as we adapt to new developments and the inevitable setbacks.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: But we will not stand down until we have achieved our goals of repairing and reforming our financial system and restoring prosperity.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The crisis we face in the financial markets has many novel aspects, largely arising from the complexity and sophistication of today's financial institutions and instruments and the remarkable degree of global financial integration that allows financial shocks to be transmitted around the world at the speed of light.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, as a long-time student of banking and financial crises, I can attest that the current situation also has much in common with past experiences.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As in all past crises, at the root of the problem is a loss of confidence by investors and the public in the strength of key financial institutions and markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The crisis will end when comprehensive responses by political and financial leaders restore that trust, bringing investors back into the market and allowing the normal business of extending credit to households and firms to resume.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In that regard, we are, in one respect at least, better off than those who dealt with earlier financial crises: Generally, during past crises, broad-based government engagement came late, usually at a point at which most financial institutions were insolvent or nearly so.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Waiting too long to respond has usually led to much greater direct costs of the intervention itself and, more importantly, magnified the painful effects of financial turmoil on households and businesses.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: That is not the situation we face today.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Fortunately, the Congress and the Administration have acted at a time when the great majority of financial institutions, though stressed by highly volatile and difficult market conditions, remain strong and capable of fulfilling their critical function of providing new credit for our economy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This prompt and decisive action by our political leaders will allow us to restore more normal market functioning much more quickly and at lower ultimate cost than would otherwise have been the case.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, we are seeing not just a national response but a global response to the crisis, commensurate with its global nature.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This financial crisis has been with us for more than a year.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: It was sparked by the end of the U.S. housing boom, which revealed the weaknesses and excesses that had occurred in subprime mortgage lending.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, as subsequent events have demonstrated, the problem was much broader than subprime lending.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Large inflows of capital into the United States and other countries stimulated a reaching for yield, an underpricing of risk, excessive leverage, and the development of complex and opaque financial instruments that seemed to work well during the credit boom but have been shown to be fragile under stress.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The unwinding of these developments, including a sharp deleveraging and a headlong retreat from credit risk, led to highly strained conditions in financial markets and a tightening of credit that has hamstrung economic growth.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve responded to these developments in two broad ways.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, following classic tenets of central banking, the Fed has provided large amounts of liquidity to the financial system to cushion the effects of tight conditions in short-term funding markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, to reduce the downside risks to growth emanating from the tightening of credit, the Fed, in a series of moves that began last September, has significantly lowered its target for the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, last week, in an unprecedented joint action with five other major central banks and in response to the adverse implications of the deepening crisis for the economic outlook, the Federal Reserve again eased the stance of monetary policy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We will continue to use all the tools at our disposal to improve market functioning and liquidity, to reduce pressures in key credit and funding markets, and to complement the steps the Treasury and foreign governments will be taking to strengthen the financial system.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notwithstanding our efforts and those of other policymakers, the financial crisis intensified over the summer as mortgage-related assets deteriorated further, economic growth slowed, and uncertainty about the financial and economic outlook increased.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: As investors and creditors lost confidence in the ability of certain firms to meet their obligations, their access to capital markets as well as to short-term funding markets became increasingly impaired, and their stock prices fell sharply.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Prominent companies that experienced this dynamic most acutely included the government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs) Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the investment bank Lehman Brothers, and the insurance company American International Group (AIG).
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve believes that, whenever possible, the difficulties experienced by firms in financial distress should be addressed through private-sector arrangements--for example, by raising new equity capital, as many firms have done; by negotiations leading to a merger or acquisition; or by an orderly wind-down.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Government assistance should be provided with the greatest reluctance and only when the stability of the financial system, and thus the health of the broader economy, is at risk.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In those cases when financial stability is broadly threatened, however, intervention to protect the public interest is not only justified but must be undertaken forcefully and without hesitation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac present cases in point.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To avoid unacceptably large dislocations in the mortgage markets, the financial sector, and the economy as a whole, the Federal Housing Finance Agency put Fannie and Freddie into conservatorship, and the Treasury, drawing on authorities recently granted by the Congress, made financial support available.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The government's actions appear to have stabilized the GSEs, although, like virtually all other firms, they are experiencing effects of the current crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have already seen benefits of their stabilization in the form of lower mortgage rates, which will help the housing market.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The difficulties at Lehman and AIG raised different issues.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Like the GSEs, both companies were large, complex, and deeply embedded in our financial system.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In both cases, the Treasury and the Federal Reserve sought private-sector solutions, but none was forthcoming.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: A public-sector solution for Lehman proved infeasible, as the firm could not post sufficient collateral to provide reasonable assurance that a loan from the Federal Reserve would be repaid, and the Treasury did not have the authority to absorb billions of dollars of expected losses to facilitate Lehman's acquisition by another firm.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consequently, little could be done except to attempt to ameliorate the effects of Lehman's failure on the financial system.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importantly, the financial rescue legislation, which I will discuss later, will give us better choices.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the future, the Treasury will have greater resources available to prevent the failure of a financial institution when such a failure would pose unacceptable risks to the financial system as a whole.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve will work closely and actively with the Treasury and other authorities to minimize systemic risk.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the case of AIG, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury judged that a disorderly failure would have severely threatened global financial stability and the performance of the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We also judged that emergency Federal Reserve credit to AIG would be adequately secured by AIG's assets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To protect U.S. taxpayers and to mitigate the possibility that lending to AIG would encourage inappropriate risk-taking by financial firms in the future, the Federal Reserve ensured that the terms of the credit extended to AIG imposed significant costs and constraints on the firm's owners, managers, and creditors.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: AIG's difficulties and Lehman's failure, along with growing concerns about the U.S. economy and other economies, contributed to extraordinarily turbulent conditions in global financial markets in recent weeks.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Withdrawals from prime money market mutual funds led them to reduce their holdings of commercial paper--an important source of financing for the nation's nonfinancial businesses as well as for many financial firms.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The cost of short-term credit, where such credit has been available, jumped for virtually all firms, and liquidity dried up in many markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: By restricting flows of credit to households, businesses, and state and local governments, the turmoil in financial markets and the funding pressures on financial firms pose a significant threat to economic growth.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury and the Fed have taken a range of actions to address financial problems.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address illiquidity and impaired functioning in commercial paper markets, the Treasury implemented a temporary guarantee program for balances held in money market mutual funds to help stem the outflows from these funds.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve put in place a temporary lending facility that provides financing for banks to purchase high-quality asset-backed commercial paper from money market funds, thus reducing their need to sell the commercial paper into already distressed markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, we soon will implement a new, temporary Commercial Paper Funding Facility that will provide a backstop to commercial paper markets by purchasing highly rated commercial paper directly from issuers at a term of three months when those markets are illiquid.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address ongoing problems in interbank funding markets, the Federal Reserve has significantly increased the quantity of term funds it auctions to banks and accommodated heightened demands for temporary funding from banks and primary dealers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Also, to try to mitigate dollar funding pressures worldwide, we have greatly expanded reciprocal currency arrangements (so-called swap agreements) with other central banks.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, this week we agreed to extend unlimited dollar funding to the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, the Bank of Japan, and the Swiss National Bank.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These agreements enable foreign central banks to provide dollars to financial institutions in their jurisdictions, which helps improve the functioning of dollar funding markets globally and relieve pressures on U.S. funding markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: It bears noting that these arrangements carry no risk to the U.S. taxpayer, as our loans are to the foreign central banks themselves, who take responsibility for the extension of dollar credit within their jurisdictions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The expansion of Federal Reserve lending is helping financial firms cope with reduced access to their usual sources of funding and thus is supporting their lending to nonfinancial firms and households.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Nonetheless, the intensification of the financial crisis over the past month or so made clear that a more powerful, comprehensive approach involving the fiscal authorities was needed to address these problems more effectively.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: On that basis, the Administration, with the support of the Federal Reserve, asked the Congress for a new program aimed at stabilizing our financial markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The resulting legislation, the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act, provides important new tools for addressing the distress in financial markets and thus mitigating the risks to the economy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The act allows Treasury to buy troubled assets, to provide guarantees, and to inject capital to strengthen the balance sheets of financial institutions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The act also raises the limit on deposit insurance from $100,000 to $250,000 per account, effectively immediately.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) authorized by the legislation will allow the Treasury, under the supervision of an oversight board that I will head, to undertake two highly complementary activities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, the Treasury will use the TARP funds to help recapitalize our banking system by purchasing non-voting equity in financial institutions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Details of this program were announced yesterday.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Initially, the Treasury will dedicate $250 billion toward purchases of preferred shares in banks and thrifts of all sizes.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The program is voluntary and designed both to encourage participation by healthy institutions and to make it attractive for private capital to come in along with public capital.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We look to strong institutions to participate in this capital program, because today even strong institutions are reluctant to expand their balance sheets to extend credit; with fresh capital, that constraint will be eased.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The terms offered under the TARP include the acquisition by the Treasury of warrants to ensure that taxpayers receive a share of the upside as the financial system recovers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, as required by the legislation, institutions that receive capital will have to meet certain standards regarding executive compensation practices.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, the Treasury will use some of the resources provided under the bill to purchase troubled assets from banks and other financial institutions, in most cases using market-based mechanisms.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Mortgage-related assets, including mortgage-backed securities and whole loans, will be the focus of the program, although the law permits flexibility in the types of assets purchased as needed to promote financial stability.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Removing these assets from private balance sheets should increase liquidity and promote price discovery in the markets for these assets, thereby reducing investor uncertainty about the current value and prospects of financial institutions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Unclogging the markets for mortgage-related assets should put banks and other institutions in a better position to raise capital from the private sector and increase the willingness of counterparties to engage.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: With time, the provision of equity capital to the banking system and the purchase of troubled assets will help credit flow more freely, thus supporting economic growth.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These measures will lead to a much stronger financial system over time, but steps are also necessary to address the immediate problem of lack of trust and confidence.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Accordingly, also announced yesterday was a plan by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) to provide a broad range of guarantees of the liabilities of FDIC-insured depository institutions, including their associated holding companies.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The guarantee covers all newly issued senior unsecured debt, including commercial paper and interbank funding, and it will also cover all funds held in non-interest-bearing transactions accounts, such as payroll accounts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This broad guarantee will be effectively immediately, and fees for coverage will be waived for 30 days.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: After the 30-day grace period, banks may continue to participate in the guarantee program by paying reasonable fees.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I would like to stress once again that the taxpayers' interests were very much in our minds and those of the Congress when these programs were designed.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The costs of the FDIC guarantee are expected to be covered by fees and assessments on the banking system, not by the taxpayer.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the case of the TARP program, the funds allocated are not simple expenditures, but rather acquisitions of assets or equity positions, which the Treasury will be able to sell or redeem down the road.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, it is possible that taxpayers could turn a profit from the program, although, given the great uncertainties, no assurances can be provided.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, the program is subject to extensive controls and to oversight by several bodies.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The larger point, though, is that the economic benefit of these programs to taxpayers will not be determined primarily by the financial return to TARP funds, but rather by the impact of the program on the financial markets and the economy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: If the TARP, together with the other measures that have been taken, is successful in promoting financial stability and, consequently, in supporting stronger economic growth and job creation, it will have proved itself a very good investment indeed, to everyone's benefit.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
