text: Stabilization of the financial markets is a critical first step, but even if they stabilize as we hope they will, broader economic recovery will not happen right away.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic activity had been decelerating even before the recent intensification of the crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: The housing market continues to be a primary source of weakness in the real economy as well as in the financial markets, and we have seen marked slowdowns in consumer spending, business investment, and the labor market.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Credit markets will take some time to unfreeze.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: And with the economies of our trading partners slowing, our export sales, which have been a source of strength, very probably will slow as well.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These restraining influences on economic activity, however, will be offset somewhat by the favorable effects of lower prices for oil and other commodities on household purchasing power.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Ultimately, the trajectory of economic activity beyond the next few quarters will depend greatly on the extent to which financial and credit markets return to more normal functioning.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Inflation has been elevated recently, reflecting the steep increases in the prices of oil, other commodities, and imports that occurred earlier this year, as well as some pass-through by firms of their higher costs of production.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, expected inflation, as measured by consumer surveys and inflation-indexed Treasury securities, has held steady or eased, and prices of imports now appear to be decelerating.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: These developments, together with the recent declines in prices of oil and other commodities as well as the likelihood that economic activity will fall short of potential for a time, should lead to rates of inflation more consistent with price stability.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: This past weekend, the finance ministers and central bank governors of the Group of Seven industrialized countries met in Washington.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We committed to work together to stabilize financial markets and restore the flow of credit to support global economic growth.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We agreed to use all available tools to prevent failures that pose systemic risk.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We affirmed we will ensure our deposit insurance programs instill confidence in the safety of savings.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We agreed to ensure that our banks and other major financial intermediaries, as needed, can raise capital from public as well as private sources.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: We further agreed that we would take all necessary steps to unfreeze interbank and money markets, and that we will act to restart the secondary markets for mortgages and other securitized assets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Finally, we recognized that we should take these actions in ways that protect taxpayers and avoid potentially damaging effects on other countries.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I believe that these are the right principles for action, and I see the steps announced by our government yesterday as fully consistent with them.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I have laid out for you today an extraordinary series of actions taken by policymakers throughout our government and around the globe.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Americans can be confident that every resource is being brought to bear to address the current crisis: historical understanding, technical expertise, economic analysis, financial insight, and political leadership.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: I am not suggesting the way forward will be easy, but I strongly believe that we now have the tools we need to respond with the necessary force to these challenges.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although much work remains and more difficulties surely lie ahead, I remain confident that the American economy, with its great intrinsic vitality and aided by the measures now available, will emerge from this period with renewed vigor.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Financial Markets and the Economy
speech_venue: At the Economic Club of New York, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: We gather in difficult times for our financial markets and our economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Recent weeks have seen a sharp intensification of the turmoil in financial markets: There has been a broad-based pullback in risk-taking and a virtual seizing up of term lending to many banks and other financial institutions; interest rates have risen for many borrowers, and credit availability has significantly diminished; and equity prices have fallen sharply, on net.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The authorities have responded with a series of forceful and innovative measures that promise to rebuild confidence and free up lending.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Tonight I will try to put these developments in the context of the recent course of our economy and its prospects for the future.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Before commenting on the current situation and its economic implications, I thought it might be useful to begin by giving you my perspective on where the economy stood prior to the recent intensification of financial turmoil.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Overall economic activity--as measured by the growth of real gross domestic product (GDP)--held up surprisingly well over the first half of 2008 given the ongoing stresses in broader financial markets and the further rise in oil prices.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, however, a number of disquieting signs lay underneath the surface of the aggregate growth figures.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Conditions in housing markets, as had been widely expected, were continuing to deteriorate, with further declines in home sales, new construction, and house prices in most markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: And, while consumer spending posted moderate gains during the spring, it seemed likely that much of that strength stemmed from the sizable tax rebate checks that began to go out to households at the end of April.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Meanwhile, on the business side, employers had been reducing payrolls since the turn of the year, industrial production fell from February through May, and many corporations were seeing their profits squeezed by rising costs and weak demand.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: During the summer, it became increasingly clear that a downshifting in the pace of economic activity was in train.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In particular, the long list of negative factors weighing on domestic demand--including high prices for oil and other commodities, tight credit conditions, and the housing downturn--were beginning to take a significant toll on the economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The deterioration was led by a noticeable retrenchment in consumer spending.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Although rebate checks continued to provide a boost to incomes in June and July, households were facing some stiff headwinds.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Ongoing job losses and sharp increases in energy and food prices subtracted from household purchasing power, declining home prices and falling equity values led to a further drop in household wealth, and consumers remained extremely downbeat about prospects for jobs and income.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, credit became more difficult to obtain as lenders became increasingly concerned about the prospects for loan performance in a softening economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Many banks and other creditors tightened standards for credit cards and other consumer loans, and some lenders either reduced borrowing limits on or eliminated home equity lines of credit.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result of all these influences, real consumer outlays fell from June through August, putting real consumer spending for the third quarter as a whole on track to decline for the first time since 1991.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Business investment also appears to have slowed over the summer.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Orders and shipments for nondefense capital goods have weakened, on net, in recent months, pointing to a decline in real outlays for new business equipment.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Similarly, outlays for nonresidential construction projects edged lower in July and August after rising at a robust pace over the first half of this year.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Although the deteriorating sales outlook and increased uncertainty about the economy undoubtedly played a role, the softening in business outlays also appeared to reflect reduced credit availability from banks and other lenders.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, conditions in housing markets have remained on a downward trajectory.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Sales and construction of new homes continued to decline over the summer, and while existing home sales showed signs of stabilizing at low levels, many of the sales that did occur appear to have been stimulated by sharp price reductions for distressed properties.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: National indexes of house prices continued to post sizable declines.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Unfortunately, our trading partners have proven not to be immune from financial turmoil and economic weakness.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Incoming data indicate that the pace of activity in many foreign economies slowed in recent quarters, reflecting many of the same forces of credit contraction, rising energy prices, and housing market decelerations that have affected the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This weakening in foreign activity suggests that the support to domestic production from net exports that was evident in the first half of this year is likely diminishing.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: We can see evidence of this in manufacturing production outside of motor vehicles, which had benefited from the earlier decline in the dollar and strong foreign growth; it fell for a third consecutive month in August, and indications for September suggest a further decline last month, even after excluding the effects of the recent hurricanes and the strike at Boeing.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Meanwhile, inflation remained uncomfortably high through much of the summer.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The sharp increases in the prices of oil and many agricultural commodities showed through to consumer food and energy prices, and producers passed through some of their higher input costs into retail prices for "core" goods and services.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: More recently, however, the prices of oil and other commodities have posted substantial declines, non-oil import prices have edged down, and the prospect of greater slack in resource markets and weak demand seems likely to restrain labor cost pressures and pricing power.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Reflecting these developments, inflation expectations appear to have eased a bit.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The weakening U.S. economy and ongoing declines in house prices, with their implications for credit performance, put further pressure on exposed financial institutions over the summer.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Investors lost confidence in some of these institutions, which then saw their access to liquidity dry up, causing some to fail and others to require government assistance or to consolidate via their acquisition by healthier institutions.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The speed with which these developments occurred, along with worries about losses throughout the financial system, led banks and other lenders to pull back from extending credit except at the very shortest maturities.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, conditions in funding markets deteriorated substantially further in September and early October, with interbank lending rates moving up sharply from already-high levels and spreads over comparable-maturity overnight index swaps widening to unprecedented levels.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the commercial paper market became severely disrupted as money market mutual funds, the largest investors in that market, substantially reduced their demand in response to outflows and the difficulty of liquidating commercial paper in secondary markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, yields on commercial paper skyrocketed for most issuers, and funding became increasingly concentrated in paper with overnight maturities.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Similarly, interest rates on longer-term corporate bonds rose sharply even for investment-grade firms, and bond markets were closed off to many issuers.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: These developments quickly led to sharp declines in equity prices more generally, as well as to widespread disruptions in other markets, including the markets for municipal bonds.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Market distress fed on itself, as efforts by lenders to protect themselves triggered calls for increased margins, sales of assets that accentuated price declines, large increases in volatility in an uncertain and unfamiliar environment, and a sharp cutback in the willingness to extend credit.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Financial stresses have intensified in major foreign economies as well, with many also experiencing a drying up of liquidity in financial markets, sharp increases in the cost of short-term credit, and steep declines in equity prices.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The net result of the erosion of confidence, declines in asset prices, and freezing up of many financial markets has been a marked deterioration in the outlook for economic growth both here and abroad.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Already, the latest readings on the U.S. economy have become more downbeat.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In the labor market, private payroll employment fell 170,000 in September, a faster pace of decline than had been evident in preceding months, and the Institute for Supply Management survey of conditions in the manufacturing sector turned down sharply.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, motor vehicle sales fell to a 12-1/2 million unit pace in September, and today's report on retail sales indicated that purchases of other goods also dropped sharply last month.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Meanwhile, pressures in financial markets have undoubtedly further restricted the availability of credit to households and businesses.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, many of our contacts for the Beige Book, which was published today, highlighted tight and tightening credit conditions, and, in increasing numbers, indicated that a lack of credit availability is negatively affecting their customers' ability to spend or impairing their own ability to maintain the normal working capital they need to manage their day-to-day operations.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To combat the increased stresses in financial markets and their effects on the economy, the U.S. authorities, as well as those of many foreign governments, have taken a number of forceful and innovative steps in recent weeks.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Of greatest consequence was the passage of the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act (EESA) with its authority for the government to use up to $700 billion to support financial markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Importantly, the U.S. Treasury has indicated that a significant share of this authority will be used to inject capital into financial institutions.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As the turmoil has persisted and deepened, it has become increasingly clear that the fear and uncertainty gripping markets stems from questions about the exposure of many financial intermediaries to losses on mortgages and other loans.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Banks and other lenders need greater capital cushions to reassure their counterparties that they will be able to meet their obligations, and they need it soon.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The capital purchase plan announced by the Treasury yesterday is a start on building capital and confidence, and, by strengthening lenders, should make it easier for them to access the private capital they also require.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the troubled asset purchase program should help by counteracting the effect of forced sales and impaired market liquidity on asset prices.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Although capital is the bedrock of confidence, it probably will take some time for enough to be raised to completely reassure those who extend funds to many intermediaries.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In the meantime, the inability of lenders to fund themselves beyond the very near term creates vulnerability in the financial system and impedes their capacity to make loans to households and businesses to finance the purchases of cars, houses, and business capital.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To bridge the gap to stronger capital, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) is offering banks and their holding companies an opportunity to issue guaranteed obligations for the next nine months.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This guarantee covers the obligations most likely to be withdrawn when confidence erodes, but it is also structured to encourage banks to lengthen the maturity of their borrowing to provide stability, rebuild confidence, and stimulate lending.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The FDIC program will operate alongside the earlier Treasury guarantee of money market fund balances designed to stabilize investments in those accounts and hence reduce the need for these funds to liquidate assets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: For its part, the Federal Reserve has greatly expanded its provision of liquidity to banks here and abroad and to other borrowers.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: We could do so in part because the EESA accelerated the authority for the Federal Reserve to pay interest on reserves.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: With that power, we can expand our lending and still maintain the federal funds rate target established by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Under normal circumstances, we face no tension between supplying liquidity and achieving our interest rate objective, because we supply a relatively small amount of funds to the private sector through our open market operations with primary dealers and discount window lending to banks.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Over the past 15 months, however, as lenders have become increasingly reluctant to lend to each other, the Federal Reserve has had to take on a much greater role in the financial system to carry out its public policy responsibilities to provide a backstop source of liquidity.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At first, we did this by expanding the amount and lengthening the maturity of our lending to banks at the discount window and through our traditional open market operations with dealers.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Then, we found that we needed to supply credit against a greater variety of collateral to primary dealers so we opened the discount window to them and expanded our securities lending facilities.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: And just within the past few weeks we determined that, with normal intermediation increasingly disrupted, economic and financial stability required us to lend to firms that issued commercial paper.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, we have greatly expanded our dollar swaps with foreign central banks to help them meet the dollar funding needs of their domestic banks--needs that have been adding to pressures on our markets here at home.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: By opening and expanding these facilities, we are trying to assure banks, dealers, and commercial paper issuers that they can extend credit without worrying about whether they will be able to borrow to fund those loans.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: We are also trying to assure those who lend to these firms that the borrowers will have a source of funding to pay them back.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Clearly, the willingness of the Federal Reserve to lend substantial amounts to more counterparties over longer periods has not, by itself, been sufficient to unlock private credit flows; but Federal Reserve credit has been a critical ingredient in the mix of policy tools.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As I noted earlier, the troubles in the financial markets have spilled over to the economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, fear of economic weakness and the associated deterioration in credit quality contributed to the adverse dynamics in credit markets.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To counter this dynamic and adjust its policy to the evolving economic outlook, the FOMC reduced the target federal funds rate 50 basis points last week.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, the effects of the easier stance of policy on the cost and availability of credit were overwhelmed last week by the further erosion in confidence.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: But, over time, lower rates will help to support asset prices and reduce the cost of capital to encourage spending, economic expansion, and job creation.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Importantly, this easing action was taken alongside similar actions by many other central banks.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Financial markets are connected around the world by the free flow of capital, and the freezing up of credit has occurred, to one degree or another, in many foreign economies as well as our own.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In these circumstances, measures to address financial market problems within each country are likely to be more effective if other countries are also taking similar steps, as they are doing not only in monetary policy but also in their efforts to recapitalize banks, guarantee bank obligations, and shore up the confidence of lenders.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: I am optimistic that this multipronged approach is laying the groundwork for a return to more normal functioning in financial markets and a restoration of vigorous economic growth.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The initial reaction has been positive, but it will take some time before we know to what extent the current stresses in the financial sector are being resolved.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Over time, financial firms will need to bolster profits to offset losses and attract capital, to delever by reducing debt relative to equity, and in many cases to consolidate through mergers and acquisitions.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: All of this points to a prolonged period of cautious lending and a high cost of capital relative to benchmark interest rates like the federal funds rate, even as market functioning improves.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Similarly, although the adjustment in housing markets is well under way, it likely still has further to go.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: House prices will probably continue to fall for a while, and inventories of unsold homes, while decreasing, will remain elevated.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At some point, however, house prices will begin to stabilize, demand will be bolstered by the lower level of prices and low interest rates, and inventories will come into better alignment with sales.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: To be sure, any rebound in housing activity will likely be modest, but even a stabilization in housing markets will remove what has been a significant drag on the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Given the likely drawn-out nature of the prospective adjustments in housing and financial markets, I see the most probable scenario as one in which the performance of the economy remains subpar well into next year and then gradually improves in late 2009 and 2010.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As credit restraint abates, the low level of policy interest rates will begin to show through into more accommodative financial conditions.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: This improvement in financial conditions, together with the gradual stabilization of housing markets and the stimulative effects of lower oil and commodity prices, should lead to a pickup in jobs and income, contributing to a broad recovery in the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: At the same time, inflation seems likely to move onto a downward track.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: If sustained, the recent declines in commodity prices should soon lead to a sharp reduction in headline inflation.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, I expect core inflation to slow from current levels as lower commodity prices and greater economic slack moderate upward pressures on costs.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Similar reductions in inflation abroad, as well as the recent appreciation of the dollar, should restrain increases in the prices of imported goods.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: I would caution, however, that the uncertainty around my forecast is substantial.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The path of the economy will depend critically on how quickly the current stresses in financial markets abate.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: But these events have few if any precedents, and thus we can have even less confidence than usual in our economic forecasts.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: Here's what I do know: The authorities around the world have brought to bear on this situation an array of actions that are unprecedented in scope and force; these actions show every promise of being successful in restoring confidence in lending institutions and freeing the flow of credit to households and businesses; and governments in the United States and elsewhere have shown themselves able to work across political parties and across international boundaries to craft new approaches to problems.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: As Chairman Bernanke has often remarked, at the Federal Reserve we will utilize all the tools at our disposal to meet our responsibilities for fostering high employment and stable prices.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: I also know that the U.S. economy has proven itself over the years to be flexible and resilient as well as innovative and productive, qualities which enable it to rebound from serious economic shocks.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: I am confident that we will emerge from this episode with a stronger and more robust financial system and with a restoration of solid and sustainable economic growth.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: The views expressed are my own and do not necessarily represent the views of other members of the Board or the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kohn
text: William Wascher, of the Boardâs staff, contributed to these remarks.
speech_title: Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Georgetown University Wall Street Alliance, New York, New York

speaker: Kroszner
text: Governor Kroszner presented identical remarks to the National Conference on the Securities Industry, New York, New York, on October 30, 2008
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is not an overstatement to say that we are in the midst of a fundamental transformation in financial services, with market-wide ramifications.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the heart of that transformation lies a much more intense emphasis on funding and liquidity.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Additionally, we are all witnessing the extent to which banking and financial markets are interconnected.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The current environment certainly presents some fundamental challenges for banking institutions of all types and sizes.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: 1 Their boards of directors and senior management, who bear the responsibility to set strategy and develop and maintain risk management practices, must not only address current difficulties, but must also establish a framework for the inevitable uncertainty that lies ahead.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Notably, the ongoing fundamental transformation in financial services offers great potential opportunities for those institutions able to integrate strategy and risk management successfully, and I will argue that survival will hinge upon such an integration in what I will call a "strategic risk management framework."
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the remainder of my remarks, I plan to discuss the necessity for institutions to improve the linkage between overall corporate strategy and risk management, and how they can develop concrete strategic risk management frameworks.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: I will argue that in the highly interconnected financial world, funding and liquidity need to be at the center of such frameworks.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: But before doing so, I will briefly review recent events.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recent Events in Financial Markets We are indeed witnessing dramatic shifts in the structure of financial markets.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: These are quite extraordinary times that have required extraordinary responses from the Federal Reserve, the Treasury, and other governmental bodies in the United States and around the world.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Since last summer, there had been a continuous deterioration of conditions in financial markets, becoming much more acute since March of this year.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For instance, we have seen significant disruption in several key sectors of our financial system, such as normally creditworthy companies having difficulty issuing commercial paper, dramatic increases in interbank lending rates, and significant concerns about money market funds "breaking the buck."
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: These are sectors usually considered to be relatively low risk and quite liquid, so disruptions here have signaled the extent and depth of this turmoil and the lack of confidence among financial market participants.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve has responded to these developments in two broad ways.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, following classic tenets of central banking, the Federal Reserve has provided large amounts of liquidity to the financial system to cushion the effects of tight conditions in short-term funding markets.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, to reduce the downside risks to growth emanating from the tightening of credit, the Fed, in a series of moves that began last September, has significantly lowered its target for the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, earlier this month, in an unprecedented joint action with five other major central banks and in response to the adverse implications of the deepening crisis for the economic outlook, the Federal Reserve again eased the stance of monetary policy.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: We will continue to use all the tools at our disposal to improve market functioning and liquidity, to reduce pressures in key credit and funding markets, and to complement the steps the Treasury and foreign governments will be taking to strengthen the financial system.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a result of these ongoing upheavals, we are witnessing substantial institutional changes, in which some long-standing financial institutions have either failed, sought government assistance, or were forced to merge with other institutions.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: What were the major U.S. investment banks have essentially disappeared, such as by merging with bank holding companies or becoming bank holding companies themselves.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Other major banks and thrifts have been absorbed into other banking organizations.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Financial institutions and investors have placed much more emphasis on the banking charter, likely driven by banks' more stable funding and deposit insurance, even before the recently announced government support of the banking system.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Over the past year, there has been increasing concern among financial institutions and other counterparties about the health of some financial institutions.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Uncertainty about the value of assets and other exposures, as well as uncertainty about the ability of institutions to sustain continued access to funding, has caused financial institutions to operate with great caution and hoard funds.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: What was once a healthy, active interbank market has become frozen from time to time, as some institutions feel that conditions are so uncertain that they cannot even lend to long-standing clients or counterparties.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In quite a dramatic shift from just 18 months ago, there is much more scrutiny being placed on capital adequacy, with financial institutions trying to retain as much capital as they can, raise as much as possible, and demonstrate that their capital positions are not impaired.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Capital Purchase Plan by the U.S. Treasury Department under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act is focused on improving capital adequacy and, hence, improving confidence in the interbank market.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Perhaps one of the most pressing issues, as I mentioned briefly earlier, is the intense emphasis on funding.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This dramatic shift in concerns about a financial institution's funding base results in much more focus on the stability of funding sources--one of the reasons that the bank charter has become so attractive.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, we are seeing the emphasis on funding driving many other factors that affect financial institutions, including the viability of various aspects of firms' business models.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: And problems with liquidity have affected capital levels, which in turn have further exacerbated liquidity concerns.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is indeed quite remarkable how this "flight to liquidity" has brought about so many institutional and structural changes, and become essentially the most important factor (at least now) for the viability of a financial institution.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Over the past year there have been a number of studies analyzing the causes of the current turmoil, which include shortcomings in the risk management practices of financial institutions.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 It is absolutely clear that many financial institutions need to undertake a fundamental review of risk management.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: They now realize that ignoring risk management in any aspect of the banking business usually creates problems later on.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Risk management shortcomings need to be addressed not only to improve the health and viability of individual institutions, but also to maintain stability for the financial system as a whole.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Framework for Strategic Risk Management At this time, I would like to explain a bit more about what I mean by a "strategic risk management framework."
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In my view, an effective overall corporate strategy combines a set of activities a firm plans to undertake with an adequate assessment of the risks included in those activities.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Unfortunately, many firms have forgotten the second part of that definition.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, there can be no real strategic management in financial services without risk management, hence my use of the term "strategic risk management."
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Risk management needs to be interwoven into all aspects of the firm's business and should be part of the calculus for all decision-making.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Strategic decisions about what activities to undertake should not be made unless senior management understands the risks involved; assessing potential returns without fully assessing the corresponding risks to the organization is incomplete, and potentially hazardous, strategic analysis.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ensuring that risk management permeates an entire organization may require some fundamental changes for certain firms.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: And this lesson applies not just to the prominent organizations mentioned in the headlines of late, but also to smaller firms.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Even if smaller firms have been less affected by the recent turmoil (and perhaps have even won back some market share as customers seek more "traditional" places to put their money), their managements must understand that the financial landscape has changed and needs to be surveyed anew because events outside of their control in market-wide flight to liquidity, for example, can have direct impacts on them.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of vital importance will be incorporating into strategic risk management the lesson that funding and liquidity will be a major determinant of institutions' success going forward.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Building a rigorous strategic risk management framework requires an institution to reexamine both its internal practices and its external environment, and to understand how closely the two are connected.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, external factors have an impact on internal practices, but those internal practices, because financial markets are so interconnected, can in turn have an impact on how the institution is viewed externally--and even have an impact on the marketplace more broadly.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have witnessed several such examples of late, in which an institution encountered severe liquidity needs, which then affected funding for other institutions.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Institutions need to understand better that a number of factors affecting their business are beyond their control, and that events can have secondary or tertiary "knock-on" effects.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The real art is to realize that while all institutions may be affected by external factors, each is affected in its own way.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Now that I have laid out a general framework for strategic risk management, I would like to offer a few examples of its application.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Funding and liquidity As I noted, the clear driver of the fundamental transformation in financial services is the increased importance of funding and liquidity.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The ability to secure funding is a fundamental task in banking, and banks have been managing expected liquidity demands since the beginning of banking itself.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In times of stress, such as now, having a solid and reliable funding structure becomes much more important, in some cases so much so that it affects most other banking activities.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The current turmoil has brought about substantial deleveraging in financial services.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Managing this process is an immediate challenge for banking institutions, as they must consider the need to reduce leverage at their own institution as well as understand the consequences of deleveraging at other firms.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This is clearly an example of external factors affecting internal practices, and vice versa.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: From a strategic perspective, bank directors must examine their current and future funding situation in light of recent deleveraging, its near-term prospects, and the state of overall liquidity in financial markets.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Financial institutions rely on external funding in some fashion--either through retail deposits, interbank lending, or debt offerings.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Therefore, they must understand that their funding can be subject to the vagaries of the market, such as sudden shortages of market liquidity or rapid swings in investor sentiment.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, banks may benefit in the near term in attracting deposits and thereby improve their funding positions, but they also may experience more difficulty securing other sources of funds and find that situation persisting for some time.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Additionally, counterparty reactions to changes in the business mix or risk profile of an institution (or even the perceived change in its risk profile) could suddenly hamper the ability to find funding.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In recognizing the inherent leverage in the business of banking, institutions must examine longer-term implications of funding and liquidity, and begin to build those into the overall strategic plan for their organizations.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The market for external funding is an international one, so liquidity troubles in one market can have repercussions in others.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accordingly, banks should be prepared for a range of adverse situations related to funding and market liquidity that can be precipitated by a range of sources.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Bank directors and senior management need to anticipate potential difficulties in funding the bank, and demand that solid contingency plans are in place--and are regularly updated--for a variety of funding and liquidity problems.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such plans should include the potential for external factors to generate a funding squeeze for the institution, even if its own positions and risk profile have not materially changed.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Preparing for sudden changes in the pricing and availability at any price of funding sources is something that, leading up to the current turmoil, most banks did not fully consider.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Instead, their managements focused mostly on building market share, growing revenues, and realizing the short-term profitability of their activities--a telling example of banks not properly including risk management in their overall corporate strategy.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As the Senior Supervisors Group Survey of major financial institutions pointed out, there have been numerous examples of failures of strategic risk management and these must be rectified going forward.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Finally, strategic risk management for funding and liquidity needs to consider potential liquidity problems on both sides of the balance sheet.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: We saw such examples recently when there were draws on liquidity commitments to structured investment vehicles and commercial paper conduits, and when banks faced difficulty selling exposures in illiquid markets.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: When there is a marketwide scramble for liquidity, a bank must be prepared to manage funding challenges and unplanned asset expansions simultaneously.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Developing a strong strategic risk management framework that recognizes the vital importance of funding and liquidity to both sides of the balance sheet is one way in which directors and senior management can help ensure that their institutions are ready for such outcomes.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: They should also ensure that they fully understand that funding and liquidity issues will drive many of the activities in which they will be able to engage, something to which I will now turn.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Choice of financial services activities While the financial landscape is by no means settled, certain emerging trends will affect which activities make sense, which exposures should be assumed, and which risks should be undertaken.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: One immediate trend is that much of the future of business activities of banking organizations will be driven by the increased focus on funding and liquidity.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Accordingly, this trend must be integrated into a strategic risk management framework.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For instance, there may be less opportunity to pursue activities that were quite prolific under the previous "originate-to-distribute" model, such as securitizations, given current disruptions or longer-term uncertainties about the reliability of market liquidity.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For similar reasons, other activities, such as investing in collateralized debt obligations or structured investment vehicles--which typically relied on relatively easy maturity transformation--may not be as viable in this new environment.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Whether transactions take place on an organized exchange or in the so-called over the counter market is another important aspect of the strategic risk management choices undertaken by an organization.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: When contracts are traded on an exchange, clearing and settlement, for example, may have less uncertainty associated with them.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, an exchange that has a centralized counterparty--perhaps the clearinghouse of the exchange--can reduce uncertainty about counterparty risk and help to avoid market dislocations that can arise from such uncertainty, not only for an individual firm but, potentially, more broadly in that market.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, market infrastructure and its impact on how organizations are connected to each other can have a large impact on market confidence in times of stress.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, we have seen that uncertainty, fear, and lack of trust among key counterparties can dramatically affect trading in some products across markets in many countries, again an example of the impact of interconnectedness.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: These days, institutions are seeking more assurance that their counterparties will not default from one day to the next.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Whether there is a shift to more trading on clearinghouses will be driven by firms' analysis of counterparty credit risk and the extent to which they are comfortable doing business with leveraged counterparties about which they have limited information.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Firm managers should take these infrastructure and interconnectedness issues into account in undertaking their own strategic risk management choice about what activities to undertake and the risks posed by each.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This is a clear example of how external structures should be taken into account in a firm's strategic planning.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In their strategic risk management frameworks, institutions should also understand the broader issue of potential gravitation to a model in which most or all types of financial services are brought together in single institutions.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is, institutions have to prepare for the possibility that they could lose customers and/or be less competitive if they are unable to provide the full set of financial products.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Importantly, however, bank directors and senior management, in assembling their strategic risk management framework, should fully understand the complications associated with offering multiple products and engaging in a wide array of activities--such as reputational risk.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: And they should not automatically assume that engaging in multiple activities in multiple geographic markets will provide so-called "natural diversification."
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As I just noted, different financial markets and different types of financial services are quite interconnected, and during times of stress all can experience losses concurrently.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, there may also be an opportunity for some institutions to benefit from more traditional, "bread-and-butter banking," with exposures and risks tied more closely to bank balance sheets.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This potential opportunity for niche banking could have certain benefits, as clients and investors, because of the fear of contagion, seek institutions that are specifically not involved in multiple markets and activities.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: And local banks can often provide more personalized service and have a better understanding of their clients' needs.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In such cases, however, institutions conducting specialized or local business must understand the inherent risks, such as potential risk concentrations.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Compensation As many of you know, as an economist I am particularly interested in the impact that compensation has on incentives for bank management.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
text: 3 I am pleased that the industry has also begun to address this issue, as reflected in a recent report by the Institute of International Finance.
speech_title: Strategic Risk Management in an Interconnected World
speech_venue: At the Risk Management Association Annual Risk Management Conference, Baltimore, Maryland

speaker: Kroszner
