speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The resulting legislation, the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act (EESA), provides the necessary authorizations and resources to strengthen the financial system and, in particular, to deal with the potential failure of a systemically important firm.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, funds provided under the act facilitated the recent government actions to stabilize Citigroup.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: More broadly, the act allows the Treasury to recapitalize and stabilize our banking system by purchasing preferred stock in financial institutions.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Capital Purchase Program is voluntary and designed to encourage participation by a broad range of institutions while maintaining the ability of participating institutions to raise private capital.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Up to $250 billion has been committed to this program.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition to measures being implemented by the Treasury, the FDIC has announced programs to guarantee selected liabilities of FDIC-insured depository institutions and their holding companies.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: With time, these measures should help strengthen the banking system, allowing credit to flow more freely to support economic growth.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Collectively, the Treasury, the FDIC, and the Federal Reserve are now much better equipped to address potential systemic risks quickly and effectively, and we are firmly committed to doing so.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, measures such as the Capital Purchase Program and the FDIC guarantee are temporary.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the longer term, the development of a statutory framework for resolving systemically critical nonbank financial institutions in ways that do not destabilize the financial system as a whole must be another key priority.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic Outlook Despite the efforts of the Federal Reserve and other policymakers, the U.S. economy remains under considerable stress.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Economic activity was weakening even before the intensification of the financial crisis this fall.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The sharp falloff in consumer spending during the summer was particularly striking.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: According to the latest estimates, real gross domestic product (GDP) declined at an annual rate of 0.5 percent in the third quarter, with personal consumption falling at an annual rate of 3.7 percent.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, economic activity appears to have downshifted further in the wake of the deterioration in financial conditions in September.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Employment losses, which had been averaging about 100,000 per month for much of the year, accelerated to more than 250,000 per month, on average, in September and October, and the unemployment rate jumped to 6.5 percent in October.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, recent increases in the number of new claims for unemployment insurance suggest that labor market conditions worsened further in November.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Housing markets remain weak, with low demand and the increased number of distressed properties on the market contributing to further declines in house prices and ongoing reductions in new construction.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In reaction to worse economic prospects and tightening credit conditions, households have continued to retrench, putting consumer spending on a pace to post another sharp decline in the fourth quarter.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, sales of light motor vehicles fell to an annual rate of 10-1/2 million units in October, the lowest level since 1983, and November sales reports are downbeat.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Business activity also slowed in recent months.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Excluding the effects of the hurricanes and the Boeing strike on production, manufacturing output fell 2 percent over the months of September and October, orders and shipments of nondefense capital goods fell markedly in October, and most survey measures of business conditions are at or close to record lows.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Amid the bad news, there have been some positives.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The pronounced declines in the prices for crude oil and other commodities have helped to reverse what had been a significant drag on household purchasing power through much of the year.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: And there have been a few tentative signs of stabilization in financial markets.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: For instance, short-term funding costs for banks and commercial paper issuers have come down recently, and issuance of investment-grade bonds by nonfinancial corporations appears to have held up well.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Banks have recently issued bonds backed by the FDIC guarantee.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: That said, investor concerns about credit quality have increased further, and risk aversion remains intense.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result, in almost all credit markets, spreads remain wider, maturities shorter, and availability more constrained than was the case before the intensification of the crisis this fall.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The likely duration of the financial turmoil is difficult to judge, and thus the uncertainty surrounding the economic outlook is unusually large.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: But even if the functioning of financial markets continues to improve, economic conditions will probably remain weak for a time.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, household spending likely will continue to be depressed by the declines to date in household wealth, cumulating job losses, weak consumer confidence, and a lack of credit availability.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The global economy has also slowed.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Many industrial countries were affected by the financial crisis from the beginning, but the latest economic data point to a more noticeable weakening of conditions.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: And emerging market economies, which were little affected at first, are slowing now as well.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: One implication of these developments is that exports are not likely to be as great a source of strength for U.S. economic activity in coming quarters as they had been earlier this year.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the same time, the increase in economic slack and the declines in commodity prices and import prices have alleviated upward pressures on consumer prices.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, inflation expectations appear to have eased slightly.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: These developments should bring inflation down to levels consistent with price stability.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although the near-term outlook for the economy is weak, a number of factors are likely over time to promote the return of solid gains in economic activity and employment in the context of low and stable inflation.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Among those factors are the stimulus provided by monetary policy and possible fiscal actions, the eventual stabilization in housing markets as the correction runs its course, and the underlying strengths and recuperative powers of our economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The time needed for economic recovery, however, will depend greatly on the pace at which financial and credit markets return to more-normal functioning.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Outlook for Policy Going forward, our nation's economic policy must vigorously address the substantial risks to financial stability and economic growth that we face.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will conclude my remarks by discussing the policy options of the Federal Reserve, focusing on the three aspects of policy that I laid out earlier: interest rate policy, liquidity policy, and policies to stabilize the financial system.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Regarding interest rate policy, although further reductions from the current federal funds rate target of 1 percent are certainly feasible, at this point the scope for using conventional interest rate policies to support the economy is obviously limited.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, the actual federal funds rate has been trading consistently below the Committee's 1 percent target in recent weeks, reflecting the large quantity of reserves that our lending activities have put into the system.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In principle, our ability to pay interest on excess reserves at a rate equal to the funds rate target, as we have been doing, should keep the actual rate near the target, because banks should have no incentive to lend overnight funds at a rate lower than what they can receive from the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In practice, however, several factors have served to depress the market rate below the target.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: One such factor is the presence in the market of large suppliers of funds, notably the government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs) Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which are not eligible to receive interest on reserves and are thus willing to lend overnight federal funds at rates below the target.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 We will continue to explore ways to keep the effective federal funds rate closer to the target.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although conventional interest rate policy is constrained by the fact that nominal interest rates cannot fall below zero, the second arrow in the Federal Reserve's quiver--the provision of liquidity--remains effective.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, there are several means by which the Fed could influence financial conditions through the use of its balance sheet, beyond expanding our lending to financial institutions.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, the Fed could purchase longer-term Treasury or agency securities on the open market in substantial quantities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: This approach might influence the yields on these securities, thus helping to spur aggregate demand.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, last week the Fed announced plans to purchase up to $100 billion in GSE debt and up to $500 billion in GSE mortgage-backed securities over the next few quarters.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: It is encouraging that the announcement of that action was met by a fall in mortgage interest rates.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, the Federal Reserve can provide backstop liquidity not only to financial institutions but also directly to certain financial markets, as we have recently done for the commercial paper market.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Such programs are promising because they sidestep banks and primary dealers to provide liquidity directly to borrowers or investors in key credit markets.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this spirit, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury jointly announced last week a facility that will lend against asset-backed securities collateralized by student loans, auto loans, credit card loans, and loans guaranteed by the Small Business Administration.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's credit risk exposure in this facility will be minimized because the collateral will be subject to a "haircut" and because the Treasury is providing $20 billion of EESA capital as supplementary loss protection.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Each of these approaches has the potential to improve the functioning of financial markets and to stimulate the economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Expanding the provision of liquidity leads also to further expansion of the balance sheet of the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: To avoid inflation in the long run and to allow short-term interest rates ultimately to return to normal levels, the Fed's balance sheet will eventually have to be brought back to a more sustainable level.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The FOMC will ensure that that is done in a timely way.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, that is an issue for the future; for now, the goal of policy must be to support financial markets and the economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Finally, working together with the Treasury, the FDIC, and other agencies, we must take all steps necessary to minimize systemic risk.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: The capital injections into the banking system under the EESA, the FDIC's guarantee program, and the provision of liquidity by the Federal Reserve have already served to greatly reduce the risk that a systemically important financial institution will fail.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: We at the Federal Reserve and our colleagues at other federal agencies will carefully monitor the conditions of all key financial institutions and stand ready to act as needed to preserve their viability in this difficult financial environment.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: I have not discussed the international response to the crisis today, but policymakers abroad as well as those in the United States have taken a series of extraordinary steps to address an extraordinary situation.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: These steps include strong fiscal and monetary actions as well as measures to stabilize key financial institutions and markets and to strengthen the financial infrastructure.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: I am not suggesting the way forward will be easy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: But I believe that the policy responses taken here and by our international partners, together with the underlying vitality and resilience of the American economy, will help to restore confidence to our financial system and place our economy back on the path to vigorous growth.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: Banks have an incentive to borrow from the GSEs and then redeposit the funds at the Federal Reserve; as a result, banks earn a sure profit equal to the difference between the rate they pay the GSEs and the rate they receive on excess reserves.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, thus far, this type of arbitrage has not been occurring on a sufficient scale, perhaps because banks have not yet fully adjusted their reserve-management practices to take advantage of this opportunity.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
speech_venue: At the Greater Austin Chamber of Commerce, Austin, Texas

speaker: Kroszner
text: As you have heard, this report represents an extraordinary and comprehensive effort by staff in all 12 Reserve Banks and at the Board of Governors to explore the problem of concentrated poverty.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The 16 case studies in the report represent urban and rural areas, immigrant and Native American communities, as well as older "weak" market cities and newer "strong" market areas.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: By covering a wide variety of communities, the report adds depth and texture to the existing literature on poverty and offers important insights regarding the relationship between public services and private investment.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For those who may not be familiar with the Federal Reserve System's Community Affairs function, this report illustrates one of the many ways in which it supports the System's objectives for economic growth by promoting community development and fair and impartial access to credit.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The System's strength in research, together with its unique structure, makes it particularly well suited to pursue this kind of work.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Community Affairs program takes advantage of the 12 Federal Reserve Banks located in different regions of the country to gather information on local conditions and to conduct outreach and education efforts through regular contact with financial institutions and market intermediaries.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The System's network of Community Affairs staff works with lenders, community organizations, and local governments to identify trends and issues affecting low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This communication with both financial markets and communities allows the Federal Reserve to act as a bridge between the private and public sectors.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The System's reputation for high-quality research, outreach, and analysis and its regional presence made these 16 case studies and the comparative analysis possible.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This report makes an important contribution to the literature on the dynamics of poor people living in poor communities by recognizing the existence and persistence of concentrations of poverty beyond the urban areas where it has been well documented.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, the study confirms that poverty persists in places, such as rural and suburban communities, where it is not so easily seen.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The report also identifies the existing avenues for bringing poor people and communities into the economic mainstream.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This topic is at the center of today's discussions.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Federal Reserve, together with the other federal financial regulatory agencies, has had some experience in addressing the credit needs of underserved communities, using the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) as our guide.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: CRA encourages financial institutions not only to extend mortgage, small business, and other types of credit to lower-income neighborhoods and households, but also to provide investments and services to lower-income areas and people as part of an overall effort to build the capacity necessary for these places to thrive.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some critics of the CRA contend that by encouraging banking institutions to help meet the credit needs of lower-income borrowers and areas, the law pushed banking institutions to undertake high-risk mortgage lending.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We have not yet seen empirical evidence to support these claims, nor has it been our experience in implementing the law over the past 30 years that the CRA has contributed to the erosion of safe and sound lending practices.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the remainder of my remarks, I will discuss some of our experiences with the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I will also discuss the findings of a recent analysis of mortgage-related data by Federal Reserve staff that runs counter to the charge that the CRA was at the root of, or otherwise contributed in any substantive way, to the current subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Regulatory Efforts to Meet Credit Needs in Underserved Markets In the 1970s, when banking was still a local enterprise, the Congress enacted the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The act required the banking regulators to encourage insured depository institutions--that is, commercial banks and thrifts--to help meet the credit needs of their entire community, including low- and moderate-income areas.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The CRA does not stipulate minimum targets or goals for lending, investments, or services.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Rather, the law provides incentives for financial institutions to help meet the credit needs of lower-income people and areas, consistent with safe and sound banking practices, and commensurately provides them favorable CRA consideration for those activities.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: By requiring regulators to make CRA performance ratings and evaluations public and to consider those ratings when reviewing applications for mergers, acquisitions, and branches, the Congress created an unusual set of incentives to promote interaction between lenders and community organizations.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Given the incentives of the CRA, bankers have pursued lines of business that had not been previously tapped by forming partnerships with community organizations and other stakeholders to identify and help meet the credit needs of underserved communities.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This experimentation in lending, often combined with financial education and counseling and consideration of nontraditional measures of creditworthiness, expanded the markets for safe lending in underserved communities and demonstrated its viability; as a result, these actions attracted competition from other financial services providers, many of whom were not covered by the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: There are many fine examples of community development lending and investment activities designed to address needs in the poorest of areas, including many of those highlighted by the case studies in this report.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: During trips to the regional Federal Reserve Banks and Branches, I have spent a lot of time visiting areas with high concentrations of poverty.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For many years, the Fed has promoted community banking services for the unbanked and underbanked population.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: It was gratifying for me to find that financial services were accessible in, for example, central Cleveland, thanks to the efforts of one local bank that offers check-cashing services at much lower rates than competing nonbank check cashers.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Similarly, in the Little Haiti neighborhood in Miami, another case-study community that I had the opportunity to visit last year, one banking institution has committed to serving the neighborhood's unbanked residents by hiring Creole-speaking staff to promote a prosperity campaign built around the Earned Income Tax Credit.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am sure that today's luncheon speaker, Tom Barrett, mayor of Milwaukee, could share similar observations about a local financial institution serving that case-study neighborhood by providing low-income residents complimentary electronic income tax filing combined with financial education seminars, innovative credit repair programs, and low-cost banking services.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These services benefit lower-income customers by providing a simple means of accessing Earned Income and Homestead Tax Credits and the services necessary to maximize the benefits of these programs.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition to providing financial services to lower-income people, banks also provide critical community development loans and investments to address affordable housing and economic development needs.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These activities are particularly effective because they leverage the resources available to communities from public subsidies and tax credit programs that are targeted to lower-income people.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In just the past two years, banks have reported making over $120 billion in community development loans nationwide.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 This figure does not capture the full extent of such lending, because smaller institutions are not required to report community development loans to their regulators.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Evidence on CRA and the Subprime Crisis Over the years, the Federal Reserve has prepared two reports for the Congress that provide information on the performance of lending to lower-income borrowers or neighborhoods--populations that are the focus of the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 3 These studies found that lending to lower-income individuals and communities has been nearly as profitable and performed similarly to other types of lending done by CRA-covered institutions.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, the long-term evidence shows that the CRA has not pushed banks into extending loans that perform out of line with their traditional businesses.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Rather, the law has encouraged banks to be aware of lending opportunities in all segments of their local communities as well as to learn how to undertake such lending in a safe and sound manner.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recently, Federal Reserve staff has undertaken more specific analysis focusing on the potential relationship between the CRA and the current subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This analysis was performed for the purpose of assessing claims that the CRA was a principal cause of the current mortgage market difficulties.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For this analysis, the staff examined lending activity covering the period that corresponds to the height of the subprime boom.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The research focused on two basic questions.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, we asked what share of originations for subprime loans is related to the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The potential role of the CRA in the subprime crisis could either be large or small, depending on the answer to this question.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We found that the loans that are the focus of the CRA represent a very small portion of the subprime lending market, casting considerable doubt on the potential contribution that the law could have made to the subprime mortgage crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, we asked how CRA-related subprime loans performed relative to other loans.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Once again, the potential role of the CRA could be large or small, depending on the answer to this question.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We found that delinquency rates were high in all neighborhood income groups, and that CRA-related subprime loans performed in a comparable manner to other subprime loans; as such, differences in performance between CRA-related subprime lending and other subprime lending cannot lie at the root of recent market turmoil.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In analyzing the available data, we focused on two distinct metrics: loan origination activity and loan performance.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: With respect to the first question concerning loan originations, we wanted to know which types of lending institutions made higher-priced loans, to whom those loans were made, and in what types of neighborhoods the loans were extended.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 5 This analysis allowed us to determine what fraction of subprime lending could be related to the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our analysis of the loan data found that about 60 percent of higher-priced loan originations went to middle- or higher-income borrowers or neighborhoods.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such borrowers are not the populations targeted by the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, more than 20 percent of the higher-priced loans were extended to lower-income borrowers or borrowers in lower-income areas by independent nonbank institutions--that is, institutions not covered by the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Putting together these facts provides a striking result: Only 6 percent of all the higher-priced loans were extended by CRA-covered lenders to lower-income borrowers or neighborhoods in their CRA assessment areas, the local geographies that are the primary focus for CRA evaluation purposes.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This result undermines the assertion by critics of the potential for a substantial role for the CRA in the subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, the very small share of all higher-priced loan originations that can reasonably be attributed to the CRA makes it hard to imagine how this law could have contributed in any meaningful way to the current subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, loan originations are only one path that banking institutions can follow to meet their CRA obligations.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: They can also purchase loans from lenders not covered by the CRA, and in this way encourage more of this type of lending.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The data also suggest that these types of transactions have not been a significant factor in the current crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Specifically, less than 2 percent of the higher-priced and CRA-credit-eligible mortgage originations sold by independent mortgage companies were purchased by CRA-covered institutions.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I now want to turn to the second question concerning how CRA-related subprime lending performed relative to other types of lending.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: To address this issue, we looked at data on subprime and alt-A mortgage delinquencies in lower-income neighborhoods and compared them with those in middle- and higher-income neighborhoods to see how CRA-related loans performed.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 7 An overall comparison revealed that the rates for all subprime and alt-A loans delinquent 90 days or more is high regardless of neighborhood income.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 8 This result casts further doubt on the view that the CRA could have contributed in any meaningful way to the current subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Unfortunately, the available data on loan performance do not let us distinguish which specific loans in lower-income areas were related to the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As noted earlier, institutions not covered by the CRA extended many loans to borrowers in lower-income areas.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Also, some lower-income lending by institutions subject to the law was outside their local communities and unlikely to have been motivated by the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: To learn more about the relative performance of CRA-related lending, we conducted more-detailed analyses to try to focus on performance differences that might truly arise as a consequence of the rule as opposed to other factors.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Attempting to adjust for other relevant factors is challenging but worthwhile to try to assess the performance of CRA-related lending.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In one such analysis, we compared loan delinquency rates in neighborhoods that are right above and right below the CRA neighborhood income eligibility threshold.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, we compared loan performance by borrowers in two groups of neighborhoods that should not be very different except for the fact that the lending in one group received special attention under the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: When we conducted this analysis, we found essentially no difference in the performance of subprime loans in Zip codes that were just below or just above the income threshold for the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 9 The results of this analysis are not consistent with the contention that the CRA is at the root of the subprime crisis, because delinquency rates for subprime and alt-A loans in neighborhoods just below the CRA-eligibility threshold are very similar to delinquency rates on loans just above the threshold, hence not the subject of CRA lending.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: To gain further insight into the potential relationship between the CRA and the subprime crisis, we also compared the recent performance of subprime loans with mortgages originated and held in portfolio under the affordable lending programs operated by NeighborWorks America (NWA).
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a member of the board of directors of the NWA, I am quite familiar with its lending activities.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The NWA has partnered with many CRA-covered banking institutions to originate and hold mortgages made predominantly to lower-income borrowers and neighborhoods.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: So, to the extent that such loans are representative of CRA-lending programs in general, the performance of these loans is helpful in understanding the relationship between the CRA and the subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We found that loans originated under the NWA program had a lower delinquency rate than subprime loans.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 10 Furthermore, the loans in the NWA affordable lending portfolio had a lower rate of foreclosure than prime loans.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The result that the loans in the NWA portfolio performed better than subprime loans again casts doubt on the contention that the CRA has been a significant contributor to the subprime crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The final analysis we undertook to investigate the likely effects of the CRA on the subprime crisis was to examine foreclosure activity across neighborhoods grouped by income.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: We found that most foreclosure filings have taken place in middle- or higher-income neighborhoods; in fact, foreclosure filings have increased at a faster pace in middle- or higher-income areas than in lower-income areas that are the focus of the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Two key points emerge from all of our analysis of the available data.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, only a small portion of subprime mortgage originations are related to the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, CRA- related loans appear to perform comparably to other types of subprime loans.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Taken together, as I stated earlier, we believe that the available evidence runs counter to the contention that the CRA contributed in any substantive way to the current mortgage crisis.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Conclusions Our findings are important because neighborhoods and communities affected by the economic downturn will require the active participation of financial institutions.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Considering the situation today, many neighborhoods that are not currently the focus of the CRA are also experiencing great difficulties.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Our recent review of foreclosure data suggested that many middle-income areas currently have elevated rates of foreclosure filings and could face the prospect of falling into low-to-moderate income status.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In fact, 13 percent of the middle-income Zip codes have had foreclosure-rate filings that are above the overall rate for lower-income areas.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Helping to stabilize such areas not only benefits families in these areas but also provides spillover benefits to adjacent lower-income areas that are the traditional target of the CRA.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recognizing this, the Congress recently underscored the need for states and localities to undertake a comprehensive approach to stabilizing neighborhoods hard-hit by foreclosures through the enactment of the new Neighborhood Stabilization Program (NSP).
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The NSP permits targeting of federal funds to benefit families up to 120 percent of area median income in those areas experiencing rising foreclosures and falling home values.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In conclusion, I believe the CRA is an important model for designing incentives that motivate private-sector involvement to help meet community needs.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The CRA has, in fact, been helpful in alleviating the financial isolation of many areas of concentrated poverty, but as our report illustrates, there is much more that could be done in these communities.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Contrary to the assertions of critics, the evidence does not support the view that the CRA contributed in any substantial way to the crisis in the subprime mortgage market.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Today's discussion is an important first step in the process of identifying other initiatives and areas of cooperation between government and the private sector that will effectively address the continuing challenge of poverty in the United States.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

text: Such lending is not the focus of the CRA and is frequently not considered in CRA performance evaluations.

speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For the analysis, Zip code delinquency data were classified by relative income in two different ways.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, the data were classified using information published by the U. S. Census Bureau on income at the Zip Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA) level of geography.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Because the ZCTA data provide an income estimate for each Zip code, delinquency rates can be calculated directly from the LP data based on the Zip code location of the properties securing the loans.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, delinquency rates for each relative income group (lower, middle, and higher) were calculated as the weighted sum of delinquencies divided by the weighted sum of mortgages, where the weights equal each Zip code's share of the population in census tracts of the particular relative income group.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Relative income is based on the 2000 decennial census and is calculated as the median family income of the census tract divided by the median family income of its metropolitan statistical area or nonmetropolitan portion of the state.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Both approaches yield virtually identical results.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The analysis focused on loans originated from January 2006 through April 2008 with performance measured as of August 2008.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, a virtually identical relationship in loan performance across neighborhood income groups is found if the pool of loans evaluated is expanded to cover those originated in 2004 or 2005.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The only material difference is that the levels of delinquency are lower for the loans covering longer periods.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Loans that are 90 days or more delinquent include those that end in foreclosure or as real estate owned.Delinquency rates were somewhat higher in the lower-income areas.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: However, the somewhat higher delinquency rates in lower-income areas is not a surprising result because lower-income borrowers tend to be more sensitive to economic shocks given that, among other things, they have fewer financial resources on which to draw in emergencies.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

text: No information was available on the geographic distribution of the NeighborWorks America loans.
speech_title: The Community Reinvestment Act and the Recent Mortgage Crisis
speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The geographic pattern of lending can matter, as certain areas of the country are experiencing much more difficult conditions in their housing market than other areas.

speech_venue: At the Confronting Concentrated Poverty Policy Forum, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, D.C.
