speaker: Bernanke
text: The U.S. financial system has been in turmoil during the past 16 months.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Credit conditions have tightened and asset values have declined, contributing substantially, in turn, to the weakening of economic activity.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the participants in this conference are keenly aware, I am sure, housing and housing finance played a central role in precipitating the current crisis.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the crisis has persisted, however, the relationships between housing and other parts of the economy have become more complex.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Declining house prices, delinquencies and foreclosures, and strains in mortgage markets are now symptoms as well as causes of our general financial and economic difficulties.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These interlinkages imply that policies aimed at improving broad financial and economic conditions and policies focused specifically on housing may be mutually reinforcing.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, the most effective approach very likely will involve a full range of coordinated measures aimed at different aspects of the problem.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will begin this morning with some comments on developments in the housing sector and on the interactions among house prices, mortgage markets, foreclosures, and the broader economy.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will then discuss both some steps taken to date and some additional measures that might be taken to support housing and the economy by reducing the number of avoidable foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As we as a nation continue to fashion our policy responses in coming weeks and months, we must draw on the best thinking available.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I expect that the papers presented at this conference will add significantly to our understanding of these important issues.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Developments in Housing and Housing Finance As you know, the current housing crisis is the culmination of a large boom and bust in house prices and residential construction that began earlier in this decade.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Home sales and single-family housing starts held unusually steady through the 2001 recession and then rose dramatically over the subsequent four years.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: National indexes of home prices accelerated significantly over that period, with prices in some metropolitan areas more than doubling over the first half of the decade.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 One unfortunate consequence of the rapid increases in house prices was that providers of mortgage credit came to view their loans as well-secured by the rising values of their collateral and thus paid less attention to borrowers' ability to repay.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, no real or financial asset can provide an above-normal market return indefinitely, and houses are no exception.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: When home-price appreciation began to slow in many areas, the consequences of weak underwriting, such as little or no documentation and low required down payments, became apparent.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Delinquency rates for subprime mortgages--especially those with adjustable interest rates--began to climb steeply around the middle of 2006.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: When house prices were rising, higher-risk borrowers who were struggling to make their payments could refinance into more-affordable mortgages.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But refinancing became increasingly difficult as many of these households found that they had accumulated little, if any, housing equity.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, lenders tightened standards on higher-risk mortgages as secondary markets for those loans ceased to function.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Higher-risk mortgages are not the only part of the mortgage market to have experienced stress.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, while some lenders continue to originate so-called jumbo prime mortgages and hold them on their own balance sheets, these loans have generally been available only on more restrictive terms and at much higher spreads relative to prime conforming mortgage rates than before the crisis.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Mortgage rates in the prime conforming market--although down somewhat from their peaks--remain high relative to yields on longer-term Treasury securities, and lending terms have tightened for this segment as well.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As house prices have declined, many borrowers now find themselves "under water" on their mortgages--perhaps as many as 15 to 20 percent by some estimates.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, as the economy has slowed and unemployment has risen, more households are finding it difficult to make their mortgage payments.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: About 4-1/2 percent of all first-lien mortgages are now more than 90 days past due or in foreclosure, and one in ten near-prime mortgages in alt-A pools and more than one in five subprime mortgages are seriously delinquent.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 Lenders appear to be on track to initiate 2-1/4 million foreclosures in 2008, up from an average annual pace of less than 1 million during the pre-crisis period.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Predictably, home sales and construction have plummeted.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Sales of new homes and starts of single-family houses are now running at about one-third of their peak levels in the middle part of this decade.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Sales of existing homes, including foreclosure sales, are now about two-thirds of their earlier peak.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notwithstanding the sharp adjustment in construction, inventories of unsold new homes, though down in absolute terms, are close to their record high when measured relative to monthly sales, suggesting that residential construction is likely to remain soft in the near term.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As I mentioned earlier, the problems in housing and mortgage markets have become inextricably intertwined with broader financial and economic developments.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, mortgage-related losses have eroded the capital of many financial institutions, leading them to become more reluctant to make not only mortgage loans, but other types of loans to consumers and businesses as well.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Likewise, some homeowners have responded to declining home values by cutting back their spending, and residential construction remains subdued.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, weakness in the housing market has proved a serious drag on overall economic activity.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A slowing economy has in turn reduced the demand for houses, implying a further weakening of conditions in the mortgage and housing markets.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Reducing Preventable Foreclosures Because developments in the housing sector have become so interlinked with the evolution of the financial markets and the economy as a whole, both macro and micro policies have a role in addressing the strains in housing.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At the macro level, the Federal Reserve has taken a number of steps, beginning with the easing of monetary policy.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To the extent that more accommodative monetary policies make credit conditions easier and incomes higher than they otherwise would have been, they support the housing market.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has also implemented a series of actions aimed at restoring the normal functioning of financial markets and restarting the flow of credit, including providing liquidity to a range of financial institutions, working with the Treasury and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) to help stabilize the banking system, and providing backstop liquidity to the commercial paper market.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve supported the actions by the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) and the Treasury to put the housing-related government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs), Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, into conservatorship, thereby stabilizing a critical source of mortgage credit.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has also recently announced that it will purchase up to $100 billion of the debt issued by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and the Federal Home Loan Banks and up to $500 billion in mortgage-backed securities issued by the GSEs.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although broad-based macroeconomic policies help to create an economic and financial environment in which a housing recovery can occur, policies aimed more narrowly at the housing market are important, too.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the remainder of my remarks, I will focus on policy options for reducing preventable foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Foreclosures impose large costs on families who face the loss of their homes and reduced future access to credit.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the public policy case for reducing preventable foreclosures does not rely solely on the desire to help people who are in trouble.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Foreclosures create substantial social costs.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Communities suffer when foreclosures are clustered, adding further to the downward pressure on property values.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Lower property values in turn translate to lower tax revenues for local governments, and increases in the number of vacant homes can foster vandalism and crime.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 5 At the national level, the declines in house prices that result from the addition of foreclosed properties to the supply of homes for sale create broader economic and financial stress, as I have already noted.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the surface, private economic incentives to avoid foreclosure would appear to be strong for the lender as well as the borrower.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Foreclosure dissipates much of the value of the property:  Indeed, recent losses on defaulted subprime mortgages have averaged around 50 to 60 percent of the loan balance.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 7 Besides the general decline in property values and foregone payments, fees related to foreclosure, such as court costs, maintenance expenses, and others, can amount to 10 to 15 percent of the loan balance; furthermore, the discount in value due to foreclosure status can be an additional 5 to 15 percent.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, despite the substantial costs imposed by foreclosure, anecdotal evidence suggests that some foreclosures are continuing to occur even in cases in which the narrow economic interests of the lender would appear to be better served through modification of the mortgage.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This apparent market failure owes in part to the widespread practice of securitizing mortgages, which typically results in their being put into the hands of third-party servicers rather than those of a single owner or lender.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The rules under which servicers operate do not always provide them with clear guidance or the appropriate incentives to undertake economically sensible modifications.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 9 The problem is exacerbated because some modifications may benefit some tranches of the securities more than others, raising the risk of investor lawsuits.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: More generally, the sheer volume of delinquent loans has overwhelmed the capacity of many servicers, including portfolio lenders, to undertake effective modifications.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: During more normal times, mortgage delinquencies typically were triggered by life events, such as unemployment, illness, or divorce, and servicers became accustomed to addressing these problems on a case-by-case basis.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although taking account of the specific circumstances of each case remains important, the scale of the current problem calls for greater standardization and efficiency.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Loan modification programs with clearly defined protocols can both help reduce modification costs and protect servicers from the charge that they have acted arbitrarily.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The federal banking regulators have urged lenders and servicers to work with borrowers to avoid preventable foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The regulators recently reiterated that position in a joint statement that encouraged banks to make the necessary investments in staff and capacity to meet the escalating workload and to adopt systematic, proactive, and streamlined modification protocols to put borrowers in sustainable mortgages.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A number of initiatives have attempted to address the problem of unnecessary foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Working in collaboration with the Treasury Department, the Hope Now Alliance, a coalition of mortgage servicers, lenders, housing counselors, and investors--led by Faith Schwartz, a member of the Fed's Consumer Advisory Council--has produced a set of guidelines that participating servicers have agreed to use as they work to prevent foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, servicers in the Alliance agreed to delay foreclosure proceedings if an alternative approach might allow the homeowners to stay in their home.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Recently, in conjunction with the FHFA, the coalition announced that its members will adopt a streamlined modification program for certain loans that they service for the GSEs.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This program will closely follow the one that the FDIC has introduced for modifying the loans in the portfolio that it took over from IndyMac.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has also been actively supporting efforts to prevent unnecessary foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Through the System's Homeownership and Mortgage Initiative, we have conducted studies on housing and foreclosures, provided community leaders with detailed analyses to help them better target their borrower outreach and counseling efforts, and convened forums like this one to facilitate the exchange of ideas and the development of policy options.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Taking advantage of the Federal Reserve's nationwide presence, the twelve Reserve Banks have sponsored or co-sponsored more than 100 events related to foreclosures around the country since last summer, bringing together more than 10,000 lenders, counselors, community development specialists, and policymakers.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A particular focus of the Fed's efforts has been the mitigation of the costs to communities of high rates of foreclosure.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, we have partnered with NeighborWorks America on a neighborhood stabilization project and helped them develop responses to community needs as well as train local leaders.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Beyond these efforts, two government programs to facilitate loan modifications have been authorized, both through the Federal Housing Administration (FHA).
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The FHASecure program has provided long-term fixed-rate mortgages to borrowers facing a rise in payments due to an interest rate reset.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Another, more recent program, dubbed Hope for Homeowners (H4H), allows lenders to refinance a delinquent borrower into a new, FHA-insured fixed-rate mortgage if the lender writes down the mortgage balance to create some home equity for the borrower and pays an up-front insurance premium.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In exchange for being put "above water" on the mortgage, the borrower is required to share any subsequent appreciation of the home with the government.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although the basic structure of the H4H program is appealing, some lenders have expressed concerns about its complexity and cost, including the requirement in many cases to undertake substantial principal write-downs.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a result, participation has thus far been low.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In response to these concerns, the board of the H4H program--on which Governor Duke represents the Federal Reserve--recently approved a number of changes, using the authority granted to it under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act (EESA).
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These changes would reduce the necessary write-down on some loans, address the complications caused by subordinate liens by permitting up-front payments to those lien holders, allow lenders to extend mortgage terms from 30 to 40 years to increase affordability, and eliminate the trial modification period to expedite loan closings.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It is still too early to know what the ultimate demand for H4H loans under this set of rules will be, but as I will discuss further momentarily, a case can be made for further adjusting the terms of the program to make it more attractive to both lenders and borrowers.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Despite good-faith efforts by both the private and public sectors, the foreclosure rate remains too high, with adverse consequences for both those directly involved and for the broader economy.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: More needs to be done.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the remainder of my remarks I will discuss, without ranking, a few promising options for reducing avoidable foreclosures.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These proposals are not mutually exclusive and could be used in combination.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Each would require some commitment of public funds.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be effective, loan modifications should aim to put borrowers into mortgages that they can afford over the longer term.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: During more normal times, many homeowners could be helped with a temporary repayment plan--for example, a deferral of interest payments for a period.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But under the current circumstances, with house prices declining and credit tight, permanent loan modifications will often be needed to create sustainable mortgages and keep people in their homes.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Most current proposals to reduce foreclosures incorporate this view and thus emphasize permanent modifications.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A more difficult design question turns on the extent to which the probability of default or redefault depends on the borrower's equity position in the home, as well as on the affordability of the monthly payment.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although not conclusive, the available evidence suggests that the homeowner's equity position is, along with affordability, an important determinant of default rates, for owner-occupiers as well as investors.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: If that evidence is correct, then principal write-downs may need to be part of the toolkit that servicers use to achieve sustainable mortgage modifications.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: If one accepts the view that principal write-downs may be needed in cases of badly underwater mortgages, then strengthening the H4H program is a promising strategy, as I have noted.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Beyond the steps already taken by the H4H board, the Congress might consider making the terms of H4H loans more attractive by reducing the up-front insurance premium paid by the lender, currently set in law at 3 percent of the principal value, as well as the annual premium paid by the borrower, currently set at 1â1/2 percent.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Congress might also grant the FHA the flexibility to tailor these premiums to individual risk characteristics rather than forcing the FHA to charge the same premium to all borrowers.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, consideration might be given to reducing the interest rate that borrowers would pay under the H4H program.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: At present, this rate is expected to be quite high, roughly 8 percent, in part because it is tied to the demand for the relatively illiquid securities issued by Ginnie Mae to fund the program.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To bring down this rate, the Treasury could exercise its authority to purchase these securities, with the Congress providing the appropriate increase in the debt ceiling to accommodate those purchases.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Alternatively, the Congress could decide to subsidize the rate.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A second proposal, put forward by the FDIC, focuses on improving the affordability of monthly payments.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Under the FDIC plan, servicers would restructure delinquent mortgages using a streamlined process, modeled on the IndyMac protocol, and would aim to reduce monthly payments to 31 percent of the borrower's income.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As an inducement to lenders and servicers to undertake these modifications, the government would offer to share in any losses sustained in the event of redefaults on the modified mortgages and would also pay $1,000 to the servicer for each modification completed.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 13 The strengths of this plan include the standardization of the restructuring process and the fact that the restructured loans remain with the servicer, with the government being involved only when a redefault occurs.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As noted, the FDIC plan would induce lenders and servicers to modify loans by offering a form of insurance against downside house price risk.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A third approach would have the government share the cost when the servicer reduces the borrower's monthly payment.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, a servicer could initiate a modification and bear the costs of reducing the mortgage payment to 38 percent of income, after which the government could bear a portion of the incremental cost of reducing the mortgage payments beyond 38 percent, say to 31 percent, of income.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This approach would increase the incentive of servicers to be aggressive in reducing monthly payments, which would improve the prospects for sustainability.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Relative to the FDIC proposal, this plan would pose a greater operational burden on the government, which would be required to make payments to servicers for all modified loans, not just for loans that redefault.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, this approach could leverage existing modification frameworks, such as the FDIC/IndyMac and Hope Now streamlined protocols, and in this respect would build on, rather than crowd out, private-sector initiatives.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Yet another promising proposal for foreclosure prevention would have the government purchase delinquent or at-risk mortgages in bulk and then refinance them into the H4H or another FHA program.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This approach could take advantage of the depressed market values of such mortgages, and buying in bulk might help avoid adverse selection problems.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, scale efficiencies could be achieved by contracting with specialty firms (perhaps including the GSEs) capable of re-underwriting large volumes of loans to make them eligible for H4H or another program.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury has already considered how to undertake bulk purchases as part of its work under EESA, and the Federal Reserve has submitted to the Congress an analysis of bulk purchases per a legislative requirement in the H4H bill.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Even so, this program could take some time to get up and running, and the re-underwriting required for H4H loans would likely take more time and incur greater operational costs than other plans.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But such an approach could result in many homeowners being refinanced into sustainable mortgages.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion The housing market remains central to the economic and financial challenges that we face.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because housing and mortgage markets are tightly interlinked with the rest of the economy, actions to strengthen financial markets and the broader economy are important ways to address housing issues.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: By the same token, steps that stabilize the housing market will help stabilize the economy as well.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this regard, reducing the number of preventable foreclosures would not only help families stay in their homes, it would confer much wider benefits.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Significant efforts have been taken in this direction, but more can be done.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Today I have briefly discussed a few promising options, which are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As we as a country consider ways to address our financial and economic challenges, policy initiatives to reduce the number of preventable foreclosures should be high on the agenda.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Estimates for specific metropolitan areas are based on Case-Shiller Home Price Indexes.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: See Kristopher Gerardi, Andreas Lehnert, Shane Sherlund, and Paul Willen (forthcoming), "Making Sense of the Subprime Crisis," Brookings Papers on Economic Activity (Washington:  Brookings Institution Press).
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Also see Chris Mayer, Karen Pence, and Shane Sherlund (2008), " The Rise in Mortgage Defaults ," Finance and Economics Discussion Series 2008-59 (Washington:  Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, November).
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Estimates of delinquencies are based on data from the Mortgage Bankers Association and from First American LoanPerformance.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Foreclosure starts are based on data from the Mortgage Bankers Association, adjusted to reflect the limited coverage of their sample.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Historically, about half of foreclosure starts resulted in the borrower losing the home, but recent rates appear higher.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For evidence that concentrations of foreclosures lead to lower house prices throughout the neighborhood, see, for example, William C. Apgar, Mark Duda, and Rochelle Nawrocki Gorey (2005),  "The Municipal Cost of Foreclosures:  A Chicago Case Study," Housing Finance Policy Research Paper 2005-1 (Minneapolis, Minn.:  Homeownership Preservation Foundation, February), www.995hope.org/content/pdf/Apgar_Duda_Study_Full_Version.pdf; and John P. Harding, Eric Rosenblatt, and Yao Vincent (2008), " The Contagion Effect of Foreclosed Properties ,"  Social Science Research Network working paper 1160354 (July).
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be sure, policy should not attempt to keep house prices from falling sufficiently to stabilize the demand for housing.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But preventing avoidable foreclosures does not block necessary adjustments.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, failing to prevent such foreclosures may heighten the risk that house prices will move lower than they would otherwise need to go.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: See J.P. Morgan (2008), "SOS--Summary of Subprime, Alt-A, Prime Jumbo," Global Structured Finance Research (November 2); and Credit Suisse (2008), "Deep Dive into Subprime Mortgage Severity," Fixed Income Research Report (June 19).
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: See "Deep Dive," note 8.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Servicers of mortgages in securitized pools must abide by the pooling and servicing agreements, which state what modifications may be prohibited but provide limited guidance about what types of modifications investors would consider to be appropriate.
speech_title: Housing, Mortgage Markets, and Foreclosures
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Kroszner
text: I very much appreciate the opportunity to participate in this conference and to hear your insights firsthand about such a range of important topics.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As you know, housing markets are weak.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Sales of new homes and of existing homes are well below their respective peaks around the middle of this decade.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: House prices have fallen sharply--the national price index published by the Federal Housing Finance Agency is down almost 8 percent from its high in the spring of 2007, and the Case-Shiller national index is down more than 20 percent from its peak about 2-1/2 years ago.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Residential construction has remained weak, with single-family housing starts having declined to less than a third the number seen early in 2006.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Even with the drop in homebuilding, the inventory of unsold new homes represents more than 10 months' supply at the recent pace of sales.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Taken together, these data suggest continuing near-term challenges for stabilization of the housing market.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: With the plunge in home sales and house prices as well as very tight lending conditions, mortgage borrowing by households has fallen sharply over the past two years or so.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, the latest information suggests that, on net, home mortgage debt may not have increased at all since the spring.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, most of the new mortgages that were originated in the past several months were funded with mortgage-backed securities (MBS) guaranteed by the government housing agencies--Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: That is, origination of mortgages not eligible for a government guarantee has fallen dramatically as issuance of private-label MBS has virtually come to a halt this year.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The rapid deterioration in credit quality of mortgages in subprime and so-called alt-A MBS pools--and the subsequent severe rating downgrades of the securities they backed--has significantly eroded the value of and investor confidence in private-label MBS.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In my remarks today, I would like to suggest some fundamental changes in the structure of private-label MBS that might help a recovery, over time, in investor confidence and in the market for these securities.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe that mortgage securitization has the potential to deliver economic value to investors, lenders, and, ultimately, borrowers.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Several conditions would be necessary for the potential of private-label MBS to be realized going forward.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A necessary condition is for comprehensive and standardized loan-level data covering the entire pool of loans backing MBS to be made available and easily accessible so that the underlying credit quality can be rigorously analyzed by market participants more easily than is now the case.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: But comprehensive data will not be sufficient.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, a number of aspects of the securities themselves will probably need to be changed.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, the structures of cash flows from mortgage payments in the pool to the various tranches of MBS should be much less complex than some of those created in recent years.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, securitization contracts will need to be made more homogeneous so as to allow greater comparability of risk profiles across deals and perhaps promote more robust liquidity.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, securitizations should involve fewer and larger tranches of MBS, which, in addition to further promoting liquidity, could also reduce the exposure of some securities to certain tail risks and model uncertainty.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe that a new infrastructure built upon these foundations might reasonably be expected to lower the costs of information production and processing in the marketplace.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The reduction of these costs will facilitate broader independent credit analyses, greater due diligence by potential purchasers, and, hence, greater ability to provide a double check on credit rating agencies' evaluation of the riskiness of the securities.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, market participants would be more likely to acquire the expertise to evaluate securities issues that were more homogeneous and less complex.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This change would make the situation closer to what occurs in the corporate bond market, in which standardized disclosures about relatively homogeneous and straightforward securities of publicly traded companies allow many analysts and potential purchasers to come up with their own evaluations, in addition to those of the credit rating agencies.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Moreover, such changes might also lead to the creation of structures whose credit analyses are less sensitive to certain tail risks and types of model uncertainty and more likely to be liquid even in times of market stress.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, this new infrastructure might allow investors gradually to regain confidence in their ability to assess the risk-return tradeoffs inherent in MBS, allowing them to reconsider how those securities may best fit into their overall portfolios.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As I mentioned, in principle, mortgage securitizations make good economic sense: By providing access to the broad capital market, securitization allows loan originators to access a wider source of funding than they can obtain directly.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, securitization can limit an originator's exposure to prepayment risks associated with interest rate movements, to geographic concentrations of loans, and to credit and funding risks associated with holding mortgages all the way to maturity.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Effectively, securitization can significantly lower the cost of extending home loans, and some of those cost savings can be passed along to homeowners in the form of lower mortgage rates.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: It seems clear that the housing government-sponsored enterprises (or agencies) played an important role in the development of mortgage securitization in the United States.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In large part, the broad appeal of agency MBS can be traced to the explicit guarantee of the securities by the sponsoring agencies.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This agency support may have meant that the returns to undertaking a thorough and costly credit analysis of underlying mortgages in agency MBS pools were low, so that task was essentially left to the agencies themselves.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, even as agency MBS issuance took off in the 1970s and 1980s, the most basic infrastructure needed to conduct credit analysis on home mortgage pools--comprehensive loan-level data that was broadly accessible in a standardized format--went essentially undeveloped.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, I believe that markets for private-label MBS are unlikely to recover unless comprehensive and standardized data for home mortgage pools are made widely available to market participants.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As you may be aware, the American Securitization Forum (ASF) is in the midst of a large-scale project called RESTART, or Residential Securitization Transparency and Reporting.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: This project seeks to develop a standardized format for mortgage data that would be available to all investors and other market participants, with the goal of substantially improving disclosure and transparency related to private-label MBS.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: RESTART has wide support in the industry, and the project is receiving input from a wide range of market participants, including investors, mortgage originators, loan servicers, credit bureaus, credit rating agencies, MBS trustees, legal counselors, and data vendors.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, just yesterday, a report issued by a consortium of several securitization industry groups endorsed the RESTART project in its first recommendation for an "action plan" to work to restore confidence in securitization markets.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: 2 Although, to be sure, some time will be required to develop specific recommendations and then to overcome implementation issues, I am encouraged by the ambition of the project and the vigor with which participants appear to be working on it.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: While comprehensive loan-level data for mortgage pools are necessary to rebuild confidence in private-label MBS, I now wish to elaborate a bit on improvements in the contractual structure of private-label MBS that are, in my view, also needed to revive the market.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, in recent years, the complexity of many deals made non-agency MBS difficult to value.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, looking at private-label MBS deals constructed in the heyday of 2006, some subprime trusts included three separate pools of mortgages--for example, prime-rated jumbo loans, alt-A first liens, and a blend of subprime first and junior liens--with cash flows that were prioritized using complicated payoff rules among more than a dozen different securities.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: The securitization contract might have dictated that one AAA-rated tranche might have been paid using only cash flows from the prime jumbo loans, while another AAA-rated tranche could have received no payments at all from that pool.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Second, non-agency mortgage securitization contracts contained numerous idiosyncratic features that limited the comparability of deals that may have appeared to be similarly structured.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Not only might there have been subtle but significant differences in the cash flow obligations to each tranche, but there was also much variation in other important provisions, such as duties on servicers of the loans in the pool and the representations and warranties that govern the circumstances under which poorly performing loans can be put back to the originator.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, even if comprehensive data on the loans in the pools had been available, a thorough credit analysis would have required both a detailed reading of the deal-specific documentation describing a particular deal's potentially unique structure and a careful analysis of how its cash flow prioritization would affect returns to holders of the particular tranches of securities as laid out in the contract.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Although such an analysis is possible, it may be beyond the available resources for many investors.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe that more homogeneous mortgage securitization contracts could significantly lower the barriers to entry for credit analysts, thereby promoting greater transparency and perhaps more confidence among investors about the securities' underlying risk-return attributes.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Third, larger tranches in private-label MBS could have a couple of key benefits.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: For instance, investors might view larger security issues as being more likely to sustain liquid trading conditions, which would allow investors to rebalance their portfolios, as conditions evolve, at reasonably predictable prices and with transaction costs comparable to those of other securities traded in "thick" markets.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, as has become evident, tranched securitizations are exposed to tail risks--situations that can be expected to occur only rarely but which convey very negative returns.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: My intuition is that thinner tranches are more vulnerable to tail risks, because it seems more likely in the latter case that widespread credit losses in the underlying loan pool could wipe out designated cash flows for the entire tranche--so-called nonlinear, or cliff, effects.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, future mortgage securitizations that rely on simpler cash flows and larger tranches might reduce some of the exposure to tail risks and enable investors to gain confidence.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: As an aside, I should note that I do not expect a revival for some of the most complex structures that were created in recent years to finance a portion of subprime and alt-A mortgages.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am thinking specifically of collateralized debt obligations (CDOs) that were themselves backed by other structured credit products, including the lower-rated tranches of private-label MBS.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: These so-called two-layer securitizations were far more complex and much more exposed to systematic losses than were the MBS themselves.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, investors in--and more importantly, financial institutions that retained--the super senior tranches of CDO-squared securities took substantial losses as the severity of the downturn in the housing market and in mortgage credit quality became evident.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Given the magnitude of those losses and the recognition that rigorous credit analyses are extremely information-intensive (and very sensitive to assumptions about loss correlations), I would expect investors to remain skeptical of two-layer securitized financial products for the foreseeable future.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: To the extent that larger tranches of simpler and more homogeneous securities might encourage broader information processing and credit analyses, they could play a role in rebuilding investor confidence.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Corporations that issue large amounts of bonds, for example, tend to be followed by quite a number of analysts.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Consequently, investors can access a wide range of information and opinions about those companies, providing a check--and less overall reliance--on credit analyses produced by the credit rating agencies themselves.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In sum, an improved infrastructure for non-agency MBS should include comprehensive, loan-by-loan data that are available in a standardized format that is readily accessible, but a robust data platform will not be sufficient.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: A new infrastructure will probably also include less-complex cash flow waterfalls, more homogeneous contract designs, and larger tranches of securities.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: With these features, the new infrastructure could increase transparency, and promote independent, objective credit analysis for the various classes of non-agency MBS.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: By facilitating detailed information processing and independent risk analyses, the reliance on credit rating agencies could be reduced, easing the way for investors to regain confidence in these securities and for liquidity to return in these valuable markets.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: That said, the recovery in the market for non-agency MBS--and, more broadly, for the origination of home mortgages that depend on these securities for funding--is bound to be a gradual process.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: It will take time to develop and implement a new infrastructure such as the one I have outlined, and for investor confidence to be rebuilt.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: In addition, investors could remain wary of re-engaging in the market for private-label MBS until they become convinced that housing markets around the country are on the mend.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some form of government backstop may be necessary to keep the market functioning under the most stressed circumstances.
speech_title: Improving the Infrastructure for Non-Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
