speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve System Conference on Housing and Mortgage Markets, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: One consequence of the distress in financial markets is that banks are being pushed to take a greater role in financial intermediation, which reverses, in part, a long-term trend away from bank-based financial intermediation and toward market-based intermediation.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: And, indeed, bank lending surged earlier in the fall following a lull over the summer.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the degree to which the pickup represented deliberate choices by banks is unclear, as many households and businesses reportedly drew on previously committed lines of credit, and selling of loans in securitization markets was hampered by further deterioration in those markets.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In recent weeks, bank lending appears to have dropped back, consistent with the significant tightening of terms and standards reported by bank loan officers in recent quarters as well as the weakening of economic activity.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The need for greater bank intermediation has occurred at a time when banks are managing losses and are worried about meeting their funding needs.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Concerns about banks' creditworthiness have made it costly for them to issue long-term debt.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Growth in bank deposits has been fairly strong this year, and the recognition that deposits can be a reliable source of funds protected by the federal safety net has perhaps helped to draw investment banks to convert to bank holding companies.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: But the competition for deposits has raised their relative cost, and deposits cannot be expected to make up fully for reduced funding from other sources.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The challenge for regulators and other authorities is to create an environment that supports greater bank intermediation, which should help to restore the health of the financial system and the economy.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: We want banks to be willing to deploy capital and liquidity, but they must do so in a responsible way that avoids past mistakes and does not create new ones.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Banks need access to funds to make loans--especially with securitization markets impaired--and the authorities have taken several steps to enhance the supply of funds to banks.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Treasury, working with the regulators, has used its authority under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act, or EESA, to inject capital into banks so they will be stronger and more stable.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation has expanded its guarantee on deposits and is insuring new senior debt obligations of banking firms.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve has reduced the cost of borrowing at the discount window and created a new facility to provide term credit to banks.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve and the other federal banking agencies have also issued regulatory guidance to promote greater lending by banks.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: This guidance encouraged banks to meet the needs of creditworthy borrowers in a manner consistent with safety and soundness--specifically, by taking a balanced approach in assessing borrowers' ability to repay and making realistic assessments of collateral valuations.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: 2 Additional capital, liquidity backstops, and regulatory encouragement should all reinforce financial stability and set the stage for increased bank lending.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As it is neither realistic nor desirable for banks to meet all financial intermediation needs, the Federal Reserve and other authorities are also making efforts to stabilize financial markets more broadly.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In this regard, the Federal Reserve has created facilities to lend to primary dealers, to purchase highly rated commercial paper at a term of three months, and to provide backup liquidity for money market mutual funds.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: We are also creating a facility to support the issuance of asset-backed securities collateralized by student loans, auto loans, credit card loans, and loans guaranteed by the Small Business Administration.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: In related actions, policymakers are taking steps to address the problems in housing and mortgage markets.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve supported placing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship to help stabilize an important source of housing finance.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: More recently, the Federal Reserve has announced that it will purchase $600billion in debt issued by the housing-related government-sponsored enterprises and in mortgage-backed securities backed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae, which could reduce funding costs for mortgages.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: It also is supporting foreclosure prevention and neighborhood stabilization efforts, which help reduce unnecessary foreclosures and their costs on communities.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Limiting foreclosures will also help reduce the risk that house prices will sink significantly below the level justified by fundamentals.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The events of the past year and a half have highlighted the need for changes in our financial system.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Presumably, such changes may include a different balance between bank-based and market-based financial intermediation.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: As regulators of banks and thrifts, our job is not to determine what this balance should be.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Rather, our job is, and has been, to create an environment in which, in the short run, banks can step up to fill as much of the gap as possible that has been left by still-dysfunctional markets, consistent with a strong, stable banking system.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Over time, of course, we will need to work with the Congress and the new Administration to construct a system of oversight over both markets and institutions that better protects the stability of the financial system and the U.S. economy.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: The views expressed are my own and not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Reserve Board and the Federal Open Market Committee.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: Karen Dynan , J. Nellie Liang , and Sabeth Siddique of the Board staff contributed to these remarks.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kohn
text: See Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, and Office of Thrift Supervision (2008), " Interagency Statement on Meeting the Needs of Creditworthy Borrowers ," joint press release, November 12.
speech_title: Restoring Financial Intermediation by Banks: The Role of Regulators
speech_venue: At the Office of Thrift Supervision National Housing Forum, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Kroszner
text: I am honored to give the opening remarks at this impressive conference.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Today, I would like to offer some thoughts about risks in financial markets and the manner in which banking organizations need to assess those risks.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: 1 In particular, I will note the problems that can arise when the safeguards that market participants employ for their individual positions can have the unintended effect of actually exacerbating market-wide distress and amplifying losses among multiple market participants during times of market turbulence.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: But before offering recommendations that might serve to address these problems for banking institutions, I believe it is worthwhile to take a step back and explore some conceptual issues about the organization of markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A conceptual framework for the organization of markets In the simplified world of an introductory economics class, a market brings together the potential buyers and sellers of a product to negotiate prices and quantities.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this paradigm, the invisible hand of the market matches all willing buyers and sellers at a single, market-clearing price.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Transactions occur instantaneously and costlessly.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: While this stripped-down story is remarkably powerful in its essential predictions about the behavior of markets and economic agents, it leaves the operation of the market itself as a mystery.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Any real-world market must deal with at least two fundamental questions:  first, how do the buyers and sellers find one another?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: And second, how can buyers be assured that sellers will deliver as promised, and that the goods will be of the quality and value that the buyer expects?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: To understand how markets deal with the fundamental issues of transaction costs and information costs is an important and enduring challenge for economists.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Market institutions arise to overcome these barriers to trade, but do not arise wholly-formed and perfect.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Buyers and sellers gravitate towards markets that prove most effective in fostering transactions, and this rewards successful innovation and refinement in the institutional forms of markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As market institutions adapt to serve the particular needs of their participants, they grow more varied and specialized.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The imperfections and ongoing evolution of market institutions have inspired a rich and insightful literature within economics.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Returning to the first question, how do buyers and sellers find one another in the real world?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Each side might be aware that potential counterparties exist , but not where and when to find them.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Information problems of this sort, often termed search costs , have since ancient times been overcome by designating a market by location, time and product.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The Pushkar camel fair, which draws 50,000 camels for trade to a small desert town in western India at the full moon in November, is a colorful but not atypical example.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the financial world, a corresponding institution is the exchange.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Many exchanges have their historical roots as gatherings of speculators at a coffee house or other designated public place for a daily or weekly session to buy and sell securities.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The introduction of new technology can change the institutional structure of markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Improved telecommunications has made it possible to relax coordination on the physical location of markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Once a building, the exchange is now a network of screens.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Furthermore, by dramatically reducing the cost of locating counterparties and comparing prices, technology has increased the scope for decentralized markets such as OTC derivative markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Decentralized markets excel at providing variety and thus at accommodating the idiosyncratic needs of investors and consumers.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Returning to our second question, then, how can buyers be assured of quality goods in a real-world marketplace?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Whenever quality and value are costly to verify, how can buyers be assured that the seller will not deliver subpar goods?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Market institutions have arisen to address these concerns.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A seller might invest in bolstering its reputation for delivering quality goods or offer a warranty.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Standardized grading is a convention that facilitates the unambiguous specification of quality in a contract.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: An important milestone in the development of commodity markets was the promulgation in 1856 by the Chicago Board of Trade of standardized grades of wheat.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: 3 This allowed buyers and sellers of wheat to trade in standardized "warehouse receipts," rather than specific lots, with inexpensive quality verification by third-party policy and certification.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The idea of standardized grading and third-party assessment was introduced to credit markets by rating agencies in the early 20th century.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, as recent events have made clear, the qualitative and multi-faceted nature of credit risk limits the extent to which investors can or should rely on ratings as the sole measure of quality.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A more subtle form of the quality assurance problem arises when a transaction results in future contingent obligations by the counterparties.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Future obligations are common in financial markets, where the risk of nonperformance is known as counterparty credit risk.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In a credit default swap, for example, each side is seeking to alter credit exposure to the reference entity.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The resulting contingent credit exposure to the counterparty is entirely incidental to the reason for the transaction, yet may be a first-order determinant of future performance.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Financial markets have developed mechanisms that are specific to the control of counterparty risk.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The simplest of these is the posting of collateral against counterparty exposures.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ensuring the efficacy of collateral is challenging even under ordinary circumstances, and may leave counterparties especially vulnerable to large sudden changes in market prices, also called gap risk.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A more sophisticated convention for mitigating counterparty credit risk is a central counterparty or a clearinghouse.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In markets with a clearinghouse, all trades are intermediated through a central counterparty.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This arrangement can and, in practice, does vastly reduce counterparty risk.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The central counterparty runs a balanced book, so generally has no direct market exposure.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the case of a member's default, the central counterparty can draw upon the proprietary margin of the defaulting member, its own reserve fund, and the assessment of members for share purchase.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As you know, plans are currently being developed to establish one or more central counterparties in the credit derivatives market.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: So why do we not find a central counterparty in every financial market?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A key reason is that the gain in safety may come at the expense of flexibility.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Like an exchange, a central counterparty imposes a degree of standardization upon contracts.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As noted earlier, OTC derivative markets have grown so rapidly in large part due to the demand for variety and customization of contracts.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: That said, many OTC contracts are already eligible for clearing through a central counterparty.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, SwapClear, a central counterparty for interest rate swaps, clears about half of global single-currency swaps between dealers.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Assessing recent financial market performance Now that I have laid out a conceptual framework about markets and how participants ensure the quality of transactions, I would like briefly to apply that conceptual framework to the events of the past 18 months.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Financial crisis can serve as a powerful stimulant to the evolution of market mechanisms, and I expect that the aftermath of the present turmoil will see both innovation and incremental refinement to quality assurance in credit markets and in counterparty credit risk management.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: I would like to highlight two themes that I believe will influence this process.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: First, for quality assurance to be effective, some of the products traded in financial markets have to become simpler and more transparent.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Product complexity and a lack of transparency are at the root of many of the problems that have emerged, especially in the markets for securitizations and structured credit products.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: I elaborated on these themes in remarks I made at a Federal Reserve conference last week on the future of the mortgage market.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: 4 There I argued that a recovery in the market for mortgage-backed securities (MBSs) will require greater transparency and less complexity, and importantly, comprehensive and standardized loan-level data that will allow more independent credit analysis.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, the structures of cash flows from mortgage payments in the pool to the various tranches of MBSs should be much less complex than some of those created in recent years, and securitization contracts will need to be made more homogeneous so as to allow greater comparability of risk profiles across deals and perhaps promote more robust liquidity.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: I believe that a new infrastructure for MBSs built upon these foundations might be reasonably expected to lower the costs of information production and processing in the marketplace.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The reduction of these costs will facilitate broader independent credit analyses, greater due diligence by potential purchasers, and, hence, greater ability to provide a double check on credit rating agencies' evaluation of the riskiness of the securities.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, market participants would be more likely to acquire the expertise to evaluate securities issues that were more homogeneous and less complex.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A second key factor for effective quality assurance relates to the institutional and contractual framework for ensuring future performance on financial transactions, namely counterparty credit risk management.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Counterparty credit risk management should be focused on its effectiveness in different market situations and its implications for financial stability.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: There is a broad class of market practices that can provide useful protections when an individual firm experiences trouble but these practices may not provide useful protections--and could be potentially harmful--when the trouble is marketwide.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A representative example is the use of rating triggers in counterparty credit risk management.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some debt contracts and OTC derivative contracts link collateral requirements to a counterparty's credit rating.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: If a counterparty is downgraded past some threshold, it may become subject to an immediate margin call.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Counterparty credit risk appears to remain contained so long as the rating trigger is breached long before the counterparty could reach insolvency--that is, the trigger is set at a relatively high rating.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In such cases, this type of clause can be quite valuable in mitigating counterparty credit risk and in giving the counterparty strong incentives to try to maintain its financial health and, hence, its rating.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This type of protection against counterparty risk is most effective when changes in risk are specific to the counterparty and not correlated with increases in risks to other counterparties and in other markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In this case, the posting of additional collateral long before a firm reaches insolvency can provide valuable protection.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such a provision may not provide protection, however, if the rating change comes too late, the firm is on the brink of insolvency, and the requirement to post the margin can push it into insolvency.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: More importantly, such a provision may also fail to provide protection if the trouble at the counterparty is correlated with trouble at other institutions and in other markets, that is, due to marketwide distress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In times of widespread distress, many counterparties may have to sell assets simultaneously to post margin.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This occurrence can potentially lead to a situation in the market in which assets are sold quickly and below their fundamental values.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: When many counterparties are forced to liquidate similar assets, prices for those assets are pushed down.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: If these assets are used as collateral on other positions, then the decline in value leads to additional margin calls.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This set of circumstances, in turn, forces further liquidation and price declines.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A widespread use of rating triggers can accelerate this downward slide, with further losses in asset values triggering additional downgrades and requirements to post collateral and liquidate positions.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Recent events have demonstrated this potentially destabilizing dynamic at work.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Rating triggers are certainly only one example of market practices that can exacerbate the impact of a systemic event and make financial markets less stable.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Credit enhancements and guarantees can also create fragility while seeming to offer protection.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A highly-rated guarantor, for example, could offer effective protection against the default of a small number of instruments.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In the event of a market-wide increase in credit risk, however, there is an increased probability that the guarantor would be required to pay out on many positions simultaneously.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As the market comes to realize that the credit enhancement may not be effective, further pressure may come upon the institutions that would be left exposed.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Thus, widespread reliance on credit enhancements could induce a form of "wrong way risk" in which the seller of protection becomes most likely to default in precisely the circumstances where protection is most valued.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: What might seem like a "herd" behavior in some markets may be at least in part a response to the fragile interconnections affecting the stability of those markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such apparent herding behavior, reflecting a collective loss of confidence, may be generated by a market infrastructure that induces co-movements across markets and institutions during times of stress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In these circumstances, contractual provisions that might seem on the surface to be prudent counterparty risk management could increase financial market stress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Improving banks' risk management for participation in financial markets Marketwide credit events and stresses, and how market infrastructure could exacerbate them, did not receive sufficient attention in risk management efforts in the period leading up to the current turmoil.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: For example, risk managers did not fully contemplate the possibility that many participants would need to unwind their positions at the same time, that such actions might present substantial losses for several key counterparties, and that collateral posted as protection for positions would fall in value at the same time.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: There was not sufficient understanding of the correlation between declines in collateral value and the likelihood that collateral would need to be called upon.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Similar issues arose with third-party guarantees and with hedging strategies that had less effectiveness than anticipated.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Even when risk managers had some understanding of these issues, each individually likely faced difficulty in demanding more collateral or guarantees during good times because no risk manager wanted to be the first.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: A key factor for assuring market quality, as I noted above, is assessing the behavior of counterparties in stressful times.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Not only do banks need to assess counterparty creditworthiness and behavior on an individual basis, they also need to assess counterparties on a collective basis.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: They need to understand how their own actions to protect positions can put pressure on key counterparties, especially when other market participants are likely to be taking similar action to protect themselves.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: So beyond ensuring that their own individual positions are sound and well protected, banks need to assess whether there is a systematic component to a market that could adversely affect multiple counterparties at the same time, and thereby affect their own risk exposures.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As we have seen, a counterparty does not need to be technically insolvent for it to be shunned by other market participants.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: The anticipation of downgrades, triggers, and so forth could very quickly cause a firm to lose funding and fail.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In short, banks and regulators need to understand the type of market conditions that will exist when there is likely to be reliance on collateral, guarantees, or other contract clauses.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: It is then important to assess the likelihood that the bank's safeguarding actions could worsen market conditions and actually increase its losses.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Might the bank only realize collateral at substantially reduced prices?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Would multiple counterparties suffer distress at the same time?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Would guarantors perform in times of distress?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In other words, would the collateral, guarantee, insurance, hedge, and so forth work in precisely the time the institution would need it most, that is, during a market stress event?
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: These are important questions that regulators and supervisors are asking in the Basel Committee and in the Financial Stability Forum, and I represent the Federal Reserve System on both of these bodies.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Naturally, these types of questions underscore the importance of stress testing and scenario analysis that focus on market-wide events.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Such stress tests would include the potential for key counterparties to fail or suffer difficulty at the same time, for market liquidity to erode and remain low for some time, and for market participants to view the bank itself as an impaired counterparty.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: And these stress tests, when properly designed, can provide information that typical statistical models may leave out or have trouble capturing, such as abnormally large jumps or market moves, evaporation of liquidity, prolonged periods of market distress, or structural changes in markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Stress tests are most useful when they aim to include potential secondary or "knock-on" effects, which are also often difficult to model with standard techniques.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In these ways, stress tests can serve as a complementary tool to other risk measures.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Even if the ex ante estimate of the probability of joint distress among counterparties appears small, it is still useful to know the severity of such an outcome, since it may clearly reveal an unacceptable loss.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Importantly, banks should also conduct stress tests across several markets, since some counterparties are key players across many financial markets and their inability to repay could cascade across those markets.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Of course, based on their consideration of the factors noted above and the results of their stress tests, banks may reassess their participation in certain markets and exercise greater caution to account for potential "tail" risks and better protect themselves in times of market-wide stress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: One of the first things they may do is increase their internal assessments of capital needs for these activities, given the added risks that stress tests reveal.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: They may wish to restructure contracts or alter terms.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Institutions also might ask for higher initial margin, given that subsequent calls may not provide as much risk mitigation during distress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: They may wish to ask for more collateral, or ensure that the collateral is less linked to the counterparty's condition or broader market distress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Or they might look for other ways to enhance their assessment of counterparties, and, perhaps more importantly, the potential for counterparties to encounter difficulties during marketwide stresses.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Additionally, they may wish to conduct more of their trading and hedging on more organized exchanges or with clearinghouses, to benefit from the safeguards I noted earlier in my remarks.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Some banks, acting on a collective basis, may decide to take action to improve the quality assurance performance of markets during future times of stress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Trade associations in the banking industry may consider additional safeguards to reduce the impact of systematic risks among counterparties; for example, banks may collectively act to remove uncertainty associated with back-office inefficiencies and related risks in the credit default swaps market.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Another example, as I noted in remarks last week, is an attempt to enhance mortgage markets so that there is greater standardization of data and simpler, more homogeneous provisions in the securitizations, and less reliance on third-party monitoring.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: As a more general step, banks should hold higher liquidity and capital buffers, since the enhancements I just noted are still no guarantee against future market distress that could cause correlated and cascading losses among market participants.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Finally, banks need to exercise strong discipline so that when good times return, they do not forget the current market difficulties and return to more profligate ways.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Indeed, now is the time for banks to establish good risk management policies addressing the issues I have just discussed, so that strong risk discipline is codified.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Concluding thoughts Of course, it is not just the banking industry, but also those of us in the public sector who have some key lessons to learn.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Banks and supervisors alike need to undertake additional work to facilitate the building of robust methods of quality assurance in the financial markets that will help to restore and maintain confidence.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Ensuring that banks exercise good risk management, of course, is an important job for bank supervisors, which includes overseeing their ability to properly capture the risks in the markets in which they operate, as well as their ability to conduct appropriate stress testing to explore potential consequences of different types of market distress.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: Doing so requires that supervisors themselves develop a strong understanding of the value, limits, and potential harms associated with banks' attempts to protect their exposures.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the Federal Reserve, we have already begun to enhance our supervisory work in this area and are communicating expectations to banks.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: At the international level, we are working with our colleagues in other countries and within international bodies, such as the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision--which is meeting later this week--and the Financial Stability Forum, to investigate whether other practices could be adopted around the world to mitigate the challenges I have outlined above.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: This work will be a major focus during the next few months and over the course of 2009.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
text: In my remarks, I will use the terms "banks," "banking institutions," and "banking organizations" interchangeably.
speech_title: Assessing the Potential for Instability in Financial Markets
speech_venue: At the Risk Minds Conference, International Center for Business Information, Geneva, Switzerland

speaker: Kroszner
