speaker: Duke
text: In the summer of 2007, the U.S. and global economies entered a period of unprecedented financial turmoil, which has since led to a significant slump in macroeconomic activity.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Problems in both the housing sector and the housing finance sector played a central role in precipitating the crisis, and ongoing weakness in housing activity, along with persistent strains in mortgage markets, continue to inhibit a broader recovery.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In particular, we have entered a cycle where high levels of default on mortgage debt have led to a reduction in the availability of mortgage debt as well as a tightening of terms for it.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: This situation has led to lower levels of home sales and prices paid for homes, which, in turn, contributes to yet more defaults by borrowers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: As financial risk managers, I am sure you are aware of the important steps that have already been taken to try to break this cycle, but that you also recognize the need to do more.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: My remarks today will focus on the next steps--efforts to increase demand for homes, efforts aimed at further reducing preventable foreclosures, and efforts aimed at limiting the costs imposed on households and communities by foreclosures that cannot be avoided.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Both the government and the private sector have important roles in these efforts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: These suggestions and recommendations are my opinion alone and do not reflect the views of other members of the Federal Reserve Board or any other government entity.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The Current Weakness in Housing Markets Housing activity remains extraordinarily weak.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Sales of new and existing homes have been running at a pace that is 60 percent of that seen at the peak in 2005.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Single-family housing starts are now less than one-quarter of their peak level.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: With the cutbacks in construction, inventories of unsold new homes have declined, but the months' supply--that is, inventories relative to sales--is still very high by historical standards.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The inventory of existing homes for sale is also quite elevated--and it would be even higher if not for would-be sellers that have withheld or withdrawn their homes from the market amid poor selling conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: We have also seen sharp drops in home prices.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: When home prices were at their peak three years ago, most analysts agreed that housing valuations looked to be substantially higher than warranted by fundamentals.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: However, home prices at the national level are now 17 percent off their peak, with some states, such as California and Florida, seeing declines on the order of 40 percent.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: 1 These declines may have reversed much, or perhaps all, of the earlier overvaluation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Notwithstanding this correction, all indications are that the softness in housing activity is likely to persist for some time.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In normal times, population growth and the attendant formation of new households tend to support housing demand.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Indeed, by some estimates, the current stock of housing is not high relative to the number of housing units that would be predicted by long-run trends in household formation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: However, the actual number of households has fallen well short of trend household formation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Macroeconomic conditions no doubt explain part of the shortfall in household formation, as, for example, younger people facing weak job prospects defer striking out on their own.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: More generally, the soft economy has diminished demand for housing among already-established households.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: High rates of job loss and weak income growth are directly reducing what some individuals can spend on housing, and the prospect of losing a job or suffering an income loss is damping the housing demand of others.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The cost and availability of mortgage credit is also bearing critically on housing demand.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: With private-label securitization markets almost completely closed, most purchases are financed with some form of government-supported credit.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Purchasers with strong credit histories and sufficient down payments can obtain a "conforming" mortgage, one that can be sold to the housing government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs).
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Loans insured through the Federal Housing Administration (FHA) are also available to eligible borrowers, who have historically been first-time homebuyers, borrowers without significant down payments, and higher-risk borrowers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, veterans with eligibility can obtain virtually 100 percent financing through VA loans.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: However, households without access to government-supported programs are having much more difficulty obtaining a mortgage than in the past.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: One obstacle is that the private mortgage securitization markets that previously supported most non-GSE mortgage lending are now shut down.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Subprime and near-prime mortgages--which traditionally were funded almost exclusively through securitization--are essentially unavailable, leaving those higher-risk households that do not qualify for FHA programs without access to mortgage credit.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Prime jumbo mortgages are still available for those seeking to finance a more expensive home, but lenders are being more selective, and spreads to conforming rates remain very high.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, the availability of products that complement conforming loans is impaired.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For example, second liens are more difficult and more expensive to obtain, which has deterred some households from making purchases that previously would have been financed by combining a conforming loan with a second lien that would cover some additional amount.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Access to private mortgage insurance is more restricted, which holds back some households that lack a sufficient down payment but otherwise qualify for a conforming mortgage.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: A key factor inhibiting recovery is that the adverse conditions in the housing and mortgage markets have been, and continue to be, mutually reinforcing.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: As I am sure you are painfully aware, delinquencies on mortgages have risen sharply in recent years.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: By way of background, the problems began in the nonprime mortgage market.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: As house prices boomed in the middle part of this decade, mortgage originators relaxed underwriting standards and extended mortgages with low or no down payments to households with weak credit histories or that did not fully document their income.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Many of these loans had low initial interest rates that reset to market rates after a couple of years, which resulted in a significant increase in the monthly payment.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Had house prices continued to rise, many borrowers would have been able to refinance to avoid higher payments and perhaps to extract accumulated home equity to use for future payments.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: However, the downturn in house prices meant that many borrowers did not have sufficient equity to refinance.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Payment problems began to rise, which, in turn, led lenders to tighten standards and made it even more difficult for borrowers to obtain new loans, which put even more upward pressure on delinquencies.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Eventually, investors became unwilling to fund high-risk mortgages at any price.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: While the high delinquency levels and subsequent pullback of credit for subprime loans was certainly foreseeable, what was less obvious was the degree to which problems in the subprime market would spread to the market for prime loans.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Loans in the prime loan market are going delinquent for all the traditional reasons: economic conditions and life events, such as job loss, medical problems, and divorce.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In a rising or even stable price environment, these delinquencies would often be cured through refinance or sale of the property, which would result in low levels of actual foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: However, loss of equity and tighter standards on all types of mortgages mean that even prime loans are more difficult to refinance, and weak housing demand has made it difficult to sell.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: According to the latest data, 25 percent of subprime loans and 13 percent of near-prime loans are now seriously delinquent--that is, more than 90 days past due or in foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The serious delinquency rate for prime mortgages, at between 3 percent and 4 percent, is much lower than for nonprime loans, but it has almost doubled over the past year.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Foreclosures have also risen sharply.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The available data suggest that lenders initiated 2-1/4 million foreclosures last year, more than double the number seen in 2006.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: 2 While the percentage of mortgages entering foreclosure is likely to increase further, the decline in the number of subprime loans means that this percentage will be applied to a smaller base of loans, which will tend to damp the overall number of foreclosures.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In the past, about one-half of foreclosures initiated were cured through a repayment plan or some other arrangement, but the remaining one-half resulted in the loss of a home.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The share resulting in home loss could well be higher now given the large numbers of distressed households and the bleak underlying economic conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: So, even if the number of foreclosures initiated begin to drop, we are still likely to see higher levels of property taken into real estate owned (REO) as foreclosures initiated earlier are completed and the share of those foreclosures resulting in the loss of a home increases.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Addressing the Problems in Housing and Mortgage Markets Several considerations underscore the need for policymakers to take further actions to address the problems in housing and mortgage markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: To begin, the weakness in the housing sector remains a significant drag on the macroeconomy and is reinforcing the strains in the financial system.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Moreover, the wave of foreclosures has the potential to exacerbate the problems going forward.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In past housing cycles, house prices have tended to fall below the level warranted by fundamentals, presumably as weak market conditions led sellers to make aggressive price cuts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The potential for an overcorrection of house prices in this cycle seems particularly acute, given the potential for foreclosures to create a glut of properties for sale.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: And, of course, further large declines in house prices would accentuate the broader problems in the macroeconomy and financial system through the channels that I just discussed.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, foreclosures cause significant distress among the families that lose their homes.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Whether the foreclosure is the result of inadequate underwriting by the mortgage lender, irresponsibility on the part of homeowner, or uncontrollable life events such as job loss, the result is the same: Displaced families with depleted resources and impaired credit have difficulty finding a new place to live.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: They may have to move significant distances, which may affect their ability to retain their jobs and disrupt other aspects of their lives as well as the lives of their family members.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The effects of foreclosures extend beyond these immediate families.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: One in five foreclosures appears to be affecting renter-occupied units.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The families in these units may also be displaced, even if they are paying their rent on time and abiding by the terms of their lease agreement.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In areas where foreclosures are concentrated, communities will suffer.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Clusters of vacant properties can foster vandalism and crime, and studies have shown that they lead to lower house prices throughout the neighborhood.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: 3 Municipal governments may have to spend more on maintaining properties and preventing crime, such as vandalism and arson, just when resources are stretched thin, in part because of the lower tax revenue associated with lower house prices.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Such spending may well crowd out the provision of other types of public services.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Fiscal and monetary stimulus directed at improving employment conditions and federal support for housing finance will ultimately strengthen the housing market.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: However, we also need measures that directly address the foreclosure problem.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In designing such measures, we must consider the different types of borrowers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: First, there are distressed borrowers who can avoid foreclosure through an appropriate modification of their loan.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Second, there are some borrowers who, due to resources or circumstance, will be unable or unwilling to sustain their mortgage payments even with reasonable loan adjustments from the lender or support from government programs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In such cases, foreclosures will happen, and we need to limit both the direct costs to the borrower and the broader social costs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Of course, there is a third group of borrowers--those who are still successfully meeting their mortgage obligations.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: One might be tempted to view these households as a lesser concern, but we must be mindful that they will be more likely to shift into one of the distressed groups if we do not reduce both the number of foreclosures and the cost of the foreclosures that do occur.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Reducing Preventable Foreclosures To help distressed households for which foreclosure can be prevented, servicers must implement effective and sustainable modifications.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Key private and public steps toward preventing unnecessary foreclosures have already been taken.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For example, the industry-led Hope Now Alliance--a coalition of mortgage servicers, lenders, housing counselors, and investors--has produced loss mitigation guidelines for servicers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, Hope Now members have agreed to adopt a streamlined modification program for certain loans that they service for the GSEs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Among government efforts, the FHASecure program provided long-term fixed-rate mortgages to borrowers facing a rise in payments due to an interest rate reset.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The more recent FHA "HOPE for Homeowners" (H4H) program, on whose oversight board I sit, allows lenders to refinance a delinquent borrower into an FHA-insured fixed-rate mortgage if the lender writes down the mortgage balance to create some home equity for the borrower and pays an up-front insurance premium.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In exchange for being put "above water" on the mortgage, the borrower is required to share any equity created through the refinancing and any subsequent appreciation of the home with the government.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Although the pace of loan modification has picked up over the past year, more needs to be done.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Indeed, many cases still seem to be appearing in which foreclosure is occurring even though both the borrower and lender would benefit from avoiding that outcome.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: There are several potential ways that the Congress and policymakers could help expand the number of at-risk borrowers who can obtain assistance and reduce the incidence of preventable foreclosures.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For example, the impact of the H4H program has so far been limited because of the terms and conditions for program loans mandated by the authorizing legislation and because of the general reluctance of servicers and lenders to write down the principal of delinquent mortgages.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The Congress is currently considering several modifications to the H4H program that have the potential to make the program more attractive to both servicers and homeowners.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: These modifications include eliminating the upfront mortgage premium that must be paid by the owner of the current mortgage and the requirement that borrowers share with the government a portion of any future appreciation in the property.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Among other options that the Congress or the government might consider is reducing the interest rate that H4H borrowers pay, either through a direct subsidy or through Treasury purchases of the relatively illiquid Ginnie Mae securities to which the borrowers' interest rate is tied.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The government might also consider purchasing delinquent or at-risk mortgages in bulk and then refinancing them into the H4H or other FHA programs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, government funds might be used to offer some general inducement for servicers to modify loans at risk of default.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For example, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) has proposed that, for loans modified in accordance with a streamlined process adapted from the protocol that the FDIC has used for IndyMac loans, the government would agree to absorb some of the losses on the modified loans that redefault.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Another approach would have the government share with the servicer the cost of a reduction in the borrower's monthly payment.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Alternatively, the government might make payments directly to homeowners who--because of temporary job loss or a similar event--need help meeting their mortgage obligations.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: 4 Because institutional and legal obstacles may be holding back modifications by servicers, these plans could be effective ways to deliver assistance to some distressed homeowners.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: While speed and volume in modifications are important, in my view, it is equally essential that the new obligations be sustainable in the long run.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: By "sustainable" I mean that the payment should be fixed for the life of the loan, it should be affordable, and it should be based upon verified income.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In changing the terms of the mortgage, servicers may start with changing the interest rate or adjusting the maturity to make the payments more affordable, but they also need to consider whether writing down loan principal amounts make sense.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Doing the latter may be more effective at reducing the probability of redefault.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: 6 These design principles for modifications are all included in the Homeownership Preservation Policy recently adopted by the Federal Reserve Board.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: 7 The Federal Reserve will apply this policy to the residential mortgage assets held by the special purpose vehicles established by the Federal Reserve to facilitate the acquisition of Bear Stearns by JPMorgan Chase and to assist the American International Group, Inc.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Although it is encouraging that so many policymakers are focused on the issue of loan modifications and making thoughtful proposals, I think it is equally important that the government decide how it wishes to move forward, and then do so.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: As long as uncertainty exists as to the scope and terms of the additional steps that likely will be offered, borrowers, lenders, and servicers will continue to hold out in hope of securing a better deal.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In this case, the cost of delay could easily outweigh the differences in outcome between the proposals.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For these reasons, I am pleased that the Administration is moving ahead on this front.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Reducing Costs When Foreclosures Cannot Be Prevented Without in any way minimizing the need for continued emphasis on foreclosure prevention, I don't believe we can fully formulate appropriate policy responses to the crisis unless we acknowledge and address the large numbers of foreclosures that are not avoidable.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: We are likely only beginning to see the serious costs of the foreclosures that have already been initiated, both because of the often-substantial amount of time required to complete a foreclosure and because the costs likely compound as the number of foreclosures grows larger.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Moreover, even under optimistic assumptions for the number of loan modifications and other forms of private and public assistance that may be realized, the pace at which foreclosures are initiated is likely to remain extremely elevated for some time.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Just as public focus, experimentation, and policy debate have informed best practices with regard to loan modifications, we must also begin the work of developing responsible foreclosure and real estate inventory management protocols.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Minimizing the amount of time that properties remain vacant and maximizing the price at which they are sold will serve the interests of both lenders and the communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: At this moment, lenders and communities alike are woefully under-resourced and unprepared for the volume of real estate that will need to be processed.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Given the likely number of properties that will enter foreclosure and the time and resources involved in the foreclosure process, financial institutions can help minimize the cost by developing clear policies and procedures for approval of short sales and deeds-in-lieu-of-foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For homeowners who cannot, or no longer wish to, stay in their homes, such strategies would release them from their obligation and avoid foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Some institutions offer a so-called fresh start or cash-for-keys program, in which they provide a payment to consumers in exchange for voluntarily surrendering the deed to the home.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Such arrangements reduce the cost of foreclosure and effectively provide the borrower with funds that can help offset some of the expenses associated with relocation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Other lenders are offering borrowers the option to remain in the house as renters rather than owners.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Options such as these could be offered in conjunction with loan modification programs as further inducement for borrowers to engage in loan resolution discussions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: If renters occupy the property, servicers of REO properties should extend existing lease arrangements, when possible, and while tenants are abiding by the terms of their lease.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Some REO owners, including Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, are already taking steps to minimize the disruption and displacement to renters living in foreclosed-upon properties.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Vacant properties are especially problematic for communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Ideally, lenders would identify early in the process whether or not property securing delinquent loans is occupied and, if occupied, by whom.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Lenders might be provided the incentive to do so if foreclosure laws permitted lenders who agree to secure and maintain the property to accelerate foreclosure in cases where the property has been vacated.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: If a property is likely to sit vacant for long periods of time and create problems for the surrounding area, servicers might consider sale of REO properties to, or partnerships with, responsible third parties, including local governments and nonprofit groups.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: And financial institutions should look for ways to partner with community groups and governments to support strategies to stabilize communities affected by foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Last summer, the Congress set aside $3.92 billion through the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008 to assist state and local governments with REO purchases and related efforts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: It is likely that such efforts will require significantly more funding.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, regulators should consider whether to review regulations regarding real estate held for extended periods of time on bank balance sheets to be sure that they do not preclude creative solutions to the foreclosure problem.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The last credit cycle primarily involved loans secured with commercial property.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: The properties liquidated by banks and the Resolution Trust Corporation weighed on commercial property values for years.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: This time we are talking about homes, and we are talking about neighborhoods.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Whether mortgage assets are taken off banks' balance sheets, ring fenced, or left alone, the REO problem remains the same.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Regardless of which entities actually own the loan assets--be they financial institutions, investors, or government entities--the servicers who represent them are going to have to deal with large real estate inventories.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Wholesale dumping of those inventories that leads to sharply lower prices and recovery rates will not serve the interests of the public or the investors.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: But strategies to avoid dumping and to maximize the ultimate value of the properties could be beyond the normal liquidity and expertise resources of servicers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: To avoid such an outcome, owners of the assets will need to adequately fund servicers or separately engage property managers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: For example, they may need funding to repair and improve properties, which will lead to higher returns than sale of those same properties in "as is" condition.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: They may need to offer seller financing.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: Bulk sale or land banking strategies may offer the best likely outcome.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

speaker: Duke
text: In the most recent credit cycle, much of the commercial inventory was sold through auction, and many of the buyers realized a substantial profit.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market:  Next Steps
speech_venue: At the Global Association of Risk Professionalsâ Risk Management Convention, New York, New York

text: However, as I have discussed today, there is also a pressing need for more policy measures that specifically address the problems in the housing sector.
