speaker: Duke
text: It is great to be back here with community bankers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The last time I addressed this conference, I was a community banker and also chairman of the American Bankers Association.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: I never dreamed that I would be back four years later as a member of the Board of Governors.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Before I took office, I wrestled with the question of how I could contribute to the work of the Board and how difficult it might be to change from the perspective of a banker to the perspective of a public policy maker.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: So I asked a friend of mine, who had spent most of his career as an attorney before becoming an appellate court judge, just how he had made the transition from advocate to jurist.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: He told me that he found that he developed a different framework for decisionmaking, a different mindset, but one that was enriched by his experience and knowledge of the law.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: He said it happened quite naturally and predicted that I would experience the same thing.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: So I thought I would begin by talking a little about how I approach my role at the Fed and then discuss the housing and mortgage markets, with particular emphasis on the impact this crisis is having on communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: I want to emphasize that any opinions I express here today are mine alone and do not represent the opinions of anyone else within the Federal Reserve System.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), as you all know, is responsible for overseeing open market operations, which is the principal tool of monetary policy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: On a voting basis, it is composed of all of the members of the Board of Governors, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and 4 of the 11 remaining Reserve Bank presidents, who vote on a rotating basis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: While only five vote, all of the Reserve Bank presidents contribute equally to the discussion.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: My contributions to the discussion of current and projected financial and economic conditions are shaped largely by my conversations with bankers, my knowledge of bank management principles, and the Main Street perspective on the economy that I developed in my years as a banker working with consumers and small businesses.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In the six months that I have been at the Board, actions taken by bankers have had a tremendous influence on the economy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: As part of preparing for FOMC meetings, I call a number of bankers at different size banks around the country to get their assessments of conditions in their banks and in their markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: My questions recently have focused primarily on the effect of government initiatives and on lending conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: I also think through the actions that I might take as a banker if confronted by prevailing circumstances.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: For example, in evaluating the likely impact of the Treasury's recent Capital Purchase Program, I mentally walked through what would have been my own decision tree when trying to decide whether to apply for capital and, if I did receive capital, how I might use it.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In addition to the FOMC, I sit on the Board's Committee on Supervisory and Regulatory Affairs and chair the Committee on Consumer and Community Affairs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In these roles, I have been able to use my deeply ingrained knowledge of existing regulations, including their purposes and origins, as well as my familiarity with the examination process.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: And while I have long been an advocate for reducing regulatory burden, I have never questioned the need for strong regulation and supervision, only the efficiency of its implementation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: So, now I have the opportunity to shape the implementation of new regulations and review existing ones, including those for safety and soundness as well as for consumer protection.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: But, as you know, regulations are only one part of the Federal Reserve's role in ensuring a sound banking industry; those regulations must be complemented by strong supervision.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: That is, not only do we establish a set of rules for bankers to follow, but we also ensure that while abiding by those rules, the banking industry remains in an overall safe and sound condition.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In fulfilling my new role as a policymaker, I find that there are some basic beliefs that I held as a banker that continue to guide me.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Much of my time is currently absorbed by activities related to this last point, as well as the broader housing and mortgage crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In addition to my Board committee assignments, I represent the Fed on the oversight board of the HOPE for Homeowners (H4H) program, an FHA program created by the Congress that allows lenders to refinance a delinquent borrower into an FHA-insured fixed-rate mortgage if the lender and borrower agree to certain conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Again representing the Fed, I also recently joined the board of directors of NeighborWorks America, a national, congressionally chartered nonprofit organization focused on affordable housing and, in the face of growing needs, on responses to problems facing communities as a result of the housing and mortgage crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Today I would like to share my thoughts about the problems in housing markets and mortgage lending, with a focus on how they affect communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Every time someone talks of troubled mortgages on bank balance sheets, they are also talking about distressed homeowners, distressed neighborhoods and distressed communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: I've heard many of you say to me, "We didn't cause this problem.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We didn't make any subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: It's not fair that we should have to pay the price."
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: I understand that many of you may be frustrated because you feel you have acted in a prudent manner while others have not.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: But additional parties are also suffering from the imprudent actions of others, such as the homeowners in your community who dutifully pay their mortgages but still see their houses fall sharply in value.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: More broadly, the recovery of the macroeconomy and the financial system are being inhibited by ongoing problems in the housing and mortgage markets.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: At this moment, we all simply need to do whatever we can to address the enormous challenges facing our communities, including those of us who believe we were being prudent and were not a cause of the difficulty in the first place.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: With that in mind, let me delve a bit more into the details of the current housing problems and offer some thoughts about what might be done to improve the situation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The Current Weakness in Housing Markets Housing activity remains extraordinarily weak.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Sales of new and existing homes have been running at a pace that is 60 percent of that seen at the peak in 2005.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Single-family housing starts are now less than one-quarter of their peak level.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: With the cutbacks in construction, inventories of unsold new homes have declined, but the months' supply--that is, inventories relative to sales--is still very high by historical standards.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The inventory of existing homes for sale is also quite elevated--and it would be even higher if not for would-be sellers who have withheld or withdrawn their homes from the market amid poor selling conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We have also seen sharp drops in home prices.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: When home prices were at their peak three years ago, most analysts agreed that housing valuations seemed to be substantially higher than warranted by fundamentals.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: However, home prices at the national level are now 18 percent off their peak, with some states, such as California and Florida, experiencing declines on the order of 40 percent.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: 1 These declines may have reversed much, or perhaps all, of the earlier overvaluation.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: That said, futures markets and many analysts foresee further declines.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Expectations that house price declines have not yet reached their trough are probably deterring some prospective homeowners from making purchases and thereby contributing to the current weakness in housing demand.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: A key factor inhibiting recovery is that the adverse conditions in the housing and mortgage markets have been, and continue to be, mutually reinforcing.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: As I am sure you are painfully aware, delinquencies on mortgages have risen sharply in recent years.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: By way of background, the problems began in the nonprime mortgage market.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: As house prices boomed in the middle part of this decade, mortgage originators relaxed underwriting standards and extended mortgages with low or no down payments to households with weak credit histories or those that did not fully document their income.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Many of these loans had low initial interest rates that reset to market rates after a couple of years, which resulted in a significant increase in the monthly payment.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Had house prices continued to rise, many borrowers would have been able to refinance to avoid higher payments and perhaps to extract accumulated home equity to use for future payments.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: However, the downturn in house prices meant that many borrowers did not have sufficient equity to refinance.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Payment problems began to rise, which, in turn, led lenders to tighten standards and made it even more difficult for borrowers to obtain new loans, which put even more upward pressure on delinquencies.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Eventually, investors became unwilling to fund higher-risk mortgages at any price.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Although the current problems appear to be rooted in high-risk subprime lending, I would like to dispel the notion that these problems were caused in any way by Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) lending.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The CRA is designed to promote lending in low- to moderate-income areas; it is not designed to encourage high-risk lending or poor underwriting.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Our analysis of the data finds no evidence, in fact, that CRA lending is in any way responsible for the current crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In our analysis of loan originations, we found that approximately 60 percent of higher-priced loans went to middle- or higher-income borrowers or neighborhoods, which are populations not targeted by the CRA.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Additionally, more than 20 percent of the higher-priced loans that were extended in low- to moderate-income areas, or to low- to moderate-income borrowers, were loans originated by lenders not covered by the CRA.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In fact, the analysis found that only 6 percent of all higher-priced loans were made by CRA-covered lenders to borrowers and neighborhoods targeted by the CRA.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: This very small share makes it hard to imagine how CRA could have caused, or even contributed in a meaningful way, to the current crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Further support for this conclusion comes from our finding that serious delinquency rates for subprime loans are high in all neighborhood-income categories, not only those in lower-income areas, as might be thought if the CRA were a contributing force to the subprime crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The problems in the high-risk mortgage market, together with the more general pullback in risk-taking across virtually all financial assets, reduced the willingness of lenders to fund all types of mortgages.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We are now seeing widespread payment problems in every category of mortgages.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: To be sure, the deterioration partly reflects households straining to meet their mortgage obligations amid the broader weakening of macroeconomic conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: However, it also reflects the fact that reduced home equity and tighter mortgage credit have impaired borrowers' ability to refinance their mortgages in order to cope with income loss, unexpected expenses, or adverse life events.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: According to the latest data, 25 percent of subprime loans and 13 percent of near-prime loans are now seriously delinquent--that is, more than 90 days past due or in foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The serious delinquency rate for prime mortgages, at between 3 percent and 4 percent, is much lower than for nonprime loans, but it has doubled over the past year.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Foreclosures have also risen sharply.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The available data suggests that lenders initiated 2-1/4 million foreclosures last year, more than twice the number seen in 2006.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: 3 In the past, about one-half of foreclosures initiated were cured through a repayment plan or some other arrangement, but the remaining one-half resulted in the loss of a home.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The share resulting in home loss could well be higher now given the large numbers of distressed households and the bleak underlying economic conditions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Addressing the Problems in Housing and Mortgage Markets Several considerations underscore the need for policymakers to take further actions to address the current problems in the housing and mortgage sectors.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: To begin, the weakness in the housing sector remains a significant drag on the macroeconomy and is reinforcing the strains in the financial system.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Moreover, the wave of foreclosures has the potential to exacerbate the problems going forward.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In past housing cycles, house prices have tended to fall below the level warranted by fundamentals, presumably as weak market conditions led sellers to make aggressive price cuts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The potential for an overcorrection of house prices in this cycle seems particularly acute given the potential for foreclosures to create a glut of properties for sale.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: A high level of foreclosures results in lower prices, and lower prices tend to accelerate the pace of foreclosures.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: And, of course, further large declines in house prices would accentuate the broader problems in the macroeconomy and financial system through the channels that I just discussed.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Foreclosures also cause significant distress among the families that lose their homes.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Whether the foreclosure is the result of inadequate underwriting by the mortgage lender, irresponsibility on the part of the homeowner, or uncontrollable life events such as job loss, the result is the same:  Displaced families with depleted resources and impaired credit have difficulty finding a new place to live.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: They may have to move significant distances, which may affect their ability to retain their jobs and disrupt other aspects of their lives as well as the lives of their family members.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, one in five foreclosures appears to be affecting renter-occupied units.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The families in these units may also be displaced, even if they are paying their rent on time and abiding by the terms of their lease agreement.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Such disruptions, apart from creating personal and emotional strains, can also have detrimental economic effects.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Large numbers of displaced families will further strain inadequate supplies of rental housing that are affordable to low- and moderate-income families.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Although the overall supply of rental housing has been slowly expanding in recent years, new units have largely been built for the higher end of the market, with median asking rents being 38 percent higher than average, while more-affordable units have been demolished or permanently removed from the inventory.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: 4 In the current environment, this lack of new production has been exacerbated by the restricted availability of financing for multifamily housing, reduced support by government-sponsored enterprises for multifamily housing, and lower utilization of the Low Income Housing Tax Credit program.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In areas where foreclosures are concentrated, communities will suffer.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Clusters of vacant properties can foster crime, such as vandalism and arson, and studies have shown that they lead to lower house prices throughout the neighborhood.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: 5 Municipal governments may have to spend more on maintaining properties and preventing crime just when resources are stretched thin, in part because of the reduced tax revenue associated with lower house prices.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Such spending may well crowd out the provision of other types of public services.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Fiscal and monetary stimulus directed at improving employment conditions and federal support for housing finance will ultimately strengthen the housing market.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: However, we also need measures that directly address the foreclosure problem associated with the current crisis.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In designing such measures, we must consider that there are different types of borrowers.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: First, there are distressed borrowers who can avoid foreclosure through an appropriate modification of their loan.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Second, there are some borrowers who, due to resources or circumstance, will be unable or unwilling to sustain their mortgage payments even with reasonable loan adjustments from the lender or support from government programs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In such cases, foreclosures will happen, and we need to limit both the direct costs to the lender and the borrower as well as the broader social costs.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Of course, there is a third group of borrowers--those who are still successfully meeting their mortgage obligations.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: One might be tempted to view these households as a lesser concern, but we must be mindful that they will be more likely to shift into one of the distressed groups if we do not reduce both the number of foreclosures and the cost of the foreclosures that do occur.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Reducing Preventable Foreclosures To help those distressed households for which foreclosure can be prevented, servicers must implement effective and sustainable modifications.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Key private and public steps toward preventing unnecessary foreclosures have already been taken, but much more must be done.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: While community bankers typically do not have large portfolios on which to perform wholesale modifications, I would urge you to be sure that you are making reasonable accommodations whenever possible to keep homeowners in their homes.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: While speed and volume in modifications are important, in my view, it is equally essential that the new obligations be sustainable in the long run.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: By "sustainable" I mean that the payment should be fixed for the life of the loan, it should be affordable, and it should be based upon verified income.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In changing the terms of the mortgage, servicers may start with changing the interest rate or adjusting the maturity to make the payments more affordable, but they also need to consider whether writing down loan principal amounts make sense.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Doing the latter may be more effective at reducing the probability of redefault.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: 6 These design principles for modifications are all included in the Homeownership Preservation Policy recently adopted by the Federal Reserve Board.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: 7 The Federal Reserve announced that it would apply this policy to the residential mortgage assets held by the special purpose vehicles established by the Federal Reserve to facilitate the acquisition of Bear Stearns by JPMorgan Chase and to assist the American International Group, Inc.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Reducing the Costs When Foreclosures Cannot Be Prevented Without in any way minimizing the need for continued emphasis on foreclosure prevention, I don't believe we can fully formulate appropriate policy responses to the crisis unless we acknowledge and address the large numbers of foreclosures that are not avoidable.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We are likely only beginning to see the serious costs of the foreclosures that have already been initiated, both because of the often-substantial amount of time required to complete a foreclosure and because the costs likely compound as the number of foreclosures grows larger.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Moreover, even under optimistic assumptions for the number of loan modifications and other forms of private and public assistance that may be realized, the pace at which foreclosures are initiated is likely to remain extremely elevated for some time.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Just as public focus, experimentation, and policy debate have informed best practices with regard to loan modifications, we must also begin the work of developing responsible protocols for the management of foreclosures and real estate inventory.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Minimizing the amount of time that properties remain vacant and maximizing the price at which they are sold will serve the interests of both lenders and the communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: During the time properties do remain vacant, servicers have a responsibility to follow local codes and ensure that the properties are secured and maintained.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: At this moment, lenders and communities alike are woefully under-resourced and unprepared for the volume of real estate that will need to be processed.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Some attention has already been focused on getting renters or owners into real estate owned (REO) and vacant properties and thus off of servicers' books--something that is in the shared interest of servicers, investors, and communities, particularly as the inventories of these types of properties mount.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: At the national level, there is some movement to enable state and local governments, as well as nonprofits, to purchase properties from servicers' REO inventories where sales are otherwise stagnant.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Such efforts are challenging in many areas because of a lack of financial resources and experience in the kinds of activities that are required.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Some help will be provided through the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008, in which the Congress set aside $3.92 billion to assist state and local governments with REO purchases and related efforts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The Department of Housing and Urban Development created the Neighborhood Stabilization Program (NSP) to distribute these funds.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Many servicers are stepping up their efforts to sell their large and growing inventories of REO properties, although setting an appropriate price in the current environment remains difficult.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: To facilitate REO sales, the National Community Stabilization Trust (NCST), a new entity formed by four national nonprofit intermediaries, is trying to create a common platform for servicers to efficiently sell REO properties to public entities and nonprofit organizations.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Some REO owners, such as Fannie Mae, are also creating dedicated sales channels to sell REO properties to public entities and nonprofits, either through the NCST or through discounted bulk sales.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: And some local governments are crafting comprehensive approaches using the NSP funds to bring in private- and public-sector entities to manage and sell REO inventories.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The Federal Reserve has also taken steps to help address the costs of foreclosures on communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: The Community Affairs offices of the Board of Governors and all 12 Reserve Banks held a series of forums in 2008, entitled "Recovery, Renewal, Rebuilding," that explored the problems and highlighted promising solutions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We have also partnered with NeighborWorks America to support its efforts to help community leaders grappling with these issues; that effort has led to the creation of new tools, training, and the spread of information.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: But current efforts are not sufficient to deal with the scale and scope of the problem, and more needs to be done.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: State and local governments and nonprofits are working hard but often lack the capacity and scale to address the magnitude of the REO disposition problem.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: More dollars alone will not solve this problem.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: State and local governments need to do more to partner with private-sector entities that have experience managing scattered-site housing inventories, including rental housing.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, we need to make sure that we are using all of the available public-sector capacity--such as state housing finance agencies and local public housing authorities--that have experience managing affordable rental housing inventories.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Finally, we need to do more to explore creative solutions to speed the acquisition of REO properties so that they do not languish vacant.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Given the likely number of properties that will enter foreclosure and the time and resources involved in the foreclosure process, financial institutions can help minimize the cost by developing clear policies and procedures for approval of short sales and deeds-in-lieu-of-foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: For homeowners who cannot, or no longer wish to, stay in their homes, such strategies release them from their obligation and avoid foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Some institutions already offer a so-called fresh start or cash-for-keys program, in which they provide a small payment to consumers in exchange for voluntarily surrendering the deed to the home.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Such arrangements reduce the cost of foreclosure and provide consumers with relocation assistance.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Other lenders are offering borrowers the option to remain in their home as renters rather than owners.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: More lenders should consider these options, perhaps in conjunction with loan modification programs, as further inducement for borrowers to engage in discussions about loan resolution.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: At the same time, governments might develop policies to accelerate foreclosure in cases where the property has been vacated and the lender has agreed to secure and maintain the property.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: If renters occupy the property, servicers of REO properties should extend existing lease arrangements whenever possible and while tenants are abiding by the terms of their lease.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Some REO owners, including Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, are already taking steps to minimize the disruption and displacement to renters living in foreclosed-upon properties.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: If a property is likely to sit vacant for long periods of time and create problems for the surrounding area, servicers might consider sale of REO properties to, or partnerships with, responsible third parties, including local governments and nonprofit groups.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Financial institutions should look for ways to partner with community groups and governments to support strategies to stabilize communities affected by foreclosure.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: They can bring invaluable technical capacity to plan and execute stabilization efforts.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Banks can also support efforts to reuse REO properties by providing home loans to new homebuyers and by financing nonprofit entities and others for the acquisition and rehabilitation of REO properties.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, they can help victims of foreclosure to rebuild their credit histories and thereby facilitate their re-entry into the economic mainstream.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Finally, regulators should consider whether existing regulations regarding real estate held for extended periods of time on bank balance sheets act as an obstacle to creative solutions to the foreclosure problem.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Conclusion In summary, broad policy measures are a central ingredient to restoring the health of the U.S. economy and global financial system.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: However, as I have discussed today, there is also a pressing need for more targeted policy measures that specifically address the current problems in the housing sector.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We need considerable public support for housing finance until private credit and securitization markets are restarted.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: We need to strengthen and augment our efforts to reduce preventable foreclosures.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: In addition, we need to turn far greater attention to limiting the costs of foreclosures that do occur.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Such efforts are not only in the interest of the families who are directly affected and their immediate communities, but are also in the interest of the financial institutions involved and the broader economy.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Because much of the cost does not occur as soon as a foreclosure has been initiated and can grow with time, we must be forward-looking and affirmatively engage in efforts to mitigate the consequences now.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: As community bankers, you have a long history of engagement in your communities.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: You have served on the boards of public and nonprofit entities focused on housing.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: You have built Habitat for Humanity houses, and you have rebuilt entire neighborhoods following natural disasters.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Your financial resources will be needed as we work toward solutions for the current crisis, but, even more important, your experience, expertise, contacts, and creativity will be needed.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: If you believe in the saying that "all real estate markets are local," you also understand that it will take local knowledge to assess community needs and craft solutions.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: If you are not quite sure where to start, contact your local housing nonprofit or Federal Reserve Bank.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Contact municipal authorities or housing counselors.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: Partner with other banks in your market or do it alone.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Duke
text: As always, your communities depend on you.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities

text: See Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (2009), " Board Announces Policy to Help Avoid Preventable Foreclosures on Certain Residential Mortgage Assets Held, Owned, or Controlled by a Federal Reserve Bank ," press release, January 30; and Board of Governors (2009), "Homeownership Preservation Policy for Residential Mortgage Assets (26 KB PDF)," Board policy, January 30.
speech_title: Stabilizing the Housing Market: Focus on Communities
speech_venue: At the American Bankers Association National Conference for Community Bankers, Phoenix, Arizona

speaker: Bernanke
text: We live in extraordinarily challenging times for the global economy and for economic policymakers, not least for central banks such as the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you know, the recent economic statistics have been dismal, with many economies, including ours, having fallen into recession.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And behind those statistics, we must never forget, are millions of people struggling with lost jobs, lost homes, and lost confidence in their economic future.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In examples that resonate with me personally, the unemployment rate in the small town in South Carolina where I grew up has risen to 14 percent, and I learned the other day that what had once been my family home was recently put through foreclosure.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Traditionally the most conservative of institutions, central banks around the world have responded to this unprecedented crisis with force and innovation.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the United States, the Federal Reserve has done, and will continue to do, everything possible within the limits of its authority to assist in restoring our nation to financial stability and economic prosperity as quickly as possible.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Policy innovation has been necessary because conventional monetary policies, which focus on influencing short-term interest rates, have proven insufficient to overcome the effects of the financial crisis on credit conditions and the broader economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To further ease financial conditions, beyond what can be attained by reducing short-term interest rates, the Federal Reserve has taken additional steps to improve the functioning of credit markets and to increase the supply of credit to households and businesses--a policy strategy that I have called "credit easing."
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the first portion of my remarks, I will briefly outline the three principal approaches to easing credit that we have undertaken, over and above cutting the short-term interest rate, and assess their effectiveness to date.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Each of these policy approaches involves the provision of credit or the purchase of debt securities by the Federal Reserve, which collectively have resulted in a substantial expansion in the size of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The second portion of my remarks addresses some issues raised by the changes in the size of the Fed's balance sheet.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In particular, I will discuss how the size of the balance sheet affects the ability of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the body that sets monetary policy, to foster maximum sustainable employment and price stability, as well as the steps that are being taken to manage the balance sheet appropriately.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Finally, the expansion of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet has raised some concerns--and led to some misconceptions--about the credit risk being taken by the Fed.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will address the issue of credit risk today.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And I would also like to talk about steps that the Fed is taking to improve the transparency of its programs to the public, consistent with our obligations in a democracy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Federal Reserve Policy during the Crisis The Federal Reserve has responded forcefully to the crisis since its emergence in the summer of 2007.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The FOMC began to ease monetary policy in September 2007, reducing the target for the federal funds rate, its policy instrument, by 50 basis points, or 1/2 percentage point.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As indications of economic weakness proliferated, the Committee continued to respond, bringing down its target for the federal funds rate by a cumulative 325 basis points by the spring of 2008.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In historical comparison, this policy response stands out as exceptionally rapid and proactive.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Monetary easing helped support employment and incomes during the first year of the crisis.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Unfortunately, the intensification of financial turbulence last fall led to further significant deterioration in the economic outlook.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Committee responded by cutting the target for the federal funds rate an additional 100 basis points in October, with half of that reduction coming as part of an unprecedented coordinated interest rate cut by six major central banks on October 8.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In December, the Committee reduced its target further, setting a range of 0 to 25 basis points for the target federal funds rate.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed's monetary easing has been reflected in significant declines in a number of lending rates, especially shorter-term rates, thus offsetting to some degree the effects of the financial turmoil on the cost of credit.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, that offset has been incomplete, as widening credit spreads, more-restrictive lending standards, and credit market dysfunction have worked against the monetary easing and led to tighter financial conditions overall.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, in addition to easing monetary policy, the Federal Reserve has made use of a range of additional tools to ease credit conditions and support the broader economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These additional components of the Fed's toolkit can be divided into three sets.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The first set is closely tied to the central bank's traditional role of provider of short-term liquidity to sound financial institutions.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Over the course of the crisis, the Fed has taken a number of extraordinary actions to ensure that financial institutions have adequate access to short-term credit.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In fulfilling its traditional lending function, the Federal Reserve enhances the stability of our financial system, increases the willingness of financial institutions to extend credit, and helps to ease conditions in interbank lending markets, thereby reducing the overall cost of capital to banks.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, some interest rates, including the rates on some adjustable-rate mortgages, are tied contractually to key interbank rates, such as the London interbank offered rate (Libor).
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To the extent that the provision of ample liquidity to banks reduces Libor, other borrowers will also see their payments decline.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because interbank markets are global in scope, the Federal Reserve has also approved temporary bilateral liquidity agreements with 14 foreign central banks.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These so-called currency swap facilities have allowed these central banks to acquire dollars from the Federal Reserve that they may lend to financial institutions in their own jurisdictions.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The purpose of these swaps is to ease conditions in dollar funding markets globally.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Improvements in global interbank markets, in turn, promote greater stability in other markets, such as money markets and foreign exchange markets.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although the provision of ample liquidity by the central bank to financial institutions is a time-tested approach to reducing financial strains, it is no panacea.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Today, concerns about capital, asset quality, and credit risk continue to limit the willingness of many intermediaries to extend credit, notwithstanding the access of these firms to central bank liquidity.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, lending to financial institutions does not directly address instability or declining liquidity in critical nonbank markets, such as the commercial paper market or the market for asset-backed securities, which under normal circumstances are major sources of credit for U.S. households and firms.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address these issues, the Federal Reserve has developed a second set of policy tools, which involve the provision of liquidity directly to borrowers and investors in key credit markets.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, we have introduced facilities to purchase highly rated commercial paper at a term of three months and to provide backup liquidity for money market mutual funds.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The purpose of these facilities is to serve, once again in classic central bank fashion, as backstop liquidity provider, in these cases to institutions and markets that were destabilized by the rapid withdrawal of funds by short-term creditors and investors.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury have jointly announced a facility--expected to be operational shortly--that will lend against AAA-rated asset-backed securities collateralized by recently originated student loans, auto loans, credit card loans, and loans guaranteed by the Small Business Administration.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Last week, in conjunction with the Treasury, we announced that we were prepared to expand significantly this facility, known as the Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility, or TALF, to encompass other types of newly issued AAA-rated asset-backed securities, such as commercial mortgage-backed securities and private-label mortgage-backed securities, as well.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: If this program works as planned, it should lead to lower rates and greater availability of consumer, business, and mortgage credit.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's third set of tools for supporting the functioning of credit markets involves the purchase of longer-term securities for the Fed's portfolio.
