speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, we are purchasing up to $100 billion in the debt of government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs) and up to $500 billion in mortgage-backed securities guaranteed by federal agencies by midyear.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve is engaged in continuous assessment of the effectiveness of its credit-related tools, and we have generally been encouraged by the market responses.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our lending to financial institutions has helped to relax the severe liquidity strains experienced by many firms and has been associated with improvements in interbank lending markets; for example, we believe that liquidity provision by the Fed and other central banks is a principal reason that liquidity pressures around the end of the year--often a period of heightened liquidity strains--were relatively modest.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Libor has fallen sharply as well.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our commercial paper facility has helped to stabilize that market, lowering rates significantly and allowing high-quality firms access to financing at terms longer than a few days.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Together with other government programs, our actions to stabilize the money market mutual fund industry have also shown some success, as the sharp withdrawals from funds seen in September have given way to modest inflows.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And rates on 30-year conforming fixed-rate mortgages have fallen nearly 1 percentage point since we announced the program to purchase GSE-related securities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Thus, taken together, these policies appear to give the Federal Reserve some scope to affect credit conditions and economic performance, notwithstanding that the conventional tool of monetary policy, the federal funds rate, is nearly as low as it can go.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's Policies and its Balance Sheet The various credit-related policies I have described have implications for the Federal Reserve's balance sheet.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the remainder of my remarks I will discuss those implications as well as some related issues.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The three sets of policy tools I have focused on today--lending to financial institutions, providing liquidity directly to key credit markets, and buying longer-term securities--each represents a use of the asset side of the Fed's balance sheet.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Specifically, loans that the Fed extends--either to financial institutions, through the discount window and related facilities, or to other borrowers in programs like our commercial paper facility--are recorded as assets on our balance sheet, as are securities acquired in the open market, such as the GSE securities we are purchasing.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed's assets also include about $500 billion of Treasury securities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: About 5 percent of our balance sheet, or $100 billion, consists of assets we acquired in the government interventions to prevent the failures of Bear Stearns and American International Group (AIG).
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: I won't say much about those interventions today, except to note that the failures of those companies would have posed enormous risks to the stability of our financial system and economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because the United States has no well-specified set of rules for dealing with the potential failure of systemically critical nondepository financial institutions, we believed that the best of the bad options available was to work with the Treasury to take the actions we did to avoid those collapses.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The liability side of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet is relatively simple, consisting primarily of currency issuance (Federal Reserve notes) and reserves held by the banking system on deposit with the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The various credit-related policies I have described today all act to increase the size of both the asset and liability sides of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, the purchase of $1 billion of GSE securities, paid for by crediting the deposit account of the seller's bank at the Federal Reserve, increases the Fed's balance sheet by $1 billion, with the acquired securities appearing as an asset, and the seller's bank's deposit at the Fed being the offsetting liability.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The quantitative impact of our credit actions on the balance sheet has been large; its size has nearly doubled over the past year, to just under $2 trillion.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some observers have expressed the concern that, by expanding its balance sheet, the Federal Reserve will ultimately stoke inflation.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed's lending activities have indeed resulted in a large increase in the reserves held by banks and thus in the narrowest definition of the money supply, the monetary base.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 1 However, banks are choosing to leave the great bulk of their excess reserves idle, in most cases on deposit with the Fed.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consequently, the rates of growth of broader monetary aggregates, such as M1 and M2, have been much lower than that of the monetary base.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 At this point, with global economic activity weak and commodity prices at low levels, we see little risk of unacceptably high inflation in the near term; indeed, we expect inflation to be quite low for some time.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, at some point, when credit markets and the economy have begun to recover, the Federal Reserve will have to moderate growth in the money supply and begin to raise the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To reduce policy accommodation, the Fed will have to unwind some of its credit-easing programs and allow its balance sheet to shrink.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To some extent, this unwinding will happen automatically, as improvements in credit markets should reduce the need to use Fed facilities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, where possible, we have tried to set lending rates and other terms at levels that are likely to be increasingly unattractive to borrowers as financial conditions normalize.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, some programs--those authorized under the Federal Reserve's so-called 13(3) authority, which requires a finding that conditions in financial markets are "unusual and exigent"--will, by law, have to be phased out once credit market conditions substantially normalize.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: However, the principal factor determining the timing and pace of that process will be the Federal Reserve's assessment of the condition of credit markets and the prospects for the economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: A significant shrinking of the balance sheet can be accomplished relatively quickly, as a substantial portion of the assets that the Federal Reserve holds--including loans to financial institutions, temporary central bank liquidity swaps, and purchases of commercial paper--are short-term in nature and can simply be allowed to run off as the various programs and facilities are scaled back or shut down.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As the size of the balance sheet and the quantity of excess reserves in the system decline, the Federal Reserve will be able to return to its traditional means of making monetary policy--namely, by setting a target for the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Importantly, the management of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet and the conduct of monetary policy in the future will be made easier by the recent congressional action to give the Fed the authority to pay interest on bank reserves.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Because banks should be unwilling to lend reserves at a rate lower than they can receive from the Fed, the interest rate the Fed pays on bank reserves should help to set a floor on the overnight interest rate.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, other tools are available or can be developed to improve control of the federal funds rate during the exit stage.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, the Treasury could resume its recent practice of issuing supplementary financing bills and placing the funds with the Federal Reserve; the issuance of these bills effectively drains reserves from the banking system, thereby improving monetary control.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: As we consider new programs or the expansion of old ones, the Federal Reserve will carefully weigh the implications for the exit strategy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And we will take all necessary actions to ensure that the unwinding of our programs is accomplished smoothly and in a timely way, consistent with meeting our obligation to foster maximum employment and price stability.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Credit Risk and Transparency Two other frequently asked questions about the Federal Reserve's balance sheet are: First, how much credit risk is the Fed taking in its lending activities?
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And, second, is the Fed informing the public adequately about these activities?
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address the first question, for the great bulk of Fed lending, the credit risks are extremely low.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The provision of short-term credit to financial institutions--our traditional function--exposes the Federal Reserve to minimal credit risk, as the loans we make to financial institutions are generally short-term, overcollateralized, and made with recourse to the borrowing firm.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In the case of the liquidity swaps, the foreign central banks are responsible for repaying the Federal Reserve, not the financial institutions that ultimately receive the funds, and the Fed receives an equivalent amount of foreign currency in exchange for the dollars it provides foreign central banks.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Treasury stands behind the debt and other securities issued by the GSEs.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our special lending programs have also been set up to minimize our credit risk.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The largest program, the commercial paper funding facility, accepts only the most highly rated paper.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It also charges borrowers a premium, which is set aside against possible losses.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: And the TALF, the facility that will lend against securities backed by consumer and small business loans, is a joint Federal Reserve-Treasury program, as I mentioned, and capital provided by the Treasury will help insulate the Federal Reserve from credit losses.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The transactions we undertook to prevent the systemically destabilizing failures of Bear Stearns and AIG, which, as I noted, make up about 5 percent of our balance sheet, carry more risk than our traditional activities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But we intend, over time, to sell the assets acquired in those transactions in a way that maximizes the return to taxpayers, and we expect to recover the credit we have extended.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, in assessing the financial risks of those transactions, once again one must also consider the very grave risks our nation would have incurred had public policy makers not acted in those instances.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Finally, I should remind you that all the Federal Reserve's assets pay interest, and the expansion of our balance sheet thereby implies increased interest income, income that will accrue to the benefit of the federal budget.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: From the point of view of the federal government, the Federal Reserve's activities do not imply greater expenditure or indebtedness.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: To the contrary, the Federal Reserve's interest earnings have always been, and will continue to be, a significant source of income for the Treasury.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: On the second question, transparency, I firmly believe that central banks should provide as much information as possible, both for reasons of democratic accountability and because many of our policies are likely to be more effective if they are well understood by the markets and the public.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: During my time at the Federal Reserve, the FOMC has taken important steps to increase the transparency of monetary policy, such as moving up the publication of the minutes of policy meetings and adopting the practice of providing projections of the evolution of the economy at longer horizons and four times per year rather than twice.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Later today, with the release of the minutes of the most recent FOMC meeting, we will be making an additional significant enhancement in Federal Reserve communications: To supplement the current economic projections by governors and Reserve Bank presidents for the next three years, we will also publish their projections of the longer-term values (at a horizon of, for example, five to six years) of output growth, unemployment, and inflation, under the assumptions of appropriate monetary policy and the absence of new shocks to the economy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: These longer-term projections will inform the public of the Committee participants' estimates of the rate of growth of output and the unemployment rate that appear to be sustainable in the long run in the United States, taking into account important influences such as the trend growth rates of productivity and the labor force, improvements in worker education and skills, the efficiency of the labor market at matching workers and jobs, government policies affecting technological development or the labor market, and other factors.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The longer-term projections of inflation may be interpreted, in turn, as the rate of inflation that FOMC participants see as most consistent with the dual mandate given to it by the Congress--that is, the rate of inflation that promotes maximum sustainable employment while also delivering reasonable price stability.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: This further extension of the quarterly projections should provide the public a clearer picture of FOMC participants' policy strategy for promoting maximum employment and price stability over time.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Also, increased clarity about the FOMC's views regarding longer-term inflation should help to better stabilize the public's inflation expectations, thus contributing to keeping actual inflation from rising too high or falling too low.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Likewise, the Federal Reserve is committed to keeping the Congress and the public informed about its lending programs and balance sheet.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, we continue to add to the information shown in the Fed's H.4.1 statistical release, which provides weekly detail on the balance sheet and the amounts outstanding for each of the Federal Reserve's lending facilities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Extensive additional information about each of the Federal Reserve's lending programs is available online.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 The Fed also provides bimonthly reports to the Congress on each of its programs that rely on the section 13(3) authorities.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Generally, our disclosure policies are consistent with the current best practices of major central banks around the world.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, the Federal Reserve's internal controls and management practices are closely monitored by an independent inspector general, outside private-sector auditors, and internal management and operations divisions, and through periodic reviews by the Government Accountability Office.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: All that said, recent developments have understandably led to a substantial increase in the public's interest in the Fed's balance sheet and programs.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For this reason, we at the Fed have begun a thorough review of our disclosure policies and the effectiveness of our communication.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Today I would like to mention two initiatives.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, to improve public access to information concerning Fed policies and programs, in coming days we will unveil a new website that will bring together in a systematic and comprehensive way the full range of information that the Federal Reserve already makes available, supplemented by explanations, discussions, and analyses.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, at my request, Board Vice Chairman Donald Kohn is leading a committee that will review our current publications and disclosure policies relating to the Fed's balance sheet and lending policies.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The presumption of the committee will be that the public has a right to know, and that the nondisclosure of information must be affirmatively justified by clearly articulated criteria for confidentiality, based on factors such as reasonable claims to privacy, the confidentiality of supervisory information, and the need to ensure the effectiveness of policy.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion Extraordinary times call for extraordinary measures.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Responding to the very difficult economic and financial challenges we face, the Federal Reserve has gone beyond traditional monetary policy making to develop new policy tools to address the dysfunctions in the nation's credit markets.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have done so in a responsible way: The credit risk associated with our nontraditional policies is exceptionally low, and, by carefully monitoring our balance sheet and developing tools to drain bank reserves as needed, we will ensure that policy accommodation can be reversed at the appropriate time to avoid risks of future inflation.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We provide a great deal of information about our lending programs and our balance sheet to the Congress and the public.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: But, as I have discussed today, we will do more on this front, both expanding the information we provide and improving how we communicate that information.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: Increased transparency is the best way to demonstrate that the Federal Reserve's nontraditional policies are well conceived, well managed, and produce substantial public benefit.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: The monetary base is the sum of currency in circulation and bank reserves.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: M1 consists of currency, traveler's checks, demand deposits, and other checkable deposits.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: M2 consists of M1 plus savings deposits, small-denomination time deposits, and balances in retail money market mutual funds.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: M2 has grown more rapidly than normal in recent months, at about a 15 percent annual rate on a quarterly average basis in the fourth quarter.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We attribute this increase primarily to investors' demand for greater safety, which has led them to increase their holdings of government-guaranteed bank deposits.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: We expect growth in M2 to slow considerably in 2009, barring a similar shift in portfolio preferences.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: For links and references, see Ben S. Bernanke (2009), " Federal Reserve Programs to Strengthen Credit Markets and the Economy ," testimony before the Committee on Financial Services, U.S. House of Representatives, February 10.
speech_title: Federal Reserve Policies to Ease Credit and Their Implications for the Fed's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the National Press Club Luncheon, National Press Club, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: I am pleased to be here to discuss the future of the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA).
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: As many of you probably know, I joined the Federal Reserve Board last year after having spent many years as a community banker.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: My experience gives me both a practical and theoretical interest in today's discussion of CRA's future.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: When the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston celebrated the 30 th Anniversary of CRA's enactment, it did so by hosting a forum in October 2007 that focused not just on the law's contributions to making financial services more readily available in low- and moderate-income communities, but also on the challenges of applying the law in a financial landscape that is vastly different from the one that existed in 1977.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: It was at that gathering of researchers, regulators, bankers, nonprofit practitioners, and community advocates familiar with the CRA that Congressman Barney Frank challenged the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston to collect the best thinking about how the CRA might be improved for the future.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The Bank took this challenge to heart and, together with the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, invited an impressive group of experts to contribute to the creation of a publication serving as the center of discussion at today's forum, Revisiting the CRA:  Perspectives on the Future of the Community Reinvestment Act .
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: This volume presents a variety of perspectives from many who have been closely involved in the development and implementation of CRA policy over the years.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: As one might imagine, there is no shortage of good ideas contained in these pages including suggestions for statutory as well as regulatory changes.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: While many divergent views are expressed in this publication, its most striking feature is an expression of a shared understanding that access to financial services for all, including low- or moderate-income communities and individuals continues to be an important goal for policymakers.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In my remarks today, I will highlight what I consider to be the most compelling reasons for making changes to the CRA at this time, discuss many of the themes and issues raised in this publication, and suggest a framework for how, as policymakers concerned with ensuring the full participation of every individual in our economic recovery, we might weigh the various policy options before us.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: CRA :  A Model for Government Intervention Being among experts today, I need not revisit how CRA came into being.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Suffice it to say that Congress, concerned with the worsening condition of many older, urban neighborhoods in the 1970s, wanted to address the lending practices of some financial institutions that took deposits from households in their local communities but made loans and investments outside those same communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In addition to this disinvestment, some lenders engaged in redlining, a practice based sometimes on race, at other times on income, and in still others on both factors.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: These practices motivated Congress to enact the CRA and, in so doing, it clarified an affirmative obligation for banks and thrifts to serve the credit needs of their entire communities, including low- and moderate-income areas.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: At the time, Congress justified this obligation by citing the special privileges conferred upon depository institutions including federal deposit insurance.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: By focusing the attention of regulators on this obligation and requiring that a financial institution's performance under the CRA be considered part of its application to merge or acquire another institution, the law provided a strong incentive to meet community credit needs while leaving regulators with a great deal of flexibility to improve upon the implementing regulations as markets evolved.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The most significant changes to the CRA regulations were in response to an executive order issued in 1993 by President Clinton that directed banking agencies to make regulations more performance-oriented.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The regulations created several evaluation methods based on a bank's size and business strategy.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In particular, they created separate lending, investment, and service-test evaluation criteria for large banks.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The revisions helped to stimulate increased lending and investment activity in low- and moderate-income areas.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In fact, some studies suggest that these changes to the regulations coincided with an increase in annual lending commitments from $ 1.6 billion in 1990 to $103 billion in 1999.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: 1 Research that directly tested for the effects of CRA, by comparing mortgage lending volumes and neighborhood outcomes in neighborhoods just above and just below CRA's income threshold, shows that the law has led to additional lending and has had favorable effects on homeownership rates, home values, and vacancy rates.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: CRA was written in a simpler time for banks.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: By and large, a local bank's focus, even that of a larger one, was local.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Over time, however, it has become apparent that changes in the structure of the financial industry since CRA's enactment pose a significant challenge to the law as it is written.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The notion of serving a local community has been challenged not only by industry consolidation that has resulted in the creation of very large banks that operate across the nation, but also by advancements in technology that allow banking services to be delivered without traditional branch networks.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The article by Avery, Courchane, and Zorn noted that, by 2007, the 25 largest depository institutions operated nearly 40 percent of all retail banking offices, up from just 10 percent in 1987.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: During that same period, their share of deposits more than doubled to nearly 55 percent, while their share of mortgages soared nearly threefold to 67 percent.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: 3 Given merger activity in recent months, consolidation continues to present challenges to local communities as the largest financial institutions grow even larger.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: At the same time, many financial institutions have perfected lending through loan production offices, agents, brokers, and electronic means, making the notion of a local lending area based on deposit-taking branches and automated teller machines seem outmoded.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Perhaps even more striking is the dramatic increase in lending from institutions other than the CRA-regulated financial institutions.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: As securitization grew, the share of mortgage originations by non-CRA-regulated institutions also grew:  in 1990, only 17 percent of mortgage lending was originated by institutions not covered by the CRA.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: This share compares with a peak of 40 percent in 1993 and an average around 30 percent thereafter.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: 4 Moreover, nonbank financial service providers who offer a range of products, such as payday loans, check cashing, remittance services, and other services, have proliferated in recent years and target lower- income areas in particular.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: These services are offered at a very high cost, and yet serve needs that are not fully met by regulated financial institutions.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: While the trend in mortgage lending has abated very recently due to the subprime crisis, the prevalence of alternative financial services has not, and it is clear that CRA's coverage and, arguably, its impact, have diminished as a result.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: After having worked with CRA over the years, I am still surprised at the misperceptions that persist about it.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: One widely held misperception is that CRA is only about mortgage lending to low- and moderate-income borrowers in lower-income neighborhoods.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: As a former community banker, I know that CRA's impact is just as important in meeting the needs of small farms and businesses and, as such, it serves as a valuable catalyst for job creation in both urban and rural areas across the country.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: This point is particularly noteworthy at a time when mounting job losses are adding to the woes of consumers and exacerbating the problems in housing and mortgage lending.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The most recent misperception promulgated by many who either do not know much about the law or don't like it, is that the CRA caused the subprime mortgage meltdown.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Our recent analysis of CRA-related lending found no connection between CRA and the subprime mortgage problems.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In fact, the Board's analysis found that nearly 60 percent of higher-priced loans went to middle- or higher-income borrowers or neighborhoods, which are not the focus of CRA activity.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Additionally, about 20 percent of the higher-priced loans that were extended in low- or moderate-income areas, or to low- or moderate-income borrowers, were loans originated by lenders not covered by the CRA.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Our analysis found, in fact, that only 6 percent of all higher-priced loans were made by CRA-covered lenders to borrowers and neighborhoods targeted by the CRA.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Further, our review of loan performance found that rates of serious mortgage delinquency are high in all neighborhood groups, not just in lower-income areas.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: These conclusions were supported by research conducted by the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco and published in the Revisiting the CRA volume under discussion today.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Moreover, an analysis of foreclosure rates in that study found that loans originated by CRA-covered lenders were significantly less likely to be in foreclosure than those originated by independent mortgage companies.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: 5 Clearly, claims that CRA caused the subprime crisis are not supported by the facts.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The question of the moment, then, is not whether the current crisis was caused by the CRA, but what can be done to make CRA a more effective regulatory incentive going forward as we face an unprecedented set of community needs in the wake of the current foreclosure crisis and the resulting economic slowdown.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Lower-income neighborhoods that were once stable thanks to the efforts of community development practitioners and their banking partners now suffer from the negative effects of high foreclosure rates, including increased numbers of vacant and abandoned property, a loss of equity in their own homes, and higher rates of crime and arson.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Infrastructure in these communities is eroding:  retailers, service providers, and other contributors to the economic health of these neighborhoods are departing.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Communities with lower levels of personal and neighborhood assets, including many minority communities targeted for higher-priced subprime mortgages, have been particularly hard hit.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: 6 As credit has tightened, less capital is available for these communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The pool of loan and investment capital is shrinking at the same time that philanthropic dollars are challenged by investment losses.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: To make matters even more challenging, state and local governments face extraordinary budget deficits and have fewer resources to offer these communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Given this context, it is no surprise that some members of Congress have expressed an interest in considering measures to improve the supervision of financial institutions, including the role of CRA in providing financial products and services to lower-income communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The Federal Reserve Banks of Boston and San Francisco have offered a valuable place to start the discussion of what should come next.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Revisiting the CRA offers more detailed background information about CRA's origins and the developments in the banking industry that I have alluded to here.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Some of the contributing authors recommend revisions to the current regulations, others advocate for the expansion of CRA's coverage, and still others suggest that we start all over again with the creation of a new model for providing financial products and services to underserved communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: A Framework for Change There is no shortage of good thinking in this volume.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: And while I am not prepared to pick and choose among the many options presented in it today, I would like to discuss several in the context of some principles that I think provide a useful framework for thinking about any new regulatory initiative.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Framing the issue may be particularly helpful in trying to imagine CRA's future in a new financial environment.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: First, I believe it is important to be clear about the problem that we are trying to solve.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: When CRA was enacted, the concern was that lower-income communities did not have access to capital and financial services.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: While concern about credit access has begun to resurface in a tightening credit environment, I would hesitate to limit the focus of a new CRA in this way.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Access to credit in lower-income areas has been less of a problem in recent years than has been access to loan products that were fairly priced, well-underwritten by lenders, and well-understood by consumers.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The analysis that I cited earlier regarding the targeting of lower-income and minority communities indicates that we continue to have a problem that warrants regulation.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Whether, as Stella Adams suggests in her article, race should be explicitly considered in evaluating a financial institution's CRA performance or, as Lawrence White suggests in his piece, stronger enforcement of the existing fair lending and antitrust laws make CRA unnecessary, these issues deserve serious debate.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Perhaps, as Larry Lindsey suggests, we should think of financial products and services as a public good and regulate them accordingly.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In any case, it is important that, first, we clarify the problem that needs to be addressed.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Then, we can address whether the solution requires statutory change or whether it can be successfully resolved through revisions to the regulations.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Second, policymakers need to identify who is in the best position to solve the problem identified.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Bill Apgar argues in his paper that an uneven regulatory structure encouraged mortgage companies and non-bank subsidiaries to engage in subprime lending that banks bypassed because of fair lending and CRA requirements.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: He argues that all lenders should have a CRA obligation.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: For years, policymakers have hesitated to expand the coverage of CRA because of the nexus the law created between a financial institution's obligation to its community and its access to deposit insurance and other banking system benefits.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Changing that nexus, it has been argued, could make CRA look more like a tax, which could be more easily attacked politically, than a quid pro quo.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: While the recent expansion of access to the Federal Reserve's discount window might be seen as an opportunity to expand coverage to new entities, it is not clear to me that this nexus alone should be the basis for expanding CRA's coverage.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The concern Apgar raises over the unintended impact of uneven regulation may, in itself, be reason enough to extend CRA coverage to providers of all consumer credit and financial services.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: This concern leads me to my third principle for developing a new CRA structure.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Any new regulatory initiative should be transparent.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: As a former banker, I fully appreciate both the need for regulations that are designed to achieve their goals and the need for those goals to be clearly stated.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: As a former president of the American Bankers Association, I advocated reductions in the regulatory burden.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Regulatory burden refers not just to the number of regulations that an industry must follow, but also the quality of those regulations.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Much of the motivation for the CRA regulatory amendments in the 1990s stemmed from the vagueness of the original 12-assessment-factor approach.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The revised regulations provided the clarity necessary to spur the increases in lending and investment activity that I referred to earlier.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: They provided clearer standards by which financial institutions could organize their activities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: From a consumer perspective, the fact that Congress amended the CRA statute in 1989 to make evaluations public provided the transparency necessary to help create a dialogue between banks and community advocates.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: This dialogue contributed to an increased number of public/private partnerships that were uniquely successful in addressing the economic and community development needs of lower-income communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: A fourth principle, closely related to the need for transparency, is that policymakers should balance the benefits and costs of regulation by taking care to tailor laws and regulations to meet their stated goals as effectively and efficiently as possible.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The documentation requirements should take into account the size and resources of the institution, and they should not overwhelm the activities themselves.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: There is still room to improve CRA in this respect.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: A great deal of justification is required to demonstrate that certain activities qualify for consideration under the regulations.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Much of this is related to the need to demonstrate a benefit to an institution's assessment area.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In order to simplify the regulation's approach to meeting the credit needs of lower-income areas, it may be necessary to consider a different way of measuring impact.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Moreover, measuring performance for any institution must take a broad view of community needs, balancing quantitative measures of performance with consideration of the quality of the credit, investments, and services extended.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Or, as the introductory piece in Revisiting the CRA , by Olson, Chakrabarti, and Essene, suggests, the story of CRA may be one of a regulation that began by measuring process, evolved to a system of measuring outputs, but perhaps, in the future, needs to measure outcomes in lower-income communities.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Finally, any new CRA regulation should be flexible.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: One of CRA's strengths has been the flexibility that the consideration of a bank's performance context provides.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: The regulatory agencies' ability to redesign CRA regulations over the years kept it relevant as the financial markets changed.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: For example, recent revisions recognized the difficulty in meeting the credit needs of rural communities that do not have clearly delineated neighborhoods with differing income levels.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: It also offered added incentives for financial institutions to provide assistance in disaster areas.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: These provisions may not have been possible if Congress had dictated the exact terms of the CRA evaluation that regulators should apply in determining an institution's CRA rating, and, as a general matter, I believe that Congress was wise not to be overly specific in the CRA.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Conclusion The future health of communities depends on each of us doing our part to focus attention on the needs of those communities that have been affected by the combined impact of foreclosures and a weak economy.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: At the encouragement of Congressman Frank, the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston and San Francisco were inspired to broaden policy discussions by inviting CRA experts to contribute to a very thoughtful volume on the future of CRA.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: In formulating a new approach to CRA, I would recommend keeping the most effective feature of the law--its flexibility.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: Any new regulatory structure should also be clear about the problem we are trying to solve, it should determine who is in the best position to solve the problem, and it should be transparent and designed to ensure that community benefit is maximized without placing excessive regulatory burden on financial institutions.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Duke
text: If we follow these principles, I am sure that, together, we can determine the most effective way to improve upon a regulation that has had demonstrated success in making credit available to low-and moderate-income communities, and we can further determine the most effective way to strengthen its role as we meet the challenges ahead.
speech_title: CRA: A Framework for the Future
speech_venue: At the Revisiting the CRA Policy Discussion, Washington, D.C.

speaker: Bernanke
text: It is a great pleasure to be back in Dillon today and to enjoy the signal distinction of having Exit 190 on Interstate 95 named in my honor.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As some of you know, my family ties to Dillon extend back more than six decades.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: My paternal grandparents, Jonas and Lina Bernanke, purchased a drugstore on Dillon's Main Street in 1941 and moved here from New York.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Jonas called the store Jay Bee Drugs, after his own initials.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Eventually, my dad, Philip, and his brother, Mort--who still lives in Dillon--bought the store from my grandfather and ran it for many years.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Dillon had very few doctors at the time, so a lot of people came to my dad and uncle for advice on basic health matters.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: They became known to their customers as "Dr. Phil" and "Dr.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: When my mother, Edna, wasn't keeping an eye on me or my siblings, she kept the store books and paid the bills.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I remember working in the store as a boy, or, as Uncle Mort likes to remind me, avoiding work by hiding out by the comic-book rack.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I attended East Elementary, J.V.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Martin Junior High, and Dillon High School, where I played saxophone in the marching band.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: (I wish Dillon High had a math team when I was attending; I understand this year's team had done quite well.)
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I especially remember with fondness the many friends I made during those years.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I remember, too, in the summer after I graduated from high school, working construction to help build Saint Eugene Hospital, now McLeod Medical Center, and I remember, during the summers of my college years, waiting tables six days a week at South of the Border.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As a teenager, like many teenagers, I itched to get away from the small town in which I grew up.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I got my wish when I left Dillon to attend Harvard University.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: And, although I have since been privileged to study and teach at some of the finest universities in this country, I realize now how much I learned during my 17 years here.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: First and foremost, I learned how very hard people in small towns like Dillon, and in communities large and small all across the United States, have to work to support themselves and their families and to offer opportunities to their children.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I got a taste of that when, on the first day I came home from working on the construction site at St. Eugene's, I was too tired to eat and fell asleep in my chair.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, I learned in Dillon that Americans are economically ambitious.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I remember the fellow construction worker who wanted to become a foreman and the waitress at South of the Border who wanted to be the first in her family to go to college.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I knew that these things characterized Americans then, and know that they still do today.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: So, in that way and many others, I carry my hometown with me, and it is very good to return, if only for a short visit to accept this honor.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I must confess that, until recently, I did not realize that highway interchanges were named after people.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: But, as I thought about it, I realized that it is indeed a high honor for someone whose job is focused on supporting the economy.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Efficient transportation is crucial to economic development.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Indeed, Dillon owed its early prosperity to the railroad station at the center of town, as well as to the cotton and tobacco that flowed through it.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Just as railroads were instrumental to economic development in the 19th century, interstate highways such as I-95--the vision of President Eisenhower--have been crucial in our own time.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The interstates lowered transportation costs markedly and knitted our national economy together, thereby raising productivity.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The proximity of Interstate 95, which stretches the length of the East Coast from Maine to Florida, supports manufacturing and distributive industries in and around Dillon.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Of course, I am aware that Dillon faces challenges today, as do many communities.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: But the area has much to offer.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: This Wellness Center, for example, just two years old, serves as a valuable community resource.
speech_title: Brief Remarks
speech_venue: At the Interstate Interchange Dedication Ceremony, Dillon, South Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: But perhaps Dillon's greatest resource is the determination and resilience of its people.
