speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The perceived stigma of borrowing at the discount window threatened to prevent the Federal Reserve from getting much-needed liquidity into the system.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address this issue, in late 2007, the Federal Reserve established the Term Auction Facility (TAF), which, as the name implies, provides fixed quantities of term credit to depository institutions through an auction mechanism.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The introduction of this facility seems largely to have solved the stigma problem, partly because the sizable number of borrowers provides anonymity, and possibly also because the three-day period between the auction and auction settlement suggests that the facility's users are not relying on it for acute funding needs on a particular day.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As of April 1, 2009, we had roughly $525 billion of discount window credit outstanding, of which about $470 billion had been distributed through auctions and the remainder through conventional discount window loans.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Like depository institutions in the United States, foreign banks with large dollar funding positions were also experiencing powerful liquidity pressures.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: This unmet demand for dollars was spilling over into U.S. markets, including the federal funds market.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: To address this issue, the Federal Reserve has cooperated with foreign central banks in establishing what are known as reciprocal currency arrangements, or liquidity swap lines.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In these arrangements, the Federal Reserve provides dollars to foreign central banks which they, in turn, lend to banks in their jurisdictions.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Credit risk is minimal in these arrangements, as the foreign central bank is responsible for repayment, rather than the institutions that ultimately receive the funds; in addition, the Fed receives foreign currency from its central bank partner of equal value to the dollars lent.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Liquidity provided through such arrangements peaked ahead of year-end 2008 but has since declined as pressures in short-term funding markets have eased; the outstanding amount currently stands at about $310 billion.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, following the sharp deterioration in market conditions in March 2008, the Federal Reserve used its emergency lending authority to provide primary dealers access to central bank credit.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Primary dealers can obtain short-term collateralized loans from the Fed through the Primary Dealer Credit Facility, or PDCF.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The PDCF, which is closely analogous to the discount window for commercial banks, currently has about $20 billion in borrowings outstanding.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Another program for primary dealers, called the Term Securities Lending Facility, lends Treasury securities to dealers, taking investment-grade securities as collateral.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The primary dealers then use the more-liquid Treasury securities to obtain private-sector funding.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Extensions of credit under this program, which currently total about $85 billion, do not appear as distinct assets on the Fed's balance sheet, because the Federal Reserve continues to own the Treasury securities that it lends.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As I mentioned, the provision of liquidity on a collateralized basis to sound financial institutions is a traditional central bank function.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: This so-called lender-of-last-resort activity is particularly useful during a financial crisis, as it reduces the need for fire sales of assets and reassures financial institutions and their counterparties that those institutions will have access to liquidity as needed.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: To be sure, the provision of liquidity alone cannot address solvency problems or erase the large losses that financial institutions have suffered during this crisis.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Yet both our internal analysis and market reports suggest that the Fed's ample supply of liquidity, along with liquidity provided by other major central banks, has significantly reduced funding pressures for financial institutions, helped to reduce rates in bank funding markets, and increased overall financial stability.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, despite ongoing financial stresses, funding pressures around year-end 2008 and the most recent quarter-end appear to have moderated significantly.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Before leaving this category of assets, I should mention briefly the Fed's actions to ensure liquidity to another category of financial institution, money market mutual funds.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In September, a prominent money market mutual fund "broke the buck"--that is, was unable to maintain a net asset value of $1 per share.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: This event led to a run on the other funds, which saw very sharp withdrawals.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: These withdrawals in turn threatened the stability of the commercial paper market, which depends heavily on money market mutual funds as investors.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Following the long-standing principle that the central bank should lend into a panic, the Federal Reserve established two programs to backstop money market mutual funds and to help those funds avoid fire sales of their assets to meet withdrawals.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Together with an insurance program offered by the Treasury, the Fed's programs helped end the run; the sharp withdrawals from the funds have been replaced by moderate inflows.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although credit extended to support money funds was high during the intense phase of the crisis in the fall, borrowings have since declined substantially, to about $6 billion.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Direct Lending to Borrowers and Investors A second set of programs initiated by the Federal Reserve--including the Commercial Paper Funding Facility (CPFF) and the Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility (TALF)--aims to improve the functioning of key credit markets by lending directly to market participants, including ultimate borrowers and major investors.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The lending associated with these facilities is currently about $255 billion, corresponding to roughly one-eighth of the assets on the Fed's balance sheet.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The sizes of these programs, notably the TALF, are expected to grow in the months ahead.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The commercial paper market is a key source of the short-term credit that American businesses use to meet payrolls and finance inventories.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Following the intensification of the financial crisis in the fall, commercial paper rates spiked, even for the highest-quality firms.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, most firms were unable to borrow for periods longer than a few days, exposing both firms and lenders to significant rollover risk.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: By serving as a backstop for commercial paper issuers, the CPFF was intended to address rollover risk and to improve the functioning of this market.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Under this facility, the Fed stands ready to lend to the highest-rated financial and nonfinancial commercial paper issuers for a term of three months.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As additional protection against loss, and to make the facility the last rather than the first resort, the CPFF charges borrowers upfront fees in addition to interest.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Borrowing from this facility peaked at about $350 billion and has since declined to about $250 billion as more firms have been able to issue commercial paper to private lenders or have found alternative sources of finance.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conditions in the market have improved markedly since the introduction of this program, with spreads declining sharply and with more funding available at longer maturities.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Market participants tell us that the CPFF contributed to these improvements.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Most recently, the Federal Reserve launched the TALF, which is aimed at restoring securitization markets, now virtually shut down.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The closing of securitization markets, until recently an important source of credit for the economy, has added considerably to the stress in credit markets and financial institutions generally.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Under the TALF, eligible investors may borrow to finance their holdings of the AAA-rated tranches of selected asset-backed securities.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The program is currently focused on securities backed by newly and recently originated auto loans, credit card loans, student loans, and loans guaranteed by the Small Business Administration.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The first TALF subscription attracted about $8 billion in total asset-backed securities deals and used about $4.7 billion in Federal Reserve financing.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Over time, the list of securities eligible for the TALF is expected to expand to include additional securities, such as commercial mortgages, as well as securities that are not newly issued.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Relative to the Fed's short-term lending to financial institutions, the CPFF and the TALF are rather unconventional programs for a central bank to undertake.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I see them as justified by the extraordinary circumstances in which we find ourselves and by the need for central bank lending practices to reflect the evolution of financial markets; after all, a few decades ago securitization markets barely existed.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Notably, other central banks around the world have shown increasing interest in similar programs as they address the credit strains in their own countries.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: These programs also meet the criteria I stated at the beginning of my remarks regarding credit risk and credit allocation.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Credit risk is very low in both programs; in particular, the TALF program requires that loans be overcollateralized and is further protected by capital provided by the Treasury.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Both programs are directed at broad markets whose dysfunction impedes the flow of numerous types of credit to ultimate borrowers; consequently, I do not see these programs as engaging in credit allocation--the favoring of a particular sector or a narrow class of borrowers over others.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Purchases of High-Quality Assets The third major category of assets on the Fed's balance sheet is holdings of high-quality securities, notably Treasury securities, agency debt, and agency-backed MBS.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: These holdings currently total about $780 billion, or about three-eighths of Federal Reserve assets.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Of this $780 billion, holdings of Treasury securities currently make up about $490 billion.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Some of these Treasury securities are lent out through the Term Securities Lending Facility that I mentioned earlier.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Obviously, these holdings are very safe from a credit perspective.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Longer-term securities do pose some interest-rate risk; however, because the Federal Reserve finances its purchases with short-term liabilities, on average and over time, that risk is mitigated by the normal upward slope of the yield curve.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed's holdings of high-quality securities are set to grow considerably as the FOMC, in an attempt to improve conditions in private credit markets, has announced large-scale open-market purchases of these securities.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Specifically, the Federal Reserve will purchase cumulative amounts of up to $1.25 trillion of agency MBS and up to $200 billion of agency debt by the end of the year, and up to $300 billion of longer-term Treasury securities over the next six months.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The principal goal of these programs is to lower the cost and improve the availability of credit for households and businesses.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As best we can tell, so far the programs are having the intended effect.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, 30-year fixed mortgage rates, which responded very little to our cuts in the target for the federal funds rate, have declined 1 percentage point to 1-1/2 percentage points since our first MBS purchase program was announced in November.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Over time, lower mortgage rates should help to improve conditions in the housing market, whose persistent weakness has had a major impact on economic and financial conditions more broadly, and will improve the financial condition of some households by facilitating refinancing.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, open-market purchases should benefit credit markets by adding liquidity and balance sheet capacity to the system.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Support for Specific Institutions In addition to those programs I have just discussed, the Federal Reserve has provided financing directly to specific systemically important institutions.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: With the full support of the Treasury, we used emergency lending powers to facilitate the acquisition of Bear Stearns by JPMorgan Chase & Co. and also to prevent default by AIG.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: These extensions of credit are very different than the other liquidity programs discussed previously and were put in place to avoid major disruptions in financial markets.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: From a credit perspective, these support facilities carry more risk than traditional central bank liquidity support, but we nevertheless expect to be fully repaid.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Credit extended under these programs has varied but recently has accounted for only about 5 percent of our balance sheet.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: That said, these operations have been extremely uncomfortable for the Federal Reserve to undertake and were carried out only because no reasonable alternative was available.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As noted in the joint Federal Reserve-Treasury statement I mentioned earlier, we are working with the Administration and the Congress to develop a formal resolution regime for systemically critical nonbank financial institutions, analogous to one already in place for banks.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Such a regime should spell out as precisely as possible the role that the Congress expects the Federal Reserve to play in such resolutions.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Liabilities Having reviewed the Federal Reserve's main asset accounts, let me now touch briefly on the liability side of the balance sheet.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Historically, the largest component of the Federal Reserve's liabilities has historically been Federal Reserve notes--that is, U.S. paper currency.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Currency has expanded over time in line with nominal spending in the United States and demands for U.S. currency abroad.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: By some estimates, a bit over one-half of U.S. currency is held outside the country.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Other key liabilities of the Federal Reserve include the deposit accounts of the U.S. government and depository institutions.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The U.S. government maintains a "checking account" with the Federal Reserve--the so-called Treasury general account--from which most federal payments are made.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: More recently, the Treasury has established a special account at the Federal Reserve as part of its Supplementary Financing Program (SFP).
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Under this program, the Treasury issues special Treasury bills and places the proceeds in the Treasury supplementary financing account at the Federal Reserve.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The net effect of these operations is to drain reserve balances from depository institutions.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Depository institutions also maintain accounts at the Federal Reserve, of course, and over recent months, as the size of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet has expanded, the balances held in these accounts have increased substantially.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The large volume of reserve balances outstanding must be monitored carefully, as--if not carefully managed--they could complicate the Fed's task of raising short-term interest rates when the economy begins to recover or if inflation expectations were to begin to move higher.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have a number of tools we can use to reduce bank reserves or increase short-term interest rates when that becomes necessary.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: First, many of our lending programs extend credit primarily on a short-term basis and thus could be wound down relatively quickly.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: In addition, since the lending rates in these programs are typically set above the rates that prevail in normal market conditions, borrower demand for these facilities should wane as conditions improve.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Second, the Federal Reserve can conduct reverse repurchase agreements against its long-term securities holdings to drain bank reserves or, if necessary, it could choose to sell some of its securities.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Of course, for any given level of the federal funds rate, an unwinding of lending facilities or a sale of securities would constitute a de facto tightening of policy, and so would have to be carefully considered in that light by the FOMC.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Third, some reserves can be soaked up by the Treasury's Supplementary Financing Program.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Fourth, in October of last year, the Federal Reserve received long-sought authority to pay interest on the reserve balances of depository institutions.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Raising the interest rate paid on reserves will encourage depository institutions to hold reserves with the Fed, rather than lending them into the federal funds market at a rate below the rate paid on reserves.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: 5 Thus, the interest rate paid on reserves will tend to set a floor on the federal funds rate.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The FOMC will continue to closely monitor the level and projected expansion of bank reserves to ensure that--as noted in the joint Federal Reserve-Treasury statement--the Fed's efforts to improve the workings of credit markets do not interfere with the independent conduct of monetary policy in the pursuit of its dual mandate of ensuring maximum employment and price stability.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: As was also noted in the joint statement, to provide additional assurance on this score, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury have agreed to seek legislation to provide additional tools for managing bank reserves.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Conclusion These are extraordinarily challenging times for our financial system and our economy.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: I am confident that we can meet these challenges, not least because I have great confidence in the underlying strengths of the American economy.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: For its part, the Federal Reserve will make responsible use of all its tools to stabilize financial markets and institutions, to promote the extension of credit to creditworthy borrowers, and to help build a foundation for economic recovery.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Over the longer term, we also look forward to working with our counterparts at other supervisory and regulatory agencies in the United States and around the world to address the structural issues--some of which have been discussed in this conference--that have led to this crisis so as to minimize the risk of ever facing such a situation again.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Department of the Treasury (2009), " The Role of the Federal Reserve in Preserving Financial and Monetary Stability: Joint Statement by the Department of the Treasury and the Federal Reserve ," joint press release, March 23.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2. Credit and Liquidity Programs and the Balance Sheet is available on the Board's website.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Agency debt, in this instance, is debt issued by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and the Federal Home Loan Banks.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Agency MBS are backed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Primary dealers are broker-dealers that trade in U.S. government securities with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: The interest rate on reserves did not establish a hard floor on the federal funds rate during the short period between the time that payment of interest on reserves was introduced and the FOMC's decision to bring the federal funds rate target close to zero.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: Possible reasons were the unfamiliarity of banks with the program, the fact that some institutions are not legally eligible to receive interest on reserve balances and were therefore willing to lend funds in the federal funds market at a rate below the rate paid by the Fed, and the reluctance of banks to use scarce balance sheet space to arbitrage the difference between the federal funds rate and the rate paid on reserves.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Bernanke
text: We expect these problems to be reduced with time.
speech_title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond 2009 Credit Markets Symposium, Charlotte, North Carolina

speaker: Kohn
text: I am glad to be back at Wooster.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: As I know from my time here, a strength of a small liberal arts school like Wooster is its ability to draw on the diverse perspectives of people of different disciplines and backgrounds to work closely with students in examining important issues, and I'm pleased to be part of such an effort today.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: My role today is to discuss the actions the government is taking to address our current financial and economic difficulties.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Although my fellow panelists will be discussing how we got here and the regulatory policies we should adopt to prevent a recurrence, I won't be able to fulfill my task without impinging a bit on their topics.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The choice of policies follows by necessity from the diagnosis of the causes of the problems being addressed.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: And, as we address the challenges of the here and now, we cannot lose sight of the longer-term policy adjustments that we will have to make to avoid similar crises in the future.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: I should say at the outset that I will focus today on the economic and financial problems and policy responses in the United States.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: However, because capital markets and financial institutions are linked globally, financial dislocations and their consequences have been felt around the world.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, other countries have taken policy steps similar to those taken here, including traditional and nontraditional monetary policy, programs to support banking institutions, and fiscal stimulus.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: This is truly a global crisis, and it is a hopeful sign that the need for forceful policy responses to the serious challenges we face is broadly recognized.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Characteristics of the Crisis A defining characteristic of the crisis has been a deepening adverse feedback loop in which financial strains have caused economic weakness, which has in turn led to credit losses and heightened financial strains, which then contribute to further economic weakness, and so on.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The trigger for the crisis when it broke in the summer of 2007 was a weakening of the housing market and a sharp rise in delinquencies on subprime mortgages.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: These delinquencies were importantly the result of a breakdown in underwriting standards that reflected, in part, incentive problems in the securitization process.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Lenders did not see a need to underwrite carefully because they did not intend to hold the loans themselves.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, based on experience over recent years, investors expected property prices to rise; they did not appreciate the extent of the bubble in housing prices, and so they did not focus as much as they should have on the ability of the borrowers to repay the loans--or pieces of loans--they were purchasing.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Complex and opaque securitizations of loans made due diligence on the underlying credits nearly impossible.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: As losses on subprime loans mounted, investors realized that even highly rated securities backed by subprime mortgages could face large write-downs, and the prices of such securities declined sharply.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Uncertainty about the extent of banks' mortgage-related losses and their potential liquidity needs to support off-balance-sheet entities led banks to become much less willing to lend to each other and to other financial institutions.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The result was a sharp widening of risk spreads in key funding markets.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Leverage in the financial sector, which had contributed to higher profits during the financial boom, was now seen to be excessive.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: As financial firms moved to reduce their exposures, they became less willing to make markets, and the liquidity of many securities declined.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Although housing was the trigger and the largest single source of problems, as time went on it became clear that problems in financial institutions and markets were more broadly based.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Risk on a variety of assets had not been priced appropriately, and risk spreads in a range of markets increased, as did the equity risk premium.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Markets for private asset-backed securities (ABS) were hit especially hard.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Reflecting the deterioration in funding conditions, as well as efforts to conserve capital and liquidity, banks tightened lending standards and terms on loans to both businesses and households.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: With both financial markets and intermediaries under considerable strain, credit became more expensive and, in some cases, unobtainable, causing spending to be reduced.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The weaker economy in turn contributed to further deterioration in asset quality and concerns about greater losses to come.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: As a result, banks and other lenders tightened their lending stance further, which put additional downward pressure on spending.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: This adverse feedback loop, which was already visible from late 2007, intensified considerably last fall.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Failures and near-failures of some major financial institutions greatly undermined confidence in financial institutions and severely disrupted financial markets, leading to a further sharp tightening of credit conditions.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Risk spreads, which were already elevated, escalated further and equity prices fell.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the financial turmoil contributed to a sharp decline in consumer and business confidence.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The result was a major pullback in spending as consumers responded to decreases in wealth and the deterioration in their future employment prospects and as businesses, worried about the demand for their products, cut back on capital spending and sharply reduced production to avoid an accumulation of unsold stocks.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: A gradual decline in economic activity through most of 2008 took a decided turn for the worse late in the year.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The Policy Response Because the threat to economic stability in the current episode has been so closely related to problems in the financial sector, most of the policy responses have been focused on financial institutions and markets and the flow of credit to households and businesses.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Many of these policies have been aimed at countering the tightening of financial conditions that occurred as lenders became more risk averse and took steps to conserve capital and liquidity.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: To that end, the Federal Reserve has lowered interest rates, made backup sources of liquidity available to private lenders, and used its own lending capacity to try to revive a variety of financial markets.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, the Federal Reserve, the Treasury, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) have taken a number of steps to stabilize and repair financial institutions in order to limit the tendency of those institutions to pull back from lending and thereby intensify the decline in spending.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Other government policies operate at the intersection of the financial and real sectors.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Foreclosure mitigation, for example, not only serves to keep people in their homes, but also should reduce downward pressures on house prices and hold down loan losses at lenders.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, fiscal stimulus works directly on demand, in effect bypassing the financial sector in its first-round effects; by strengthening aggregate demand, it too should help alleviate strains on lenders and contribute to stemming the vicious cycle.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Although I'll be discussing each of these policy initiatives separately, it is important to keep their interactions in mind.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: They all attempt to break into that adverse feedback loop we've been talking about at different points in the chain of cause and effect and then cause again.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The expectation of recovery rests importantly on the natural recuperative powers of the economy, but it also depends on the effects of the various policy efforts reinforcing each other: A stable financial system is critical to realizing the positive effects of monetary and fiscal policies; the financial system won't stabilize very quickly without monetary and fiscal stimulus to help support spending and ease credit problems.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Monetary Policy In response to the rise in credit spreads and tightening of credit conditions, the Federal Reserve has aggressively eased monetary policy, as conventionally defined by the target for the federal funds rate.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In the second half of 2007 and into the spring of 2008, the federal funds rate target was cut rapidly, and, as the financial turbulence intensified last fall and the economic outlook deteriorated, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) responded by cutting the target further, setting a range of 0 to 1/4 percent by the end of last year.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: With the federal funds rate already near zero, the FOMC noted, in the statement after its March meeting, "that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period."
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: By communicating this expectation, the Committee reinforced market beliefs that policy is likely to remain on hold, and so put downward pressure on longer-term rates.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Because it is these longer-term rates that have the largest effects on spending behavior, this sort of communication can be very useful in stimulating borrowing and spending by businesses and households.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition to easing the traditional interest rate instrument of monetary policy, the Federal Reserve has taken a range of other policy steps to ease credit conditions and support the broader economy.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: From the onset of the crisis in the summer of 2007, we could see that widening spreads in interbank funding markets were putting upward pressure on the interest rates paid and charged by banks.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: To combat the strains in these markets, the Federal Reserve provided credit to banks on more generous terms and at longer maturities than usual.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve subsequently introduced the Term Auction Facility, under which it holds auctions of fixed amounts of term credit to banks on a regular schedule.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: By providing banks with a more assured source of liquidity, these changes limited banks' need to bolster liquidity through fire sales of assets and so made them more willing to lend and to make markets.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: The Federal Reserve also expanded its provision of liquidity beyond U.S. banking institutions to other financial institutions and market participants.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Because foreign dollar funding markets affect U.S. markets, swap lines were established with foreign central banks in late 2007 (and have since been expanded significantly), allowing them to obtain dollars so that they could meet the dollar liquidity needs of banks in their jurisdictions.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: As some large investment banks came increasingly under pressure in early 2008, the Federal Reserve, consistent with its role as lender of last resort and in light of the key roles these institutions play in a range of financial markets, introduced programs under which it could provide liquidity to primary dealers.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: 2 And, as the financial situation deteriorated last fall, the Federal Reserve established liquidity facilities for money market mutual funds and introduced programs to provide liquidity directly to borrowers and investors in key credit markets, including the commercial paper market, where strains threatened the ability of many financial and nonfinancial firms to place their paper.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: More recently, the Federal Reserve and the Treasury have teamed up to try to restart the markets in which loans had been securitized to be sold to final investors.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Until the crisis, ABS issuance was a key source of funding for consumer loans, small business loans, student loans, and other types of household and business credit.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: However, after the substantial losses on residential mortgage-backed securities, and with the economy weakening, investors became wary of all structured securities; spreads on ABS rose sharply and issuance tailed off last fall.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Under the Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility (TALF), the Federal Reserve will provide loans against a variety of ABS while the private sector and the Treasury take most of the risk.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, the Federal Reserve has begun making substantial purchases of longer-term securities in order to support market functioning and reduce interest rates in the mortgage and private credit markets.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: As recently as our March meeting, the FOMC increased the total planned amount of purchases of agency-guaranteed mortgage-backed securities and initiated a program of buying longer-term Treasury securities.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: I believe these efforts have been somewhat successful at addressing the "tightening in financial conditions" side of the adverse feedback loop.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Short-term interest rates are much lower than they were when the crisis began, and so are mortgage rates--at least those on mortgages eligible to be guaranteed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Functioning of the commercial paper market has greatly improved.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Banks, investment banks, and money market mutual funds tell us that without the liquidity backstops we have provided, they would have had to shrink and deleverage much more rapidly, which would have put downward pressure on asset prices and would have further reduced credit availability for households and businesses.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: But we are not out of the woods yet.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: For many borrowers, credit remains much harder to get and far more expensive than it was in the summer of 2007.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Some reductions in leverage and tightening of credit conditions relative to earlier this decade clearly were needed, and I expect that lower leverage and tighter lending standards and terms will be enduring features of the financial landscape.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: But current credit conditions are far tighter than these adjustments would seem to justify.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Many financial markets remain under considerable stress, asset prices have been reduced by the lack of liquidity in markets, and credit spreads and availability still reflect very high aversion to risk.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: These conditions are not conducive to a substantial and sustained economic rebound, and the Federal Reserve will continue to be alert to ways that monetary policy can contribute to economic recovery.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: We are also conscious of a potential adverse feedback loop between persistent economic weakness and a continuing decline in inflation and inflation expectations.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: With the federal funds rate about as low as it can go, significant further decreases in inflation as a result of the substantial slack in resources, lower import prices, and declines in the prices of oil and other commodities could imply an increase in the real federal funds rate.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, if such a process continued for some time, we could fall into deflation, much as Japan did for a time in the 1990s and earlier this decade.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Then again, the substantial increase in the size of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet as a result of the credit programs that have been implemented have led some to worry that inflation could rise sharply when the economy recovers unless the Federal Reserve moves quickly when the time comes to unwind the programs and limit the growth in credit.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Because inflation expectations play a key role in the setting of prices and wages, firmly anchored inflation expectations can help avoid both of these outcomes.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: To help anchor inflation expectations, the FOMC is now providing extended projections of inflation--along with growth and unemployment--in its quarterly economic projections.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: To address concerns about its ability to rein in its balance sheet, the Federal Reserve must be prepared to exit from its various programs when the time is right.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: We have designed many of our facilities to discourage use when markets are functioning more normally, and securities that have been accumulated can be sold when such sales are judged to be appropriate.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: However, given very large purchases of long-term assets and substantial long-term lending for the TALF and other purposes, the Federal Reserve would benefit from new tools that would allow it to drain reserves from the banking system.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: We are working with the Treasury and the Congress to obtain such tools.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Financial Repair In addition to the Federal Reserve's monetary policy actions, which broadly support the financial sector and the economy, the government--including the Treasury, the Federal Reserve, and the FDIC--has been working to provide more direct support to financial firms.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In part, this effort has involved targeted actions to prevent the failure or substantial weakening of specific systemically important institutions, including Bear Stearns, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, AIG (American International Group, Inc.), Citigroup, and Bank of America.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: These actions were not taken to protect the affected firms' managers or shareholders from the costs of past mistakes.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Indeed, managers have been replaced in some cases, and shareholders of the weakest firms have experienced massive losses.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Instead, our actions have been driven by concerns that the disorderly failure of a large, complex, interconnected firm would impose significant losses on creditors, including other financial firms, dislocate a range of financial markets, and impede the flow of credit to households and businesses.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Losses sustained by other financial firms could erode their financial strength, limiting their ability to play their intermediation role, or even cause them to fail, reinforcing financial pressures.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the disorderly failure of a large, complex interconnected firm could undermine confidence in the U.S. financial sector more broadly, potentially triggering a widespread withdrawal of funding by investors and an additional tightening of credit conditions, which would, in turn, cause a further reduction in economic activity.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Besides this targeted support, the government has undertaken programs to inject capital more broadly into the banking system.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Since last fall, nearly $200 billion has been distributed under a Treasury program that provides government capital investments to banks in good condition.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: More recently, the Treasury, in conjunction with the bank supervisory agencies, announced a new program to ensure that U.S. banking institutions are appropriately capitalized.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Under this program, the capital needs of the major U.S. banking institutions are being evaluated relative to the losses that would be anticipated under a significantly more challenging economic environment than anticipated in the consensus of private forecasters.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Should that assessment indicate that an additional temporary capital buffer is warranted, institutions will have an opportunity to raise the capital from private sources.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: If these efforts are unsuccessful, the temporary capital buffer will be made available from the government.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: By providing additional capital, the government can reduce concerns about the adequacy of bank capital, build investor confidence in U.S. banking institutions and the U.S. financial sector more generally, and so ease financial pressures and encourage new lending.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition to providing capital, the government, through the FDIC, has temporarily guaranteed selected liabilities of insured depository institutions and their holding companies.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: This program provides a stable source of funds for these institutions and so eases the pressures on funding that some of them faced.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Finally, the Treasury recently announced a program to assist banks and other lenders in reducing their "legacy assets"--that is, real estate loans held directly on their books ("legacy loans") and securities backed by loan portfolios ("legacy securities") that were accumulated during the housing boom and which have since declined in value and become relatively illiquid.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Uncertainty about the value of legacy assets is weighing on confidence in banks, reflecting concerns that the assets will turn out to be worth much less than currently thought and so undermine the financial strength of the banks holding them.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the lack of liquid markets for legacy assets means that banks cannot readily manage the associated risks and cannot easily make room on their balance sheets for new loans if they have attractive lending opportunities.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: In part, buyers for these assets are scarce because credit is expensive and difficult to obtain and because investors are highly averse to risk.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
speech_venue: At the Forum on Great Decisions in the Economic Crisis, College of Wooster, Wooster, Ohio

speaker: Kohn
text: Under the new program, the Treasury, with the participation of the FDIC and the Federal Reserve, is establishing public-private investment funds to purchase legacy assets.
speech_title: Policies to Bring Us Out of the Financial Crisis and Recession
