speaker: Kohn
text: And tight credit conditions--especially for commercial construction--likely will be a significant negative force.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: But here too, confidence could bounce back more rapidly, and if credit conditions were to ease appreciably, businesses might move ahead quickly with capital spending projects that had been postponed during the recession.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Exports were an important source of strength for the U.S. economy in recent years.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: However, the global nature of the current economic downturn means that they are unlikely to provide much support for domestic production going forward.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Activity in foreign economies, taken together, contracted in the fourth quarter at a rapid pace--similar to that in the United States.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Recent indicators point to equally dismal outcomes in the first quarter and, although there have been a few signs of stabilization, have yet to send a clear signal that the global economy has hit bottom.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: The intensification of financial turmoil was global, and many of our trading partners are also facing constraints on credit availability.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Although the recovery in the U.S. economy is likely to be gradual in its early stages, it should gain momentum over time.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: As credit markets improve, the accommodative stance of monetary policy will show through more clearly.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: And a rebound in confidence about the future should help spur demand.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: As demand strengthens and financial markets improve, some of the adverse feedbacks should reverse and begin working to bolster activity.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: In time, as these forces come into play, economic growth will pick up, ultimately returning the economy to its full productive capacity and bringing the unemployment rate down to a more normal level.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Inflation Prospects If, as I have described, the economic recovery initially follows a relatively gradual track, margins of slack in labor and product markets are likely to remain wide for a time, implying some further downward pressure on inflation.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: The extent of a decline in inflation, however, should be limited by the relative stability of longer-term inflation expectations.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: That said, there are sizable risks on both sides of the inflation forecast.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: On the one hand, we cannot rule out the possibility that adverse economic conditions will cause deeper cuts in prices, a greater softening in wages, and a steep decline in inflation expectations.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Substantial declines in inflation would raise real interest rates, thereby restraining the recovery even more.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, the risk that inflation could be lower will be exacerbated to the extent that economic activity falls short of the path that I have described.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: In these circumstances, the Federal Reserve would continue to look for ways to relieve financial pressures and encourage spending.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: On the other hand, the Federal Reserve's actions to ease credit conditions have resulted in a tremendous increase in its assets and in bank reserves.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Some observers have expressed concern that these actions, if not reversed in a timely manner, are sowing the seeds of a sharp pickup in inflation down the road.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: As I just noted, near-term prospects appear to be for a decline in inflation rather than an increase.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: But my colleagues and I are acutely aware of the risk of higher inflation as the economic recovery gains speed.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: We are firmly committed to acting in a way that preserves price stability, and we believe we have the tools to absorb reserves and raise interest rates when needed.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Moreover, we are working with the Treasury to introduce legislation that would enlarge our tool kit for moving away from the extraordinary degree of financial stimulus we have put in place when the time arrives.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Conclusion To sum up, the uncertainty around the economic outlook is substantial.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: The path of the economy will depend critically on how quickly the current stresses in financial markets abate; these events have few if any precedents, and thus it is very difficult to predict how the  adjustment process will play out.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: But at the end of the process, our financial system will be on firmer footing.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Both markets and regulators will continue to press financial firms to employ less leverage and have more reliable sources of liquidity, and those firms will have every incentive to more effectively price, monitor, and manage risk.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Improvements to the supervisory and regulatory framework will help create a more stable financial system.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: In addition, we will have a stronger economy.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: Businesses will have boosted the efficiency of their operations.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: And households will be less indebted and saving more.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: That greater saving will, all else being equal, support greater investment or allow domestic saving to displace foreign saving for a more sustainable international position.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: The U.S. economy has proven itself over the years to be flexible and resilient as well as innovative and productive, qualities that enable it to rebound from serious economic shocks, and I am confident that, in a like manner, we will rebound from our current economic and financial challenges.
speech_title: The Economic Outlook
speech_venue: At the Hutchinson Lecture, Newark, Delaware

speaker: Kohn
text: The views are my own and not necessarily those of other members of the Federal Open Market Committee.

speaker: Bernanke
text: After more than a year and a half of financial crisis, both bankers and policymakers must contend with two questions: What have we learned from this extraordinary episode?
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: And how can we apply those lessons to strengthen our banking system and to avoid or mitigate future crises?
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Getting the answers to these questions right is critical for our future financial and economic health.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has been intensively evaluating the lessons of the crisis, both with respect to the companies we supervise and to our own policies and procedures, and we are actively incorporating what we have learned into daily supervisory practice.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Increasing the effectiveness of supervision must be a top priority for our institution.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In my remarks today I will outline some steps that the Federal Reserve has already taken in the wake of the crisis to strengthen capital, liquidity, and risk management in the banking sector, as well as to improve the supervisory process itself.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: I will also touch on what we have learned about the importance of effective consolidated supervision and the potential benefits of a more macroprudential orientation to financial oversight.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's Role in Banking Supervision It may be useful first to briefly review the Federal Reserve's bank supervisory responsibilities and how they interact with the other parts of our mission.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed has supervisory and regulatory authority over bank holding companies (including financial holding companies), state-chartered banks that choose to join the Federal Reserve System (state member banks), the U.S. operations of foreign banking organizations, and certain types of U.S. entities that engage in international banking.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 2 In fulfilling these responsibilities, we work with other federal and state supervisory authorities to promote the safety and soundness of the banking industry, foster the stability of the broader financial system, and help ensure fair and equitable treatment of consumers in their financial transactions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve Banks manage the process of onsite bank examinations, while providing a strong regional presence that allows us greater insight into local economic conditions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Besides working with other U.S. agencies responsible for the oversight of banking and other areas of the financial system, we also coordinate closely with foreign supervisors.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: These relationships are fostered through regular interactions within bodies such as the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Through these organizations we contribute to the development of international banking standards.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For example, we helped lead the Basel Committee's development of the revised Principles of Liquidity Risk Management , which was issued last year and is currently being incorporated into supervisory guidance in the United States.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 3 Our close relationships with key foreign supervisors, central banks, and other authorities have proved very helpful as we have dealt with the challenges of the crisis.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve's role in banking supervision complements its other responsibilities, especially its role in managing financial crises--a point I have made on other occasions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 4 The complementary nature of its functions was evident, for example, after the September 11 terrorist attacks, when the Federal Reserve's supervisory staff provided critical assistance to policymakers in evaluating conditions in the financial sector in a quickly evolving, chaotic situation.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: During the current crisis, supervisory expertise and information have repeatedly proved invaluable in helping us to address potential systemic risks involving specific financial institutions and markets and to effectively fulfill our role as lender of last resort.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our supervisors' knowledge of interbank lending markets and other sources of bank funding also contributed to the development of new tools to address financial stress, such as our Term Auction Facility.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Fed's prudential supervision benefits, in turn, from the expertise we develop in carrying out other parts of our mission--for example, the knowledge of financial and economic conditions we gather in the formulation of monetary policy and the insight into retail financial markets that flows from our consumer protection responsibilities.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Lessons from the Financial Crisis Since the onset of the crisis, the Federal Reserve and other U.S. supervisors--in many cases along with supervisors from other countries--have been working to identify both its causes and its lessons.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Our contributions have been reflected in reports issued by, among others, the Financial Stability Board, the President's Working Group on Financial Markets, and the Senior Supervisors Group, which includes representatives of seven industrial countries.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 5 Ongoing international collaboration, which began before the crisis, has enabled U.S. supervisors to learn from the international experience and allowed us to compare the performances of individual U.S. institutions with those of a broad cross section of global financial firms.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve is also in the midst of its own comprehensive review of all aspects of its supervisory practices.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Since last year, Vice Chairman Kohn has led an effort, with participation from Board members, Reserve Bank presidents, and staff from around the System, to develop recommendations for improvements in our conduct of both prudential supervision and consumer protection.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: We are including feedback from the Government Accountability Office, the Congress, the Treasury, and others as we look to improve our own supervisory practices.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Among other things, our analysis reaffirms that capital adequacy, effective liquidity planning, and strong risk management are essential for safe and sound banking; the crisis revealed serious deficiencies on the part of some financial institutions in one or more of the areas.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The crisis has likewise underscored the need for heightened vigilance and forcefulness on the part of supervisors to make sure that standards are met.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Strengthening Capital, Liquidity, and Risk Management Because capital serves as such an important bulwark against potential unexpected loss, U.S. supervisors have been giving it very close attention since the beginning of the crisis.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have been closely monitoring firms' capital levels relative to their risk exposures and discussing our evaluations with senior management.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have also been revisiting our policies regarding capital; for example, earlier this year we issued supervisory guidance for bank holding companies on dividends, capital repurchases, and capital redemptions, reemphasizing in the process that holding companies must serve as a source of strength for their subsidiary banks.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As you may know, the Federal Reserve is leading the interagency Supervisory Capital Assessment Program, which is aimed at ensuring that the largest and most systemically important U.S. banking organizations have a capital buffer sufficient to remain well-capitalized and actively lending, even should macroeconomic conditions prove worse than currently anticipated.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: More than 150 examiners, supervisors, and economists from the Federal Reserve, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation cooperated in a simultaneous review and evaluation of the prospective losses and earnings of 19 major institutions, which collectively hold about two-thirds of the assets of the U.S. banking system.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The exercise has been comprehensive, rigorous, forward-looking, and highly collaborative among the supervisory agencies.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Undoubtedly, we can use many aspects of the exercise to improve our supervisory processes in the future.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Although capital remains a critical bulwark of a strong banking system, the crisis has also demonstrated the importance of effective liquidity management.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Along with our colleagues at the other U.S. banking agencies, we are monitoring the major firms' liquidity positions on a daily basis and are discussing liquidity strategies, key market developments, and liquidity risks with the firms' senior managements.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As we have learned over the past year and a half, adequate liquidity management entails more than holding assets that are liquid in normal times; firms must take into account how their liquidity positions might fare under stressed market conditions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: We are also requiring firms to consider risks arising from the need to fund off-balance-sheet positions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The third key element of safe and sound banking, after capital and liquidity, is effective risk management.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The crisis exposed the inadequacy of the risk-management systems of many financial institutions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: We have stepped up our efforts to work with banks to improve their risk-identification practices.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For instance, we have emphasized to banks the importance of stress testing to help detect risks not identified by more-typical statistical models, such as abnormally large market moves, evaporation of liquidity, prolonged periods of market distress, or structural changes in markets.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As I noted in a speech last month, financial innovation can benefit consumers, the financial system, and the broader economy, but it also has risks that must be properly understood.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 6 Indeed, as you know, financial innovations in areas such as structured credit products and mortgage lending in some degree helped precipitate the current crisis.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Accordingly, we are requiring banks to evaluate more comprehensively the possible unintended consequences of proposed new financial instruments as well as how those instruments are likely to perform under stressed market conditions.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Counterparty credit risk is another area in which the Federal Reserve has been working for some time, and, as the crisis has unfolded, we have intensified our monitoring of how firms manage this type of risk.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Institutions are being pushed to further improve their understanding of key linkages and exposures across the financial system.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: They are also being asked to analyze how their own defensive actions during periods of stress might put pressure on key counterparties, especially when other market participants are likely to be taking similar measures.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: A critical component of risk management is understanding the links between incentives and risk-taking, such as in the design and implementation of compensation practices.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Bonuses and other compensation should provide incentives for employees at all levels to behave in ways that promote the long-run health of the institution.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: The Federal Reserve has been working in international forums on compensation and incentives issues; one product of those efforts was the publication last month by the Financial Stability Board of new principles for sound compensation practices.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: 7 Certainly, an important lesson of the crisis is that the structure of compensation and its effect on incentives for risk-taking is a safety-and-soundness issue.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: In this and other areas, one of the key lessons for bankers has been the need for timely and effective internal communication about risks.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: We are putting a high priority on ensuring that management and board of directors are well informed about the various risks that confront the organization and that they are actively engaged in the management of those risks.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: As we have worked with financial institutions to strengthen their governance and risk management, we are also mindful that the crisis has revealed the need for improvement in our own supervisory procedures and internal communication.
speech_title: Lessons of the Financial Crisis for Banking Supervision
speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: For instance, it directs the staff to pay special attention to activities--such as clearing and settlement in critical financial markets--that have the potential to affect not only the institution, but the financial system more broadly.

speaker: Bernanke

text: The guidance also reaffirms that examiners must assess the financial condition and risk profile of a holding company's nonbank subsidiaries to understand their potential for adversely affecting the affiliated banks or the organization as a whole.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Consolidated supervision also improves our evaluation of firms' ability to comply with applicable laws, rules, and regulations.

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke
text: Compliance with consumer protection regulations receives close scrutiny, and consumer compliance specialists participate in the evaluation of the risk assessments, supervisory plans, and annual letters that our supervisors prepare for large, complex banking organizations.

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

text: Consistent with these provisions, we have worked with other regulators and, wherever possible, sought to make good use of the information and analysis they provide.

speaker: Bernanke

speaker: Bernanke
text: Moreover, our consolidated supervision guidance has helped to clarify the protocols for relying on other supervisors, as well as to identify cases in which we need to take a more active role as the consolidated supervisor.

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speaker: Bernanke

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)

speech_venue: At the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, Chicago, Illinois (via satellite)
